# ForkMesh documentation

ForkMesh is a decentralized Git hosting network: signed repositories replicate
across independent mirror nodes, and the desktop, web and mobile clients read
and write them through a shared protocol. Every Markdown file and JSON schema in
this directory is rendered at [forkmesh.com/docs/library](https://forkmesh.com/docs/library/)
by `app/tools/docs_site.py`, which also builds the page history at
[forkmesh.com/docs/history](https://forkmesh.com/docs/history/) and the
document index at [forkmesh.com/docs/documents](https://forkmesh.com/docs/documents/).
Developer documentation per subsystem is in the [developer docs index](../../docs/README.md).

## Getting started

## Directory layout

- `design/`: protocol and federation design decisions.
- `protocol/`: the versioned protocol suite, bound to `conformance/protocol/v1`.
- `governance/`, `funding/`: charters and generated registers, bound to `conformance/governance/v1` and `conformance/funding/v1`.
- `engineering/`: quality gates, performance budgets and completion policy.
- `security/`: security boundaries and local integration contracts.
- `operations/`: deployment, recovery, gateways, headless nodes and runbooks.
- `mobile/`: mobile node contract, the mobile Git engine, and phone guides (Siri, Apple Health, file editing, agent access).
- `plugins/`, `launch/`, `strategy/`, `research/`: planned plugins, launch material and research.
- `*.schema.json`: machine-readable configuration and protocol schemas.

When reporting a problem, include the version, the action taken and the
relevant log excerpt; see the [ForkMesh desktop app guide](qt-client.md) for log locations.

pages.markdown:
# Getting started with ForkMesh

## Install

```sh
curl -fsSL https://forkmesh.com/install.sh | bash
```

To build from source, clone `https://forkmesh.com/forkmesh/forkmesh` and run
`./desktop/run.sh` (Qt 6.4+, CMake 3.16+, OpenSSL headers, Git, a C++17
compiler). See the [desktop app guide](qt-client.md) and the
[installation support matrix](install-support-matrix.md).

### Opening ForkMesh again on Linux

The installer puts the program at `~/.local/bin/forkmesh` and starts it once.
After you close it:

- Open your applications menu (on GNOME press the Super key, on KDE click the
  launcher) and search for **ForkMesh**. ForkMesh adds itself there the first
  time it runs. To keep it handy, right-click its icon in the dock and choose
  **Pin to Dash** or **Add to Favorites**.
- Or open a terminal and type `forkmesh`. If the terminal says the command is
  not found, type `~/.local/bin/forkmesh` instead.

## Accounts and instances

- **One account everywhere.** The website, the desktop app and the phone apps
  use the same ForkMesh account. There is no separate desktop password: sign
  in with the email and password that work on the website.
- **Your username** is the name on your ForkMesh profile (it appears as
  `@name`), not your email. The desktop may suggest one when you first sign in;
  change it if it is not yours. If you get it wrong, the desktop tells you
  which username your email belongs to.
- **An instance** is the ForkMesh server that holds your account.
  `forkmesh.com` is the main one; leave the instance as it is unless someone
  gave you a different address. Choosing **Continue** on the sign-in screen
  only signs you in: it does not create an account or an instance. To create
  an account, use **Create account**, which opens the website.
- **The eye button** in the password box shows what you typed.
- **Too many wrong passwords** pause sign-in for a short time. The message
  says how long to wait; your password has not changed, so use the same one
  after the pause.

## First run

1. Launch ForkMesh. A local Ed25519 node identity is created; no server URL is needed.
2. Optionally sign in from **Settings** for a portable public username.
3. Open **Chat**, pick a conversation, and press Enter to send.
4. In **Repos**, choose **New repository**, **Add local repo**, or **Fork**.
   Public repositories appear in the catalog; private ones stay hidden unless shared.

To keep a safe copy of a repository you already have on GitHub, follow
[Back up a GitHub repository](back-up-a-github-repository.md).

## Make a change

Use normal Git (`git switch -c`, `git commit`, `git push`) or the desktop:
**Code → Branches → New branch**, edit, then **Code → Changes → Commit & push**.
For another owner's project, fork it and use **Pulls → New pull request**; the
relay queues the signed pull request while the owner is offline.

## Where data lives

```text
~/projects/forkmesh/   src/ data/ config/ ssh/ logs/ state/ cache/
~/projects/<project>/  data/ config/ ssh/ logs/ state/ cache/
```

`data/` holds the node's private identity key: export it from **Settings →
Data** before moving machines. `FORKMESH_HOME` or `FORKMESH_PROJECTS_DIR`
moves the layout. Uninstalling removes only the program unless `--purge` is
given.

## Phones and the watch

Get ForkMesh for iPhone and iPad on the App Store (the Apple Watch app comes
with it) or the Android APK from the downloads page. Sign in with the same
account; see [ForkMesh apps](apps.md).

## Your own instance

To run ForkMesh under your own name on your own server, open
[forkmesh.com/start](https://forkmesh.com/start), or hand the job to a coding
agent. See [Start your own instance](start-your-own-instance.md) and
[Working with coding agents](coding-agents.md).

Next: [the desktop app](qt-client.md) or the [documentation index](README.md).

pages.title: ForkMesh product promise: proof and measurement
pages.description: ForkMesh lets developers collaborate on, mirror, and preserve source-code repositories across independent hosts—without relying on any single hosting provider.
pages.markdown:
# ForkMesh product promise: proof and measurement

> ForkMesh lets developers collaborate on, mirror, and preserve source-code repositories across independent hosts—without relying on any single hosting provider.

## Four-step proof

Use a disposable public repository; never delete the source.

### 1. Collaborate

Create a signed issue, discussion or pull request.

### 2. Add an independent mirror

Mirror it on another node until it is online, integrity `ok` and at the same commit.

### 3. Take the source mirror offline

Stop `forkmesh-mirror-node` on the source host.

### 4. Clone again

`git clone https://forkmesh.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY` must succeed at the same commit.

## Expected failures and recovery

**No eligible mirror**, a stale or integrity-mismatched mirror, or
**All serving hosts offline** make the clone fail cleanly; a
**Private repository** is outside this proof. Rollback is explicit: restart
`forkmesh-mirror-node` and wait for fresh signed health.

## Measurement and closure gate

Consented analytics count only `home-proof-opened`, `proof-clone-copied` and
`repository-clone-copied`. In every five-person cohort of maintainers,
contributors, and operators, each reader must restate the promise. A cohort passes
at 4/5 or better. Do not mark this gate complete with blank, synthetic, or inferred results.

## Linked automated evidence

`app/tests/test_installer_release.py`, `app/tests/test_mirror_serving.py`,
`app/tests/test_https_mirror_routing_integration.py`,
`app/tests/test_mirror_service_recovery.py`, `app/tests/test_product_promise.py`,
`app/tests/test_first_party_analytics.py`.

# When ForkMesh fits, and when it does not This page compares ForkMesh with other ways to host and keep Git repositories, so you can decide whether it fits before migrating. Evidence ledger: [`ledger.json`](../../conformance/category-comparisons/v1/ledger.json); check tool: [`category_comparisons.py`](../../tools/category_comparisons.py). ## How to read the comparison - *ForkMesh protocol and self-hosted software* is what anyone can run from this repository; *ForkMesh hosted service* is what forkmesh.com operates. A capability in one column does not imply the other. - Other columns describe a category of tool. A cell that names a product quotes that product's documentation, listed under *Primary sources* with its check date. - **By definition** marks a statement that follows from what the category is. **No claim made** means no primary source supports a category-wide statement. ## How the claims stay honest The block below is generated from the ledger; if they disagree, the ledger wins. `python3 tools/category_comparisons.py check` fails when a matrix cell is missing or lacks evidence, a category claim lacks a dated primary source, any claim is older than the review cadence, copy overclaims ("unlimited", "guaranteed"), a next-step UTM value is not allowlisted, or the block is out of date (run `render`). `report` prints freshness measures. Wrong claims are fixed in the ledger with a `corrections` entry; unverifiable claims become **No claim made**. ## Review status Reviewed **2026-09-14** by ForkMesh maintainers reviewing issue #509. The next review is due **2026-12-13**, every 90 days; after that date the check fails until every claim is verified again. ## At a glance | Option | What it is | Consider it instead of ForkMesh when | | --- | --- | --- | | ForkMesh protocol and self-hosted software | The MIT-licensed protocol, mirror node, gateways, and desktop app, run on hosts you or your community operate. | — | | ForkMesh hosted service | The forkmesh.com and app.forkmesh.com relay, accounts, public index, and website that ForkMesh operates. | — | | Centralized Git hosting | One company runs Git hosting, issues, pull requests, and related services for you, for example GitHub. | You need anonymous pushes, or pushes that land on a read mirror. ForkMesh takes pushes only from an authenticated account, over SSH or HTTPS, and streams them to one write endpoint.
You need a contractual uptime SLO, a support response time, or a managed private workspace today. None of these is sold yet.
Your team depends on GitHub Desktop, Sourcetree, or GitKraken being certified. They are not yet.
You need a notarized macOS app, a container image, or a cluster deployment. macOS is preview and containers are planned. | | Self-hosted forges | You install and run a complete forge on your own server, for example Gitea. | You need anonymous pushes, or pushes that land on a read mirror. ForkMesh takes pushes only from an authenticated account, over SSH or HTTPS, and streams them to one write endpoint.
You need search and organization administration with no hosted service and no Cloudflare account. Those roles are hosted-only today.
You want one private server on an internal network with no independent copies. A single host is exactly the single-operator risk ForkMesh exists to reduce.
You need a notarized macOS app, a container image, or a cluster deployment. macOS is preview and containers are planned. | | Decentralized, Git-native collaboration tools | Tools that keep issues or reviews inside Git and sync them between copies without a central forge, for example git-bug. | You want only an issue tracker inside an existing Git repository, with no accounts, relay, or mirror hosts. ForkMesh's collaboration comes with signed identities, a relay, and mirrors to run or trust. | | Replicated storage and Git backups | Copies of repositories on other disks, buckets, or machines, made with git clone --mirror, bundles, or storage replication. | You only want an offline copy of Git data. ForkMesh's mirror health, routing, and signed collaboration would be overhead you do not use. | | Basic Git servers | A bare repository served over SSH, HTTP, or the Git daemon, with no forge features. | You want one private server on an internal network with no independent copies. A single host is exactly the single-operator risk ForkMesh exists to reduce. | ## Not for you - **You need anonymous pushes, or pushes that land on a read mirror. ForkMesh takes pushes only from an authenticated account, over SSH or HTTPS, and streams them to one write endpoint.** Consider: Centralized Git hosting, Self-hosted forges. Evidence: [`git-compatibility.md` §https-receive-pack](git-compatibility.md#https-receive-pack); [test `test_receive_pack_fails_closed_without_consuming_request_body`](../../app/tests/test_git_http.py). Verified 2026-10-24. - **You need a contractual uptime SLO, a support response time, or a managed private workspace today. None of these is sold yet.** Consider: Centralized Git hosting. pages.title: Terminology and voice guide
pages.description: ForkMesh keeps standard Git forge words and explains its network ideas in place. The contract is terminology.json; tools/terminology_lint.py checks primary surfaces against it.
pages.markdown:
# Terminology and voice guide

ForkMesh keeps standard Git forge words and explains its network ideas in
place. The contract is [`terminology.json`](terminology.json);
`tools/terminology_lint.py` checks primary surfaces against it.

## Approved glossary

| Say | Meaning | Instead of |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **repository** | A Git repository with its issues, pull requests and releases. | project |
| **branch** | A named line of commits. | |
| **fork** | Your own copy of a repository. | |
| **pull request** | A proposal to merge commits, with discussion and reviews. | merge request, patch |
| **review** | Approval, change request or comments on a pull request. | peer approval |
| **mirror** | A synced full copy on another host that can serve clones. | peer, seed node, mesh node |
| **seed** | The first push that fills a new mirror. | seeder |
| **trusted maintainer** | A person whose signed actions every mirror accepts. | delegate |
| **desktop app** | The ForkMesh desktop application. | Qt client |

## Protocol terms and plain explanations

| Protocol term | Plain explanation for primary surfaces |
| --- | --- |
| node | A running copy of ForkMesh that signs and syncs for an account. |
| relay | The web service that routes requests to healthy mirrors. |
| refs attestation | The signed branch and tag list a mirror must match. |
| signed repository proof | A host's signature over the refs it serves. |
| commit DAG | Commit history. |
| CRDT / fold | How signed events merge into one state without conflicts. |
| lease | A short claim that stops two hosts doing the same work. |
| outbox | Signed events waiting for delivery. |
| opaque replica | An encrypted copy a host stores but cannot read. |
| federation | Sharing activity with ActivityPub servers. |

## Rules

- Lead with the Git task; explain a network idea once, where it appears.
- `discouragedTerms` marks each term **replace** or **explain**. Exceptions go in
  `allowances` (with a `reason`) or a `terminology: allow=<term-id>` comment.
- Run `python3 tools/terminology_lint.py` (add `--extended` or `--json`).

## Compatibility aliases

One pull request lives at `/OWNER/REPOSITORY/pull/12` (its sections at
`/pull/12/files`, `/pull/12/commits`, `/pull/12/checks`) and the list at
`/OWNER/REPOSITORY/pulls`, the split GitHub uses, so a pull request link copied
from GitHub works after swapping the host. Other familiar forge URLs
(`/pulls/12`, `/pull-requests/12`, `/merge_requests/12`, `/-/issues/5`)
redirect with 308, keeping the rest of the path and the query. Routes, JSON fields, event kinds, config keys and flags are never renamed for wording; aliases are never removed. **Rollback.** Revert the copy change; aliases stay.

## Measurement

`--json --extended` reports `discouragedTermCount` (zero on primary surfaces).
Alias usage comes from Cloudflare zone analytics. Support vocabulary is sampled
monthly. For every five-person cohort of maintainers, contributors, and operators, test core tasks without a glossary. A cohort passes at 4/5 or better. Do not mark this gate complete with blank, synthetic, or inferred results.
Evidence: `app/tests/test_terminology_contract.py`.

pages.description: Contract version 1. The machine-readable source is /business-model.json; the public entitlement matrix and homepage pricing render the same boundary.
pages.markdown:
# ForkMesh free-protocol / paid-services contract

Contract version 1. The machine-readable source is
[`/business-model.json`](../public/business-model.json); the public entitlement
matrix and homepage pricing render the same boundary.

## The durable boundary

ForkMesh sells work and infrastructure, not permission to participate in the
protocol. The protocol, reference software and self-hosting unit are
MIT-licensed and need no account or payment. Public reading and cloning,
standard Git data, signed `.forkmesh` records, independent operation and
protocol governance can never become paid entitlements. Paid services operate
replaceable roles (hosting, administration, indexing, replicas, recovery,
runners, support) and give ForkMesh no authority over protocol objects.

Tokens, rewards, tips and bounties are optional and never affect identity,
permissions, ranking, moderation or governance
(`tokenOrBlockchainRequired: false`); see
[incentive independence](incentive-independence.md).

## Initial plans

| Plan | Price and status | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Protocol + self-hosted | $0; available | Full MIT rights; the operator supplies capacity and support. |
| Hosted Free | $0; public preview | Best-effort public reads, clones, relay and index. No reserved capacity, SLO or support time. |
| Supporter membership | $5/member/month | Funds infrastructure; no extra capability or authority. |
| Pro membership | $10/member/month | Published Pro workflows within safety and capacity limits; not unlimited. |
| Managed services | Research preview; not for sale | Metered hosting, replicas, recovery, runners and support; checkout disabled until research, cost, security, portability and recovery gates pass. |

No paid plan may be `unlimited` for a variable-cost service. Usage units map to
cost drivers (member-month, replica GiB-month, egress GiB, runner minute,
support hour, request counts); unknown cost stays unknown, never zero.

## Portability commitments

Repository data stays Git objects and refs; collaboration data stays signed
`.forkmesh` records. Export is free at any time, including before
cancellation. A managed plan cannot be sold until a drill exports a managed
project, imports it into a clean self-hosted deployment, compares object IDs
and signatures, and restores from the same export.

## Support boundary

Community support covers documentation, discussions and reproducible issues;
free use and memberships carry no response time. A paid support order must
state platform, channel, hours, response target, exclusions and included human
time. Preservation orders use a
[repository availability contract](availability-contract.md), backed only by
demonstrated capacity (`app/tests/test_availability_contract.py`).

## No data sale

ForkMesh does not sell personal data, repository data, collaboration data,
telemetry, or derived profiles, and does not use them to sell advertising.
Optional analytics is off by default and consent-based. First-party ads are
placed by surface, never by viewer (the `advertising` block of the contract).

## Acquisition and paid adoption model

Public projects are the acquisition loop and stay free: anonymous read or
clone, signed contribution or mirror, a qualified service need, a bounded trial
with export available, and a paid proposal only when cost supports the target
margin. The funnel reports aggregate public projects reaching proof, qualified
service conversations, trials, paid customers, trial-to-paid conversion,
revenue, service cost and gross margin, without identifying readers.

## Unit-economics model and instrumentation

```text
gross profit = recognized service revenue - service cost
gross margin = gross profit / recognized service revenue
```

The admin usage report emits a `unitEconomics` projection from provider
analytics; `tools/unit_economics.py` combines it with invoice-backed costs.
Exports carry no raw account, repository, path or IP data. Provider analytics
unavailability is a failed sample, not a zero-cost day.

Managed pricing stays a hypothesis until the
[pricing-interview register](research/pricing-interviews.md) holds qualifying
interviews. Rollout and recovery steps:
[business-model rollout](operations/business-model-rollout.md). Contract test:
`app/tests/test_business_model_contract.py`.

pages.title: Incentive independence
pages.description: Repository access, identity, contribution, governance, and essential network participation work fully without a token, blockchain, reward system, or speculative asset.
pages.markdown:
# Incentive independence

Repository access, identity, contribution, governance, and essential network participation work fully without a token, blockchain, reward system, or speculative asset.

Optional incentives (tips, bounties, reward pool, microjobs, hackathon prizes,
memberships) are **adapters**. An adapter may read canonical state; canonical
state never reads an adapter. Requirements:
`conformance/incentives/v1/requirements.json`.

## Architecture

Canonical state is Git data and signed refs pins, accounts and keys, signed
`.forkmesh` collaboration records, organizations and roles, discovery, and
governance. Adapters include `solana.py`, `reward_policy.py`, `ledger.py`,
`microjobs.py`, `hackathon.py` and `patreon.py` with their own tables.

1. Canonical modules never import an adapter.
2. Hooks from canonical writes to adapters are best effort and cannot fail the write.
3. No foreign key points into an adapter table.
4. Identity, authorization, ranking, moderation and governance never read
   wallets, balances, tokens, tips or payment history.

## Commercial commitment

`/business-model.json` publishes `tokenOrBlockchainRequired: false` and
`incentivesAffectIdentityPermissionsRankingModerationOrGovernance: false`.

## Protocol governance

Collaboration authority comes only from the repository policy document's keys.
Changing that requires a new protocol version.

## Payment and no-payment paths

Every incentive has a no-payment path; conventional payment is preferred over
crypto. Grants follow [public-interest funding](funding/README.md).

## Disabled deployment

With no adapter configured, signup, keys, repositories, clone, collaboration
records, organizations, discovery and marketplace approval all work.
Unconfigured adapters answer explicitly (for example HTTP 503
`patreon_oauth_not_configured`) and never block a canonical response.

## Failure, rollback, and recovery

A failed or removed adapter pauses payouts only: unset its configuration. A
coupling regression fails the `incentive-independence` quality gate; revert it.

## Telemetry and measures

- Essential no-incentive journey pass rate
- Adapter coupling violations (target zero)
- User comprehension: a cohort must answer that no wallet or token is needed

## Linked automated evidence

- `app/tests/test_incentive_independence.py`
- `app/tests/test_marketplace_governance.py`
- `app/tests/test_non_custodial_surfaces.py`

pages.markdown: # Stock Git compatibility Conformance suite **forkmesh-stock-git 1.0.0**. Statuses were computed **2026-09-14** from 2 retained stock-Git runs: **39 of 39** support claims have a passing run from the last 30 days. Supported rows use an unmodified Git executable (minimum 2.34.0); every run records the exact client and platform version in its JSON evidence. A claim is never published on its own: with no passing run it is **unverified**, when its newest passing run ages past the freshness window it is **stale**, and when a retained run failed it is **failing**. [Filter results by client and workflow](/docs/git-compatibility/) or download [results.json](/docs/git-compatibility/results.json). The offline reference probe uses disposable repositories and the same smart-HTTP framing as the public read path. Product gateway contract tests cover authorization, hidden refs, read-only failures, and rollback behavior. Repository shape: A bare repository whose main branch has three commits: an SSH-signed commit adding a README, a 128 KiB binary payload, and a gitlink submodule at deps/fixture resolved through a relative URL, followed by two history commits. A lightweight tag points at the signed commit; receive and transfer fsck are enabled, and a read-only replica rejects every push. ## Statuses | Status | Meaning | | --- | --- | | **supported** | Covered by an automated stock-Git probe and part of the public contract. | | **local** | Runs in the stock client checkout; the transport preserves the required objects and refs. | | **conditional** | Supported when the condition in the matrix is satisfied. | | **unsupported** | Rejected or deliberately unavailable; follow the linked recovery or alternative. | | **failing** | A retained run for this cell failed; the claim is withdrawn until the same configuration passes again. | | **stale** | The newest passing run is older than the freshness window; re-run the suite before relying on it. | | **unverified** | No retained run covers this cell; treat it as experimental. | ## Paths | Path | Read | Write | Transport | Authentication | Contract | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Direct owner SSH | yes | yes | SSH (ssh://); the offline probe uses a stock smart-HTTP origin with the same pack negotiation | Registered SSH public key with repository read or write permission | A stock Git SSH session terminates at the owner-authorized forced-command gateway. | | Stable relay HTTPS | yes | no | HTTPS smart protocol under the stable repository URL | None for reading a public repository. A push to the same URL needs an account credential and goes through the authenticated push proxy, which this suite does not probe | The stable repository URL proxies upload-pack in place from one integrity-matching HTTPS mirror. | | Relay mirror failover | yes | no | HTTPS smart protocol through a relay-selected mirror | Anonymous read of a public repository; no credentials reach a mirror | Before response bytes are committed, the relay retries another healthy mirror with the same attested refs. | ## Operations | Operation | Direct owner SSH | Stable relay HTTPS | Mirror failover | Reproduce | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Clone | **supported** — SSH upload-pack. Last run 2026-09-14. | `git clone recovery.bundle recovered` | ## Evidence runs | Client | Git | Platform | Protocol | Probe transport | Result | Finished | Evidence | Reproduce | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Debian system Git | 2.47.3 | Linux 6.12.107+deb13-amd64 x86_64 | v2 | http | **pass** 15/15 | 2026-09-14 | [report](/docs/git-compatibility/evidence/df83f9aadd86159a.json) | `git checkout c792b91e35e78b54871d6814d77d8fcfb7621591 && python3 tools/git_conformance.py run --protocol-version 2 --transport http --client-label 'Debian system Git' --output artifacts/git-conformance-v2.json` | | Debian system Git | 2.47.3 | Linux 6.12.107+deb13-amd64 x86_64 | v0 | http | **pass** 15/15 | 2026-09-14 | [report](/docs/git-compatibility/evidence/f80323565e1c9af0.json) | `git checkout c792b91e35e78b54871d6814d77d8fcfb7621591 && python3 tools/git_conformance.py run --protocol-version 0 --transport http --client-label 'Debian system Git' --output artifacts/git-conformance-v0.json` | ## Tested clients | Client | Platform | Version | State | Last tested | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | ForkMesh Qt desktop | Linux, macOS, Windows | current main | **tested** | 2026-08-20 | `desktop/tests/test_mesh_e2e.cpp` | | GitHub Desktop | macOS, Windows | not yet recorded | **pending** | not yet tested | `desktop-client-validation` | | Sourcetree | macOS, Windows | not yet recorded | **pending** | not yet tested | `desktop-client-validation` | | GitKraken Desktop | Linux, macOS, Windows | not yet recorded | **pending** | not yet tested | `desktop-client-validation` | ## Known limitations ### HTTPS pushes need a credential and are not probed by this suite - Applies to: relay, mirror-failover. - Expected result: A push to the stable HTTPS URL without a credential gets HTTP 401 push_unauthorized with a Basic challenge before ForkMesh reads the push body. With a credential, the relay checks that the account may write the repository and streams the push to one endpoint that accepts receive-pack; for a repository the core nodes host, that is the core that last took a push, else the first live core in rendezvous order. Read mirrors never take writes. - Reproduce: `git push https://app.forkmesh.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY.git HEAD` - Action: When Git asks, enter your ForkMesh account name or email and either your account password (when two-factor authentication is off) or the push credential from Settings, SSH keys, Push code over HTTPS. On the core nodes the default and protected branches only fast-forward, other branches may be force-pushed by accounts that may write them, new tags are allowed, and a push never deletes a branch. - Recovery: A refused push changes no remote ref or object. Check the account name and the password or credential, then retry the same push; HTTP 403 push_forbidden means the account may not push to this repository. The Git errors page lists every message. - Last tested: 2026-10-24 · not applicable (source contract tests) · app/tests/test_git_http.py::test_receive_pack_fails_closed_without_consuming_request_body, app/tests/test_hosted_repositories.py::test_account_name_or_email_and_password_push ### Repository-controlled server hooks are disabled - Applies to: direct, relay, mirror-failover. - Expected result: Client-side hooks in a checkout run normally. Gateways set core.hooksPath to the null device so pushed repository configuration cannot execute code on a mirror. - Reproduce: `git -C worktree commit -m 'exercise local hook'` - Action: Keep developer hooks local; put shared required checks in reviewed ForkMesh Actions or another CI system. - Recovery: A rejected local hook leaves the index and remote unchanged; fix or intentionally bypass the local hook according to project policy. - Last tested: 2026-08-20 · Git 2.47.3 · forkmesh-stock-git v1 hooks probe ### A response cannot change mirrors mid-stream - Applies to: mirror-failover. - Expected result: ForkMesh retries another eligible mirror only before response bytes are committed. An interrupted pack fails as a normal Git transport error. - Reproduce: `git fetch --prune origin` - Action: Retry the fetch; Git reuses valid local objects and ForkMesh may select another matching mirror for the new request. - Recovery: Run git fsck --full --strict if the client or disk reported corruption. Do not delete the existing clone before collecting diagnostics. - Last tested: 2026-08-20 · Git 2.47.3 · forkmesh-stock-git v1 mirror-failover and integrity probes ### Partial clone requires Git protocol v2 - Applies to: direct, relay, mirror-failover. - Expected result: A protocol-v0 filtered clone may receive the initial commits and trees, but its first lazy blob fetch is rejected as an unadvertised-object request so hidden ForkMesh objects remain inaccessible. - Reproduce: `git -c protocol.version=0 clone --filter=blob:none --no-checkout '{clone_url}' worktree` - Action: Use Git 2.34 or newer and retry with -c protocol.version=2, or omit --filter for a full clone. - Recovery: Remove the incomplete disposable clone, or keep it for diagnostics and clone into a new directory with protocol v2; no remote ref or object was changed. - Last tested: 2026-08-20 · Git 2.47.3 · forkmesh-stock-git v1 protocol-v0 rejection and protocol-v2 partial-clone probes ### Submodules are separate repositories - Applies to: direct, relay, mirror-failover. - Expected result: The superproject clone succeeds, then Git names the exact submodule whose independent URL is unavailable or unauthorized. - Reproduce: `git clone --recurse-submodules '{clone_url}' worktree` - Action: Confirm every .gitmodules URL uses a published public HTTPS route or an SSH route your key may read, then run git submodule update --init --recursive. - Recovery: The superproject and any completed submodules remain valid; Git resumes the missing child without recloning successful repositories. - Last tested: 2026-08-20 · Git 2.47.3 · forkmesh-stock-git v1 submodules probe ### Third-party desktop UI certification is not complete - Applies to: direct, relay, mirror-failover. - Expected result: GitHub Desktop, Sourcetree, and GitKraken are not release-supported rows until their exact application and bundled-Git versions produce a retained report. - Reproduce: `python3 tools/git_conformance.py run --git /path/to/the/client/bundled/git --client-label 'CLIENT VERSION'` - Action: Use a tested Git CLI or ForkMesh Qt build, or run the versioned probe with the desktop application's bundled Git before relying on it. - Recovery: The probe uses disposable repositories and makes no production write. Attach its JSON report when requesting a new supported row. - Last tested: not yet tested · not applicable · No support claim is published without retained evidence. ## Run the suite ```sh python3 tools/git_conformance.py validate python3 tools/git_conformance.py render --check python3 tools/git_conformance.py run --protocol-version 0 \ --output artifacts/git-conformance-v0.json python3 tools/git_conformance.py run --protocol-version 2 \ --output artifacts/git-conformance-v2.json python3 tools/git_conformance.py attest \ artifacts/git-conformance-v0.json artifacts/git-conformance-v2.json python3 tools/git_conformance.py gate ``` Use `--git /path/to/git --client-label 'client version'` to exercise a desktop application's bundled, unmodified Git. Reports contain operation status, elapsed milliseconds, exact client/platform versions, generalized request counts, and test object IDs. They exclude temporary paths, URLs, repository contents, credentials, and client addresses.

pages.description: The Qt client is a workspace application: chat and repository UI, local Git data, signed collaboration records, actions, and coding agents. It does not serve repositories or…
pages.markdown:
# Qt desktop client

The Qt client is a workspace application: chat and repository UI, local Git
data, signed collaboration records, actions, and coding agents. It does not
serve repositories or publish the catalog; the Go mirror service does that.

## Install a release

```sh
curl -fsSL https://forkmesh.com/install.sh | bash
```

The installer verifies signed release metadata and the artifact checksum and
never compiles as a fallback. Native `.exe`, `.dmg`, and `.AppImage` packages
are on the [desktop downloads](https://forkmesh.com/desktop) page.

## Build and run from source

Requirements: Qt 6.4+ (Widgets, Network, SVG, Concurrent; D-Bus on Linux),
CMake 3.16+, a C++17 compiler, OpenSSL 3.0+ with headers, Python 3, and Git.
Private mirrors and the Password Vault need OpenSSL 3.5; on older systems pass
`-DFORKMESH_BUNDLED_OPENSSL=ON` (fetches and verifies a pinned OpenSSL) or
`-DOPENSSL_ROOT_DIR=...`. Optional: `libnghttp3` for the HTTP/3 log-feed client,
Qt 6 Multimedia for in-app video playback, and Qt 6 WebEngine
(`qt6-webengine-dev`) for the Browser tab and YouTube inside the app.

```sh
sudo apt install build-essential cmake git libssl-dev openssl \
  qt6-base-dev qt6-svg-dev qt6-base-dev-tools pkg-config \
  qt6-webengine-dev                                         # Debian/Ubuntu
brew install cmake git openssl@3 qt                         # macOS
```

From the repository root:

```sh
./desktop/run.sh           # incremental Release build and launch
./desktop/run.sh test      # build and run the critical contracts
./desktop/run.sh clean     # delete desktop/build
./desktop/run.sh rebuild   # clean, build, and launch
```

Manual CMake (prefer Ninja; its job pool caps concurrent heavy units):

```sh
cmake -S desktop -B desktop/build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DFORKMESH_BUILD_TESTS=ON
cmake --build desktop/build --parallel 12
ctest --test-dir desktop/build --output-on-failure
```

On macOS add `-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="$(brew --prefix qt)"` and
`-DOPENSSL_ROOT_DIR="$(brew --prefix openssl@3)"`. `ccache`, `ninja`, and
`mold` speed up rebuilds. In-app *Rebuild & restart* builds `RelWithDebInfo`,
re-runs a pass if sources changed mid-build, and installs only a build of an
unchanged tree. Developer notes:
[docs/desktop/build-and-test.md](../../docs/desktop/build-and-test.md).

Qt 6.4 is the floor. Guard newer APIs with
`#if QT_VERSION >= QT_VERSION_CHECK(6, 5, 0)` and verify with
`tools/qt64-build-check.sh [ubuntu-24.04]`, which builds against each
distribution's own Qt in a private sysroot.

Never run ForkMesh as root.

## KVM-isolated coding workspace

On Linux, coding agents can run in a Lima QEMU/KVM guest while the UI stays on
the host. Only the launch directory (mounted at the same path), the Git metadata
it needs, and a temporary agent-worktree root are shared; the home directory,
sockets, SSH agent, and unrelated environment are not. It needs Lima 2.0+,
QEMU, and `/dev/kvm`; there is no software-emulation fallback.

Launch ForkMesh from the narrowest directory holding your repositories (the
home directory is refused), enable **Settings → General → KVM workspace**,
choose **Prepare / start VM**, sign in to agents in **Open VM shell**, then
restart. Toggling the mode requires a restart; repositories outside the launch
directory are rejected while it is active.

## First run and navigation

A first launch creates the node identity, connects to the default relay, and
syncs the ForkMesh project. The left rail holds the main areas: Chat, Repos,
Code, Issues/Pulls/Actions, Agents, Network, Team, Pings, Health, Settings,
and others. Add a project with **Repos → Add local repo**; contribute elsewhere
with **Repos → Fork**.

**Network → Hosts** can create managed Vultr mirrors and optionally size the
fleet automatically to a target healthy count. Only instances this client
created are ever destroyed; an unreachable catalog makes no change.

### Team and teammate run modes

**Team** loads teammate definitions from `.forkmesh/teammates/`. Each teammate
runs on demand, on a bounded cron cadence, on repository events, or in
**Continual** mode, and only while the desktop is open. A continual teammate
runs one bounded cycle, then waits at a decision card (Yes/No, or three
options) before the next; **Stop work** pauses it. Permission mode, repository
grants, concurrency limits, and any VM boundary apply to every cycle. A Git
worktree separates branches but is not a sandbox.

### Multiple relay instances

The relay selector holds any number of named relay instances, each with its
own remembered account. The active relay is a security boundary: catalogs,
account requests, bearer capabilities, channel membership, chat history, and
queued agent work are scoped to its local instance id and exact origin.
Switching clears active credentials first; chat never fails over to another
relay. Bearer tokens are never written to `QSettings`. Each repository record
belongs to the relay it was added under and is only synced with that relay.
Private channels and direct messages keep their device-to-device layer; see
[Chat encryption and integrations](security/sealed-chat.md).

### Connectors

Discord and Sentry connectors are Market packages. Discord uses a bot token
(never a user token) and the server's permissions; Sentry reads unresolved
issues read-only with an `org:read`/`project:read` token. Tokens live in
device-local package settings, never in logs, arguments, or chat. Removing the
package clears its token and cached data.

## Create a pull request

Within your own repository: create a branch under **Code → Branches**, commit
in **Code → Changes**, then select the branch and click **Create PR**. ForkMesh
records the commit series and a signed binary-safe patch. Agents work the same
way in isolated worktrees under `.worktrees/` in the project.

For another owner's repository: **Fork** it, commit a feature branch, open
**Pulls → New pull request**, set the target node, base, and head, and submit.
The signed patch is delivered to the owner's inbox; the relay holds it until
the owner is online. See [Contributing](../../CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Run a managed mirror

Do not use the desktop binary as a repository server; run the Go mirror daemon
per the [headless mirror runbook](operations/headless-mirror-refresh.md).

## Logs and diagnostics

- The footer CPU/RAM/stall indicator shows UI-stall details.
- **Network diagnostics** shows connections and recent endpoint results;
  per-request logging is opt-in in Settings.
- **Settings → Data** shows the data, preferences, mirror, and cache
  directories for the current OS.

Diagnostic journals (default layout):

```text
~/projects/forkmesh/logs/diagnostics/actions.jsonl   action lifecycle journal
~/projects/forkmesh/logs/diagnostics/stalls.log      UI freezes longer than 500 ms
```

Each `actions.jsonl` record names `source`, `function`, `routine`, `cwd`,
`queued_ms`, and an `outcome`. The data directory also holds `network_log.txt`
and crash records. Details:
[docs/desktop/diagnostics.md](../../docs/desktop/diagnostics.md).

When reporting a problem include `forkmesh --version`, OS and display server,
the triggering action, and a log excerpt with secrets and private content
removed.

## Common fixes

- **CMake cannot find Qt6:** install the Qt development packages; on macOS
  pass `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`.
- **Qt platform plugin error:** launch from a graphical session.
- **Stale CMake cache after moving the checkout:** `./desktop/run.sh clean`.
- **Repository actions are read-only:** fork it or add its local working tree.
- **Backup:** **Settings → Data → Export configuration**; **Control → Deploy →
  Export complete system…** writes clear-text secrets, so protect it.

Back to [Getting started](getting-started.md) or the
[documentation index](README.md).

pages.title: ForkMesh surface capability matrix
pages.description: A capability is present on a surface when the surface implements it or offers a safe deep link to its canonical interface. The contract is capability-matrix.json: every row names…
pages.markdown:
# ForkMesh surface capability matrix

A capability is present on a surface when the surface implements it or offers a
safe deep link to its canonical interface. The contract is
[`capability-matrix.json`](capability-matrix.json): every row names a canonical
path and a non-missing mode for the app server (`worker` column), dashboard/Web, World,
and Qt, and CI validates it. The phone and watch apps are tracked in
[PARITY.md](../../docs/native/PARITY.md).

Owner-device secrets never leave the device: Cloudflare tokens, repository
decryption keys, mirror process control, wallet signing keys, SSH private keys,
agent-provider credentials, and microphone audio. Web and World show authorized
state and link to the local flow. The app server supplies authenticated APIs,
policy, encrypted envelopes, and public-safe projections; an API entry does
not imply custody or plaintext access. Raw SSH terminates only at the
node-side forced-command gateway.

pages.markdown:
# Installation support matrix

The machine-readable matrix is
[`install-support-matrix.json`](install-support-matrix.json); CI checks that
every supported artifact is in the latest signed release.

**Supported** artifacts are in the Ed25519-signed release manifest, SHA-256
verified and tested; **Preview** is packaged but not fully published;
**Source-only** builds with `FORKMESH_FROM_SOURCE=1`; **Planned** is not
installable.

The iPhone and iPad app is on the
[App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/forkmesh/id6803060735), and the Apple
Watch app installs with it. Apple signs and delivers it, so it is never in the
signed release manifest and stays listed as Preview here.

## Profiles

| Profile | Tier | Artifact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `linux-desktop-x86_64` | Supported | `forkmesh-linux-x86_64`, `.AppImage` |
| `linux-cli-headless-x86_64` | Supported | `forkmesh-linux-x86_64` |
| `linux-server-mirror-node-x86_64` | Supported | `forkmesh-mirror-node-linux-x86_64` |
| `windows-desktop-x86_64` | Supported | `forkmesh-windows-x86_64-setup.exe` |
| `android-universal` | Supported | `forkmesh-android-universal.apk` |
| `macos-desktop-arm64` | Preview | `forkmesh-macos-arm64.dmg` |
| `macos-desktop-x86_64` | Preview | `forkmesh-macos-x86_64.dmg` |
| `linux-desktop-arm64` | Preview | `forkmesh-linux-arm64.AppImage` |
| `linux-arm-small-device` | Source-only | none |
| `ios` | Preview (on the App Store) | [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/forkmesh/id6803060735), with the watch app inside |
| `oci-container` | Planned | none |
| `cluster` | Planned | none |

## Lifecycle

| Action | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Install or upgrade | `curl -fsSL https://forkmesh.com/install.sh \| bash` |
| Roll back | `curl -fsSL https://forkmesh.com/install.sh \| FORKMESH_RELEASE=candidate-<version> bash` |
| Uninstall, keeping data | `curl -fsSL https://forkmesh.com/uninstall.sh \| bash` |
| Uninstall and erase all data | `curl -fsSL https://forkmesh.com/uninstall.sh \| bash -s -- --purge --yes` |

Each install verifies the manifest signature, its binding of `SHASUMS256.txt`
and the artifact digest before replacing the binary. Upgrade, rollback and
uninstall touch only program files; user data in
`~/projects/forkmesh/{data,config,ssh,state,logs}` (and `/var/lib/forkmesh`
for a mirror node) is removed only by `--purge` or a confirmed desktop
uninstall. Back up the identity key first: see
[Portable identities and recovery](portable-identities.md).

pages.title: Portable identities and recovery
pages.description: Keys, the recovery kit and authenticators stay with the user; ForkMesh stores only public authority state. Never send keys or kits to support.
pages.markdown:
# Portable identities and recovery

Keys, the recovery kit and authenticators stay with the user; ForkMesh stores
only public authority state. Never send keys or kits to support.

## Enroll and revoke authenticators

Use a passkey for sign-in plus a hardware key and a second device. Revoking a
device kills its key and sessions; revoked keys only verify old signatures.
Delegates get scoped, expiring authority.

## Recovery drills

Practise each before relying on an identity: lost device, compromised device
(revoke first), key rotation (old key revoked atomically), social recovery
(threshold of contacts, who never hold the key) and organization delegation
(minimal scope, expiry).

## Portable encrypted export

The kit is JSON of type `forkmesh.portable-identity`, `schemaVersion` 1:
PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 (600000 iterations, 16-byte salt) and AES-256-GCM (12-byte
IV, tag appended, associated data `forkmesh.portable-identity/v1`) over at most
128 KiB of plaintext, all base64url without padding. Passkey and hardware-key
secrets are never exported. Web, iOS, Android and desktop share the format.

## External-account proofs

Signed short-lived challenges with `private`, `members` or `public` visibility;
revocable, and shown unverified once revoked or expired.

pages.title: Portable social signals
pages.description: Suite 1.0.0 · Vectors: conformance/social-signals/v1/vectors.json · Implementations: tools/social_signals.py (Python), app/public/social-signals.js (JavaScript).
pages.markdown:
# Portable social signals

Suite `1.0.0` · Vectors: `conformance/social-signals/v1/vectors.json` ·
Implementations: `tools/social_signals.py` (Python), `app/public/social-signals.js`
(JavaScript).

Stars, watches, bookmarks, follows, recommendations, usage endorsements,
security reviews and mirroring commitments are signed records the user owns.
They can be exported, imported, merged and revoked, and any implementation can
verify them. This page is normative for requirements `FM-SOC-*`; it reuses the
protocol's canonical JSON and strict Ed25519 rules
([encoding](protocol/encoding-and-identifiers.md),
[signatures](protocol/signatures-and-authentication.md)).

Status: records, bundles, merge, verification, recommendations and the CLI ship.
Client screens, a hosted import/export endpoint and telemetry: Not yet. Hosted
stars and follows are still unsigned per-account rows.

## Tiers

| Kind | Tier | Scope | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `star`, `watch`, `bookmark`, `recommendation`, `follow` | interest | `{}` | `[]` |
| `usage-endorsement` | attestation | `environment`, `version`, `since` | 1–16 links |
| `security-review` | attestation | `revision`, `method`, `findings` | 1–16 links |
| `mirror-commitment` | attestation | `https` `endpoint`, `protocols`; `expiresAt` required | 1–16 links |

- **FM-SOC-001** `tier` is fixed by `kind` (`tier_mismatch`).
- **FM-SOC-002** Interest records carry no scope or evidence
  (`interest_claims_scope`); attestations need evidence (`evidence_required`),
  each item exactly `{label, uri, sha256}`.
- **FM-SOC-003** Attestations are displayed with category, scope and evidence
  count (`describe`), never merged with stars. Evidence is the signer's claim.

## Record format

Schema `forkmesh-social-signal-v1` with keys `schema, kind, tier, signer,
subject, issuedAt, expiresAt, visibility, scope, evidence, note, signalId,
signature`.

- **FM-SOC-004** Exactly these keys; subjects are protocol repository
  identifiers or, for `follow`, `urn:forkmesh:identity:ed25519:<key>` other than
  the signer (`self_follow`); millisecond timestamps; `note` ≤ 1024 bytes.
- **FM-SOC-005** Signing bytes are `"forkmesh-social-signal-v1\n"` + canonical
  JSON without `signalId`/`signature`; `signalId` is `sha256:` of those bytes;
  strings are NFC-normalized.
- **FM-SOC-006** Verification order ends with `signal_id_mismatch`,
  `invalid_signature` and `issued_in_future` (more than five minutes ahead); the
  first failure code is reported.
- **FM-SOC-007** Signed `visibility`: `public`, `followers` or `private`.
  Exports enforce it; records are signed, not encrypted.

## Revocation

- **FM-SOC-008** Schema `forkmesh-social-revocation-v1`, prefix
  `"forkmesh-social-revocation-v1\n"`, reason `withdrawn`, `superseded`,
  `compromised` or `mistaken`. Only the record's signer can revoke; otherwise
  status `signer_mismatch` and no effect. A revocation arriving first is
  `pending` until its record arrives.
- **FM-SOC-009** Revocation is final; sign a new record instead.

## Export, import, and merge

Bundle: `{"schema": "forkmesh-social-signal-bundle-v1", "exportedAt", "signals", "revocations"}`.

- **FM-SOC-010** Each record is validated independently; invalid ones are
  reported in `{accepted, duplicate, rejected}` and skipped. Only a bad envelope
  or more than 10,000 records rejects the bundle.
- **FM-SOC-011** The store is the union keyed by ID, so merge order does not
  matter. State digest: `sha256` over `"forkmesh-social-signal-state-v1\n"` +
  canonical sorted ID lists.
- **FM-SOC-012** Status precedence: `revoked`, `superseded` (newer record, same
  signer, kind and subject), `expired`, `active`.
- **FM-SOC-013** Export audience `public`, `followers` or `self`; revocations
  travel with their targets.

## Recommendations

- **FM-SOC-014** Local controls `{viewer, enabled, asOf, limit, mutedSigners,
  mutedSubjects}`, never exported; `enabled: false` computes nothing.
- **FM-SOC-015** Only signers the viewer actively follows count (no
  transitivity); mutes apply at once.
- **FM-SOC-016** Weights: `star` 1, `watch` 1, `recommendation` 2,
  `mirror-commitment` 2, `usage-endorsement` 3, `security-review` 3. One signer
  adds at most their highest weight per subject.
- **FM-SOC-017** Each result lists score, supporters and every contributing
  record, plus counts of what was excluded and why.

## Command line

```sh
python3 tools/social_signals.py keygen --out ~/.forkmesh/social.seed
python3 tools/social_signals.py sign --seed-file ~/.forkmesh/social.seed star.json > signed.json
python3 tools/social_signals.py revoke --seed-file ~/.forkmesh/social.seed sha256:<signalId> --reason withdrawn
python3 tools/social_signals.py merge a.json b.json --audience public --output public.json
python3 tools/social_signals.py verify public.json
python3 tools/social_signals.py recommend public.json --viewer <key> [--disable]
python3 tools/social_signals.py gate
```

`gate` checks the committed vectors, runs both implementations against them and
a cross-implementation round trip (quality gate `social-signal-portability`).
Any rule change regenerates vectors (`vectors --write`), updates both
implementations and bumps the suite version.

## Failure and recovery

| Situation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Tampered or malformed record in a bundle | Rejected with its code; the rest imports |
| Revocation before its record | `pending` until the record arrives |
| Revocation by another signer | `signer_mismatch`, no effect |
| Compromised key | Revoke with `compromised`, rotate identity ([portable identities](portable-identities.md)), re-sign |
| Lapsed mirror commitment | `expired`; sign a new one |
| Two services disagree | Compare state digests and merge both bundles |

pages.markdown:
# Empty repositories created from the web

Create an empty repository from **Repositories → New** and push with plain
`git` to `https://app.forkmesh.com/<owner>/<name>`. When git asks, enter your
account name or email and your account password (if two-factor authentication
is off), or the push credential shown.
The credential is a
keyed MAC over account,
repository, session and a seven-day expiry; it is not stored, dies with the
session, and every push re-checks permissions. After each push ForkMesh records
the attestation (the signed list of branch and tag commits) that reads route
against.

Packs are bounded by the gateway's `limits.receiveMaxInputBytes` (git's
`receive.maxInputSize`). Where core nodes host
repositories (`HOSTED_GIT_CORE_NODES`) the form also offers private
repositories, initial files and imports, up to 10 repositories of 200 MB per
account.

## Contributing without write access

Step by step, with the commands: [Contribute with git only](contributing-with-git.md).

The usual way: open the repository, choose **Forks → Fork this repository**,
create a push credential for your fork (Settings → SSH keys → Push code over
HTTPS, `<you>/<name>`), push any branch to it, and choose **Contribute: Open
pull request** on your fork. A fork shares the original's history, so it is
created at once whatever the repository's size.

On a repository the operator opened to contributors, anyone signed in with a
verified email address can also push a branch and open a pull request without
a fork:

1. **Settings → SSH keys → Push code over HTTPS**: enter `<owner>/<name>` and
   choose **Create push credential**.
2. Push a branch named `pr/<your-account>/<topic>`:
   `git push https://<host>/<owner>/<name>.git pr/<your-account>/<topic>`.
   When Git asks, use your account name or email with your account password
   (if two-factor authentication is off), or the credential.
3. Open the pull request from that branch on the repository's **Pull
   requests** tab.

Every other ref is refused (Git prints `[remote rejected]` with the reason),
and a contributor keeps at most 32 branches there. You may force-push your own
`pr/<your-account>/` branches to update a pull request after a rebase or
amend; use `git push --force-with-lease`, and if it is refused because the
branch moved on the server, run `git pull --rebase` first. The previous tip is
kept, and the pull request shows "force-pushed from … to …" with a compare
link. Ordinary pushes to the branch update the pull request too ("pushed N
commits").
Contributors cannot delete branches, even their own: when the limit is
reached, a maintainer deletes merged ones. Only new objects are sent, so a
large repository costs no more than the change.

## Operator notes

Production hosts repositories on the core nodes listed in
`HOSTED_GIT_CORE_NODES`: a push goes to the core that took the last push, else
the first live core by rendezvous hash, and the others replicate from it
([HOSTED_REPOS.md](../../docs/HOSTED_REPOS.md)). Without core hosting the
fallback is `HOSTED_GIT_WRITE_NODE`, a node with `writableRepositoryRoot` and
`"writableOwners": ["*"]`. With neither, the API answers
`hosted_git_unavailable`.
See [direct-https-mirror-gateway.md](operations/direct-https-mirror-gateway.md).
Endpoints are `POST /api/hosted-repositories` and
`POST /api/hosted-repositories/push-credential`; records are marked
`source: "hosted-web"` until a signed publication from the owner's node takes
over.

Contributor pushes are off unless `HOSTED_GIT_CONTRIBUTOR_PUSH` lists
repositories: `owner/name`, `owner/*` or `*`, separated by spaces or commas
(an organization alias or its backing node both match). Only public
repositories qualify, and only active user accounts with a verified email.
The relay (the app on the core nodes) signs `pushPrefix=refs/heads/pr/<account>/` (and
`rewrite=` with the same prefix, which lets the contributor force-push only
there) into the receive-pack capability; the gateway refuses refs outside it, so both
must be updated together (an older gateway refuses the field, failing closed).
Contributor pushes never queue Actions runs.

There is no per-account byte quota or push rate limit on this path: each push
may be up to the gateway's `limits.receiveMaxInputBytes`, and pushes are
unlimited. Listing `*` lets any verified account store data in every public
repository, so prefer naming repositories or owners.

pages.title: External repository imports and resumable migrations
pages.description: Racing a shutdown, a takedown, a lost account, or censorship? Start with preservation-first crisis onboarding.
pages.markdown:
# External repository imports and resumable migrations

Racing a shutdown, a takedown, a lost account, or censorship? Start with
[preservation-first crisis onboarding](crisis-preservation.md).

An import copies a project's issues, pull requests and their history once. It
does not copy the code and is not kept up to date, so it is not a backup; to
keep a copy of the code, see [Back up a GitHub repository](back-up-a-github-repository.md).

## Setup

On **Repositories**, choose **New repository**, select **GitHub / GitLab /
Codeberg**, paste the URL (a gitea.com URL works there too), and select
**Start resumable import**. A read-scoped
provider token is optional for public repositories and required for private
ones. Tokens are used per request and never stored, logged, or returned, so a
private import asks for one again on **Continue import**.

Imports live apart from the live catalog: `/api/repositories` lists published
ForkMesh repositories, `/api/repository-imports` lists external metadata entries
and stubs. An external entry is never routed or called mirrored until a node
hosts it (see [Ending the provider dependency](#ending-the-provider-dependency)).

## API

```http
POST /api/repository-imports                     # metadata entry or stub (mode: import | stub)
POST /api/repository-imports/discover            # expand a GitLab group or a Codeberg or Gitea profile, max 200 public repos
POST /api/repository-imports/migrations          # durable job, 202 with a mig_… id
POST /api/repository-imports/migrations/{id}/resume
GET  /api/repository-imports/migrations/{id}
GET  /api/repository-imports/migrations/{id}/objects?type=reviews&limit=100
GET  /api/repository-imports/migration-metrics   # setupP50Ms, setupP95Ms, transfer, retries
DELETE /api/repository-imports/{id}
```

Only canonical `github.com`, `gitlab.com`, `codeberg.org`, and `gitea.com`
HTTPS URLs are accepted. Codeberg (Forgejo) and gitea.com share one adapter,
because both serve Gitea's `/api/v1`; other Gitea or Forgejo instances are
not accepted, so the import cannot be pointed at an arbitrary host. `targetOwner` is the caller or an organization they administer.
Each `/resume` call advances one provider page and returns the next checkpoint;
clients repeat it until `completed`, `429`, or an explicit error. Setup time
(form to accepted job) and transfer time are measured separately; the setup
gate is p50 at most 180,000 ms.

Every adapter emits the same object families: `git_refs`, `issues`,
`pull_requests` (GitHub pull requests and GitLab merge requests), `reviews`,
`releases`, `documentation`, `labels`, `users`, and `collaboration_history`.
Each object keeps the original provider payload plus a common projection.
Credential-shaped fields are redacted and counted. Git objects travel through
the normal bare-mirror path; wikis, workflow logs, and artifact bytes are
reported as out of scope. Provider rate limits are honored: the job becomes
`rate_limited` and resumes on the same page.

## Idempotence, checkpoints, and signed completion

Object identity is `SHA-256(object family + preserved source id)`. Objects are
upserted before the checkpoint advances, so a crash can repeat work but never
duplicate it. An object must be absent from two consecutive complete scans
before it is pruned. On completion the sorted `(objectType, sourceKey,
payloadHash)` tuples are hashed and signed; run numbers and timestamps are
excluded, so an unchanged source yields the same state hash on every rerun.

## Failure, abandonment, and rollback

- Retry a `paused`, `failed`, or `rate_limited` job with `/resume`.
- `POST …/{id}/abandon` stops work but keeps objects; resume with `{"recover": true}`.
- `POST …/{id}/rollback` removes the job, its objects, and its telemetry. It
  keeps the external listing and never touches the source forge.
- A missing optional stream goes to `report.skipped`. A required page the
  provider will not serve pauses the job; resume with `{"deferFailure": true}`
  to continue and leave that work listed as retryable.
- A single record that cannot be stored is counted as failed; the rest of its
  page is imported.

## Migration reports

```http
GET  /api/repository-imports/migrations/{id}/report[?sequence=N]
POST /api/repository-imports/migrations/{id}/retry
```

Every import ends with a signed `forkmesh-repository-migration-report-export-v1`
report (owner-only, `no-store`), issued on completion, abandonment, and each
retry. Sections: `summary`, `reconciliation.rows`, `refs`, `artifacts`,
`checksums`, `retries`, `failures`, `externalDependencies`, `verification`,
`remediation`.

Each provider record lands in exactly one class: `imported`, `skipped`,
`failed`, `external`, or `unclassified`. Any `unclassified` record makes the
outcome `unreconciled`. Outcomes are `verified`, `completed_with_failures`,
`completed_with_unmeasured_sources`, `unreconciled`, and `abandoned`.

The report hash is signed with the relay's Ed25519 router key (published as
`routerPublicKey` on `GET /api/mirrors/https`) over
`forkmesh-repository-migration-report-v1\n<reportHash>`, or HMAC when no key is
configured. Reports chain through `sequence` and `supersedes`. `/retry` queues
only failed pages and deferred streams (`409 no_failed_work` if none).

`tools/verify_migration_report.py` checks a report without ForkMesh code:
hash, signature, reconciliation arithmetic, chain, and, with `--objects`, every
payload hash. Exit 0 verified, 1 failed check, 2 unreadable input.

```bash
python3 tools/verify_migration_report.py report.json \
  --objects objects.json --public-key "$ROUTER_PUBLIC_KEY"
```

Tests: `app/tests/test_repository_migration.py`,
`app/tests/test_repository_migration_report.py`.

## Visibility and statuses

Anonymous listings filter private entries before decryption; a private id
returns the same `404` whether absent or forbidden. Statuses:
`external_repository`, `stub_only`, `mirror_requested`, `partially_mirrored`,
`actively_mirrored`, `mirror_unavailable`, `archived`. The mirrored states
require a matching catalog record; `actively_mirrored` also needs a live host
heartbeat.

## Ending the provider dependency

Public imports become ForkMesh-hosted repositories:

1. `tools/hosted_repository_sync.py` runs on mirror nodes from
   `forkmesh-hosted-repository-sync.timer` (every 30 minutes), reads the public
   import listing, and keeps a `git clone --mirror` of each eligible entry
   under `/srv/forkmesh-git/imports/<node>/<name>.git`.
2. The node publishes a signed catalog record, so the gateway serves the copy
   with no provider in the path.
3. The relay links that record to the import entry, which becomes
   `actively_mirrored` and routes `/<targetOwner>/<name>` to the hosting node.

Only canonical public provider URLs without credentials qualify. Private and
archived imports are never hosted. A node caps its imports root at 20 GiB and a
first clone at 10 minutes; over budget an entry is deferred. Deleting the
import removes the hosted copy on the next run; nothing is deleted at the
provider.

## Mirror volunteers, invitations, and logos

- `POST /api/repository-imports/{id}/mirror-volunteers` needs a mirror node the
  caller owns (`eligible_owned_mirror_node_required` otherwise).
- `POST /api/repository-imports/{id}/invitations` is limited to
  provider-verified administrators, needs a durable provenance record
  (`public_for_invitations`, `prior_consent`, or `owner_supplied`) and
  `confirm: true`, is rate limited, and stores only masked addresses and blind
  indexes. Every message carries opt-out and abuse-report links.
- Each entry gets a locally generated SVG logo (`aiGenerated: false`).
  `POST /api/repository-imports/{id}/logo-suggestions` accepts PNG, JPEG, or
  WebP for owner approval.

pages.title: Admin dashboard (/product-analysis)
pages.description: An internal, read-only dashboard at https://app.forkmesh.com/product-analysis for account, signup-origin, mirror, and clone counts. It has no public version.
pages.markdown:
# Admin dashboard (`/product-analysis`)

An internal, read-only dashboard at `https://app.forkmesh.com/product-analysis`
for account, signup-origin, mirror, and clone counts. It has no public version.

## Access

| Secret | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `PRODUCT_ANALYSIS_USER` | Login username. |
| `PRODUCT_ANALYSIS_PASS` | Login password and session-cookie key material. |

- With either secret unset the route returns the ordinary 404 (a signed-in
  `is_admin` account is still admitted).
- Unauthenticated `GET` shows only a sign-in form, `noindex`. Unknown paths,
  methods, views, and actions return 404.
- Login sets `forkmesh_product_analysis` (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict,
  12 hours). Rotating the password ends every session.
- Failed logins share the account-login rate limit (`429` with `Retry-After`).
- No JavaScript; CSP `default-src 'none'`; `no-store`. Rendered inside the
  shared admin shell (`app/src/admin_shell.py`).

## Sections

All windows are UTC (last 30 days, previous 30 days, 90-day and 30-day daily
charts). Five tabs:

- **Overview**: total accounts, accounts with a mirror, activation (first
  mirror within 7 days of signup), returning accounts, mirrors created,
  repositories cloned and anonymous clones (from `product_clone_daily`), and
  all-time clones (`mirror_serve_counters`).
- **Signup sources**: accounts and mirror creators per origin.
- **Users**: sortable, paginated, read-only list with last activity.
- **Repositories**: catalog records with mirror count, size, clones, and
  `hostedSince`.
- **Acquisition**: pending; served without building a report
  (`VIEWS_WITHOUT_REPORT`).

## Signup origin

`users.signup_origin` is `job_flow`, `referral`, `organic`, or `unknown`,
stamped at signup by `_record_signup_origin`. Rules (`v1`): a referral
attribution or referrer marker gives `referral`; a signup inside
`PRODUCT_ANALYSIS_JOB_FLOW_WINDOWS` (none configured) gives `job_flow`; a
captured marker without referrer gives `organic`; everything else is `unknown`.
Migration `0175_product_analysis.sql` backfills the referral rule; the app
backfills the encrypted rules once, guarded by `schema_meta` key
`product_analysis_signup_origin_backfill:v1`.

## Data correctness and placement

Every source table is read with keyset pagination (`scan_table`) and checked
against `COUNT(*)`; a mismatch renders an error for the affected figures only.
Requests run in their own app ingress shard (an emulated Durable Object on
the core nodes) because a report decrypts every account and repository row.

## Operations

- Rotate the password on the fleet: edit `PRODUCT_ANALYSIS_PASS` in
  `secrets.env`, then run `python3 tools/next_vault.py sync --execute`
  ([OPERATIONS.md](../../docs/OPERATIONS.md)).
- Disable the route by deleting either secret.
- Each public HTTPS clone does one best-effort `product_clone_daily` upsert.
- Down migration: `app/migrations/down/0175_product_analysis.sql`.

pages.title: Cloudflare Workers AI coding agent
pages.description: tools/forkmesh_coding_agent.py is a standard-library coding agent with pluggable model providers: Cloudflare Workers AI, Ollama, or any OpenAI-compatible local server. The…
pages.markdown:
# Cloudflare Workers AI coding agent

`tools/forkmesh_coding_agent.py` is a standard-library coding agent with
pluggable model providers: Cloudflare Workers AI, Ollama, or any
OpenAI-compatible local server. The desktop embeds it.

## Architecture

The loop (`Agent`, `Conversation`, `Memory`, `Session`, `PromptBuilder`) is
separate from transport (`CloudflareProvider`, `OllamaProvider`,
`LocalLlamaProvider`) and from repository tools (`ToolRegistry`, `FileEditor`,
`GitManager`, `SearchEngine`, `CommandExecutor`). Tools include `read_file`,
`write_file`, `replace_text`, `apply_patch`, `undo_edit`, `grep`,
`execute_command`, `git_*`, `run_tests` and `lint_project`. Tool arguments are
coerced to schema, tool results are bounded, and repeated or stalled turns end
the run.

## Desktop

Choosing **Cloudflare AI** creates an isolated worktree and sends each turn
straight to Cloudflare's `/ai/v1/chat/completions` with the account ID and API
token saved in Settings (`CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`);
tools run only locally, and no turn passes through the relay. Models come from
Cloudflare's `/ai/models/search`, with a built-in list when that is
unreachable. **Local Llama** uses an Ollama server at
`127.0.0.1:11434`; when `GET /api/version` answers, the native `/api/chat`
route is used, which sizes `num_ctx`, controls thinking, and keeps the model loaded.

## Command line

```bash
export FORKMESH_AGENT_PROVIDER=cloudflare   # or local-llama
export FORKMESH_AGENT_ACCOUNT_ID=… FORKMESH_AGENT_API_TOKEN=…
export FORKMESH_AGENT_MODEL='@cf/google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it'
python3 tools/forkmesh_coding_agent.py issue.md
```

Other `FORKMESH_AGENT_*` settings: `ENDPOINT`, `TEMPERATURE` (0.2),
`MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` (2000), `CONTEXT_WINDOW` (32000), `TIMEOUT` (600),
`STREAMING`, `RETRY_COUNT` (4), `MAX_TURNS` (120), `SESSION_PATH`,
`TEST_COMMAND`, `LINT_COMMAND`, `PREVIEW_EDITS`, `TOOL_OUTPUT_LIMIT`,
`THINKING`, `KEEP_ALIVE`, `LOCAL_API` (`ollama` or `openai`),
`SHOW_REASONING`.

## Safety

Paths are repository-relative with no `..` or symlink escapes; commands have
closed stdin, bounded output and a timeout; global Git config writes are
isolated; nothing is pushed automatically. Tests:
`app/tests/test_coding_agent.py`, `app/tests/test_local_agent.py`. After
editing the tool, run `python3 tools/sync_coding_agent_header.py`.

pages.markdown:
# Reading and cloning without an account

Public projects are readable without an account. The website never redirects
to sign-up or log-in to read; it asks you to sign in only when you change
something.

## What works without an account

Repository overview, code, branches, commits, issues, pull requests and
reviews, discussions, releases and their manifests, mirrors
(`/owner/repo/mirrors`), public profiles (`/@name`), and
`git clone https://forkmesh.com/owner/repo`. Other forges' URL shapes redirect
to the readable page. See [Git compatibility](git-compatibility.md).

## Where you are asked to sign in

Starring, forking, writing issues, pulls, comments or reviews, changing issue
state, copying an agent prompt, linking a desktop node, and account pages send
you to `/login?next=<page>`. So does a write rejected with `401`, and nothing
else.

## Not yet available

A passkey-backed **browser identity** for signing contributions, and handing it
to a full node, are not yet available. See
[Portable identities and recovery](portable-identities.md).

## Evidence

`app/browser_tests/tests/anonymous-public-reading.spec.js` and
`app/tests/test_anonymous_public_reading.py` check the rule.

pages.markdown:
# Activation-to-revenue weekly scorecard

Weekly reporting template. Definitions live only in the [metric
dictionary](outcome-metrics.json); monthly KPIs go in the [monthly outcome
review](outcome-review.md).

## Reporting contract

- Report the last complete Monday–Sunday week in UTC.
- Read every source to exhaustion. A page size of 100 is a transport limit, never a population limit.
- If source and collected totals do not reconcile, write `UNKNOWN`; never show the partial first page.
- Keep acquisition cohorts, anonymous clone totals and accounting periods separate.
- A missing input is a blocker, not a zero.

```text
Week: YYYY-MM-DD through YYYY-MM-DD UTC
Dictionary: forkmesh-outcome-metric-dictionary-v2 / version 2
Pagination audit: pages collected=<n>; provider/source rows=<n>; all continuations exhausted=true|false
Quality state: COMPLETE | PARTIAL | UNKNOWN
Decision: <one sentence>
```

| Stage | Metric id | This week | Prior week | WoW | Coverage/confidence |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Acquisition | `landing_activation` |  |  |  |  |
| Activation | `anonymous_clone` |  |  |  |  |
| Activation | `signup` |  |  |  |  |
| Activation | `first_mirror` |  |  |  |  |
| Activation | `contribution` |  |  |  |  |
| Revenue | `managed_service_qualification` |  |  |  |  |
| Revenue | `paid_conversion` |  |  |  |  |
| Revenue | `retention` |  |  |  |  |
| Product | `feature_adoption` |  |  |  |  |
| Sustainability | `support_load` |  |  |  |  |
| Sustainability | `infrastructure_cost` |  |  |  |  |
| Sustainability | `gross_margin` |  |  |  |  |

## Reconciliation checklist

1. `python3 tools/outcome_metrics.py validate-dictionary`, then `review --input week.json`.
2. Run `cd app && pytest -q tests/test_attribution.py -k 'report_returns_all_250_rows_not_the_page_size or page_past_100_rows or count_mismatch_raises'`.
3. Reconcile anonymous clones to daily snapshots. Never add `clone_url_copied` to that total.
4. `python3 tools/unit_economics.py validate-contract` and `python3 tools/unit_economics.py report --input period.json`.
5. Do not include raw email, account, repository, path, IP, customer or support identifiers.

pages.markdown:
# ForkMesh apps

ForkMesh runs on the web, the desktop, iPhone and iPad, Apple Watch and
Android. Every app signs in to the same account and instance, so a change
made on one shows up on the others. Downloads are at
[forkmesh.com/#downloads](https://forkmesh.com/#downloads); the platforms
and their release status are in the
[installation support matrix](install-support-matrix.md).

| App | Get it | What it is for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Web | [app.forkmesh.com](https://app.forkmesh.com) or your own instance | Repositories, pull requests, issues, chat, the dashboard and the admin console |
| Desktop (Linux, Windows, macOS) | The install script in [Getting started](getting-started.md), or the installers on the downloads page | The full node: mirrors repositories, runs coding agents in their own worktrees, runs Actions, hosts and agents |
| iPhone and iPad | [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/forkmesh/id6803060735) | A mobile node: browse, edit and commit, run and steer agents, chat and calls, review diffs, Siri, widgets |
| Apple Watch | Installs with the iPhone app | Follow, steer and hear your agents from your wrist |
| Android | Signed APK, `forkmesh-android-universal.apk`, from the downloads page | The iPhone app's features and look; a few newer chat and call changes are still being ported |

## Desktop

The desktop app is a ForkMesh node. It creates its own Ed25519 identity on
first run, mirrors repositories, runs agents in isolated worktrees with live
transcripts and diffs, and turns their work into pull requests. See
[Getting started](getting-started.md) and the
[desktop app guide](qt-client.md).

## iPhone and iPad

The phone is a node too: it holds its own key and has its own Git engine, so
it can clone and commit without the desktop. You can start, steer, stop and
merge agents running on your desktop or on cloud runners, review their diffs
file by file, chat (direct messages are end-to-end encrypted) and make calls,
and use the Market's phone tools. Guides:
[Siri](mobile/siri.md), [Apple Health](mobile/apple-health.md),
[editing files](mobile/mobile-file-editing.md),
[agent access](mobile/mobile-agent-access.md).

## Apple Watch

The watch app is new and still growing. Today it works through your iPhone,
which holds your session and keys:

- **Agent list.** Every active and recent agent with its model, repository,
  status, turns and tokens; running agents first.
- **Live view.** Watch the agent work, with the last reply on screen.
- **Controls.** Stop, Continue, Retry, and send a prompt by dictation or
  Scribble.
- **Review changes.** Read an agent's diff file by file and mark files as
  reviewed.
- **Listen.** Each agent plays as sound and haptics, so you can tell what it
  is doing without looking. The optional Announcer also says short lines
  such as "run done" or "is waiting for you".
- **Siri.** Say "Start a new ForkMesh agent" to start one. Name a
  repository, or it uses the repository and model you last used on the
  phone.
- **Complications and Smart Stack** show the current run at a glance.

Next: a standalone mode that signs in on the watch itself, so it works
without the phone nearby.

## Android

The Android app is built from the same design as the iPhone app (the same
Liquid Glass theme) and talks to the same endpoints, so the server cannot
tell them apart. New phone features land on iPhone first; each one is
tracked until Android matches it, and a few recent chat and call changes
(including group calls) are still on that list. It is distributed as a signed APK from the
downloads page.

Developer documentation for the native apps is in
[docs/native/README.md](../../docs/native/README.md).
