pages.description: A repository page shows an About box on the right: description, website and links. Any folder in a repository can have its own About box too. This is useful for monorepos that…
pages.markdown:
# Folder About boxes

A repository page shows an **About** box on the right: description, website
and links. Any folder in a repository can have its own About box too. This is
useful for monorepos that keep one project per folder: opening the folder on
the web shows that project's name, logo, description, website, links and
topics instead of an empty right-hand side.

## Add an About box to a folder

Commit a file named `.forkmesh/info.json` inside the folder. It is the same
file name the repository uses for its own About (`.forkmesh/info.json` at the
top of the repository), so one convention covers both.

```
bolt-c/
  .forkmesh/info.json
  logo.svg
  README.md
  src/
```

`bolt-c/.forkmesh/info.json`:

```json
{
  "name": "Bolt-C",
  "about": "Track and monitor GitHub pull request readiness.",
  "website": "https://leaf.example.net/",
  "links": [
    {"label": "Source", "url": "https://code.example.org/Bolt/Bolt-C"},
    {"label": "Contributing", "url": "https://code.example.org/Bolt/Bolt/blob/main/bolt-c/CONTRIBUTING.md"}
  ],
  "topics": ["security", "github", "cloudflare-workers"]
}
```

Every field is optional; an empty object (`{}`) is enough to turn the box on.

| Field | Meaning | Limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | Title of the box | 80 characters; defaults to the folder name |
| `about` | One-paragraph description (`description` is accepted too) | 240 characters |
| `website` | Project website (`homepage` is accepted too) | `http` or `https` only, 240 characters |
| `links` | List of `{"label", "url"}` rows | up to 8; `url` must be `http`/`https`, 400 characters; `label` 60 characters, defaults to the address's host |
| `topics` | List of topic words (`tags` is accepted too) | up to 20; lowercased, spaces become `-`, letters, digits and `-` only, 50 characters each |

Text is shown as plain text: HTML and Markdown are not interpreted. Links
with any other scheme (`javascript:`, `data:`, `ftp:`), with a user name or
password in the address, or with spaces are dropped. A field of the wrong
type is ignored. A file that is not valid JSON, or larger than 64 KB, still
shows the box, but with only the fallbacks below.

## Logo

Put `logo.svg` or `logo.png` in the folder itself (not in `.forkmesh/`). If
both exist, the SVG is used. The logo appears at the top of the folder's About
box and next to the folder path above the file list.

- Up to 512 KB.
- A PNG must be a real PNG file.
- An SVG must start with an `<svg>` element (an XML declaration, comments or a
  doctype may come first) and may not declare entities.
- The logo is always shown as an image, never inlined into the page, so
  scripts inside an SVG never run.

## Fallbacks from the folder's README

When the About file has no `about`, the description is the first paragraph of
prose in the folder's `README.md` (also `readme.md`, `Readme.md`,
`README.markdown`, `README.txt` or `README`). Headings, HTML blocks, images,
badges, code blocks, lists and lines like `**Live Site:** ...` are skipped;
links keep their text. It is cut to 240 characters.

When the About file has no `website`, a README line such as
`**Live Site:** https://...`, `**Website:** ...` or `**Homepage:** ...`
supplies it.

## Monorepos with project addresses

On an instance whose administrator set up project addresses (one address per
folder, such as `/Bolt/Bolt-C`), every folder in that project table gets an
About box without committing an About file: its name comes from the table, and
the description, website and logo come from the README and logo files above.
A committed `.forkmesh/info.json` still wins for every field it sets. The web
page looks for a folder About when the folder contains a `.forkmesh` folder,
`logo.svg` or `logo.png`, so a project folder needs one of them.

## Contributor roster

The repository page's Contributors section counts git author names, so bots
are left out but one person with several commit names still counts more than
once, and there are no pictures. To show your own list, commit
`.forkmesh/contributors/contributors.json` at the repository root:

```json
{
  "count": 2,
  "contributors": [
    {"slug": "alice", "name": "Alice", "commits": 120, "profile": "https://example.com/@alice"},
    {"slug": "bob", "name": "Bob", "commits": 40}
  ]
}
```

and a square picture for each person at `.forkmesh/contributors/<slug>.png`.
The page shows `count`, the eight people with the most `commits` (name and
commit count on hover, a link to `profile` when it is an `https://` address,
initials when there is no picture), and a "+N" link to the file.

## What stays the same

Folders without an About file (and not in a project table) look exactly as
before. The repository's own About box on the main page is unchanged; inside a
folder that has an About, the folder's box takes the right-hand column.
Private repositories show folder About boxes and logos only to people who can
read the repository.

pages.title: Two-way forge sync
pages.description: tools/forge_sync.py keeps ForkMesh issues and comments (fields, labels, assignees, state, edits, comment deletions) in step with GitHub (github adapter) or Gitea, Forgejo and…
pages.markdown:
# Two-way forge sync `tools/forge_sync.py` keeps ForkMesh issues and comments (fields, labels, assignees, state, edits, comment deletions) in step with GitHub (`github` adapter) or Gitea, Forgejo and Codeberg (`gitea` adapter). Branches and tags use the ref sync in [Connecting to GitHub](github-sync.md). ## Usage ```bash python3 tools/forge_sync.py connect --provider gitea --repository octo/app \ --base-url https://git.example.org --slo-minutes 15 FORKMESH_FORGE_TOKEN=… FORKMESH_BRIDGE_SIGNING_KEY="$(cat sync-key.pem)" \ python3 tools/forge_sync.py sync --report sync-report.json python3 tools/forge_sync.py status python3 tools/forge_sync.py resolve --issue 12 --field body --take forkmesh python3 tools/forge_sync.py pause --reason "maintenance"; python3 tools/forge_sync.py resume ``` `connect` writes the ledger `.forkmesh/forge-sync.json`; commit it after each pass. `sync --avatars` and `--attachments` also make the provider copies ([Avatars](#avatars), [Attachments](#attachments)). Exit codes: `0` converged, `1` conflicts, `2` configuration error, `75` retryable provider failure. A paused connection sends no requests. ## Merge rules - The ledger stores a digest of each field and comment as last agreed. A change on one side is copied over; differing changes on both sides become a conflict and nothing is written until it is resolved. - `sourceOfTruth` sets a per-field rule: `manual` (default), `forkmesh` or `provider`. Discarded values are kept in ledger `history`. - Synced records carry a `forkmesh-forge-sync:v1` marker so echoes and lost ledgers never create duplicates. Issues are never deleted. ## Mirror mode `connect --mirror` makes a one-way, read-only copy of a provider's issues, for a repository that mirrors a project whose home stays on the forge (for example a community that discusses in GitHub issues). `--two-way` switches back. The ledger stores `"mode": "mirror"`; a ledger without `mode` is two-way. - Every issue is imported, open and closed, with every comment, labels, assignees and state. Titles, bodies and comments are copied in full, in any language and script: there is no length, label or comment cap beyond the 16 MiB per-issue record limit of the git node (`maxIssueRecordBytes`). Line endings are stored as `\n`, leading or trailing blank lines are trimmed and titles lose leading or trailing spaces, the canonical form every ForkMesh client signs. - The provider wins every field. A change made in ForkMesh to a mirrored title, body, state, label set, assignee list or comment is replaced on the next pass by the provider's value, without a conflict. Comments deleted on the provider are deleted in ForkMesh (signed `delete` events). - Nothing is written to the provider: no issue is exported, no ForkMesh comment is posted, and no comment is edited or deleted there. The engine wraps the adapter so any write method raises before a request is made, so a read-only token is enough and a token with write scope is never used to write. - ForkMesh-only comments and issues stay in ForkMesh. - Provider records are always imported as new mirrored records: a `forkmesh-forge-sync` marker in a provider issue or comment is ignored, so a forged marker cannot claim, and then overwrite, a ForkMesh-only issue or comment. ## Where the ledger lives The ledger defaults to `.forkmesh/forge-sync.json` in the checkout. `--ledger PATH` (or `FORKMESH_FORGE_LEDGER`) keeps it anywhere else, for example on the sync server, so the repository carries only the records; it is about 3 KB per issue (field and comment digests), 1.7 MB for a 609-issue forum, and its timestamps change on every pass. Each pass also writes the small public `.forkmesh/forge-source.json` (`forkmesh-forge-source-v1`: `provider`, `repository`, `baseUrl`, `issueUrl` with a `{number}` placeholder, and `renumbered`, the issues whose ForkMesh number differs from the provider's), which is all a reader needs to link an issue to its original. A mirror of the repository that wants its own provider sync builds a fresh ledger on its first pass. ## Identities Imported records are signed by the sync key and credited as `:`. The web dashboard shows a `github:` author as `@`, linked to `https://github.com/` in a new tab (`forgeIdentity` in `app/public/dashboard/js/02-helpers.js`); its avatar is the picture the sync stored in the repository ([Avatars](#avatars)), else the initial, and list rows show plain `@` text (`userNameHtml`; the server renderer `user_name_html` matches), so a page never loads anything from GitHub (readers of a mirror may be on networks where GitHub is blocked or watched). The ledger `identities` map links provider logins to ForkMesh accounts for assignees only; ambiguous links are ignored. ## Avatars With `--avatars`, a `sync` pass also copies each provider author's picture into the repository, so pages can show it without the reader's browser ever contacting the provider. Without it the pass leaves `.forkmesh/contributors` alone and authors show their initials, as before. - **Who.** Every issue author the pass lists, every comment author it reads, and every `:` author already in the records (comments on issues that have not changed since an earlier pass are not listed again, so the records fill those in). People are kept in the ledger `avatars` map (`login`, the API's `avatar_url`, `fetchedAt`, `fetchedUrl`, `failed`). - **Where from.** The API's `avatar_url` (`user.avatar_url` on issues and comments, `RemoteIssue.author_avatar` / `RemoteComment.author_avatar`), asked for at 96 px (`&s=96` on GitHub). Without one, GitHub's `https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/?s=96`. Only `https` on the provider's picture host is fetched: `avatars.githubusercontent.com` for GitHub, the `baseUrl` host for Gitea; a redirect anywhere else is refused. At most 1 MiB, 10 s, 100 pictures per pass (a big forum fills in over a few passes). The token is never sent. - **What is stored.** `.forkmesh/contributors/-.png`. With Pillow installed the picture is decoded and written as a 96x96 PNG. Without it, a picture whose bytes start like a PNG or a JPEG is kept as it came (browsers draw a JPEG served as `image/png`, since `` decodes by content); anything else is dropped and the page keeps the initial. - **When again.** Only when the file is missing, the provider's URL changed, or it is 30 days old (`AVATAR_REFRESH_MS`); a failed fetch waits a day (`AVATAR_RETRY_MS`). An unchanged pass downloads and writes nothing. - **Roster.** `.forkmesh/contributors/contributors.json` gets one row per person (`slug`, `name`, `github` or `login`, a `profile` link for GitHub, `avatar` when the picture exists), sorted by login, in the schema of [the contributor roster](folder-about.md#contributor-roster). Rows whose slug does not start with `-` are kept as they are, before the synced ones, with the file's own `count`; a file that is not valid JSON is left alone. - **Mirror mode** is unchanged: pictures are read from the picture host, nothing is written to the provider. The dashboard and the server-rendered pages draw the stored picture for a `github:` author (`issueActorAvatarHtml` / `avatar_html`) from the repository's own raw URL, over the initial, when the issue index lists the person in `forgeAvatars`. ## Attachments On a `github` connection a `sync --attachments` pass also copies the images and files that issue titles, descriptions and comments embed from GitHub into the repository (`tools/forge_attachments.py`), so a reader's browser never asks GitHub for them. Readers of a mirror may be on networks where GitHub is watched or blocked; a picture that loads from GitHub would tell the network which thread they are reading. Without `--attachments`, or with `FORKMESH_FORGE_ATTACHMENTS=off`, nothing is copied. - **Which addresses.** `https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/`, `https://github.com/user-attachments/files//`, `https://github.com///assets//`, `https://github.com///files//`, `https://user-images.githubusercontent.com//`, `https://private-user-images.githubusercontent.com//?jwt=…` and `https://objects.githubusercontent.com/github-production-repository-file-5c1aeb/…`, wherever they appear: `![](…)`, `[](…)`, ``, `` or a bare address (`SOURCE_RE`; `&` reads as `&`, trailing `.,:;!?` are not part of the address). Every event's `title` and `body` is read, earlier versions of an edited text included. Images on any other host (ehgt.org, labs.ripe.net, …) stay as they are and are not copied. - **Where from.** Only `https`, no port or user name, on `github.com` (only the `user-attachments/` and `//assets|files/` paths), the three `*.githubusercontent.com` hosts above, and the two S3 buckets GitHub redirects to (`github-production-user-asset-6210df.s3.amazonaws.com`, `github-production-repository-file-5c1aeb.s3.amazonaws.com`). Redirects are followed only inside that list; one that leaves it is refused before it is requested. A public repository's attachments need no token, and none is sent (the token would otherwise follow the redirect to S3). - **Links that expire.** A `private-user-images` address carries a JWT that lives five minutes. While it is still valid it is used; otherwise the same picture is fetched from `user-images.githubusercontent.com//`, then `github.com/user-attachments/assets/` (the uuid is in the file name). An `objects.githubusercontent.com` address with an expired S3 signature is fetched as `github.com/user-attachments/files//`, the name taken from its `response-content-disposition`. Tested on github.com/example/forum on 2026-10-21: all of these answer without a token. - **What is kept.** Each file is checked by its first bytes: PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, SVG, PDF, ZIP, gzip, 7z, xz, bzip2, MP4/QuickTime, WebM, pcap and pcapng, and plain UTF-8 text when the name ends in a text extension (`.txt`, `.log`, `.csv`, `.json`, `.c`, …; stored as `.txt`). Anything else (an HTML login page, an executable) is not stored. At most 25 MiB a file (`MAX_BYTES`, by `Content-Length` and by what is read), 30 s a request. Files are stored by content as `.forkmesh/attachments/.`, so two addresses of the same picture share one file. SVG is stored but the raw route serves it as a download (`raw_spec`); pages draw it as an image through `data-repo-svg-src`, never inline. - **Index.** `.forkmesh/attachments/index.json`: `{"schema": "forkmesh-attachments-v1", "files": {"
": {"path", "type", "bytes"}}, "unavailable": {"
": {"reason", "tries", "nextTry"}}}`, sorted, written only when it changes. Each issue with a copied file also gets `.forkmesh/attachments/issues/.json` (`{"schema": "forkmesh-attachments-issue-v1", "files": {…}}`, the same rows for the addresses in that issue), which is what an issue page reads. The signed issue records are never changed. Nothing is ever deleted: a file stays when the comment that used it is edited away. - **Retries.** A file that could not be fetched is listed under `unavailable` and asked again after a day, then 2, 4, … days, at most every 30 days; one that is too large or of a type that is not kept waits 30 days. A rate limit (`429`, or `403` with `Retry-After`) waits once if `Retry-After` is at most 60 s, otherwise the pass stops copying and leaves the rest for the next pass; neither marks the file unavailable. - **Pace and budget.** One request at a time, 0.5 s apart, newest issues first; at most `--attachment-files` (300) downloads, `--attachment-megabytes` (256) and 300 s per pass. The rest waits for the next pass, so a large forum fills in over a few passes; an unchanged pass requests and writes nothing. The repository as a whole keeps at most 1 GiB of copies (`TOTAL_BYTES`, summed from `index.json`); past that a pass stops with `stopped: "total"` and leaves the rest as links. Every copy stays in Git history for good, so without this cap anyone who can comment upstream could grow every clone by 256 MB a pass. - **Size.** github.com/example/forum (611 issues, about 5,900 comments) has 912 such addresses: 763 pictures and 149 files. A sample of 45 averaged 54 KB a picture and 500 KB a file, so the copies add roughly 110-120 MB to the repository, once; every clone and mirror carries them. Pages draw a copied file from the repository's own raw URL and a GitHub attachment that was not copied as a link, never as an `` ([repo-views.md](../../docs/app/repo-views.md#issue-page-first-view)). ## Rate limits and status A rate limit (`429`, or `403` with an exhausted quota) waits for `Retry-After`; other failures back off exponentially, and a stopped pass keeps its progress. Reports (`forkmesh-forge-sync-report-v1`, see [synchronization status](sync-status.md)) give lag against the SLO (default 15 minutes), convergence and conflict rates, and retries. They never contain tokens.

pages.title: Public-interest funding
pages.description: The program funds public repositories, volunteer mirrors, accessibility, documentation, education and independent tooling through donations, sponsorship, grants and matching.…
pages.markdown:
# Public-interest funding

The program funds public repositories, volunteer mirrors, accessibility,
documentation, education and independent tooling through donations,
sponsorship, grants and matching. Funding never buys access, votes or network
rights. Program and rounds live in
[`conformance/funding/v1/`](../../../conformance/funding/v1/program.json); the
[funding register](funding-register.md) and `/docs/funding/register.json` are
generated from them. See also [incentive independence](../incentive-independence.md).

## Eligibility

Public, openly licensed work in a program area. No ForkMesh account, plan,
wallet or token is needed. The forkmesh.com operator, its staff, and a round's
funders and reviewers are excluded.

## Selection

Weighted 0-5 scores (benefit 30, feasibility 20, accessibility 20,
sustainability 15, decentralization 15); an award needs 60/100 from at least 3
reviewers including a non-maintainer, and no recipient may exceed 25% of a round.

## Conflicts

Reviewers with a shared employer or funder, or who are the applicant, must
recuse; funders never review.

## Payment rails

Recipient's choice of bank transfer, Open Collective, Liberapay or Solana; a
conventional rail is always offered.

## Independence

An award's `grants` list must be empty, and the business-model flags such as
`tokenOrBlockchainRequired` must stay `false`.

## Disclosure and reporting

Pool, funders, administrative cost (at most 10%), reviewers, scores, recusals,
awards and receipted milestone payments are published; the outcome report is
recomputed by the ledger.

## Community review

At least 14 days on concentration, accessibility and conflict findings.

## Failure, rollback, and recovery

Fix failing records; never waive the gate or delete records. Use `returned`,
`missed`, `waived` and `cancelled` states, and `render` for a stale register.

## Measures

`status` reports money flows, recipients, milestones, concentration and overdue
reports.

## Closure criteria for issue #515

A pilot round is reported, paid on chosen rails, reviewed, and nothing is
overdue (`closure` exits zero).

## Linked automated evidence

`python3 tools/public_interest_funding.py gate` runs in CI with
`app/tests/test_public_interest_funding.py`.

# Public-interest funding register

Program `1.0.0-rc.1` · Status: **proposed**. How to apply, review, and report is in the [program guide](README.md). The same data is published as searchable JSON at `/docs/funding/register.json`.

## Offers

| Offer | Status | Eligibility | Selection |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Donation | planned | Anyone may donate. Gifts that carry conditions beyond an area restriction are declined. | Donations join the pool of the next announced round in their area. |
| Recurring sponsorship | planned | Anyone may sponsor. Sponsorship buys no placement, ranking, seat, vote, or say in selection. | Sponsorship funds rounds in the sponsored area. Sponsors are listed as funders of the rounds they fund. |
| Targeted grant | planned | The area eligibility and general eligibility rules. | Disclosed reviewers score the published selection criteria. Awards go to eligible applications above the minimum score, in score order, within the pool and the concentration limits. |
| Matching | planned | The area eligibility and general eligibility rules. Matched contributions need public receipts. | Scored like a targeted grant. The award may not exceed the matched contributions times the ratio. |

## Areas and eligibility

- **Public repositories** (`public-repositories`): The repository is public, and anyone can read and clone it without an account. The code or content is under an OSI-approved or Creative Commons license. Where it is hosted does not matter: forkmesh.com, a self-hosted mirror, or another forge.
- **Volunteer mirrors** (`volunteer-mirrors`): The applicant operates a public mirror, relay, or gateway that people other than the operator have used for at least 60 days. The service publishes a health endpoint or status page.
- **Accessibility** (`accessibility`): The work improves a ForkMesh-compatible client, website, or document against WCAG 2.2 AA or the platform's accessibility guidelines. The plan includes testing with at least one person who uses assistive technology.
- **Documentation** (`documentation`): Public documentation, translations, or tutorials under an open license.
- **Education** (`education`): Courses, workshops, or learning materials about decentralized collaboration, under an open license and free to attend or read.
- **Ecosystem tooling** (`ecosystem-tooling`): An independent client, relay, index, verifier, or library with a public https source under an OSI-approved license. A certification badge is welcome but not required.

Every application must also meet these rules:

- Individuals, informal groups, and organizations in any jurisdiction the funder can lawfully pay may apply.
- Applying, being reviewed, and being paid need no ForkMesh account, plan, client, wallet, or token.
- The operator of forkmesh.com and people it pays are not eligible for awards.
- A round's funders and reviewers are not eligible in that round.
- Work whose use requires a paid plan on any ForkMesh-operated service is not eligible.

## Selection criteria

| Criterion | Weight | What reviewers score |
| --- | --- | --- |
| public-benefit | 30 | How many people outside the applicant benefit, and how directly. |
| feasibility | 20 | Whether the milestones, budget, and schedule are realistic for the applicant. |
| accessibility-inclusion | 20 | Whether the work serves people with disabilities, low bandwidth, or languages the ecosystem under-serves. |
| sustainability | 15 | Whether the result keeps working, or is handed on, after the award ends. |
| decentralization | 15 | Whether the work adds a new operator, region, implementation, or maintainer, and so reduces concentration. |

Reviewers score each criterion from 0 to 5. An award needs a weighted score of at least 60 out of 100, from at least 3 reviewers, of whom at least 1 is not a ForkMesh maintainer.

- Conflicts: A reviewer who is the applicant, or who shares an employer or funder with the applicant, must record a recusal and must not score that application. Any other conflict a reviewer declares is recorded and recused the same way. A funder never reviews, never chooses a recipient, and may restrict a gift only to an area.
- Concentration: at most 25% of a round's awards to one recipient. More than 50% to one area, or more than 50% of the pool from one funder, must be addressed in community review.
- Administrative cost: at most 10% of the pool. Administrative cost covers payment fees, accounting, and reviewer stipends. It is published per round before applications open.

## Payment rails

| Rail | Kind | Recurring | ForkMesh account or plan needed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bank transfer (SEPA, ACH, or international wire) | conventional | yes | no |
| Open Collective, through the recipient's own fiscal host | conventional | yes | no |
| Liberapay | conventional | yes | no |
| Solana transfer to an address the recipient controls | on-chain | no | no |

## Independence

An award, donation, or sponsorship pays for work. It never changes who can reach a repository, what an identity may do, who votes, or what the network requires.

Awards never grant: `repository-access`, `identity-rights`, `protocol-votes`, `governance-seats`, `ranking-or-discovery`, `moderation-outcomes`, `required-network-behavior`, `hosted-product-use`.

The only obligations an award may carry: `milestone-report`, `outcome-report`, `open-license`, `accessibility-statement`, `public-receipt`, `conflict-disclosure`.

## Rounds

| Round | Title | Pilot | Stage | Pool | Awarded | Disbursed | Recipients |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [PIF-0001](#pif-0001) | Pilot round: volunteer mirrors, accessibility, and documentation | yes | draft | not published | USD 0 | USD 0 | 0 |

### PIF-0001

**Pilot round: volunteer mirrors, accessibility, and documentation**

Milestone grants and matching for people who run public mirrors, make ForkMesh-compatible clients and documents accessible, and write open documentation. Recipients choose their own payment rail.

- Areas: volunteer-mirrors, accessibility, documentation. Offers: targeted-grant, matching.
- Payment rails: bank-transfer, open-collective, liberapay, solana.
- Apply through: An issue labelled funding-application on any forge mirror of forkmesh/forkmesh. Email to the address in the round announcement, for applicants who cannot apply in public.
- Timeline: announced —; applicationsOpen —; applicationsClose —; selectionsPublished —; finalReportDue —; reported —
- Pool: not published. Administrative cost: not published.

The round opens when:

- A funder commits the pool and publishes the amount, source, conflicts, and any area restriction.
- Administrative cost is published and stays within 10% of the pool.
- At least three reviewers with current governance disclosures are seated, and at least one is not a ForkMesh maintainer.
- The application window is announced with at least 21 days to apply.

#### Funders

None committed.

#### Reviewers

None seated.

#### Applications and selections

No applications.

#### Conflict handling

No conflicts recorded.

#### Milestones and disbursements

No awards.

#### Community review

Window: — to —.

#### Outcome report

Not published.

> No funder has committed a pool and no reviewer is seated, so the round has not opened. It has no applications, selections, or disbursements to report.

pages.markdown:
# Git errors when cloning, pulling, or pushing

ForkMesh serves Git over HTTPS at `https://app.forkmesh.com/<owner>/<repo>`.
Clones and pulls are often redirected to a mirror, so a
`warning: redirecting to ...` line is normal. Errors ForkMesh explains are
printed on `remote:` lines with a link to this page; connection failures show
only Git's own message, usually with a `curl` error.

## Messages from ForkMesh

| `remote:` message | What it means | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ForkMesh could not reach a mirror of this repository just now. | No mirror that holds the repository answered in time. | Try again in a minute. The repository's **Mirrors** page (`/<owner>/<repo>/mirrors`) shows which mirrors are up. |
| This ForkMesh mirror could not read the repository just now. | The mirror you were sent to failed while reading the repository. | Try again; the next attempt may use another mirror. |
| ForkMesh has no public repository at this address. | The owner or repository name is wrong, or the repository is private. | Check the spelling in `git remote -v`. Private repositories need their owner's credential. |
| This ForkMesh mirror has no public repository at this address. | Same as above, answered by the mirror itself. | Same as above. |
| Pushing over HTTPS needs your ForkMesh account name or email and your password, or the repository's push credential. | The push had no credential, or a wrong one, or the account cannot push here. | Use your account name or email as the username and your account password, or the push credential, as the password. See [Hosted repositories](hosted-repositories.md). |
| This repository is private. Sign in with your ForkMesh account name or email and your password, or the repository's credential. | The repository is private and the credential was missing or wrong, or your account cannot read it. | Sign in with an account that can read the repository, or use the credential its owner gave you. |
| ForkMesh could not reach the node that accepts pushes for this repository. | The node that writes this repository did not answer. | Try again in a minute. Your commits are still local and safe. |
| Use Git protocol version 0, 1, or 2. | Your Git sent a protocol version ForkMesh does not speak. | Remove `protocol.version` from your Git configuration, or set it to `2`. |

## Errors from your own Git client

These come from Git and curl on your computer; ForkMesh never saw the request.

| Git prints | What happened | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Error in the HTTP2 framing layer`, `HTTP/2 stream … was not closed cleanly`, `curl 16`, `curl 92` | The HTTP/2 connection broke partway through. VPNs, proxies, antivirus that inspects HTTPS, and unstable mobile or Wi-Fi links cause most of these. | Run the command again. If it keeps failing, use HTTP/1.1 for this repository: `git config http.version HTTP/1.1`. Add `--global` to use it everywhere. |
| `RPC failed; curl 18 transfer closed with outstanding read data remaining`, `curl 56`, `early EOF`, `unexpected disconnect while reading sideband packet` | The connection dropped while Git was downloading. | Run the command again. If it fails at the same point every time, include a trace in your report (below). |
| `Could not resolve host`, `Failed to connect`, `Connection timed out`, `Connection refused` | Your computer could not reach ForkMesh at all. | Check your network, DNS, and any VPN or proxy. |
| `SSL certificate problem` | Something between you and ForkMesh is presenting another certificate, or your clock is wrong. | Check the system clock, and any proxy or antivirus that intercepts HTTPS. |

## Reporting a problem

Open an issue on
[forkmesh/forkmesh](https://app.forkmesh.com/forkmesh/forkmesh/issues) with
`git --version`, `curl --version`, the time of failure with time zone, and a
trace (check it for secrets before posting):

```bash
GIT_TRACE_CURL=1 GIT_TRACE_CURL_NO_DATA=1 git pull origin main 2>&1 | tail -60
```

pages.markdown:
# Connecting a repository to GitHub

A GitHub Actions workflow syncs a ForkMesh repository with GitHub on events and
every 15 minutes. Refs move both ways by fast-forward only (never forced or
deleted; diverged branches are reported). Issues, discussions and pull requests
import one way into `.forkmesh` records; for two-way issues see
[Two-way forge sync](forge-sync.md).

```bash
python3 tools/github_forkmesh_bridge.py connect --github OWNER/NAME --forkmesh OWNER/NAME --key-out KEY.pem
```

`connect` writes `.forkmesh/github-sync.json`, `.forkmesh/github-bridge.py` and
`.github/workflows/forkmesh-github-sync.yml`. Set secrets
`FORKMESH_BRIDGE_SIGNING_KEY` and `FORKMESH_SYNC_SSH_KEY` and variable
`FORKMESH_SYNC_REMOTE` (optionally `FORKMESH_SYNC_KNOWN_HOSTS`).

Rules: imported events are signed by the bridge key with `authorName`
`github:LOGIN`; GitHub numbers are kept unless taken; event ids derive from
GitHub ids so reruns are idempotent; ForkMesh-side edits survive; pull request
code is fetched as data and never executed (payloads over 8 MiB skipped).
Subcommands `git-sync`, `export` and `run --dry-run` run pieces by hand; tests
are `app/tests/test_github_forkmesh_bridge.py`. To also deploy a Cloudflare
Worker from the mirror, see [Mirror and deploy a Cloudflare Worker](cloudflare-workers.md).

pages.markdown:
# Protocol and ecosystem governance

The charter governs the protocol suite, certification, compatibility and the
moderation baseline; repositories follow their own policy documents. Charter,
records and participant disclosures live in
[`conformance/governance/v1/`](../../../conformance/governance/v1/charter.json);
the [decision register](decision-register.md) and
`/docs/governance/register.json` are generated from them.

## Roles

| Body | Seats | Quorum |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Protocol council | 2 maintainers, 2 independent implementers, 2 community operators | 4 |
| Security response team | 1 maintainer, 1 independent implementer, 1 community operator | 2 |
| Appeals panel | 1 independent implementer, 1 community operator, 1 community member | 3 |

Independent constituencies must vote, and no employer or funder may cast more
than half the votes, so maintainers cannot decide alone.

## Proposals

`FMP-NNNN`: review at least 14 days (30 if breaking), last call 7 days, decision
within 14 days. A `no` vote needs a dissent statement. Narrowing a protected
right (free protocol, portable identity and repositories, token-free
governance) needs two thirds. See the [protocol suite](../protocol/README.md).

## Security decisions

Report as in [SECURITY.md](../../../SECURITY.md): acknowledge in 3 days, embargo
at most 90 days, publish `FMS-NNNN` within 7 days of disclosure, ratify within 30.

## Appeals

`FMA-NNNN` within 30 days, decided within 30 days by uninvolved panel members.

## Running the ledger

`python3 tools/protocol_governance.py validate|render|gate|status|closure`;
tests are `app/tests/test_protocol_governance.py`. Disclosures stay current for
180 days. Records are fixed or annotated, never deleted.

pages.description: How a ForkMesh hackathon campaign works. Anything worth money is gated on the referral ledger, every reward is a fixed threshold, there are no random draws, and sharing earns…
pages.markdown:
# Hackathon

How a ForkMesh hackathon campaign works. Anything worth money is gated on the
referral ledger, every reward is a fixed threshold, there are no random draws,
and sharing earns nothing.

| Area | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Policy (points, missions, rewards, judging, config validation) | `app/src/hackathon.py` |
| Routes, storage, admin page | `app/src/hackathon_runtime.py` |
| Share cards | `app/src/og_card.py` (`render_hackathon_card`) |
| Participant HQ | `app/public/dashboard/partials/views/hackathon.html` |
| Public pages | `www/public/hackathon/leaderboard.html`, `www/public/hackathon/projects.html` |
| Schema | `app/migrations/0182_hackathon.sql` |

## What /hackathon shows

`/hackathon` and `/hackathon/rules` are the current campaign's pages; they are
static templates in `www/templates/pages/`. When a campaign ends, its pages
move under `/hackathon/archive/<slug>` with an "Archived" banner, and
`/hackathon/archive` lists every finished one.

| Campaign | Dates (UTC) | Pages |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plugin Race | 19 Oct – 18 Dec 2026 | `/hackathon`, `/hackathon/rules`; engine in [docs/app/plugin-race.md](../../docs/app/plugin-race.md) |
| September Revenue Contest | 15 Sep – 15 Oct 2026 | `/hackathon/archive/revenue-contest-2026`, `/hackathon/archive/revenue-contest-2026-rules`; continued as the [affiliate program](../../docs/app/affiliates.md) |

The archive pages are routed to the website by `WWW_HACKATHON_ARCHIVE_PAGES` in
`app/src/static_routes.py`; add a new archive slug there. The Plugin Race
does not use the points engine below, because its finish line is marketplace
ratings.

## Lifecycle

A campaign is a `hackathons` row keyed by slug with status `draft`,
`registration`, `live`, `judging`, or `closed`. A `draft` campaign 404s on
every participant page and API, so unfinished campaigns can ship safely. Only an
administrator advances status.

## Points

`hackathon_points` is append-only with primary key
`(hackathon_slug, account_bi, kind, ref)`, which prevents double payment. Kinds:
`joined`, `verified`, `referral_joined`, `referral_qualified`, `first_mirror`,
`pull_accepted`, `submission`, `referral_post`. No kind is client-reportable.

A referral is *joined* when the invitee verifies email and *qualified* when the
referral ledger credits it. Anything of value reads qualified.

## Rewards

Missions and milestones award `pro_months`, `supporter_months`, a `badge`, or
nothing; cash follows judged tracks only. Grants are claimed once in
`hackathon_reward_grants` and projected into `role_grants` with
`scope_type='promotion'`, stacking months.

## Teams, submissions, and judging

A squad is an invite tree; a team (up to five) submits one project per track.
Submissions must name a public repository first hosted in the campaign window;
doubtful ones are flagged for review, not rejected. Only `valid` projects are
public. Judges score 1 to 5 on four criteria; finalizing ranks each track and
grants the prize table once.

Challenge links fix their target when sent, need a strictly higher score, and
pay no points. Share presses are measured, never paid, and nothing is sent on
anyone's behalf.

## Administration and privacy

`/admin/hackathon` and `/api/admin/hackathon` require a live `is_admin`
session. Public reads are edge-cached and bounded. No contacts are collected;
public pages show only public usernames.

pages.markdown:
# Integration contract (v1)

A versioned contract for tools that migrate, automate, discover, deploy,
analyze, or moderate repositories without scraping a UI: HTTP resources, a
`forkmesh-event-v1` event stream, command-line output, and signed webhooks.
[`conformance/integrations/v1/contract.json`](../../conformance/integrations/v1/contract.json)
is the source of truth; if this page disagrees, the JSON wins. The client,
contract runner, watcher, webhook sender, and offline fixture are one
standard-library file,
[`tools/forkmesh_integration.py`](../../tools/forkmesh_integration.py).

```sh
python3 tools/forkmesh_integration.py discover --target hosted
python3 tools/forkmesh_integration.py contract --target self-hosted --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8791
python3 tools/forkmesh_integration.py contract --target hosted --fixture next   # offline
```

`contract` prints a `forkmesh-integration-contract-report-v1` report (status
codes, fields, headers, attempts, latency, service version; no credentials).

## Services and authentication

| Service | Default base URL | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hosted` | `https://app.forkmesh.com` | The hosted application API |
| `self-hosted` | `http://127.0.0.1:8791` | The `forkmesh-mirror-node` loopback control API |

Each resource names one scheme: `anonymous` (public, may be edge cached),
`loopback-operator` (socket access is the authorization; never publish the
port), `catalog-view-token` (owner-signed `forkmesh-catalog-view-v1` `viewer`,
`ts`, `sig`; adds private repositories, `no-store` with a weak `ETag`),
`account-bearer` (`Authorization: Bearer …`, never in a URL),
`webhook-capability-url` (the 256-bit token in the URL is the credential), and
`webhook-hmac` (see [Signatures](#signatures)).

## HTTP resources

| Service | Method and path | Required fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| hosted | `GET /api/version` | `ok`, `rev`, `worker`, `version`, `now` |
| hosted | `GET /api/openapi.json` | `openapi`, `info`, `paths` |
| hosted | `GET /api/metrics/endpoints` | `ok`, `endpoints[].method`, `endpoints[].template` |
| hosted | `GET /api/repositories` | `ok`, `repositories[].owner`, `.name`, `.visibility` |
| hosted | `GET /api/repositories/search` (beta) | `ok`, `total`, `results[].owner`, `.name`, `.clone` |
| hosted | `GET /api/status` | `ok`, `now`, `systems[].id`, `systems[].status` |
| hosted | `GET /api/mirrors/https` | `ok`, `protocol`, `registration` |
| hosted | `POST /api/chat/webhooks/{token}` | inbound webhook, `202 {"ok", "messageId"}` |
| self-hosted | `GET /healthz` | `ok`, `node` |
| self-hosted | `GET /readyz` (200 or 503) | `ok`, `ready`, `version` |
| self-hosted | `GET /v1/status` | `ok`, `ready`, `node`, `version`, `uptimeSeconds`, `repositories`, `lastSyncOk`, `syncCount` |
| self-hosted | `POST /v1/control/sync` | `202 {"ok", "queued"}` |

Only these routes are stable; others discovered via OpenAPI may change.

## Pagination

Collections are bounded: `GET /api/repositories` returns at most 200 records,
newest `updatedAt` first. Time feeds resume with `since` = previous `latestTs`
(deduplicate the boundary). `GET /api/repositories/search` is keyset-paged:
pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` until it is `null`. See
[Searchable repository index](repository-index.md).

## Filtering

Only search filters server-side (`q`, `view`, `language`, `topic`, `owner`,
`cloneable`). Otherwise filter client-side on documented fields.

## Idempotency

`GET`/`HEAD` are safe to repeat. `POST /v1/control/sync` is idempotent
(`"queued": false` while pending). Inbound chat webhook POSTs are not
deduplicated. Every outbound event has a stable `id` to use as the idempotency
key.

## Ordering and the event stream

```json
{"schema":"forkmesh-event-v1","id":"4c1f…","type":"repository.changed",
 "subject":"owner/name","sequence":7,"digest":"9a0e…","occurredAt":1789347378245,
 "source":"https://app.forkmesh.com","data":{"owner":"owner","name":"name"}}
```

| Type | Service | Subject | Producer |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `repository.changed`, `repository.removed` | hosted | lowercase `owner/name` | `watch` |
| `repository.push`, `branch.push` | hosted | lowercase `owner/name` | relay |
| `pull.merged`, `release.published` | hosted | lowercase `owner/name` | relay |
| `mirror.node.changed` | self-hosted | `node:<name>` | `watch` |
| `mirror.repository.changed`, `mirror.repository.removed` | self-hosted | the daemon's repository key | `watch` |

Delivery is at-least-once, `sequence` increases by one per subject (no global
order), and every `changed` event carries full current `data`. `EventLedger`
in the tool applies the consumer rules: ignore seen ids and stale sequences,
buffer gaps, emit `resync` after `gapTimeoutSeconds` (120), and accept the
first event per subject as the baseline.

## Webhooks

`deliver` posts events as canonical JSON with these headers: `ForkMesh-Webhook-Id`
(event id), `ForkMesh-Webhook-Timestamp` (Unix seconds per attempt),
`ForkMesh-Webhook-Signature` (`v1=<hex>`, comma-separated during rotation),
`ForkMesh-Webhook-Attempt`, `ForkMesh-Event-Type`. `2xx` acknowledges, `410`
stops, retryable statuses retry, anything else goes to the dead-letter file
(replay with `deliver --input dead.ndjson`).

### Signatures

```text
signature = "v1=" + hex(HMAC-SHA256(secret, "forkmesh-webhook-v1\n" + timestamp + "\n" + id + "\n" + raw_body))
```

```python
msg = b"forkmesh-webhook-v1\n%d\n%s\n" % (ts, headers["ForkMesh-Webhook-Id"].encode()) + body
```

Reject timestamps more than 300 seconds off and deduplicate by id.

### Repository webhooks

Owners register public `https` endpoints in repository **Settings**
(`POST /api/repo/<owner>/<repo>/webhooks`); the relay generates the secret and
shows it once. Events: `repository.push` (any ref moved), `branch.push`
(default branch moved), `pull.merged`, `release.published`. Only public
repositories emit them; deliveries are queued out of band and stop after 6
attempts. `sequence` is per endpoint.

### Inbound chat webhooks

`POST /api/chat/webhooks/{token}` with `{"text": "…"}` posts to a public
channel (`202`). Errors: 400 `empty_webhook`, 404 `not_found`, 405
`method_not_allowed`, 409 `public_channel_required`.

## Retries

Retry idempotent requests on transport errors and `408`, `425`, `429`, `500`,
`502`, `503`, `504`: at most 6 attempts, exponential backoff from 0.5 s capped
at 30 s with jitter; `Retry-After` or `retryAfterMs` overrides. Non-idempotent
requests retry only on `429`.

## Rate limits

Throttled requests answer `429` with `Retry-After`. Hosted public reads are
edge cached (catalog 30 s). `watch` polls no faster than 30 s hosted, 5 s
self-hosted.

## Errors

Hosted errors are `{"error":"<snake_case>"}`; the daemon answers
`{"ok":false,"error":"<message>"}`. Branch on status class, then code. New
codes are additive.

## Command-line output

Each stdout line is one JSON object (`"schema":"forkmesh-cli-v1"`, or events
for `watch`); diagnostics go to stderr. Commands: `validate`, `discover`,
`contract`, `watch`, `deliver`, `fixture`.

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | success |
| 1 | contract failure or undeliverable events |
| 2 | usage or configuration error |
| 3 | unsupported service version skew |

`forkmesh-mirror-node` flags: `-config`, `-init`, `-check`, `-public-key`,
`-set-version`, `-register-link-code`, `-version`; exit `0` or `1`.

## Deprecation

Deprecated entries are marked `"stability": "deprecated"` and listed with
`announced`, `sunset` (at least 180 days later), and `replacement`. Removal
needs contract v2.

## Version skew

Within v1 services only add; consumers must ignore unknown fields. A version
below `serviceMinimum` is `unsupported` (exit 3); unparseable versions are
`unknown`. The fixture serves `previous`, `current`, `next`, `broken`, and
`unsupported` profiles.

## Examples

Examples in `conformance/integrations/v1/examples/` use only this contract:
`conformance/integrations/v1/examples/discovery_catalog.py`,
`conformance/integrations/v1/examples/migration_export.py`,
`conformance/integrations/v1/examples/webhook_moderation.py`,
`conformance/integrations/v1/examples/deployment_gate.py`.

## Contract tests and telemetry

`app/tests/test_integration_contract.py` checks every entry against the
serving source, runs the contract against the fixture for both services and
every profile, and runs every example. Each report's `telemetry` block records
requests, retries, transport errors, status classes, and latency.

pages.description: ForkMesh accepts public ActivityPub replies (Lemmy or Mastodon Create of a Note, Page or Article) to public federated issues, pull requests and discussions, including replies to…
pages.markdown:
# Lemmy-compatible threaded collaboration

ForkMesh accepts public ActivityPub replies (Lemmy or Mastodon `Create` of a
`Note`, `Page` or `Article`) to public federated issues, pull requests and
discussions, including replies to other verified remote replies.

## Trust boundary

Remote replies are stored encrypted in `ap_comments`
(`forkmesh-federated-thread-v1`), never in `.forkmesh` records or any signed
event stream. An HTTP signature authenticates the remote actor but does not make the reply a ForkMesh native event;
projections carry `federated: true` and `nativeEvent: false`.

A remote object cannot select a ForkMesh context: a top-level reply inherits the
context of the `/ap/o/{id}` object it targets, a nested reply that of its
stored parent, and unresolved targets are discarded.

## Lifecycle

- `Create` is idempotent per remote `id`.
- `Update` replaces the body only when the author matches; marked `edited`.
- `Delete` leaves a `tombstoned` placeholder; `Remove` (same instance only)
  leaves `moderated`.
- `Undo(Remove)` waits for redelivery instead of restoring cached content.

Blocked instances (and their subdomains) are rejected before verification and
hidden on read. Private repository threads never federate.

## Client API

```text
GET /api/repo/{owner}/{repo}/fedi-comments?kind={issue|pull|discussion}&number={n}
```

Clients render bodies as plain text, accept only HTTPS backlinks, cap nesting
depth, label edited and removed records, and never parse them as native
events. Fixtures are in `app/tests/fixtures/activitypub/lemmy/`.

pages.title: Mentions and username suggestions
pages.description: You never have to type a ForkMesh username from memory. Wherever you mention someone or enter a username, ForkMesh suggests matching accounts as you type, and every name and…
pages.markdown:
# Mentions and username suggestions

You never have to type a ForkMesh username from memory. Wherever you mention
someone or enter a username, ForkMesh suggests matching accounts as you type,
and every name and `@mention` you see opens that person's profile.

## @mentions

Type `@` and the first letters of a name. A short list of matching people
appears at the cursor:

- **Chat** (the `/chat` page and the dashboard chat panel): people in the
  room and the chat directory first, then anyone on ForkMesh.
- **Issues, pull requests, discussions and releases**: people already on that
  issue or pull request first (author, commenters, assignees, reviewers), then
  the repository's contributors, then anyone on ForkMesh.

Use the arrow keys and Enter or Tab to pick a name, or tap it on a phone.
Escape closes the list.

Mentioning someone in an issue or pull request pings them and subscribes them
to the thread. They can press **Unsubscribe** on the issue to stop hearing
about it, and a later mention does not subscribe them again.

Text that looks like a mention is left alone inside code, inside links and
web addresses (`https://x.social/@bob`), and in email addresses.

## Username fields

On the web, these fields suggest accounts as you type:

| Where | Field |
| --- | --- |
| Chat, channel settings, Members | The invite field; people already in the channel are not suggested |
| Chat, New channel | The members list: separate names with commas, and each name you add is left out of the next suggestions |
| Repository settings, Collaborators | The collaborator name; current collaborators are not suggested |
| Security advisory | The credit and collaborator name |

Your own name is never suggested. Prefix matches come first, then names that
contain what you typed. When the only suggestion is exactly what you typed,
the list hides so Enter submits the form.

The desktop app's invite dialogs search people too, and DJ Studio suggests
names when you invite people to a jam ([DJ Studio jams](dj-studio.md)). The
phone apps have no channel invite field.

## Profile links

Every account name and every `@mention` links to that person's profile at
`/@name`: in issues, pull requests, discussions, notes, tasks, chat, commit
lists, notification emails and more. In the phone apps a tap opens the
profile inside the app. The desktop app opens its own profile card when it
knows the person, and the web profile otherwise.

Some names stay plain text on purpose:

- bots, agents and system names such as Actions, runners and mirror nodes;
- Discord senders and fediverse authors, whose display names could match the
  wrong ForkMesh account;
- commit authors whose Git name is not a ForkMesh account;
- private profiles, accounts that do not exist, and names inside a row that
  is already a link.

Related: [Hosted repositories](hosted-repositories.md) and
[ForkMesh apps](apps.md).

pages.title: Mirror goals
pages.description: An instance admin turns this on with the Mirror goal plugin (admin console, Plugins). It is off until then.
pages.markdown:
# Mirror goals

An instance admin turns this on with the **Mirror goal** plugin (admin
console, Plugins). It is off until then.

A project that could be blocked or taken down survives if copies of it are
kept in many places. A repository page can show how many copies are running
and how healthy they are, in the **Mirrors** card at the bottom of the right
rail: "3 / 10 healthy" with a progress bar, then one row per copy with a
green, yellow or red dot.

- **This instance** and, for a repository synced from GitHub, Gitea or
  Forgejo, **the original** are always listed.
- **Mirrors people run** are added with **Add a mirror**. Anyone signed in can
  list a copy they run; it is checked about every 15 minutes.
- **Green** means the copy answered and has a commit this repository had in
  the last day. **Yellow** means it answered but is behind or different, or
  has not answered for a day. **Red** means it could not be reached twice in a
  row, or never. Grey means not checked yet, or an address that is listed but
  not checked (git://, ssh, .onion).

The goal is set by the repository's maintainers (the owner, an organization
maintainer or admin, or an instance administrator) with **Set target**. A goal
of 0 turns the count off.

Every repository has a page that explains all of this step by step, with the
live count: `https://<instance>/<owner>/<repository>/mirror` (for the
example forum, `https://forum.example.org/example/forum/mirror`).
While a repository is below its goal, its home page, issue list, lite pages
and feeds ask readers to help and link there.

## Run a mirror

```sh
git clone --mirror https://<instance>/<owner>/<repository>.git
cd <repository>.git && git update-server-info
```

Refresh it every 15 minutes, for example with cron:

```
*/15 * * * * cd /srv/<repository>.git && git remote update --prune && git update-server-info
```

Serve the folder over HTTPS with any web server (Git's "dumb HTTP" needs only
static files), or push it to another forge, then list its `https://` address
with **Add a mirror**. A repository synced with [forge sync](forge-sync.md)
keeps its issues in `.forkmesh/issues`, so the clone carries the whole forum,
not only the code. To serve it with issues, pull requests and a web page,
[start your own ForkMesh instance](https://forkmesh.com/start) and import the
clone.

Checking a mirror reads only its list of branches (`info/refs`); nothing is
loaded from it in visitors' browsers.

pages.title: Offline and low-bandwidth sync
pages.description: tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py moves a repository over removable media or an unreliable, metered link. It exports refs (and with them the signed .forkmesh/ collaboration records)…
pages.markdown:
# Offline and low-bandwidth sync

`tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py` moves a repository over removable media or an
unreliable, metered link. It **exports** refs (and with them the signed
`.forkmesh/` collaboration records) to a directory signed with an Ed25519 key,
**fetches** that directory in verified, resumable chunks, **imports** it in one
ref transaction, and **rolls back** any import.

Formats: manifest `forkmesh-offline-media-v1` inside the signed envelope
`forkmesh-offline-media-signed-v1`; checkpoint
`forkmesh-offline-transfer-checkpoint-v1`; import journal
`forkmesh-offline-import-journal-v1`; replica advertisement
`forkmesh-replica-scope-v1`.

## Start here: carry a repository on a USB stick

```sh
tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py keygen ~/.forkmesh-offline.key   # prints the public key
tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py export ~/src/project /media/usb/export-1 --signing-key ~/.forkmesh-offline.key
tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py verify /media/usb/export-1 --trusted-key <public key>
tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py import /media/usb/export-1 ~/src/project --trusted-key <public key>
```

Share the public key over a trusted channel. A key that starts with `-` goes
after an equals sign: `--trusted-key=-Ab…`. `export --since <earlier export>`
writes an incremental export listing its `prerequisites` and `previousExport`;
import refuses it until the base has been imported.

## Fetch over a link that keeps dropping

```sh
tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py fetch https://files.example.org/export-1/ ./incoming \
  --rate 64k --budget 20M --schedule 22:00-06:00 --trusted-key <public key>
tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py status ./incoming
```

The source is any static HTTP host that honours `Range`, or a local directory.
The signed manifest is fetched and verified once. Chunks resume from the first
missing byte and count only after their SHA-256 matches the manifest; a chunk
failing 3 times stops the fetch. The bundle is assembled only when every chunk
and the whole-file digest verify. Retries back off; `--retries N` failures
without progress pause with `link_down`; Ctrl-C pauses with `cancelled`;
`--budget` pauses with `budget_exhausted`; `--schedule` windows pause with
`outside_schedule` (`--wait` sleeps instead); `--restart` discards the
checkpoint. `status` reads only the local checkpoint and reports remaining
bytes and an ETA; `fetch --json` adds transfer counters.

## Limited exports

| Export option | Limitation code |
| --- | --- |
| `--metadata-only` | `metadata_only` |
| `--path PATH` | `path_filter` |
| `--defer-blobs-over SIZE` | `deferred_large_objects` |
| `--ref GLOB` | `branch_filter` |
| _(detected on import)_ | `missing_objects` |

The signed manifest advertises a replica scope of `full`, `filtered` or
`metadata-only`; `verify` recomputes it and fails an overclaiming export. Import
needs `--allow-limited` for a limited export and stores left-out contents as a
Git partial clone. `forkmesh_offline_sync.py replica REPO` prints what a
repository may advertise. The [availability proof](availability-proof.md)
treats any limited replica as `limited_replica` and never counts it toward a
quorum.

## Import, reconciliation, and rollback

Import verifies signature, trusted key, manifest, digests, scope, object format
and prerequisites before writing anything, then decides each ref:

| Decision | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `create` | Ref created. |
| `fast_forward` | Ref moved forward. |
| `unchanged` | Nothing. |
| `local_ahead` | Local kept. |
| `conflict` | Local kept; incoming saved under `refs/forkmesh-offline/conflicts/`. |
| `checked_out` | Local kept; incoming saved aside for `git merge --ff-only`. |

Refs are never deleted. All changes apply in one `git update-ref --stdin`
transaction after a journal is written to
`<git-dir>/forkmesh-offline/imports/<importId>.json`.
`forkmesh_offline_sync.py rollback REPO IMPORT_ID` reverses it only if every ref
still holds the imported value.

Signing is Ed25519 over `forkmesh-offline-media-v1\n` plus the canonical
manifest's SHA-256; verification is pure Python. Unpinned signers need
`--allow-unpinned`. `--telemetry FILE` appends one count-only
`forkmesh-offline-telemetry-v1` line per run, with no names, URLs, refs or keys.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Done. |
| `2` | Usage error or unreadable input. |
| `3` | Verification, integrity, or missing-object failure; nothing changed. |
| `4` | Paused with the checkpoint kept; re-run to resume. |
| `5` | Imported, with conflicts saved aside. |

Tests: `app/tests/test_offline_sync.py` (quality gate `offline-sync-conformance`).

pages.title: Monthly outcome review
pages.description: Roadmap decisions use the KPIs in the versioned outcome metric dictionary, which defines each metric's numerator, denominator, window, privacy class, consent, retention, minimum…
pages.markdown:
# Monthly outcome review

Roadmap decisions use the KPIs in the versioned
[outcome metric dictionary](outcome-metrics.json), which defines each metric's
numerator, denominator, window, privacy class, consent, retention, minimum cell
size, freshness, coverage, baseline, target and source. This page is the monthly
record template; the [weekly scorecard](activation-revenue-scorecard.md) covers
`weekly` metrics. Baselines stay `unmeasured` and targets `to-be-set` until a
recorded review adopts them.

## Privacy rules

Measurement must never become required surveillance.

- Product analytics is opt-in. Other KPIs use operational records, closed
  ledgers, synthetic probes or voluntary operator registrations.
- A self-hosted node never has to report anything. Such KPIs are `lower-bound`.
- Observation files carry counts and segment labels only; the review tool
  rejects identifier fields and any email or IPv4 value.
- Segments below `minimumCellSize` are suppressed; if only one is suppressed,
  the next smallest is suppressed too.
- Exports built only for a monthly KPI are deleted once the review is recorded.
- A record never quotes a person, repository, pull, ticket, or customer.

## Prepare the review

```sh
python3 tools/outcome_metrics.py validate-dictionary
python3 tools/outcome_metrics.py review --input /path/to/month.json
```

Collect each source to exhaustion and record source and collected totals:

```json
{
  "schema": "forkmesh-outcome-observations-v1",
  "dictionarySchema": "forkmesh-outcome-metric-dictionary-v2",
  "dictionaryVersion": 2,
  "cadence": "monthly",
  "periodStart": "2026-09-01T00:00:00Z",
  "periodEnd": "2026-10-01T00:00:00Z",
  "generatedAt": "2026-10-03T09:00:00Z",
  "observations": [
    {
      "metric": "repository_availability",
      "numerator": 1293120,
      "denominator": 1296000,
      "sourceTotal": 30,
      "collectedTotal": 30,
      "continuationExhausted": true,
      "coverage": 1.0,
      "dataCutAt": "2026-10-01T01:00:00Z",
      "segments": [{ "label": "clone", "value": 646560 }]
    }
  ]
}
```

A metric without an observation is `UNKNOWN`, never zero. Data older than
`freshnessHours` is `stale`. Confidence:

| Confidence | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `high` | Reconciled, exhausted, fresh, coverage at least 0.95, full coverage class |
| `medium` | Reconciled and fresh, partial coverage or class |
| `low` | Reconciled but stale, or coverage below 0.5 (`PARTIAL`) |
| `unknown` | Missing, unreconciled, not exhausted, or cut early (`UNKNOWN`) |

Before circulating, reconcile billing metrics with
`python3 tools/unit_economics.py report`, operations metrics with the status
history, and attach the month's Git conformance report. A failed sample makes
the metric `UNKNOWN`.

## Copy for each month

Store records as `www/docs/strategy/outcome-reviews/YYYY-MM.md`, aggregates only.

```text
Month: YYYY-MM
Dictionary: forkmesh-outcome-metric-dictionary-v2 / version 2
Data cuts: hosted=<ts>; analytics=<ts>; finance=<ts>; synthetic=<ts>
Quality state: COMPLETE | PARTIAL | UNKNOWN
```

| Stage | Metric id | Value | Baseline | Target | Freshness | Confidence | Coverage |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Acquisition | `landing_activation` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Activation | `anonymous_clone` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Activation | `signup` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Activation | `first_mirror` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Activation | `contribution` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Revenue | `managed_service_qualification` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Revenue | `paid_conversion` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Revenue | `retention` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Product | `feature_adoption` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Sustainability | `support_load` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Sustainability | `infrastructure_cost` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Sustainability | `gross_margin` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Activation | `successful_migration` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Community | `first_contribution` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Community | `active_maintainers` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Product | `hosted_service_adoption` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Availability | `repository_availability` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Availability | `independent_mirror_nodes` |  |  |  |  |  |  |

```text
Decisions:
- <decision> — evidence: <metric ids> — revisit: YYYY-MM
Experiments:
- <hypothesis> — metric: <id> — guardrail: <id> — result: <pending|kept|reverted>
Roadmap changes:
- <milestone> — <added|reprioritized|dropped> — because: <metric ids>
```

Definitions change only between periods: update `outcome-metrics.json`,
increment `version`, and never rewrite earlier records. A missing or
unreconciled source makes the metric `UNKNOWN` for the period; never carry a
prior value forward or reconstruct history by hand.

Tests: `app/tests/test_outcome_metrics.py`.

pages.title: Planned plugins
pages.description: Features that may move out of the ForkMesh core into optional Marketplace packages. Nothing on this page is shipped; each family gets its own issue once scheduled. The package…
pages.markdown:
# Planned plugins

Features that may move out of the ForkMesh core into optional Marketplace
packages. Nothing on this page is shipped; each family gets its own issue once
scheduled. The package format and lifecycle are in
[`marketplace/README.md`](../../../marketplace/README.md).

A **plugin** here is a `.fmpkg` package with a manifest: it declares its
entrypoints and permissions, owns its state, removes everything on uninstall,
and has reversible migrations. It is not a library loaded at runtime.

## Admission test

A candidate qualifies only when every answer is yes:

1. ForkMesh still browses, collaborates on, mirrors and preserves repositories
   without it.
2. It has one owner, lifecycle and configuration surface, and a reason to
   version independently.
3. Install and uninstall can be tested without rewriting or orphaning Git
   history, identity, collaboration records or security state.
4. The host can expose a narrow capability instead of arbitrary filesystem,
   process, network, database or secret access.
5. A second implementation, provider, content pack or user group benefits from
   the choice.

## Candidate families

| Family | Host socket |
| --- | --- |
| World decorative elements | `world.object` |
| Portable operations skills and shortcuts | `content.skill`, `content.shortcut` |
| Analytics (already extracted) | `web.analytics-provider` |
| Membership provider adapter | `worker.webhook`, `membership.provider` |
| Push notification adapter | `worker.notification-provider` |
| Coding-agent provider adapters | `desktop.agent-provider` |
| Repository statistics panel | `desktop.repo-panel` |
| Developer diagnostics panel | `desktop.diagnostics-panel` |
| Git conformance toolkit | `cli.command` |
| Live sky and satellite data | `world.object`, `world.data-source` |

Each socket is neutral (no package IDs or provider names in host code), carries
explicit resource budgets, and has a defined teardown.

## Stays in core

Authentication, sessions, identity and keys; Git object parsing, refs and
clone/fetch/push correctness; mirror eligibility, signed health and clone
routing; issue, pull, review, merge and release record formats; permission
evaluation, audit and abuse policy; Marketplace signature verification,
installation and rollback; wallet and payout authority; agent sandboxing and
final approval of repository mutations; chat encryption and membership; World
renderer budgets.

## Before extracting a family

- A neutral socket and a permission list that is not "arbitrary code", "all
  network", "all repositories" or "all secrets".
- Install, activate, deactivate, uninstall, reinstall, upgrade, rollback and
  crash/restart tests.
- Package-owned settings, cache and data with tested export and purge.
- Resource budgets, cancellation, and a documented degraded state when the
  package or its provider is unavailable.

pages.title: ForkMesh protocol suite
pages.description: Suite version: 1.0.0-rc.1 · Status: candidate — not yet stable; see Stable release gate.
pages.markdown:
# ForkMesh protocol suite

Suite version: `1.0.0-rc.1` · Status: **candidate** — not yet stable; see
[Stable release gate](#stable-release-gate).

This suite is the normative description of ForkMesh wire behavior. An
independent implementation should be able to derive every identifier, produce
and verify every signature, and fold collaboration state from these documents
and their vectors without reading ForkMesh source. The hosted
[protocol reference](https://forkmesh.com/docs/protocol/) remains the
narrative guide to HTTP routes and deployment; where the two disagree, this
suite wins and the disagreement is a bug.

| Document | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| [Encoding and identifiers](encoding-and-identifiers.md) | Canonical JSON, base64url, canonical strings, repository/policy/object/event/refs/migration identifiers |
| [Signatures and authentication](signatures-and-authentication.md) | Strict Ed25519, domain separation, envelope verification order, request tokens, push authorization, portable sessions, catalog publication |
| [Relay, synchronization, and migration](relay-sync-and-migration.md) | Integrity-gated clone routing, NDJSON log exchange, deterministic folding, migration receipts, rollback |
| [Version negotiation](version-negotiation.md) | Version identifiers, rejection of unknown versions, downgrade resistance, rollout order |
| [Conflict-safe collaboration](../design/conflict-safe-collaboration.md) | Collaboration event families, fold rules, moderation lineage |
| [Threat model](threat-model.md) | Trust boundaries, attackers, threat register, release blockers |
| [Certification program](certification.md) | Profiles, adapter protocol, detection classes, expiring badges, independence, governance, appeals, trademark use; current badges in the [registry](certification-registry.md) |

## Conformance language

The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, and MAY are to be interpreted
as described in BCP 14 (RFC 2119, RFC 8174) when, and only when, they appear in
a numbered requirement. A requirement is written as a bold identifier followed
by its level, in the form `**FM-AREA-NNN** MUST`. Identifiers are never reused;
a withdrawn requirement keeps its number with the text "Withdrawn".

Everything outside a numbered requirement is informative.

## Suite requirements

- **FM-SUITE-001** MUST — The documents, schemas, vectors, and threat register
  of one suite version are released together. The manifest
  (`conformance/protocol/v1/manifest.json`) records the SHA-256 of each file
  and maps every requirement to its evidence. A verifier MUST reject the suite
  when any digest, version string, requirement identifier, requirement level,
  vector citation, or threat severity/status disagrees.
- **FM-SUITE-002** MUST — An implementation that claims a vector set passes
  every case in it: valid cases produce exactly the listed values, and invalid
  cases are rejected.
- **FM-SUITE-003** SHOULD — A rejection reports the listed error code.
  Validity is normative; codes are the stable vocabulary for audit telemetry
  and interop debugging. An implementation's known code deviations are
  recorded in the manifest (`codeDeviations`) and tested for exact equality,
  so a new deviation fails like any other inconsistency.

## Vectors

Vector files live in `conformance/protocol/v1/vectors/`:

| File | Content | Implementations passing it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `canonical-json.json` | Parse and encode cases, including every rejection class | reference Python, WebCrypto JavaScript, clean-room Python |
| `identifiers.json` | Repository, policy, object, refs-state, and migration identifiers | reference Python, clean-room Python; JavaScript for repository/policy/object |
| `signatures.json` | RFC 8032 and strictness cases, canonical-string schemes, push-message normalization, freshness windows | reference Python, clean-room Python |
| `events.json` | Signed collaboration envelopes and each verification failure | reference Python, WebCrypto JavaScript, clean-room Python |
| `fold.json` | Folded NDJSON logs with state digests and telemetry | reference Python, WebCrypto JavaScript |
| `sessions.json` | Portable session tokens | reference Python, clean-room Python |

Byte-exact inputs are given as `rawHex`; `rawText` is informative. Keys and
signatures come from deterministic test identities and MUST NOT be used
outside tests.

Run the suite:

```bash
python3 conformance/protocol/v1/verify_suite.py          # clean-room verifier + consistency
python3 conformance/protocol/v1/generate_vectors.py --check
python3 -m pytest -q app/tests/test_protocol_suite.py
```

`verify_suite.py` uses only the Python standard library and was written from
these documents. It does not yet fold collaboration logs, so `fold.json` is
evidenced by the two reference implementations only.

## Compatibility policy

Wire version identifiers and the suite version are separate:

- A **wire version identifier** (for example `forkmesh-collaboration-event-v1`
  or the `v1.` session-token prefix) names frozen bytes. Its meaning never
  changes; see [Version negotiation](version-negotiation.md).
- The **suite version** uses semantic versioning. A patch release fixes
  wording or adds vectors for existing behavior. A minor release adds
  requirements, vectors, or wire identifiers without changing what an existing
  conforming implementation accepts. A major release removes acceptance of a
  wire identifier; it is announced one minor release in advance and ships
  with a migration path.

## Change process

Changes are decided under the [governance charter](../governance/README.md).
Steps 1–5 are the technical part of a proposal record (`FMP-NNNN`). Review
windows, quorum, dissent, and appeals follow the charter.

1. Open an issue that names the requirement identifiers and threats affected.
2. Change the normative text, the reference implementations, and the
   generator expectations in one change. The generator compares every vector
   with an expectation written in `generate_vectors.py`, so a behavior change
   that is not also a documented expectation fails generation.
3. Update `threats.json` and the [threat model](threat-model.md) table
   together when a control or residual risk changes.
4. Regenerate: `python3 conformance/protocol/v1/generate_vectors.py`. This
   rewrites vectors and manifest digests; `--check` fails CI on anything stale.
5. Review requires one maintainer for informative or vector-only changes and a
   security reviewer for any requirement, wire identifier, or threat status
   change.

## Stable release gate

The suite may be marked `stable` only when no `critical` or `high` threat in
the register is `open`. Each must be `mitigated` by a numbered requirement or
`accepted` with a reviewer, date, and rationale. The verifier enforces this and
reports the current blockers as `stableReleaseBlockers`.

Before the umbrella epic can close, more evidence is needed:

- a clean-room collaboration fold;
- a second-language clean-room verifier;
- stock-Git clone interoperability against an independently written relay;
- the platform matrix.

The [certification program](certification.md) packages these vectors into
profiles any implementation can run through a language-neutral adapter. Its
closure gate is an independent implementation holding a current `core`
badge.

The [Git conformance suite](../operations/git-conformance.md) already covers
stock clients.
