pages.description: Program version: 1.0.0 · Protocol suite: 1.0.0-rc.1 · Part of the ForkMesh protocol suite · Current badges: certification registry
pages.markdown:
# Protocol certification program

Program version: `1.0.0` · Protocol suite: `1.0.0-rc.1` · Part of the
[ForkMesh protocol suite](README.md) · Current badges:
[certification registry](certification-registry.md)

Independent clients, relays, indexes and providers prove compatibility by
running the published suite through a small adapter and publishing the report.
A badge says exactly one thing: *this implementation, at this version, passed
every case of this profile, against these vectors, within the last 90 days, on
these platforms*. Badges are derived from retained reports only.

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `conformance/certification/v1/program.json` | Profiles, detection classes, performance budgets, freshness window, closure gate |
| `conformance/certification/v1/implementations.json` | Registered implementations, adapter commands, profiles, platforms, independence review |
| `conformance/certification/v1/evidence/<run>.json` | Retained reports, named by content address |
| `conformance/certification/v1/results.json` | Index of retained reports |
| `tools/protocol_certification.py` | Harness, attestation, badge derivation, generated outputs |

Generated, never hand-edited: [certification-registry.md](certification-registry.md),
`/docs/certification/badges.json`, `/docs/certification/evidence/<run>.json`.

## Profiles

| Profile | For | Vector groups | Must detect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `core` | clients, relays, indexes, providers | canonical JSON; identifiers; Ed25519 strictness, canonical strings, git-push messages, freshness; signed events; portable sessions | malformed signatures, divergence, downgrade, replay, data loss, incompatible versions |
| `collaboration-fold` | clients and relays that fold collaboration logs | canonical JSON; identifiers; signed events; log folding | malformed signatures, divergence, replay, data loss, incompatible versions |

Every case is positive (exact value) or negative (rejected). Detection classes:

| Class | A failing implementation … |
| --- | --- |
| `malformed-signature` | accepts a non-canonical scalar, small-order key, tampered payload or alternate signature spelling |
| `divergence` | derives a different identifier or folded state from the same input |
| `downgrade` | verifies under an older version or another scheme |
| `replay` | accepts a stale request, expired or future session, or re-applies a redelivered event |
| `data-loss` | drops a ref, rounds an integer or discards a pending or rejected record |
| `incompatible-version` | parses an unknown or future version instead of rejecting it |

The clean-room adapter's `--fault` modes break one property at a time, and the
tests require each fault to fail its class. Each case must answer within
2,000 ms and a profile within 120 s. A rejection with a different stable error
code still passes and is recorded as a code deviation (FM-SUITE-003).

## Adapter protocol

`forkmesh-conformance-adapter-v1` is newline-delimited JSON over the adapter's
stdin and stdout, run from the repository root.

1. Harness: `{"type":"hello","protocol":"forkmesh-conformance-adapter-v1","suite":"forkmesh-protocol","suiteVersion":"1.0.0-rc.1"}`.
2. Adapter: `{"type":"hello","protocol":"forkmesh-conformance-adapter-v1","implementation":{"name":"…","version":"…"},"suiteVersions":["1.0.0-rc.1"]}`.
   A protocol or suite-version mismatch records the run as `incompatible`.
3. Per case, harness: `{"type":"case","id":"<set>:<case>","operation":"…","input":{…}}`;
   adapter: `{"id":"…","valid":true,"value":…}`,
   `{"id":"…","valid":false,"error":"<code>"}` or `{"id":"…","unsupported":true}`.

A missing, late or mismatched response fails the case; an adapter that exits
or hangs fails every remaining case, and a report is still produced.

| Operation | Input | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `canonical.parse` | `rawHex` | ignored |
| `canonical.encode` | `value` | canonical text |
| `identifier.repository` | `verifiedRoot` | repository identifier |
| `identifier.policy` | `policy` | policy identifier |
| `identifier.object` | `repository`, `family`, `creator`, `objectKey`, `references` | object identifier |
| `identifier.refs-state` | `advertisementHex` | `{"canonicalText","stateHash"}` |
| `identifier.migration` | `operation` and fields | identifier or hash |
| `signature.ed25519` | `publicKeyHex`, `messageHex`, `signatureHex` | ignored |
| `signature.canonical-string` | `messageText`, `publicKey`, `signature`, optional `scheme`/`fields`, `catalogV2Record` | ignored |
| `signature.git-push-message` | `owner`, `repo`, `method`, `ts`, `bodySha256` | message text |
| `request.freshness` | `ts`, `nowMs` | ignored |
| `event.verify` | `rawHex`, `policy`, `context` | event identifier |
| `session.parse` | `token`, `nowMs`, `routerPublicKey` | claim object |
| `log.fold` | `ndjson`, `policy` | `{"stateDigest","telemetry","rejectionReasons"}` |

Working adapters in Python and JavaScript are in
`conformance/certification/v1/adapters/`.

## Running and publishing

```sh
python3 tools/protocol_certification.py run --profile core \
  --implementation acme-relay --command "cargo run --release --bin fm-adapter" \
  --output artifacts/acme-relay-core.json
python3 tools/protocol_certification.py attest artifacts/*.json
python3 tools/protocol_certification.py validate
python3 tools/protocol_certification.py render --check
python3 tools/protocol_certification.py gate
```

`attest` retains passing and failing reports, and rejects reports that do not
match the registered implementation, profile, platform or adapter command, that
disagree with their own cases, trim the case list, or contain local paths or
loopback addresses. The newest report per implementation, profile and platform
wins. `gate` runs in the quality gates: it validates everything, checks
generated outputs and re-runs every in-repository adapter.

## Badges

A badge covers one implementation, one profile, and the platforms registered
for it. Each report binds the program version, a profile digest, the suite
version and every vector file's digest.

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `revoked` | Withdrawn by a recorded governance decision |
| `unverified` | No retained run on some listed platform |
| `failing` | The newest run on some platform failed |
| `expired` | Vectors, suite, program or profile changed, or the oldest run is older than 90 days |
| `certified` | Every listed platform passed against the current suite within 90 days |

The hosted SVG at `/docs/certification/badges/<implementation>/<profile>.svg`
checks expiry on every request, and
`/docs/certification/badges/<implementation>/<profile>` redirects to the
evidence. A badge may be cited as "passes the ForkMesh `<profile>` profile,
suite `<version>`" only while it is `certified` and only with the hosted image.

## Independence and governance

The program's closure gate needs a non-ForkMesh implementation with a current
`core` badge: source public outside ForkMesh repositories, written from the
documents and vectors without copying ForkMesh source, and reviewed by someone
who does not maintain it (recorded in the registry's `independence` block).
In-repository implementations are `independent: false`.

Decisions follow the [governance charter](../governance/README.md) and are
recorded in the [decision register](../governance/decision-register.md).
Registration is a pull request adding a registry entry and an attested report,
rerun by a reviewer who does not work on that implementation. Program changes
follow the suite's [change process](README.md#change-process): narrowing a
profile is a major version, adding cases is a minor version that expires
existing badges. Disputed vectors are fixed through the change process with no
per-implementation exemptions; refusals and revocations can be appealed within
30 days. A badge is revoked when its evidence cannot be reproduced, its
independence statement is false, or it is used outside its scope.

New cases, especially adversarial and version-skew inputs, are added to
`conformance/protocol/v1/generate_vectors.py` and listed under their class in
`program.json`.

# Encoding and identifiers

Suite version: `1.0.0-rc.1` · Vectors: `canonical-json.json`,
`identifiers.json` · Part of the [ForkMesh protocol suite](README.md)

## Canonical JSON

ForkMesh hashes and signs a deliberately small JSON subset. It is chosen so
that Python `json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True,
separators=(",", ":"))` and ECMAScript `JSON.stringify` with sorted keys emit
identical bytes for every admitted value.

- **FM-ENC-001** MUST — A canonical document is UTF-8 without a byte-order
  mark, without insignificant whitespace, and without a trailing newline. A
  signed document's top level is an object. Object keys match
  `^[A-Za-z0-9_.:/-]{1,256}$` and appear in ascending code-point order.
- **FM-ENC-002** MUST — Values are objects, arrays, strings, `true`, `false`,
  `null`, or integers whose magnitude is at most 2^53−1. Integers are written
  in shortest decimal form: no fraction, exponent, leading zero, or negative
  zero. `NaN` and infinities are not JSON and are rejected. Individual fields
  can narrow the range further; envelope counters, for example, are
  non-negative.
- **FM-ENC-003** MUST — Strings are Unicode NFC and contain no unpaired
  surrogate. An encoder normalizes strings to NFC before hashing. Within a
  string, `"` and `\` are written `\"` and `\\`; U+0008, U+000C, U+000A,
  U+000D, and U+0009 use `\b \f \n \r \t`; all other code points below U+0020
  use `\u00XX` with lowercase hex. Every other code point, including U+007F,
  U+2028, U+2029, `/`, and characters outside the BMP, is written literally.
- **FM-ENC-004** MUST — A receiver parses with duplicate-key detection,
  re-encodes the parsed value under FM-ENC-001..003, and rejects the input
  unless the result is byte-for-byte identical. An alternate spelling of the
  same value — whitespace, escapes, key order, or a non-NFC string — is a
  different, invalid input, not an equivalent one.
- **FM-ENC-005** MUST — A signed document is at most 1 MiB (1,048,576 bytes)
  and non-empty. Nesting depth is at most 32, counting the top-level object as
  depth 0 and each nested array or object as one more.

Some integrity receipts use variants that differ from signed collaboration
documents. The portable session claim (FM-AUTH-003) and the catalog v2 record
hash (FM-AUTH-004) serialize with ASCII escaping: every code point above
U+007E is written as lowercase `\uXXXX`, using surrogate pairs outside the
BMP. Migration state receipts (FM-ID-006) use the literal form without NFC
normalization. Each variant is pinned by vectors.

Rejection codes, in the order a parser meets them: `invalid_event_size`,
`invalid_json`, `invalid_number`, `floating_point_forbidden`, `duplicate_key`,
`event_not_object`, `json_too_deep`, `invalid_key`, `unsafe_integer`,
`invalid_unicode`, `noncanonical_encoding`.

## Binary encodings

- **FM-ENC-006** MUST — Keys, signatures, and object keys are base64url
  (RFC 4648 §5) without padding. A decoder rejects padding, characters outside
  the alphabet, the wrong decoded length, and any spelling that does not
  re-encode identically. The last check catches non-zero unused trailing bits:
  two textual signatures for the same bytes would otherwise produce two
  distinct envelopes. Ed25519 public keys decode to 32 bytes, signatures to
  64, and collaboration object keys to 16.

Digest identifiers are written `sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hex digits,
except where a field is specified as bare hex.

## Canonical strings

Older signed actions sign newline-joined strings rather than JSON.

- **FM-ENC-007** MUST — A canonical string is the UTF-8 encoding of a frozen
  scheme prefix `forkmesh-<scheme>-v<N>`, then each field in the order the
  scheme lists, joined by a single LF (0x0A) with no trailing LF. Timestamps
  are decimal milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Senders write them without
  sign or leading zeros; verifiers sign-check the field text exactly as
  transmitted. Variable-length content is bound as a lowercase hex SHA-256
  field, never inline.

The scheme field lists live in [Signatures and
authentication](signatures-and-authentication.md#canonical-string-schemes).

## Identifiers

- **FM-ID-001** MUST — A repository identity is
  `urn:forkmesh:repository:sha256:` followed by
  `hex(SHA-256("forkmesh-repository-identity-v1\n" || NFC(verified root)))`.
  The verified root is established out of band, for example by a signed
  repository manifest. Display names, organization aliases, and URLs are
  routing hints, never identities.
- **FM-ID-002** MUST — A collaboration policy document has exactly the keys
  `schema` (`forkmesh-collaboration-policy-v1`), `repository`, `maintainers`,
  `moderators`, and `notifiers`. Each role is a sorted, duplicate-free list of
  32-byte base64url Ed25519 keys. Its identity is
  `sha256:` + `hex(SHA-256(canonical JSON))`, with no domain prefix because
  the schema value is inside the hashed bytes. A document that is not already
  in this form is rejected, never repaired.
- **FM-ID-003** MUST — A collaboration object identity is
  `urn:forkmesh:collaboration:<family>:sha256:` followed by
  `hex(SHA-256("forkmesh-collaboration-object-v1\n" || canonical JSON of
  {repository, family, creator, objectKey, references}))`. `references` is
  the validated, sorted list of `{relation, family, object}` triples that the
  object's first event carries.
- **FM-ID-004** MUST — A collaboration event identity is
  `sha256:` + `hex(SHA-256(signingBytes || 0x00 || rawSignature))`. Here
  `signingBytes` is defined by FM-SIG-003 and `rawSignature` is the 64 decoded
  signature bytes. A receiver recomputes it and rejects a mismatch
  (`event_id_mismatch`).
- **FM-ID-005** MUST — A repository state digest is taken over the refs a node
  serves. From a protocol-v0 `upload-pack --advertise-refs` pkt-line stream,
  keep only `refs/heads/*` and `refs/tags/*`. Drop `HEAD`, peeled `^{}` lines,
  and every other namespace, including `refs/pull/` and `refs/forkmesh/`.
  Strip capabilities after the first NUL, and sort by refname in byte order.
  The canonical text joins `<object-id> <refname>` lines with LF and has no
  trailing LF. `stateHash` is its lowercase hex SHA-256; an empty
  advertisement hashes the empty string.
- **FM-ID-006** MUST — Migration identifiers are domain-separated SHA-256 over
  LF-joined parts: `hex(SHA-256(domain || "\n" || join("\n", parts)))`.
  A job is `mig_` followed by the first 24 hex digits for the domain
  `forkmesh-migration-job-v1`. An object key uses
  `forkmesh-migration-object-v1` with parts object type and source id. A
  state receipt is `sha256:` + hex SHA-256 of the literal-form canonical JSON
  (see above) of the state document.

pages.markdown:
# Relay, synchronization, and migration

Suite version: `1.0.0-rc.1` · Vectors: `fold.json`, `identifiers.json` ·
Part of the [ForkMesh protocol suite](README.md)

## Roles

- A **source of truth** is a node holding the owner's working repository. It
  signs catalog records and `forkmesh-repostate-v1` attestations.
- A **mirror** is an independently operated HTTPS origin serving a copy. Its
  own attestations prove what it serves, not what the owner published.
- The **relay** (mainnode) routes reads to mirrors, verifies signed
  submissions, and indexes metadata. It never stores repository bytes and is
  never authoritative for collaboration meaning.

## Clone and fetch routing

- **FM-REL-001** MUST — A relay serves a public clone or fetch only from a
  mirror that passes three checks. The mirror has a fresh signed health
  result. Its live advertised refs hash (FM-ID-005) to a state that a source
  of truth in the repository's logical group attested with
  `forkmesh-repostate-v1`. Mirrors are grouped by root commit, falling back to
  name. A source is checked against its current pin plus bounded recent
  history. A mirror's self-attestation never activates a repository. When the
  group has no source-signed pin, routing fails closed.
- **FM-REL-002** MUST — The two requests of a smart-HTTP clone (`info/refs`,
  then `git-upload-pack`) reach the same accepted origin. A relay may retry
  another integrity-matching origin only before any response byte is sent. It
  never splices responses from different origins and never rewrites pack
  data.
- **FM-REL-003** MUST — Receive-pack is refused before any request body is
  read unless FM-AUTH-002 authorizes the request. Both upload-pack and
  receive-pack hide the `refs/forkmesh/` namespace, which holds merge
  anchors and staging refs, and reject wants for object ids that no
  advertised ref reaches.

Protocol negotiation inside Git (protocol v0 or v2) is left to stock Git
clients and servers. The refs digest is always computed from a protocol-v0
advertisement generated for attestation.

## Collaboration log exchange

- **FM-SYNC-001** MUST — A collaboration log is exchanged as one canonical
  envelope per line, separated by LF. A reader splits only on LF and retains
  a stray CR in the record, where it fails as `noncanonical_encoding` rather
  than being normalized into a valid envelope. An importer verifies every
  record and recomputes state; it never trusts an exported snapshot. Export
  sorts unique raw records by SHA-256 of their bytes.
- **FM-SYNC-002** MUST — Folding is a pure function of the policy and the set
  of unique raw records. Permutation, duplication, and delay never change the
  result. The state digest is `sha256:` + hex SHA-256 of the canonical JSON
  state document (`forkmesh-collaboration-state-v1`). Duplicate deliveries are
  counted, not re-applied.
- **FM-SYNC-003** MUST — Beyond FM-SIG-004, a fold enforces six rules:
  - An event whose parents are not all present stays **pending**, with its
    raw bytes retained.
  - A descendant of a rejected event is rejected.
  - The Lamport `clock` is 0 without parents and otherwise one more than the
    greatest parent clock.
  - Two different events signed by one key in the same `sequence` slot are
    **equivocation**; both are excluded and counted.
  - Role authorization follows the pinned policy. Unauthorized events are
    audited but never folded.
  - Concurrent differing scalar writes produce an explicit conflict rather
    than a winner chosen by time, author, or arrival order.

  The complete family rules are normative in
  [Conflict-safe collaboration](../design/conflict-safe-collaboration.md).

A fold over an incomplete set cannot detect omission. A relay that withholds
events is an open threat (TM-008), not a property this suite guarantees.

## Migration and rollback

- **FM-MIG-001** MUST — A repository migration state receipt (FM-ID-006)
  excludes run timestamps, attempt counters, and credentials. Re-running an
  import over unchanged provider data yields the same receipt, and source
  deletions are pruned, not retained as stale objects.
- **FM-MIG-002** MUST — Each legacy collaboration record migrates through an
  importer-signed `create` or `decide` event. That event binds the exact
  legacy record digest and records whether the legacy signature is `valid`,
  `invalid`, or `unavailable`. It never presents the importer's signature as
  the legacy author's. The original bytes are kept alongside the new log.
- **FM-MIG-003** MUST — Rollback proceeds in a fixed order: stop writers
  emitting the newer version first, then roll back readers. Readers keep
  accepting and preserving newer raw envelopes they already hold. No
  implementation down-converts or deletes signed events, because that loses
  causality. Recovery restores policy and NDJSON, re-verifies, and compares
  state digests; corrupt lines stay quarantined while valid objects keep
  folding.

# Signatures and authentication

Suite version: `1.0.0-rc.1` · Vectors: `signatures.json`, `events.json`,
`sessions.json` · Part of the [ForkMesh protocol suite](README.md)

## Ed25519

- **FM-SIG-001** MUST — Signatures are Ed25519 (RFC 8032, PureEdDSA, no
  context) verified with the cofactorless equation `[S]B = R + [k]A`, where
  `k = SHA-512(R || A || M) mod L`. A verifier rejects:
  - a signature that is not exactly 64 bytes;
  - a scalar `S ≥ L`, so no `S + L` malleability;
  - a point encoding with `y ≥ p`, no square root, or `x = 0` with the sign
    bit set;
  - the identity as the public key;
  - any public key outside the prime-order subgroup (`[L]A ≠ identity`), which
    excludes all small-order and mixed-order keys.

Implementations that wrap a platform verifier (for example WebCrypto) MUST add
the checks their platform omits.

## Domain separation

- **FM-SIG-002** MUST — Every signed message begins with a frozen,
  scheme-specific prefix, and a verifier builds the message itself from the
  fields it will act on. A client-supplied message is never accepted. A
  signature valid under one prefix therefore never verifies under another
  scheme, another version, or a substituted field such as a different HTTP
  method.

### Canonical-string schemes

These follow FM-ENC-007. The fields below come after the prefix line.

| Prefix | Fields | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `forkmesh-catalog-v1` | owner, name, updatedAt | relay, catalog publish (public records only) |
| `forkmesh-catalog-v2` | recordSha256 | relay, catalog publish |
| `forkmesh-repostate-v1` | owner, repo, stateHash (FM-ID-005), updatedAt | relay, catalog publish and mirror attestations |
| `forkmesh-private-manifest-v1` | owner, name, opaqueRepoId, keyEpoch, manifestHash, updatedAt | relay, private catalog publish |
| `forkmesh-view-v1` | owner, repo, ts | relay, private browse and clone |
| `forkmesh-rotate-v1` | oldPubkey, newPubkey, ts | relay, account key rotation (signed by the old key) |
| `forkmesh-git-push-v1` | owner, repo, method, ts, bodySha256 | relay and mirror gateway, HTTPS receive-pack |

For `forkmesh-catalog-v2`, `recordSha256` is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the
normalized catalog record minus its descriptive `signature` field. The record
is serialized with sorted keys, no whitespace, and ASCII escaping. The
[published protocol reference](https://forkmesh.com/docs/protocol/#signature-schemes)
lists the remaining legacy schemes (issue, discussion, pull, release, room,
node link). Their field layout is informative until they receive vectors; see
TM-004 in the [threat model](threat-model.md).

## Collaboration envelopes

- **FM-SIG-003** MUST — A collaboration event's signing bytes are
  `"forkmesh-collaboration-event-v1\n"` followed by the canonical JSON of the
  unsigned envelope. The unsigned envelope is the event without `signature`
  and `eventId`, with exactly the keys `schema`, `repository`, `policy`,
  `family`, `object`, `action`, `author`, `sequence`, `clock`, `issuedAt`,
  `parents`, `references`, and `payload`. The author's key signs those bytes.
- **FM-SIG-004** MUST — A receiver rejects an event at the first failing step
  and never lets it influence causality, authorization, or state:
  1. size and canonical parse (FM-ENC-004, FM-ENC-005);
  2. exact key set (`invalid_envelope_keys`), then schema identifier
     (`unsupported_schema`);
  3. field shapes: repository URN, policy digest, known family and action,
     object URN of that family, author and signature encodings, non-negative
     safe integers, sorted duplicate-free `parents` (at most 64), references,
     and payload structure;
  4. event identity (`event_id_mismatch`, FM-ID-004);
  5. for `create` and `decide`, object identity (`object_id_mismatch`,
     FM-ID-003);
  6. repository binding (`wrong_repository`) and policy binding
     (`unknown_policy`) against the pinned policy;
  7. the Ed25519 signature (`invalid_signature`).

  Binding is checked before the signature. A replay into another repository
  is therefore classified as a replay even when its signature is also invalid.

Causality, sequence, equivocation, and authorization rules follow in
[Relay, synchronization, and migration](relay-sync-and-migration.md#collaboration-log-exchange).

## Request authentication

- **FM-AUTH-001** MUST — A time-bound request proof (`view`, `rotate`, and
  `git-push` schemes) is accepted only when its timestamp field is within
  300,000 ms of the verifier's clock in either direction, inclusive. Senders
  write the timestamp as ASCII decimal digits. A verifier rejects a timestamp
  that is not a base-10 integer, and it signs-checks the field text as sent
  (FM-ENC-007). The window limits replay but does not prevent it; see TM-012.
- **FM-AUTH-002** MUST — An HTTPS push is authorized by a signature over
  `forkmesh-git-push-v1`. Before signing and verifying, the owner is trimmed and
  lowercased, the repository trimmed, the method trimmed and uppercased, and
  the body digest trimmed and lowercased. Anything else is rejected: an owner
  that is not a valid account name, a repository that is not a single safe
  path segment, a method other than `GET` or `POST`, a timestamp that is not
  1–16 digits, or a body digest that is not 64 hex digits. The ref
  advertisement `GET` signs the digest of the empty body. When the relay
  streams a pack it has not buffered, it forwards the signed digest, and the
  gateway MUST check the received bytes against it before running
  receive-pack.
- **FM-AUTH-003** MUST — A portable session token is
  `v1.<claim>.<signature>`. `<claim>` is 80–1024 base64url characters of
  ASCII-escaped canonical JSON. `<signature>` is 86 characters and signs
  `"forkmesh-portable-session-v1\n" || <claim>` with the router key. The claim
  has exactly the keys:
  - `type` = `forkmesh.portable-session`;
  - `aud` = `forkmesh-mirror-dashboard`;
  - `v` = 1;
  - integer `iat` and `exp`;
  - `sub`: 32–128 lowercase hex;
  - `name`: an account name;
  - `sid` and `jti`: opaque 16–128 base64url-alphabet strings.

  A verifier rejects, in order: framing (`token_invalid`), encodings
  (`encoding_invalid`), claim shape (`claim_invalid`), time (`not_current`:
  `iat ≤ 0`, `exp ≤ iat`, lifetime over 12 hours, `iat` more than 60 s ahead,
  or `exp` more than 60 s past), a non-canonical claim
  (`claim_noncanonical`), and the signature (`signature_invalid`).
- **FM-AUTH-004** MUST — A catalog publication is signed by a key registered
  to the owner account.
  - When `catalogSigVersion` is 2, `catalogSig` MUST verify
    `forkmesh-catalog-v2`.
  - Otherwise it MUST verify `forkmesh-catalog-v1`, and only for a record
    whose visibility is `public`. Any other visibility is refused with HTTP 426
    `client_upgrade_required` and `requiredCatalogSigVersion: 2` before any
    confidential field is stored.
  - A present `stateSig` MUST verify `forkmesh-repostate-v1`, and a present but
    invalid attestation rejects the whole write.
  - A record whose `updatedAt` is older than the stored record is rejected as
    a rollback.

Inbox submissions (issues, pulls, discussions) prove only that a record was
not altered after signing. They carry no authority. The repository owner's
review and push is the authorization step.

pages.title: Threat model
pages.description: Suite version: 1.0.0-rc.1 · Register: conformance/protocol/v1/threats.json · Part of the ForkMesh protocol suite
pages.markdown:
# Threat model

Suite version: `1.0.0-rc.1` · Register: `conformance/protocol/v1/threats.json`
· Part of the [ForkMesh protocol suite](README.md)

This model covers the wire protocol in this suite. Endpoint compromise,
Cloudflare platform compromise, and supply-chain attacks against clients
belong to [SECURITY.md](../../../SECURITY.md) and the [dependency
audit](../security/dependency-security-audit.md). The register file is
authoritative. The table below MUST match its severity and status, and the
suite verifier fails if they differ.

## Assets

- Private keys: device, account, router, and importer keys.
- Repository history and the integrity of refs.
- Signed collaboration history: issues, pulls, reviews, moderation.
- Private repository names, contents, and collaborator lists.
- Session and request authorizations.
- Availability of clone and collaboration flows.

## Trust boundaries

| ID | Boundary |
| --- | --- |
| B1 | Client device and its key store |
| B2 | Client ↔ relay (Worker HTTPS and WebSocket) |
| B3 | Relay ↔ mirror origin |
| B4 | Mirror ↔ source-of-truth node |
| B5 | Relay storage (D1, Durable Objects, KV) |
| B6 | External provider ↔ migration importer |
| B7 | Portable session ↔ independent mirror dashboard |

## Attacker capabilities

| ID | Attacker | Can | Cannot (assumed) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | Network attacker | Observe timing and sizes; drop or delay traffic | Break TLS 1.2+ or Ed25519/SHA-256 |
| A2 | Malicious or compromised relay operator | Read and rewrite anything the relay receives; withhold, reorder, or replay messages; read relay-layer room traffic | Forge user signatures |
| A3 | Malicious mirror operator | Serve any bytes; lie in its own attestations; log requests | Forge a source-of-truth attestation |
| A4 | Malicious registered user | Sign any content with its own keys; equivocate; craft malformed input | Sign with another user's key |
| A5 | Holder of a stolen device key | Everything that key authorizes until rotation or revocation | Use the account password or TOTP |
| A6 | Malicious migration provider | Return inconsistent, oversized, or hostile API data | Access ForkMesh keys |
| A7 | Resource-exhaustion attacker | Send many or large requests within platform limits | Exceed Cloudflare edge limits |

## Register

| ID | Threat | Boundaries | Attackers | Severity | Status | Controls |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TM-001 | Forged authorship of signed objects | B2, B5 | A2, A4 | high | mitigated | FM-SIG-001, FM-SIG-003, FM-SIG-004 |
| TM-002 | Signature or encoding malleability that aliases event identities | B2 | A2, A4 | high | mitigated | FM-SIG-001, FM-ENC-004, FM-ENC-006, FM-ID-004 |
| TM-003 | Replay of collaboration events into another repository or policy epoch | B2, B5 | A2, A4 | high | mitigated | FM-ID-003, FM-SIG-004 |
| TM-004 | Replay of legacy issue/discussion/pull records whose canonical strings omit owner and repository | B2 | A2, A4 | high | open | FM-SIG-002, FM-MIG-002 |
| TM-005 | Cross-scheme or cross-version signature confusion | B2 | A2 | high | mitigated | FM-SIG-002, FM-VER-001, FM-VER-002 |
| TM-006 | Catalog v1 signatures, which do not bind visibility or descriptive fields, replayed for public records | B2, B5 | A2 | high | open | FM-AUTH-004, FM-VER-002 |
| TM-007 | Tampered or rolled-back history served to cloners | B3, B4 | A3 | high | mitigated | FM-REL-001, FM-REL-002, FM-ID-005 |
| TM-008 | Relay or mirror withholds collaboration events | B2, B3 | A2, A3 | high | open | FM-SYNC-003 |
| TM-009 | Signing-key equivocation | B2 | A4, A5 | high | mitigated | FM-SYNC-003 |
| TM-010 | Clock or timestamp manipulation to win conflicts or extend tokens | B2 | A4 | medium | mitigated | FM-SYNC-002, FM-SYNC-003, FM-AUTH-001, FM-AUTH-003 |
| TM-011 | Unauthorized moderation or role escalation | B2, B5 | A4 | high | mitigated | FM-ID-002, FM-SYNC-003 |
| TM-012 | Replay of view, rotate, or push proofs within the freshness window | B2 | A1, A2 | medium | open | FM-AUTH-001, FM-AUTH-002 |
| TM-013 | Theft and replay of portable session bearer tokens | B7 | A1, A3 | medium | open | FM-AUTH-003 |
| TM-014 | Tunnelled node traffic trusts the relay as an authenticated intermediary | B2, B3 | A2 | high | open | FM-SIG-002 |
| TM-015 | Relay operator reads the outer room layer, including public channel plaintext and presence | B2, B5 | A2 | medium | open | FM-SIG-002 |
| TM-016 | Metadata leakage through the catalog, presence, routing, and timing | B2, B5 | A1, A2 | medium | open | FM-REL-001 |
| TM-017 | Parser, verifier, or fold resource exhaustion | B2 | A7, A4 | medium | mitigated | FM-ENC-005, FM-SIG-004 |
| TM-018 | Account key compromise or loss without a specified recovery protocol | B1 | A5 | high | open | FM-AUTH-004 |
| TM-019 | Data loss through lossy migration, down-conversion, or snapshot trust | B5, B6 | A2, A6 | high | mitigated | FM-MIG-001, FM-MIG-002, FM-MIG-003, FM-SYNC-001 |
| TM-020 | Substituting the pack body of an authorized HTTPS push | B2, B3 | A2 | high | mitigated | FM-AUTH-002, FM-REL-003 |

Open high-severity threats — TM-004, TM-006, TM-008, TM-014, and TM-018 — block
a stable suite release until they are mitigated or explicitly accepted.

## Discussion by class

**Replay.** Collaboration v1 binds repository, object, and policy inside the
signed bytes (TM-003). The legacy `forkmesh-issue-event-v1` family binds only
type, number, author, timestamp, and a content hash. The same signed record can
therefore be presented to another repository that has a matching issue number
(TM-004). The mitigation path is FM-MIG-002 migration to collaboration v1 plus
a relay rule that stops accepting legacy inbox records after the migration
window. Request proofs carry no nonce, so capture inside the five-minute window
permits replay (TM-012). Push proofs bind the method and body digest, so a
replay can only resubmit the identical pack.

**Downgrade.** Exact identifier matching and distinct prefixes defeat
cross-version confusion (TM-005). `forkmesh-catalog-v1` is still accepted for
public records. Descriptive fields and visibility are not signed under v1, and
the rollback check permits an equal `updatedAt`. A relay-level replayer could
therefore reissue an old public record (TM-006). Removing v1 acceptance is a
major suite change (see the compatibility policy).

**Equivocation.** A key signing two events in one sequence slot loses both
(TM-009). Detection needs both events in the same fold, so equivocation hidden
by withholding reduces to TM-008.

**Omission and availability.** No fold detects missing events (TM-008).
Closing it requires availability receipts or peer exchange that cross-checks
relay-delivered logs. Clone availability degrades to fail-closed, never to
unverified bytes (TM-007).

**Metadata leakage.** The relay learns public repository names, sizes, node
versions, presence, and request timing (TM-016). Private repository names never
enter the public routing index; private reads use opaque handles and ciphertext
([private repository
confidentiality](../security/private-repository-confidentiality.md)). By
design, default rooms use a relay-derivable key; private channels add a
recipient layer (TM-015, [sealed chat](../security/sealed-chat.md)). Telemetry
exports counts only.

**Abuse.** Size and depth limits bound parsing (TM-017). Verification caches
key on fixed-size digests. Catalog publication is rate-limited per owner.
Inbox signatures prove integrity, not reputation, and owner review gates every
merge.

**Recovery and data loss.** Signed raw bytes are the source of truth, and
snapshots are disposable (TM-019). Account key rotation requires the old key
(`forkmesh-rotate-v1`). Recovering from a lost or stolen key currently relies
on account credentials and the procedures in [portable
identities](../portable-identities.md). There is no normative, independently
verifiable recovery protocol yet (TM-018).

## Review

A security reviewer changes a threat's status only by editing `threats.json`
and this table together. The reviewer cites the requirement or test that closes
it, or records `acceptance` with reviewer, date, and rationale. The 2026-07
security audit is the origin of TM-004 and TM-014. This register does not
record any acceptance until a named reviewer signs one.

pages.title: Version negotiation
pages.description: Suite version: 1.0.0-rc.1 · Vectors: events.json, identifiers.json, signatures.json, sessions.json · Part of the ForkMesh protocol suite
pages.markdown:
# Version negotiation

Suite version: `1.0.0-rc.1` · Vectors: `events.json`, `identifiers.json`,
`signatures.json`, `sessions.json` · Part of the [ForkMesh protocol
suite](README.md)

ForkMesh has no interactive handshake. Every signed or hashed structure
carries an explicit version identifier, and each receiver selects exactly one
verifier from it:

| Structure | Identifier | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Collaboration event | `forkmesh-collaboration-event-v1` | `schema` field and signing domain |
| Collaboration policy | `forkmesh-collaboration-policy-v1` | `schema` field |
| Collaboration state | `forkmesh-collaboration-state-v1` | `schema` field |
| Canonical-string schemes | `forkmesh-<scheme>-v<N>` | first line of the signed message |
| Catalog publication | `catalogSigVersion` 1 or 2 | request field; selects the scheme |
| Portable session | `v1.` token prefix and claim `v: 1` | token framing and claim |
| Repository migration | `forkmesh-repository-migration-v1`, `forkmesh-repository-migration-state-v1` | job and receipt `schema` |
| Room key proof | `forkmesh-room-key-v2` (v1 only for the compatibility room) | first line of the signed message |

The only advertised negotiation is the catalog upgrade response: HTTP 426
with `{"error": "client_upgrade_required", "requiredCatalogSigVersion": 2}`.
Git protocol v0/v2 negotiation belongs to stock Git.

- **FM-VER-001** MUST — Receivers match version identifiers exactly. They
  reject an unknown or future identifier with the structure's stable code
  (`unsupported_schema`, `invalid_policy`, `token_invalid`, `claim_invalid`),
  never parse it heuristically, and never ignore unknown fields in a signed
  structure.
- **FM-VER-002** MUST NOT — A receiver MUST NOT downgrade. A message that
  fails verification under its declared version is never retried under an
  older version's rules. An older version stays accepted only within its
  published scope: `forkmesh-catalog-v1` only for public records, and
  `forkmesh-room-key-v1` only for the public compatibility room. Because
  prefixes differ, a signature over one version never verifies as another.
- **FM-VER-003** MUST — The bytes an identifier covers are frozen. Any change
  to signed or hashed bytes, field order, normalization, or meaning requires a
  new identifier, and the committed vectors for the existing identifier stay
  unchanged.
- **FM-VER-004** MUST — A new identifier rolls out in a fixed order. First,
  readers that verify and preserve the new identifier deploy. Then writers
  begin emitting it. Readers keep accepting the previous identifier for as
  long as retained history contains it. Rollback reverses the order
  (FM-MIG-003).

pages.title: Relay data retention and deletion
pages.description: What the hosted relay behind forkmesh.com, app.forkmesh.com and world.forkmesh.com stores, how long, and what deletes it. Git objects in repositories published from desktops and…
pages.markdown:
# Relay data retention and deletion

What the hosted relay behind `forkmesh.com`, `app.forkmesh.com` and
`world.forkmesh.com` stores, how long, and what deletes it. Git objects in
repositories published from desktops and mirror nodes are not relay data and
the relay cannot delete them. "Until deleted" means no automatic limit;
**missing proof** marks a gap.

## Where the relay runs

The application code (`app/src/`) runs under `app/host/` on self-hosted core
nodes (`deploy/fleet.toml`). `app/wrangler.toml` still declares the bindings;
`app/host/forkmesh_host/env.py` maps each to a local implementation. The apex
site is fronted by an edge proxy that forwards visitor IP and country in a
signed header.

## Live stores

| Store | Holds | Retention / deletion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| rqlite database (`DB`) | Accounts, catalog, inboxes, chat backlog, status, analytics, memberships, package data, durable-object storage; full copy on every core node | Per table below |
| KV `REPOSITORY_METADATA` | Cached repository-page JSON per node, not replicated or backed up | No expiry, no delete (**missing proof**) |
| `ForkMeshRoom`, `ForkMeshNoteRoom`, `ForkMeshWorld`, `ForkMeshOfficeRoom` | Sockets and live presence in memory | Socket lifetime |
| `ForkMeshNodes`, `ForkMeshCronWatchdog`, `ForkMeshCronRunner`, `ForkMeshDiscordGate` | Push sockets, commit targets, cron progress, rate buckets (`do_storage`, `do_alarms`) | Overwritten or expired |
| Queue `forkmesh-notification-email` | Wake-up naming a recipient, in memory | Until delivered (3 retries) |
| Response cache | Public responses, ≤ 8 MiB per node | `Cache-Control` lifetime |
| Hosted Git repositories | Full copy per node | Removal moves to `.trash`; emptied by hand only |

## Database tables (rqlite)

| Data family | Retention | Deletion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accounts, devices, SSH keys, encryption keys | Until deleted; stale devices 60 days | Account delete |
| Sessions | Expired and revoked sessions pruned on login | Sign out; account delete |
| Repository catalog, health, inboxes, webhooks, provider mirrors, Internet Archive backups | Until deleted; outboxes until delivered or retries exhausted | Repository or account delete |
| Chat backlog (encrypted) | 7 days, ≤ 500 messages and 16 MiB per room; DMs removed on recipient ack | Sweep; message, room or account delete |
| Notifications | 90 days, ≤ 500 per recipient | Account delete |
| Email delivery records | 90 days | Expiry |
| Security audit log | 365 days | Expiry |
| Error and diagnostic logs | Newest 5,000 rows each | Row cap |
| Site analytics | 400 days; IP digest 24 hours | Privacy-page delete; daily sweep |
| Status history, cron ticks, presence, throttles | Hours to 30 days | Expiry |
| Account-scoped packages | Until deleted | Account delete runs each package's `purge_account_data` |
| Organization-scoped packages | Until deleted | Uninstall or organization delete (`app/src/plugin_data.py`) |
| Notes, calendar, app installs, reviews, push tokens, suppressions, IDS records, bug reports, ledger rows | Until deleted | **Missing proof:** account delete leaves them |

Account deletion (`_delete_account_namespace` in `app/src/entry.py`) removes the
account's repositories and repository-scoped rows, identity and session rows,
notifications, follows, referrals, stars, grants, ads, package rows and direct
conversations, then republishes the public catalog.

## Backups and copies

| Copy | Retention |
| --- | --- |
| Nightly encrypted rqlite backups (`tools/next_backup.py`) | Last 7 daily and 4 weekly; a restore resurrects deleted rows unless deletions are replayed |
| rqlite Raft log and snapshots | rqlite truncation defaults |
| Archives from the previous hosting stack | **Missing proof:** no retention or deletion step |
| Hosted repository `.trash` | Until emptied by hand |

## Logs

| Log | Retention |
| --- | --- |
| Core node journal (errors, request counts, statement text without values, mail delivery lines) | ≤ 64 MiB per node (`journald.conf`), rotated by size |
| Reverse-proxy access log (masked client addresses, no headers) | In the journal |
| Mail event spool | 3 days |
| Edge proxy logs | Provider default |

## Outside processors

The hosting provider (all stores), DNS and edge provider, recipients' mail
servers, optional error reporting (redacted), membership provider, AI providers
used by runner jobs, webhook receivers, food-data lookups (no account id), push
notification service (token and fixed alert only), chat bridge, ActivityPub
peers, and opt-in product analytics. Each keeps data under its own policy.
Details: [external dependency map](external-dependency-map.md).

## Known gaps

1. No user data export API.
2. Account deletion leaves the rows marked **missing proof** above.
3. `REPOSITORY_METADATA` entries never expire.
4. No step replays deletions after a backup restore.
5. Archives from the previous stack have no retention policy.
6. `.trash` is emptied only by hand.

Update this page with any change to bindings, `env.py`, backup retention, a
retention sweep, or `_delete_account_namespace`.

pages.title: Searchable public repository index
pages.description: The public index finds active projects that anyone can clone without an account. app/src/repository_index.py implements exactly this methodology.
pages.markdown:
# Searchable public repository index

The public index finds active projects that anyone can clone without an
account. `app/src/repository_index.py` implements exactly this methodology.

## Endpoint

`GET /api/repositories/search` (anonymous; public catalog data only; cacheable
30 s). Parameters: `q` (up to 8 words, all must match), `view`, `limit` (1–50,
default 20), `cursor`, `language`, `topic`, `owner`, `cloneable=1`. Errors are
`400` (`unknown_view`, `relevance_requires_query`, `invalid_limit`,
`invalid_cloneable`, `invalid_cursor`, `cursor_query_mismatch`) or
`503 catalog_unavailable`.

Each result has `identity` (the root-commit repository URN, see
[dependency workflows](dependency-workflows.md)), `clone` (a stock `git clone`
command), `maintainer` (key-signed catalog record), `availability`, and the
`ranking` inputs. Responses also give `total`, `facets`, `withheld`,
`freshness` and `budgets`.

## Budgets

Freshness 6 minutes (catalog snapshot age, reported per response); latency
250 ms for ranking a full catalog; page size 50 (larger limits are rejected).

## Determinism and pagination

The sort key always ends in the unique `owner/name`. `nextCursor` is a keyset
cursor bound to the query; walking all pages returns each match once, and it
is `null` on the last page.

## Views

- **relevance**: per-word integer scores for name, owner, topic, language and description.
- **updated**: latest head-commit time.
- **trending**: commits and merges over 4 weeks, each week capped at 50, plus
  5 points per independent mirror (at most 8 mirrors count).
- **new**: signed hosted-since time.
- **discussions**: open discussions, pull requests and issues, each capped at 500.

Trending and discussions skip records older than 14 days and zero scores.

## Anti-manipulation rules

Only signed public records appear; flagged, blocked or private ones are
withheld. Each repository is one result; only mirrors run by other accounts
count; identical heads collapse into `duplicates`; old records cannot be
replayed; heartbeats and self-reported traffic never rank; timestamps more
than 5 minutes in the future are ignored.

pages.title: Start your own instance from a settings file
pages.description: The Start your own instance page can be filled from one zip holding a settings .json file and a logo. Examples: start-config.example.zip and start-config.example.json.
pages.markdown:
# Start your own instance from a settings file

The [Start your own instance](https://app.forkmesh.com/start) page can be
filled from one zip holding a settings `.json` file and a logo. Examples:
[start-config.example.zip](https://app.forkmesh.com/start-config.example.zip)
and [start-config.example.json](https://app.forkmesh.com/start-config.example.json).

## The zip

Exactly one `.json` file; the logo is the image named by `logo`, or the only
image. Logo: PNG, JPEG, WebP or SVG up to 200 KB; zip up to 1 MB; no password.
Hidden files and `__MACOSX` folders are skipped.

## Settings

Every key is optional; missing keys keep the form's value. Keys starting with
`_` or `$` are notes; unknown keys are listed and skipped.

`theme` is empty (or `default`) for the ForkMesh colours, the id of a ready
theme from the page's theme cards, a colour preset name (`crimson`), or an
object of `#rrggbb` colours per mode, as the page's colour editor builds it:
`{"dark": {"primary": "#f97316"}, "light": {"primary": "#ea580c"}}`.
Tokens you leave out keep the ForkMesh colour.

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `projectName`, `theme`, `logo` | Name (up to 40 characters), optional theme, logo file name or data URL |
| `host`, `sshUser`, `port` | Server address, SSH user (default `root`), port (default `22`) |
| `sshPassword`, `sshPrivateKey`, `sshPassphrase` | Password, or a key as one JSON string with `\n` breaks |
| `hostKeyFingerprint` | Optional `SHA256:` fingerprint |
| `domain` | Optional; empty uses a free `sslip.io` address |
| `adminUsername`, `adminEmail`, `adminPassword` | Admin account; password at least 10 characters |
| `adminPath` | Private admin console address, like `/manage-x7k2q9`: `/` then 8 to 64 letters, numbers, `-` or `_`. Empty keeps the one the page made |
| `ownerType`, `ownerName` | `org` or `user`; organization name when `org` |
| `owners` | Up to 20 extra organization owners, each `{"username", "email", "password"}` |
| `mailProvider`, `mailApiKey`, `mailFrom` | `none`, `mailtrap`, `sendgrid` or `mailgun`; key; sender |
| `mailgunDomain`, `mailgunRegion` | Mailgun only; region `us` or `eu` |
| `ownWorld`, `listOnHomepage` | Booleans, default `true` |

## Admin console address

The page makes a fresh random `adminPath` (`/admin-` and 20 random letters
and numbers, from the browser's `crypto.getRandomValues`) every time it opens,
and every example zip or settings file it downloads carries a new one. The
instance serves its admin console only there; `/admin` answers "not found".
Save it with your password: ForkMesh does not store it, and the setup page
shows it only until you leave.

## Privacy

The file contains secrets. The page reads it in the browser only; just the
submitted settings reach ForkMesh, and secret fields are cleared once setup
starts. Delete the file afterwards.

pages.title: Start your own instance
pages.description: A ForkMesh instance is your own Git host on your own server, under your own name: repositories, pull requests, issues, chat, Actions and agents, with your logo, colours and…
pages.markdown:
# Start your own instance

A ForkMesh instance is your own Git host on your own server, under your own
name: repositories, pull requests, issues, chat, Actions and agents, with
your logo, colours and domain. Start one at
[forkmesh.com/start](https://forkmesh.com/start). No ForkMesh account is
needed, and it takes about fifteen minutes.

## What you need

- A fresh server with Debian 13 or Ubuntu 24.04, x86_64 or arm64, at least
  1 GB RAM and 6 GB free disk, with ports 80 and 443 free.
- SSH access as `root`, or as a user with passwordless `sudo`, by password
  or private key.
- Optional: a domain whose `A` record points at the server. Without one the
  instance gets a free `<ip-with-dashes>.sslip.io` address. A domain behind
  Cloudflare's proxy needs SSL/TLS mode Full (strict).
- Optional: a Mailtrap, SendGrid or Mailgun key, so the instance can send
  sign-up and password emails.

## Three ways to start

1. **Fill in the page.** Six short sections: name, logo and colour theme;
   your server; your address; your admin account and repository owner;
   email; and whether to list the instance on forkmesh.com and give it its
   own World.
2. **Upload a settings file.** Put every answer in one `.json` file, or a zip
   with the file and your logo, and upload it at the top of the page. See
   [Start from a settings file](start-config.md).
3. **Let your coding agent do it.** Copy the prompt from the page into
   Claude Code or another coding agent. It reads the
   [agent guide](https://app.forkmesh.com/forkmesh-agent.md), asks for your
   details and writes the settings file for you. See
   [Working with coding agents](coding-agents.md).

## What happens

ForkMesh connects to your server over SSH, checks the host key and runs the
installer. The page shows each step live: system check, packages, source,
build, configure, database, services, HTTPS, admin and repository. Your SSH
password or key is used once to connect and is never stored; secret fields
are cleared from the page once setup starts. If the connection drops, the
setup keeps running on the server.

When it is done:

- **Sign in within five minutes.** An instance started from the page that
  nobody signs in to removes itself, so an abandoned launch does not leave a
  server running.
- **Save your admin console address.** The page makes a private, random
  address such as `/admin-…`; `/admin` answers "not found". ForkMesh does
  not keep it, and the page shows it only until you leave.
- Your instance hosts its own copy of the platform source at
  `<owner>/forkmesh`.

## Running it yourself

If you would rather no secret passes through forkmesh.com, run the installer
on the server with the same settings file, without the SSH fields. The
installer also needs `domain` (use `<ip-with-dashes>.sslip.io` if you have
none), `publicAddress` (the server's public IP) and `adminPassword`:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://forkmesh.com/install-instance.sh -o install-instance.sh
sudo bash install-instance.sh --config forkmesh-instance.json
```

A manual install never removes itself. It joins the forkmesh.com directory
and the World only when you turn that on in the admin console, under
Platform → ForkMesh directory.

## After setup

- **Update** from the admin console (Platform → Update ForkMesh), or with
  `sudo bash install-instance.sh --update`. The new version builds beside
  the running one; data, secrets and the admin account are kept.
- **Update when a pull request is merged.** The console's Update page can
  rebuild the instance each time a pull request is merged into its own
  `<owner>/forkmesh` source. It refuses until that branch is protected, so
  only a change an owner or admin approved can deploy.
- **Branding.** The project name replaces "ForkMesh" across pages and email.
  Pick a ready theme or your own colours at setup; an admin can change the
  theme later under Settings → Instance theme. The "Powered by ForkMesh"
  badge is on by default.
- **Plugins.** Turn optional features on and off in the admin console,
  Platform → Plugins, without a reinstall. Examples: the copyable "fix this
  issue" prompt for coding agents and the Fediverse panels, both on by
  default.
- **Actions.** The installer adds a runner for repository workflows; an
  instance works without it if it fails.
- **Directory and World.** A listed instance appears on the forkmesh.com
  homepage and gets its own place in the ForkMesh World. Either can be
  switched off in the admin console.

Developer details (the API, installer steps, themes, plugins, white label and
limits) are in [docs/INSTANCES.md](../../docs/INSTANCES.md).

pages.title: Synchronization status
pages.description: All clients describe synchronization with one model, forkmesh-sync-status-v1.
pages.markdown:
# Synchronization status

All clients describe synchronization with one model, `forkmesh-sync-status-v1`.

| State | Current | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `queued`, `syncing` | no | Waiting or in flight |
| `verified` | yes | Every copy holds the latest signed state, confirmed within an hour |
| `degraded` | yes | Enough copies verified, some offline, behind or rejected |
| `stale` | no | No recent confirmation |
| `conflicted` | no | Copies disagree |
| `paused`, `external-only`, `failed` | no | Paused, only at an external provider, or rejected |

Nothing reports success without a verified copy, and conflict outranks success.
A status holds counts, timestamps and fixed wording only (`verifiedCopies`,
`trustedMirrors`, `lastConfirmedAt`, `lagMs`, `error`, `action`, `summary`), never
node names or raw errors.

Implementations: `app/src/sync_status.py` (API `syncStatus` on
`GET /api/repo/<owner>/<repo>/mirrors`), `desktop/src/SyncStatusModel.h`,
`SyncStatus.swift`, `SyncStatus.kt`, `server/syncstatus.go` and
`tools/forkmesh_sync_status.py explain` (exit 0 current, 3 not, 2 unreadable).
All match `conformance/sync-status/v1/fixture.json`, generated from `model.json`
(`staleAfterMs` 1 hour, `syncDeadlineMs` 15 minutes).

pages.title: Transports and anonymity postures
pages.description: tools/forkmesh_transports.py decides how a device reaches repositories and what it may reveal. A profile lists the device's adapters and one posture; the tool plans a route for a…
pages.markdown:
# Transports and anonymity postures

`tools/forkmesh_transports.py` decides how a device reaches repositories and
what it may reveal. A profile lists the device's adapters and one posture; the
tool plans a route for a URL, runs Git over the first permitted route that
answers (never falling back to a forbidden one), traces the Git process for
leaks in private postures, probes routes, and chooses which local addresses may
be advertised.

Formats: profile `forkmesh-transport-profile-v1`, plan
`forkmesh-transport-plan-v1`, health report `forkmesh-transport-health-v1`,
advertisement `forkmesh-transport-advertisement-v1`, telemetry
`forkmesh-transport-telemetry-v1`. Planner vectors:
`conformance/transports/v1/cases.json`.

```json
{"schema": "forkmesh-transport-profile-v1", "posture": "anonymous",
 "adapters": [{"id": "tor", "kind": "proxy", "network": "tor", "socks": "127.0.0.1:9050"}]}
```

## Adapters

| Kind | Carries | Name resolution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `clearnet` | Direct internet connections | System resolver, `standard` posture only |
| `proxy` | SOCKS5; `network` is `tor`, `i2p` or `socks` | By the proxy (`socks5h`); proxy endpoint must be a literal `IP:port` |
| `overlay` | Addresses inside its `cidrs` (WireGuard, Yggdrasil and similar) | None; literal addresses or pinned `hosts` |
| `lan` | Loopback, private, link-local, unique-local | None, except multicast DNS for `.local` |

Adapter fields: `allowPlaintext`, `authenticatedNetwork` (overlay),
`isolateStreams` and `serviceAddress` (proxy), `budgets.latencyMs` (default
2000).

Profile errors, checked in order: `profile_schema`, `unknown_posture`,
`adapters_missing`, `adapter_id_invalid`, `adapter_id_duplicate`,
`unknown_adapter_kind`, `proxy_endpoint_not_literal`, `proxy_network_unknown`,
`overlay_cidr_invalid`, `overlay_cidr_global`, `pinned_host_invalid`,
`budget_invalid`, `posture_has_no_adapter`,
`anonymous_requires_anonymity_network`.

## Postures

| Posture | Adapters | Lookups | Direct fallback | Telemetry | Advertises |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `standard` | all (`lan`, `overlay`, `clearnet`, `proxy`) | system | yes | counts | public, overlay, LAN |
| `private` | `proxy` | by proxy | never | counts | service address only |
| `anonymous` | `proxy` on `tor` or `i2p` | by proxy | never | off | service address only |
| `overlay-only` | `overlay` | none | never | counts | overlay |
| `lan-only` | `lan` | none | never | counts | LAN |

Outside `standard`, Git runs with a scrubbed environment, no system or global
config, no credential helpers or redirects, and redacted logs; `git://` and
`ssh://` go through the tool's relay. A repository config that could reroute
traffic (`insteadOf`, proxies, `core.sshCommand`, includes) is refused with
`repository_config_overrides_route`.

## Route refusals

Per adapter, first match: `adapter_not_permitted`,
`proxy_network_not_permitted`, `destination_requires_anonymity_network`,
`onion_requires_tor`, `i2p_requires_i2p`, `local_destination_via_proxy`,
`destination_outside_overlay`, `destination_outside_lan`, `name_needs_dns`,
`plaintext_via_exit`, `peer_unauthenticated`. Plan-level: `invalid_url`,
`scheme_unsupported` (only `https`, `http`, `ssh`, `git`), `no_permitted_route`.

## States

| State | Label | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `exposed` | Exposed | The trace saw a `dns_query` or `direct_connection` outside the route; wins over all others |
| `unreachable` | Unreachable | No permitted route answered, or the transfer broke |
| `degraded` | Degraded | Reachable with a reason: `failed_over`, `slow`, `intermittent`, `unauthenticated_peer` |
| `anonymous` | Anonymous | `anonymous` posture, healthy, no leak |
| `protected` | Protected | `private`, `overlay-only` or `lan-only`, healthy, no leak |
| `direct` | Direct | `standard` posture, healthy |

Clients display the report's `label`, `tone` and `explanation` verbatim. Leak
tracing uses `strace` on Linux; elsewhere `leakTrace` is `unavailable` and only
the in-process guard applies.

## Commands

```sh
tools/forkmesh_transports.py validate PROFILE
tools/forkmesh_transports.py plan --profile PROFILE URL
tools/forkmesh_transports.py probe --profile PROFILE URL [--report FILE]
tools/forkmesh_transports.py git --profile PROFILE URL [--repo DIR] [--trace auto|required|off] -- clone @URL app
tools/forkmesh_transports.py status REPORT
tools/forkmesh_transports.py advertise --profile PROFILE --address IP...
```

Use `fetch --atomic` so a broken route leaves refs unchanged. Git's own
failures do not trigger failover.

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Done. |
| `2` | Usage error, invalid profile, or required tracer missing. |
| `3` | Refused by policy before anything was sent. |
| `4` | Unreachable. |
| `5` | Exposed. |
| `6` | Git failed on a reachable route. |

Tests: `app/tests/test_transports.py` (quality gate `transport-conformance`).
Only Git traffic honours the profile so far.

pages.title: Trust lists
pages.description: A trust list is a signed list of keys its owner vouches for or warns about, each entry scoped to one role and one place (repo:, org: or community:). There is no global list…
pages.markdown:
# Trust lists

A trust list is a signed list of keys its owner vouches for or warns about, each
entry scoped to one role and one place (`repo:`, `org:` or `community:`). There
is no global list; following is local, private and optional, and nothing basic
(read, clone, sign in, push, recover) needs a list. Protocol:
[Scoped community trust lists](design/scoped-trust-lists.md).

Follows can only narrow a list. Included lists count inside the overlap of their
scopes, up to four deep. Disagreements show as conflict until a local override
(`trust`, `distrust`, `ignore`). Distrusted keys may sign an appeal. Lists
should name an offline recovery key; versions last at most 400 days. States are
Active, Recovered, Expired, Revoked, Conflicted and Missing.
`python3 tools/forkmesh_trust_lists.py drill` replays a key-compromise recovery.

Resolvers sharing one set of vectors: `app/src/trust_lists.py`,
`app/public/trust-lists.js`,
`native/ios/ForkMeshCore/Sources/FMAccount/TrustLists.swift`,
`native/android/core/src/main/kotlin/com/forkmesh/nativeapp/security/TrustLists.kt`
and `desktop/src/TrustLists.cpp`.

pages.title: ForkMesh World community services
pages.description: World keeps its event calendar, Fediverse directory and shared media rooms in the database and serves them over HTTPS; the multiplayer socket carries only presence and movement.…
pages.markdown:
# ForkMesh World community services

World keeps its event calendar, Fediverse directory and shared media rooms in
the database and serves them over HTTPS; the multiplayer socket carries only
presence and movement. Empty or unavailable data is shown as such, never as
demo content. All mutations and denied attempts write metadata-only entries to
`sensitive_audit_log`.

## UTC community events

`GET /api/world/events[/{id}]` is public and lists unexpired events.
Administrators use `POST`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` (cancel). `startsAt` and
`endsAt` are ISO-8601 UTC ending in `Z`; events last at most seven days, start
at most two years ahead, and the catalog is capped at 500 rows.

## Fediverse directory

`GET /api/world/fediverse` returns `mastodon`, `lemmy`, `x` and `reddit`
arrays. Administrator writes require `publicOnly`, `consentConfirmed`,
`consentSource` (`instance-operator`, `public-api`, `user-approved`,
`moderator-reviewed`) and a `consentCheckedAt` within the last year. Origins
must be public HTTPS with no credentials, paths, IPs or custom ports.
Relationship entries are accepted only when `public` and `consent` are both
`true`; X and Reddit records are operator attestations with
`oauthVerifiedByForkMesh: false`. No raw IPs, emails or private graphs are
stored.

## Shared media spaces

`/api/world/media/spaces` and its `items`, `playback`, `stop`, `schedules` and
`roles` sub-routes require a session. The creator owns a space and may grant
moderators; owners and moderators manage playlists, schedules and playback.
The actor always comes from the session.

Playlist items are links to allowlisted provider pages (SomaFM, YouTube,
Vimeo, SoundCloud, Twitch, Internet Archive, PeerTube) with
`termsConfirmed`, `noRebroadcast` and `autoplay: false`; raw media files are
rejected. ForkMesh never fetches or rebroadcasts media, and shared playback
state only coordinates clients.

Limits: 5 spaces per owner, 100 items, 50 schedules, 20 moderators per space.
Schedules are UTC, at most one year ahead and 24 hours long. Removed items and
finished schedules are purged after 30 days; spaces idle 180 days are archived
and purged 90 days later by the hourly retention cron.
