pages.markdown:
# Secret scanning before replication

A node copies every object it receives to mirrors, forks, clones and backups,
so **a pushed object cannot be recalled**. The only remediation for a leaked
credential is rotation; the only prevention is stopping it before the first
remote receives it. Every boundary prints this warning with its findings.

## Scanner contract

`tools/secret_gate.py` defines `forkmesh-secret-scan-v1` (standard library
only; `python3 tools/secret_gate.py contract` prints it):

- **Rules**: provider-prefixed token patterns (Git hosts, cloud providers, chat
  and payment services, AI APIs, package registries, PEM private keys) plus a
  generic password/token assignment rule, each with rotation guidance.
- **Placeholder filter**: the generic rule skips obvious placeholders
  (`example`, `changeme`, `${VAR}`, `{{ }}`).
- **Ignore marker**: `forkmesh-secret-scan:ignore-line` on a logical line skips
  it, unless the organization refuses markers.
- **Value-free findings**: rule, path, line, blob id and a fingerprint derived
  from rule, path and blob id, never from the value.

The desktop scanner carries the same patterns; `app/tests/test_secret_gate.py`
fails if they drift.

## Boundaries

| Boundary | Behaviour | Mechanism |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local commit | Blocks or warns on added lines | `secret_gate.py install-hooks` (pre-commit) |
| Local push | Blocks or warns on every outgoing object | `secret_gate.py install-hooks` (pre-push) |
| Desktop push and review diffs | Review dialog or banner per match | desktop `RepoSecurity` |
| Node receipt (HTTPS and SSH) | Refuses the push before storing anything | `secrets` in the [node operator policy](../operations/node-operator-policy.md) |
| Sync and mirror intake | Detects after replication, quarantines under `block` | `node_operator_policy.py enforce` |
| Public security report | Findings without values | `tools/security_scan.py` |

```sh
python3 tools/secret_gate.py install-hooks --repo . \
  --repository owner/app --org-policy ~/.config/forkmesh/secret-policy.json
```

The installer never overwrites a hook it did not write.

## Policy

With no policy every rule blocks. The organization policy file:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "mode": "block",
  "rules": {"generic-secret-assignment": "warn"},
  "customRules": [
    {"id": "custom-deploy-key", "title": "Deploy key",
     "pattern": "deploy_live_[A-Za-z0-9]{32}", "severity": "critical",
     "action": "block", "rotation": "Revoke it in the provider console."}
  ],
  "allowlist": [
    {"paths": ["tests/fixtures/fake/*"], "rules": ["*"],
     "reason": "synthetic credentials for parser tests"}
  ],
  "honorIgnoreMarkers": true,
  "allowRepositoryAllowlist": false,
  "allowRepositoryCustomRules": false,
  "overrides": {
    "allowedSignersPath": "/etc/forkmesh/secret-override-signers",
    "maxLifetimeDays": 90
  }
}
```

- `mode` and `rules` take `off`, `warn` or `block`.
- A repository's `.forkmesh/secret-scan.json` can only tighten rules; its
  allowlist and custom rules count only when the organization allows them.
  Deleting it in a push loosens nothing.
- Allowlist entries need a reason and cannot cover every path. Invalid or
  empty-matching patterns and unknown fields are refused.

## Signed overrides

A block is lifted only by an SSH-signed override naming exact fingerprints:

```sh
python3 tools/secret_gate.py sign-override --key ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 \
  --signer signer@example.com --repository owner/app --days 30 \
  --reason "synthetic token for a parser test" \
  --fingerprint <fingerprint> > .forkmesh/secret-overrides/parser.json
```

Signers are listed in OpenSSH allowed-signers format with
`namespaces="forkmesh-secret-override"`. An override is ignored if the
signature fails, it names another repository, it has expired or exceeds
`maxLifetimeDays`, or the policy has no `allowedSignersPath`. Accepted
overrides are written to the node audit log.

## Accuracy

`conformance/secrets/v1/corpus.json` (generated by `build_corpus.py`, all
credentials synthetic) is run by `python3 tools/secret_gate.py corpus` at every
boundary. Bounds: at most 15% false negatives and 10% false positives. Known
misses are JSON object keys, concatenated tokens and base64-wrapped keys.

## Response after replication

`python3 tools/secret_gate.py respond --report <scan.json>` prints the plan:

1. **Contain**: quarantine on nodes you operate, remove the value in a new
   commit, pause automation using it.
2. **Rotate** at the issuer and review its audit log.
3. **Notify** the owner and security contact with the value-free evidence.
4. **Residual risk**: existing copies keep the object; treat it as compromised.

## Telemetry and limits

Scan reports and `node_operator_policy.py status` count blocked, warned,
overridden, allowlisted and stored detections without values. Blobs over 1 MiB
and binary blobs are skipped and counted. Browser uploads and provider imports
are scanned only when they reach a node's `enforce`.

pages.title: World-to-desktop speech bridge
pages.description: The desktop client can expose its local speech-to-text engine to a World page without sending microphone audio anywhere. The browser is only a controller and transcript…
pages.markdown:
# World-to-desktop speech bridge

The desktop client can expose its local speech-to-text engine to a World page
without sending microphone audio anywhere. The browser is only a controller and
transcript recipient; capture and transcription stay in the desktop client. The
World currently ships no speech controls, and the desktop bridge is dormant
infrastructure.

## Pairing

1. The user enables voice control for one exact World origin in the desktop
   client.
2. The client listens on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port and shows a short-lived
   pairing capability, storing only its SHA-256 digest.
3. The page sends the capability once as `Authorization: Bearer …` to
   `POST /v1/pair`, which consumes it and returns an origin-bound ten-minute
   session capability.

Capabilities never appear in URLs, cookies, server requests, analytics or
persistent browser storage. Revoking, closing the panel or quitting the client
invalidates them.

## Capture protocol

- `POST /v1/transcription/start`, stop and cancel each carry a single-use
  `X-ForkMesh-Request-Id`; replays are rejected.
- `GET /v1/transcription` returns status and transcript text.
- Text is inserted into a World composer only after the user confirms the
  destination (`chat`, `issue` or `note`).

There is no audio upload or download endpoint, and responses report
`audioRelayed: false`. Bodies are limited to 8 KiB and headers to 16 KiB, query
strings and transfer encodings are rejected, responses are `no-store`, and
transcript and error text is bounded and stripped of control characters. One
capture runs at a time.

## Origin boundary

The origin is matched exactly (no suffix, wildcard or `null` matching). CORS
echoes only that origin and never enables credentials. Both the listener and
each peer must be loopback. The bridge is never proxied by a server.

## Auditing

Audit events (issued, paired, started, stopped, cancelled, completed, failed,
revoked) are written without capability values, transcript contents, audio,
device names or browsing history.

pages.title: Breakout authorization replica
pages.description: Mirrors replicate repository data through Git and signed ledgers. Managing repositories while the controller is unreachable also needs authorization data, but copying account or…
pages.markdown:
# Breakout authorization replica

Mirrors replicate repository data through Git and signed ledgers. Managing
repositories while the controller is unreachable also needs authorization
data, but copying account or session tables to every public host would make
each mirror a credential database. Instead each node holds a narrow, signed
authorization projection in SQLite, and browsers carry a controller-signed
portable session grant.

## Projection contents

Each monotonically numbered generation contains only: opaque account id and
public username; enabled device or passkey public keys and their capabilities;
public repository ids with owner/collaborator roles; key, account, and
repository revocation generations; and issue time, expiry, previous digest,
and Ed25519 signature.

It never contains email addresses, password hashes or reset state, TOTP seeds,
bearer or session tokens, private-message metadata, payment state, administrator
privileges, or encrypted account/repository rows. It is built by a dedicated
query, never a database export.

## Synchronization

A node refreshes after each controller authorization event and on the reconcile
interval. It verifies signature, schema, strictly increasing generation,
previous digest, size, and expiry, then applies one SQLite transaction. A bad
generation is discarded and the last good one stays. Peers exchange only
controller-signed generations. Repository content keeps syncing through Git and
event spools; this database only decides who may sign changes.

## Sessions

Each controller login also mints a signed portable session grant (opaque ids,
public username, issue/expiry, mirror-dashboard audience; no bearer token). It
travels in a separate HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict parent-domain cookie,
and mirrors verify it with the published router key. The grant lives at most
twelve hours, never outlives its controller session, and is cleared on logout
or session/device revocation. Tampering, ambiguous cookies, future grants,
expiry, and unknown keys fail closed. Custom-domain fleets set
`PORTABLE_SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN`.

Mirrors never accept password-only authentication: a password verifier on
every node would be offline attack material. Without a portable grant, an
enrolled device or passkey signs a node nonce bound to the origin and
authorization generation, creating a short-lived node-local session.

## Recovery

During an outage, authorized mutations land in local Git and signed spools.
On recovery the node reconciles revocations, forwards events idempotently,
fetches the newest generation, and reconciles refs. Billing, password reset,
account recovery, private data, and platform administration always fail
closed on a mirror.

pages.title: Business-model rollout and recovery
pages.description: This runbook publishes the free-protocol / paid-services boundary without giving the hosted operator control over protocol participation.
pages.markdown:
# Business-model rollout and recovery

This runbook publishes the free-protocol / paid-services boundary without
giving the hosted operator control over protocol participation.

## Owners and release gate

Name a product owner, infrastructure-cost owner, support owner, and privacy or
legal reviewer before enabling a managed checkout. Managed checkout stays
disabled while any gate in `www/public/business-model.json` is open.

```sh
python3 tools/unit_economics.py validate-contract
python3 tools/quality_gate.py run --profile core
python3 tools/unit_economics.py report --input /path/to/period.json
python3 tools/unit_economics.py launch-gate --input /path/to/period.json
```

A period file combines the admin usage report, invoice-backed costs, and
aggregate funnel counts. Never pass the launch gate with synthetic evidence or
zero-valued missing costs.

## Supported surfaces

- Contract page and pricing: current desktop and mobile browsers.
- Portable proof: standard Git plus the web app.
- Self-hosted desktop: macOS, Windows, and Linux release packages.
- Managed mirror evidence: the Linux headless mirror service.

Self-hosted deployments receive documentation and community support unless a
separate support order names the platform.

## Deployment

1. Validate the contract JSON, visible matrix, docs links, analytics allowlist,
   and unit-economics tests.
2. Confirm `/business-model.json`, `/docs/business-model`, `/#pricing`,
   `/privacy`, and `/terms` are served.
3. Confirm the managed plan says `research-preview-not-for-sale`, has no
   checkout control, and no variable-cost service says unlimited.
4. Deploy the site; deploy the app only when the admin usage projection changed.

## Failure paths

| Failure | Required behavior | Recovery |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Contract JSON malformed or drifts from the matrix | CI/deploy fails | Fix source and matrix together |
| Provider analytics unconfigured | Usage endpoint returns `analytics_unconfigured`; cost unknown | Restore the scoped token and retry |
| Provider analytics unavailable | Usage endpoint returns `analytics_unavailable`; never record zero | Retry later or reconcile the invoice |
| A cost source is missing | Period report incomplete; launch gate fails | Attach an attributable source |
| Export or restore differs | Trial stops | Restore the last verified copy, fix the exporter, repeat |
| Optional analytics denied | No product event is sent | Continue; consent is never a service condition |

## Rollback

The contract deployment changes no protocol object, repository, identity,
entitlement, or customer data. Roll the site back to the last reviewed asset
revision. Never roll back by deleting repositories or signed collaboration
records; a pricing rollback cannot revoke license rights or make an export paid.

## Recovery and portability drill

Before the first managed trial and each material format change: export a
disposable project from the managed service without a paid-only exporter,
import it into a clean self-hosted deployment with hosted routes disabled,
compare all Git refs, object ids, and signed `.forkmesh` records, collaborate
from the self-host, then restore the managed service from the same export. Any
mismatch blocks launch.

## Telemetry and privacy

The infrastructure projection is aggregate and holds only fixed unit ids and
quantities. Period files may hold aggregate funnel counts, revenue, and cost
labels, never account or repository names, paths, IP addresses, request ids,
provider customer ids, or interviewee identity. Pricing-page events use the
default-off first-party analytics controller and are sent only after explicit
consent; Global Privacy Control and Do Not Track disable them.

pages.title: Cloudflare deployment boundaries
pages.description: This page describes the optional, legacy Cloudflare Workers deployment. The hosted service (app.forkmesh.com and world.forkmesh.com) runs on self-hosted core nodes (PLAN.md)…
pages.markdown:
# Cloudflare deployment boundaries

This page describes the optional, legacy Cloudflare Workers deployment. The
hosted service (app.forkmesh.com and world.forkmesh.com) runs on self-hosted
core nodes ([PLAN.md](../../../docs/PLAN.md)); only forkmesh.com runs as the
`forkmesh-www` Worker. A default self-host installs on a VPS
([start your own instance](../start-your-own-instance.md)).

A Cloudflare deployment of ForkMesh uses three Workers. The App owns the whole
control plane; there is no separate API or edge-control Worker.

| Directory | Script | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `app/` | `forkmesh-app` | Product UI, `/api/*`, health and release identity, public snapshots, WebSockets, Git Smart HTTP, ActivityPub, D1, KV, AI, Cron, migrations, Durable Objects |
| `www/` | `forkmesh-www` | Landing pages, documentation, blog, shared browser assets |
| `world/` | `forkmesh-world` | World shell, modules, models, audio, avatars |

## Routing

- The App serves the root redirect, `/health`, `/api/version`, and every
  operational protocol. Identity responses are `no-store`.
- Five anonymous GET routes (`/api/repositories`, `/api/network/overview`,
  `/api/repo/<owner>/<repo>/mirrors`, `/api/status`, `/api/status/world`) read
  validated, fresh-only snapshot rows. Credentials, cookies, query strings,
  cache-bypass directives, and non-GET methods bypass snapshots; missing or
  stale rows fall back to one no-store live response; corrupt rows fail closed.
- `www` service-proxies `/api/*`, Git Smart HTTP, ActivityPub, webhooks, and
  WebSocket upgrades to the App, and redirects product and `/world*` routes.
- `world` serves its own assets, injects `APP_ORIGIN`, and delegates non-World
  routes and shared shell assets to the App through a service binding.

`app/public`, `www/public` (authored docs in `www/docs`), and `world/public`
own their respective assets. `app/tools/build_site_assets.py` stages
`app/dist`, `www/dist`, and `world/dist`.

## Scheduled maintenance

The App's one-minute Cron handler rings a singleton scheduler object whose
alarm runs every due phase. When the next phase no longer fits the
per-invocation subrequest budget, it persists progress and re-arms itself, so a
busy minute is a short chain of invocations on one object. Phases are
failure-isolated, interrupted phases are reported incomplete rather than
replayed, and each tick writes one bounded `cron_tick` row (read by
`/api/accounts/admin-cron-report`).

## Single-Worker topology

A Workers self-host is one App at one origin: set `PUBLIC_BASE_URL`,
`API_ORIGIN`, `APP_ORIGIN`, `WWW_ORIGIN`, and allowed CORS origins to it, and
`SINGLE_WORKER_SITE=true`. The bootstrapper creates one App Worker, one D1
database, one hostname, and one route. World is optional.

## Deploying

`./deploy.sh deploy` and `./deploy.sh changed` skip any target whose live
fingerprint already matches its inputs. `--force` (or
`FORKMESH_FORCE_DEPLOY=1`) uploads anyway, for a live Worker that is wrong in a
way the fingerprint cannot see; migrations, secrets, and post-deploy
verification still run.

Secret publication preserves the router signing key pair already on the App;
rotation publishes a validated pair atomically. Migrations are roll-forward, so
an application rollback must accept the newest schema; otherwise roll forward.

pages.title: Cloudflare Free-tier request audit
pages.description: In production only forkmesh-www (forkmesh.com) runs on Workers; the App and World run on the core nodes.
pages.markdown:
# Cloudflare Free-tier request audit

In production only `forkmesh-www` (forkmesh.com) runs on Workers; the App and
World run on the core nodes.

Rules for keeping a Cloudflare Workers deployment of ForkMesh inside
Free-plan request, subrequest and CPU limits. They apply to the App, WWW and
World Workers and to the mirror routing path.

## Request architecture

| Worker | Entry point | Bindings |
| --- | --- | --- |
| App | `app/src/entry.py` (built to `app/src_build/entry.py`) | D1 `DB`, KV `REPOSITORY_METADATA`, Workers AI, Durable Objects, Static Assets, one-minute cron |
| WWW | `www/worker.js` | Static Assets, `APP` service binding |
| World | `world/worker.js` | Static Assets, `APP` service binding |

- Static pages, hashed assets and dashboard chunks are served by Static Assets
  and excluded from `run_worker_first`, so they cost no Worker invocation.
- WWW and World reach the App through service bindings, not public HTTP.
- Mirror hostnames are not Workers. Repository bytes come from the
  [direct-HTTPS mirror gateway](direct-https-mirror-gateway.md), reached
  directly or through a Tunnel.

## Rules

- **No idle polling.** Browser pages refresh on push events, reconnect,
  visibility resume or explicit refresh; any remaining interval is at least
  five minutes and pauses while the tab is hidden.
- **Clients go direct.** The desktop reads saved hosts' signed `/health` and
  `/v1/public/repositories/...` directly and pulls over the host's SSH remote;
  the relay is the final fallback.
- **One socket per node.** A managed mirror node holds one event socket and
  fetches a collaboration inbox only for the kind that changed.
- **No per-request database writes on read paths.** Mirror selection uses
  stateless rotation with a short clone pin, not a stored cursor.
- **Cache verified proofs.** Signed repository proofs are cached per edge
  location for 60 seconds, keyed by node, public key, owner, repository and
  accepted refs. Authenticated responses, writes, private replicas and Actions
  output are never cached.
- **Bounded failover.** At most four mirror candidates, tried sequentially,
  with bounded timeouts; errors become bounded 404/503 responses.
- **Batch cron.** Due cron phases are packed into as few invocations as their
  measured subrequest reserves allow; `/api/accounts/admin-cron-report` shows
  the cost per tick.
- **Measure before tightening.** Apply rate-limit or WAF rules only after
  sampled logs identify abusive paths, and exclude Git clients and crawlers.
  A plan upgrade is headroom, not a fix.

pages.title: Community reward pool
pages.description: The reward system is non-custodial. The server coordinates public Solana state and unsigned transfer intents; it never creates, accepts, stores, or uses a wallet private key.
pages.markdown:
# Community reward pool

The reward system is non-custodial. The server coordinates public Solana state
and unsigned transfer intents; it never creates, accepts, stores, or uses a
wallet private key.

## Custody boundaries

- Contributors sign direct transfers from their own wallets to the public pool
  address.
- The pool private key lives only in the instance owner's desktop client,
  inside its encrypted local vault. The client shows and validates every
  source, destination, amount, network, and expiry before the owner approves.
- The database stores only public addresses, Solana Pay references, eligibility
  snapshots, unsigned plans, transaction signatures, and status.
- The server fetches each finalized transaction and requires its System Program
  transfer list to match the approved intent exactly.
- Node operators supply only a public payout address.

User funds, pool funds, pending rewards, and completed transfers are separate
states. Contributions are voluntary community support, not investments.

## Configuration

```text
COMMUNITY_REWARD_NETWORK=mainnet-beta
COMMUNITY_REWARD_RPC_URL=https://api.mainnet-beta.solana.com
COMMUNITY_REWARD_POOL_ADDRESS=<public address>   # or TREASURY_SOLANA_ADDRESS
REWARD_SIGNER_ACCOUNT=<instance owner account>
REWARD_INTERVAL_MS=3600000
REWARD_JITTER_MAX_MS=2700000
REWARD_AMOUNT_LAMPORTS=100000
REWARD_MIN_UPTIME_MS=1800000
REWARD_MIN_CONTRIBUTION_UNITS=0
REWARD_HEALTH_FRESH_MS=600000
```

`COMMUNITY_REWARD_POOL_ADDRESS` wins when set; an invalid value fails closed
rather than falling back. The pool is exposed only when the network is known,
the RPC is credential-free HTTPS, `getGenesisHash` matches the cluster, and the
pool account exists. Devnet requires explicit development configuration.

## Contributions

`POST /api/rewards/contributions` with `action=prepare` returns a one-hour,
reference-bound Solana Pay URI:

- `trickle` leaves the contribution in the pool for randomized rounds;
- `instant_all_nodes` creates an equal unsigned plan for every eligible node,
  in batches of at most eight transfers.

Confirmation checks finality, the reference, destination, amount, replay, and
that it is an ordinary System transfer. No outgoing plan is created while
finality is unknown.

## Randomized mirror rewards

Each interval the server records a round with a reproducible jitter, freezes an
eligibility snapshot, and selects one node by SHA-256 modulo over a finalized
blockhash. The intent publishes the snapshot and its hash, rejection reasons,
entropy, algorithm, selected index, payee, amount, and expiry.

Eligibility requires a fresh signed heartbeat, a healthy direct HTTPS endpoint,
signed identity registration, an independently challenged refs proof matching
the integrity pin, a public payout address, minimum observed uptime, and the
optional contribution threshold. Federated relays must forward each node's
original signed registration and nonce-bound health message; relay approval is
a disclosed, revocable trust boundary. Identity, operator, device key, and
wallet are de-duplicated. These gates reduce Sybil risk but do not eliminate it.

## Pending walletless rewards

The instance owner can create a pending allocation
(`POST /api/rewards/pending-awards`) for an active recipient without a payout
wallet. It moves no funds, expires after 24 hours, and lets the recipient
submit a public address through `POST /api/rewards/pending`.

## Public inspection

`GET /api/rewards/pool` (and its alias `GET /api/accounts/central-fund`) shows
network, address, live balance, timing and amount settings, contribution modes,
recent finalized transfers, and the non-custodial notice. Retired custodial
deposit endpoints return HTTP 410. Legacy custodial keys are handled in
[Legacy Solana custody migration](legacy-solana-custody-migration.md).

pages.title: Community reward-pool local signer
pages.description: The desktop Control node page is the only component that can sign an outgoing community-pool transaction. The server schedules and stores public plans but never receives a seed…
pages.markdown:
# Community reward-pool local signer

The desktop **Control node** page is the only component that can sign an
outgoing community-pool transaction. The server schedules and stores public
plans but never receives a seed, private key, passphrase, or signed transaction
bytes. Signing is an explicitly approved local flow, not an unattended hot
wallet.

## Provisioning

Server configuration (public values only): `COMMUNITY_REWARD_NETWORK`,
`COMMUNITY_REWARD_RPC_URL`, `COMMUNITY_REWARD_POOL_ADDRESS` (or
`TREASURY_SOLANA_ADDRESS`), and `REWARD_SIGNER_ACCOUNT` (fallback
`INSTANCE_OWNER_ACCOUNT`). The pool address must match the key imported on the
desktop.

On the owner's device: sign in as the signer account, open **Control node →
First-instance reward-pool signer**, import an existing 64-byte Solana CLI
keypair (JSON byte array or base58), set a strong vault passphrase, and choose
the network and a public HTTPS JSON-RPC origin. The importer rejects 32-byte
seeds, recovery phrases, and keypairs whose public half does not match; it never
generates a key. RPC URLs with credentials, query strings, paths, or plain HTTP
are rejected.

## Local vault

`reward-pool/pool-key.vault` in the application-data directory holds the public
address (authenticated as additional data), a scrypt salt (`N=32768`, `r=8`,
`p=1`), an AES-256-GCM nonce, the encrypted 32-byte Ed25519 seed, and the tag.
The file must be owner-only, symlinks are refused, and writes are atomic. The
passphrase and seed exist only during one approved operation. The key is never
written to settings, server storage, logs, or command lines. Back up the
original key with trusted wallet procedures; it cannot be recovered.

## Queue contract

```text
GET /api/rewards/signing-jobs?signer=<account>&ts=<epoch-ms>&sig=<identity-signature>
```

The identity signs `forkmesh-reward-jobs-v1\n<signer>\n<epoch-ms>`. The server
returns at most 50 jobs for the configured signer. The desktop requires custody
`external-local-signer` and validates each job: kind, status, expiry, network,
source address, plan schema 2, `custody.forkMeshHoldsUserKeys=false`,
`signing.method=external-local-qt`, an allowed policy
(`randomized-eligible-mirror-v2`, `instant-all-eligible-mirrors-v1`,
`pending-reward-claim-v1`), valid unique destinations with positive amounts
within per-policy caps, and no secret-shaped fields. Anything else stays
unsigned.

## Review and signing

**Review, sign and submit** shows source, total, every destination and amount,
policy, network, intent, and expiry; Cancel is the default. After approval the
desktop fetches a finalized blockhash and builds a legacy transaction with the
pool as sole signer and fee payer and only the reviewed System Program
transfers (at most 1,232 bytes). It reparses the serialized transaction and
rejects any deviation before unlocking the vault, then signs the exact message.

## Broadcast and reconciliation

The desktop broadcasts via `sendTransaction` with preflight, checks the returned
signature matches its own, and persists only public recovery fields. It reports
the receipt to `POST /api/rewards/signing-jobs` signed over
`forkmesh-reward-submit-v1\n<signer>\n<intent-id>\n<transaction-signature>\n<epoch-ms>`.
`202` means submitted. The server fetches the finalized transaction and marks
the intent complete only if it contains exactly the planned transfers; a
signature cannot be replayed across intents. **Reconcile last submission**
recovers after an interruption.

## Operational checks

Before funding a production pool, run `forkmesh-reward-pool-tests`, verify vault
permissions, rehearse the full flow on devnet, confirm the server account, pool
address, vault address, network, and RPC agree, and run the read-only preflight:

```bash
python3 tools/validate_reward_mainnet.py \
  --rpc-url https://api.mainnet-beta.solana.com \
  --pool-address "${COMMUNITY_REWARD_POOL_ADDRESS:-${TREASURY_SOLANA_ADDRESS:-}}"
```

It calls only `getGenesisHash`, `getAccountInfo`, and `getBalance`. Establish key
backup, compromise response, and rotation procedures before going live.

pages.title: Custodial deposit addresses for world-element purchases
pages.description: The World element store accepts two payment methods. The second is optional.
pages.markdown:
# Custodial deposit addresses for world-element purchases

The World element store accepts two payment methods. The second is optional.

| | Direct | Deposit |
|---|---|---|
| Buyer pays | the published pool address | a temporary ForkMesh address |
| Who holds the key | the buyer | **ForkMesh**, until the sweep lands |
| Confirmation | buyer submits the transaction signature | automatic; the address is watched |
| Mirror half | unsigned intent, signed on the operator's device | paid by the sweep transaction |

## Custody model

For a deposit, the server generates a fresh Ed25519 keypair, stores the seed
encrypted in `world_element_purchases`, and shows the public key as the payment
address. Once funded, it signs one transaction sending half to the treasury and
half to eligible online mirror nodes, then clears `deposit_secret`. Until the
sweep lands (a failed sweep is retried by cron), anyone who controls the server,
its database, or `DATA_KEY` can move those funds. The community reward pool key
is not involved.

The store shows custody text before purchase, and `/api/world/store/catalog`
marks the deposit entry with `forkMeshHoldsDepositKey: true`. Never describe
this method as non-custodial.

## Configuration

Deposits are off unless `TREASURY_SOLANA_ADDRESS` (or
`COMMUNITY_REWARD_POOL_ADDRESS`) is set. `CUSTODIAL_DEPOSITS = "0"` keeps the
treasury but disables deposits; buyers then see only the direct method.

## Invariants

- The shared read helper `_solana_rpc` cannot send; only `_solana_rpc_write`
  broadcasts, and only `sendTransaction`.
- The sweep is idempotent on `sweep_signature` and clears the seed on success;
  concurrent pollers cannot double-send.
- Payees come from the signed eligibility snapshot (`_eligible_reward_snapshot`),
  capped at `MAX_SWEEP_PAYEES`.

## Monitoring

A funded address with an empty `sweep_signature` and a `sweep_error` means the
server still holds a key for real funds:

```sql
SELECT purchase_id, deposit_address, sweep_error FROM world_element_purchases
WHERE method='deposit' AND deposit_secret<>'' AND sweep_signature='';
```

`treasury_not_configured` means the treasury variable was removed after the
address was minted; restore it and cron finishes the sweep.

pages.title: D1 database cleanup plan
pages.description: This page records the rules that came out of auditing the App's SQL database (schema in app/src/schema.py, migrations in app/migrations/). It applies to the Cloudflare D1…
pages.markdown:
# D1 database cleanup plan This page records the rules that came out of auditing the App's SQL database (schema in `app/src/schema.py`, migrations in `app/migrations/`). It applies to the Cloudflare D1 deployment and to any SQLite-compatible store that replays the same migrations. ## Goals - A clean replay of `app/migrations/*.sql` in version order builds every table the App uses. - No table remains without a reader or writer unless a keep decision is recorded. - Hot paths read shared snapshots instead of scanning tables per request. - Retention prunes run from cron at most once an hour, never per request. - No plaintext secret column remains, and sealed rows name the key that sealed them. ## Schema change rules - Take the next free migration number. Each migration has a matching `down` file. - Any change to the runtime schema text (`SCHEMA_STATEMENTS`, `SCHEMA_PRE_CREATE_ALTER_STATEMENTS`, `SCHEMA_ALTER_STATEMENTS`) moves three things together: the latest migration ends with the `schema_fingerprint:` stamp insert, `_SCHEMA_FINGERPRINT` holds the same literal, and the migration test pins that file name. A schema-only change with no DDL still needs a stamp-only migration. - `CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS` never rewrites an existing trigger; a changed body needs `DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS` first. - A new cron phase is added to `CRON_PHASE_CATALOG` in `app/src/cron_activity.py`. - Never key liveness on `checked_at`. ## Dropping a table Dropping a table takes two deploys: 1. Deploy N removes every reader, writer and the table's DDL from `schema.py` (`ensure_schema` replays `schema.py` whenever the fingerprint changes, so leftover DDL re-creates the table). 2. Deploy N+1 ships the `DROP` migration, after a full export of the database. Never put both in one change. ## Retention | Table family | Rule | | --- | --- | | Metrics and status samples | pruned from cron, at most hourly | | Rate-limit tables | pruned by age from cron | | `sensitive_audit_log` | write agent status entries only on a real transition; shorter retention for high-volume actions is an open decision | | `release_downloads` | daily roll-up of older rows is an open decision | | `feedback_email_sends` | never pruned by age: a missing row means "not sent yet" | ## Sealed rows `encrypt_row` seals JSON with AES-GCM under a key derived from `DATA_KEY`; `decrypt_row` returns `None` on any failure. Stored values do not yet name their key, so `DATA_KEY` cannot be rotated in place. The planned format is `k1.<8 hex key id>:` (key id = first 8 hex of HMAC-SHA256 over the key material with `forkmesh-data-key-id-v1`); unprefixed legacy values keep decrypting with the current key, a previous key is kept only until every row is re-sealed, and blind index output does not change. Sealing code should go through `encrypt_row`/`decrypt_row` so the format applies everywhere. ## Exports and measurement Production runs on rqlite on the core nodes. Before any destructive migration: 1. Take a fresh backup: `python3 tools/next_backup.py run --execute` keeps it only after `PRAGMA integrity_check` and table counts pass. 2. Check it and print its row counts: `python3 tools/next_backup.py verify --identity `. 3. Decrypt it into scratch SQLite: `python3 tools/next_backup.py restore --out --identity `, run the migration there and compare row counts with production. 4. List what will run: `python3 tools/rqlite_migrate.py --list`, then apply with `python3 tools/rqlite_migrate.py --url --user --password

`. Measure reads with `FORKMESH_HOST_D1_LOG=1`: each statement is followed by a `D1-done ms, rows` line ([d1.md](../../../docs/app/d1.md)). On a Cloudflare Workers deployment only, export with `wrangler d1 export --remote --output ` and measure with `wrangler d1 insights --time-period 7d --sort-by reads`; table-browser `COUNT(*)` queries come from the dashboard, not App code. ## Related - `docs/app/d1.md` - [Cloudflare free-tier audit](cloudflare-free-tier-audit.md)

pages.title: Direct-HTTPS independent mirror gateway
pages.description: tools/mirror_gateway.py is the repository-byte origin of an independently operated ForkMesh mirror. It listens on loopback HTTP only; an operator-controlled HTTPS reverse proxy…
pages.markdown:
# Direct-HTTPS independent mirror gateway

`tools/mirror_gateway.py` is the repository-byte origin of an independently
operated ForkMesh mirror. It listens on loopback HTTP only; an
operator-controlled HTTPS reverse proxy terminates public TLS. Git clients use
the mirror's standard `/<owner>/<repository>.git` Smart-HTTP URL directly. The
main routing service keeps the stable clone URL and redirects there only after
a fresh signed mirror proof.

Repository bytes always travel over HTTPS. The node event WebSocket only
announces changes (and renews the endpoint lease); the node daemon then fetches
over HTTPS, with a slow reconcile interval as recovery for missed events.

The Git data plane is read-only: it implements `upload-pack`, not general
`receive-pack`, issue writes or administration. Writes are opt-in per
repository (`merge-pull`, `git-receive-pack`, or a writable root for
push-created repositories). Requests without valid signed device headers get
`401 push_unauthorized` from the routing service before any body is read
(see [mobile node contract](../mobile/mobile-node-contract.md) section 7).
Owner-authorized stock Git writes use the [SSH gateway](git-ssh-gateway.md);
the [stock Git compatibility matrix](../git-compatibility.md) lists the split.

## Security boundary

- The listener must be `127.0.0.1`, `::1` or `localhost`.
- Public upload-pack reads need no capability. Every control, mutation, private
  and non-Git request needs a fresh, single-use Ed25519 capability from the
  routing service, bound to method, path plus query, body digest, node, request
  ID and issue time.
- Unknown, private, disabled and integrity-quarantined repositories all return
  the same `404 {"ok":false,"error":"not_found"}`. Health and manifest
  responses never enumerate repositories.
- Only configured public repositories are served, each pinned by a SHA-256
  over its sorted heads and tags, checked at startup and before serving.
- Git runs without a shell and with config, prompts, helpers, fsmonitor and
  pack hooks disabled.
- `refs/forkmesh/` is internal node state. Upload-pack hides the namespace and
  keeps `allowTipSHA1InWant`, `allowReachableSHA1InWant` and
  `allowAnySHA1InWant` disabled so hidden tips cannot be fetched by object ID.
  The SSH gateway applies the same rule plus `receive.hideRefs`.
- Release files are content addressed and re-hashed before sending.
- Logs hold only time, request ID, operation, status, duration and byte count.
- The configuration accepts no key, token, password or credential field.

Schemas: configuration `www/docs/mirror-gateway-config.schema.json`; endpoint
manifest `www/docs/mirror-gateway-manifest.schema.json` (non-proxied public
A/AAAA origin, `mainProxyMode: direct`, `/{owner}/{repository}.git` template).
A node must prove its direct HTTPS endpoint before it is published.

## Identity helpers

The gateway delegates Ed25519 to two shell-free local commands, each reading one
bounded JSON object on stdin and writing one on stdout, with credential-like
environment variables removed. Neither response may contain a private-key field.
See [Headless mirror identity](headless-mirror-identity.md) for a VPS
implementation.

| Command | Input `type` | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `healthSignerCommand` | `forkmesh.health-challenge-signing` (`publicKey`, `messageBase64`, `messageSha256`) | `publicKey`, `signature` |
| `requestVerifierCommand` | `forkmesh.request-capability-verification` (adds `signature`) | `valid`, `publicKey` |

## Configuration

```bash
python3 tools/mirror_gateway.py --refs-sha256 /srv/forkmesh/mirrors/example.git
python3 tools/mirror_gateway.py --config /etc/forkmesh/mirror-gateway.json --check
python3 tools/mirror_gateway.py --config /etc/forkmesh/mirror-gateway.json
```

Main keys: `schemaVersion`, `node` (`name`, `publicKey`), `routerPublicKey`,
`publicOrigin`, `listen` (`host`, `port`), `manifestPath`,
`requestVerifierCommand`, `healthSignerCommand`, `limits`, and `repositories[]`
with `owner`, `name`, `visibility`, `enabled`, `gitDir`, `releaseStore` and
`integrity.expectedRefsSha256`.

- An omitted `visibility` is private. A private entry cannot be enabled or
  carry a storage path; it is never inspected or announced.
- `gitDir` must be an absolute, real, service-owned, non-world-writable bare
  repository. Public data is not encrypted; public `encryptedArchive` entries
  are rejected.
- An omitted `releaseStore` falls back to `<gitDir>/forkmesh-releases` when that
  is a real directory.

## Independent mirror operation

A mirror on its own hostname can offer browsing, clone, push, fork and pull
requests without the control plane. Every capability is opt-in and additive,
and none changes repository identity: dashboard, SSH and mirror URLs are
replaceable metadata over the same canonical repositories.

### Same-codebase dashboard

The gateway can serve the same website as the main App, from the build outputs
(`app/public/**`, `www/public/**`) stored as Git blobs in a mirrored public
repository, so dashboard updates arrive through ordinary sync under the
integrity pin. `api-client.js` resolves its API origin to `location.origin` on
non-canonical hosts.

```json
"dashboard": {
  "enabled": true,
  "assetsRepository": "<owner>/<repo>",
  "canonicalOrigin": "https://app.example.com",
  "sshOrigin": "ssh://git@ssh.example.com",
  "replicaPath": "/var/lib/forkmesh-mirror/gateway/dashboard-replica.json"
}
```

- `assetsRepository` must be an enabled public repository in the same file.
- `canonicalOrigin` receives `/login` and `/signup` when the browser holds no
  valid portable session grant. A mirror never receives passwords, controller
  tokens or session rows.
- `sshOrigin` is shown as each repository's clone/push URL.
- `replicaPath` is a `0600` last-good bundle of the controller's allowlisted
  public projections (`app/src/mirror_replica.py`,
  `app/src/public_snapshots.py`). It is not a database copy; failed refreshes
  keep the prior valid documents, and responses from it carry
  `X-ForkMesh-Replica: public-projection`.

Added routes: static pages and assets, read-only `/api/repositories`,
`/api/version` and `/api/repo/<owner>/<repo>/<read-op>` (alias of
`/v1/public/repositories/...`), plus `GET /api/accounts/sessions` and
`POST /api/accounts/session-handoff`, which accept only a controller-signed,
expiry-bounded grant and keep it in an HttpOnly cookie. Rendered documents are
held in bounded LRU caches invalidated on generation change (SIGHUP, or SIGUSR1
for the replica), never by time; large bodies stream.

### SSH writes without the control plane

`tools/ssh_gateway.py` and `tools/ssh_authorization_broker.py`
([git-ssh-gateway.md](git-ssh-gateway.md)) normally authorize through the
routing service. `localAuthorization.mode` adds `fallback` (a signed local
grants file consulted only when the service is unreachable, never after a
denial) or `local` (the grants file is the whole policy). Grants map a key to an
account and per-repository `read-only`, `read-write` or `pull-request` access;
`pull-request` may push only to `refs/heads/pr/<account>/*`.

### Contributor pull requests over SSH

With `pullSubmissionSpool` set, the forced command
`forkmesh-pull-submit <owner>/<repo>` accepts a signed pull request or review
comment on stdin, verifies its Ed25519 signature (`forkmesh-pull-event-v1` /
`forkmesh-pull-comment-v1`; the author field is the public key) and spools it
with per-key and global caps. A timer replays the spool to the controller:

```bash
python3 tools/ssh_gateway.py --config … spool-forward --api-origin https://app.example.com
```

Delivered items move to `forwarded/`, permanent failures to `rejected/`.

### Forking over SSH

With `dynamicRepositoriesPath` set (and the broker's
`localAuthorization.dynamicRepositoriesFile` pointing at the same file),
`forkmesh-fork <owner>/<repo>` clones heads and tags into a new bare repository
for the caller, registers it and refreshes the gateway. Global catalog
publication still goes through the owner's signed path.

### Push-created repositories

Set in the refresh configuration (`www/docs/headless-mirror-refresh.schema.json`),
never by hand in the generated gateway file:

| Key | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `writableRepositoryRoot` | absolute, real, mode-0700 directory owned by the mirror account |
| `writableOwners` | unique owner names (max 64), or exactly `["*"]`; removing an owner stops reads and pushes from the next refresh |
| `receiveMaxInputBytes` | optional, default 256 MiB; becomes `receive.maxInputSize` |

On a capability-bound push the gateway creates
`<writableRepositoryRoot>/<owner>/<repo>.git`, runs `git receive-pack` with
deletes and repository hooks refused and non-fast-forwards refused unless the
capability carries a `rewrite=` grant (then the gateway's own pre-receive
decides per ref and keeps each replaced tip under `refs/forkmesh/history/`;
see `docs/CORE_PUSH.md#force-pushes`), records it in
`hosted-pushes.json` (treated as untrusted input) and touches
`/run/forkmesh-mirror-refresh/pending` to trigger a refresh. At most two pushes
run at once (`503 push_busy`). The pushing device, not the node, publishes the
catalog record. These repositories are exempt from the immutable refs pin;
their generation is re-proved on every signed health check.

## Private replicas

Private repositories are never materialized by the gateway. They are stored
as opaque `.fm-private` files (`desktop/src/PrivateMirrorStore.cpp`): a random
id, an AES-256-GCM archive, hybrid X25519 + ML-KEM-768 key wraps per recipient
and a key epoch, with no names or paths. Rotation re-seals to the exact
recipient set. The gateway streams `/v1/private-replicas/<opaque-id>` only
under a routing capability and cannot decrypt it.

## Routing service contract

The routing service owns authorization, mirror selection and bounded failover.
Its database stores discovery and health metadata only. Generate its capability
key pair for `app/.env.production`:

```bash
python3 -c 'import base64;from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import Ed25519PrivateKey as K;from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization as s
k=K.generate();e=lambda b:base64.urlsafe_b64encode(b).decode().rstrip("=")
print("MIRROR_ROUTER_PUBLIC_KEY="+e(k.public_key().public_bytes(s.Encoding.Raw,s.PublicFormat.Raw)))
print("MIRROR_ROUTER_SIGNING_SEED="+e(k.private_bytes(s.Encoding.Raw,s.PrivateFormat.Raw,s.NoEncryption())))'
```

Keep the seed in the operator's secret store only; mirrors get the public key.
`deploy.sh secrets` preserves it; `deploy.sh rotate-mirror-router` changes it.

1. **Registration.** `POST /api/mirrors/https` (`node`, `baseUrl`,
   `mirrorUrl`, `publicKey`, `issuedAt`, `signature` over
   `forkmesh-https-endpoint-v2`). The service verifies the signed
   `/forkmesh-mirror.json` manifest, the SSRF policy and DNS.
2. **Signed health.** `GET /health?nonce=…&issuedAt=…[&owner=…&repo=…]`
   (`forkmesh-https-health-v1` / `forkmesh-https-health-repository-v1`)
   returns `available`, `integrity`, `refsSha256` and `operationsSha256`.
   Refs are checked against the owner-signed state; health is valid for two
   minutes.
3. **Capability.** `forkmesh-masked-proxy-v1` signature in `X-ForkMesh-Node`,
   `X-ForkMesh-Request-Id`, `X-ForkMesh-Issued-At`, `X-ForkMesh-Body-Sha256`
   and `X-ForkMesh-Signature`; request IDs are single-use for 60 seconds.
4. **Selection.** Upload-pack is redirected to a `mirrorUrl` only after a fresh
   proof there; other reads are proxied. Failover happens only before response
   bytes are sent; cookies, auth headers and client IPs are never forwarded.

## Operations

`/v1/repositories/<owner>/<repo>/<operation>` requires a capability.
`/v1/public/repositories/...` serves the GET/HEAD read operations of public
repositories without one.

| Operation | Method | Query | Response |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `git-info-refs` | GET/HEAD | `service=git-upload-pack` | upload-pack advertisement |
| `git-upload-pack` | POST | none | streamed pack (gzip allowed, 8 MiB request bound) |
| `merge-pull` | POST | typed JSON | asynchronous exact-OID merge via a configured executor |
| `update-pull-branch` | POST | typed JSON | merge base into a pull head |
| `actions-status` | GET | none | redacted run summaries for the repository |
| `actions-control` | POST | none; typed JSON ≤ 4 KiB | `202` once queued for the executor |
| `tree` / `blob` / `blobs` / `raw` | GET/HEAD | `path`, `ref` | bounded JSON or streamed bytes |
| `history` / `commit` / `branches` | GET/HEAD | `ref` / `path` | commit metadata |
| `search` / `stats` / `sizes` | GET/HEAD | `path`, `ref` | bounded results |
| `release-blob` | GET/HEAD | `sha256` | verified release bytes |

`actions-status` (`actionsSummaryPath`) and `actions-control`
(`actionsControlPath`, mode 0700) are off by default; the gateway is only a
courier and the executor re-verifies each request. See
[Mirror Actions control and summary v2](mirror-actions-control.md) and
[`mirror-actions-control.schema.json`](../mirror-actions-control.schema.json).
Upload-pack supports protocol v2 filters (`--filter=blob:none`) and shallow
clones.

## Cloudflare Tunnel fallback

For nodes without a reachable origin, `tools/cloudflare_tunnel_bootstrap.py`
provisions a Tunnel to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` and a signed manifest with
`mainProxyMode: masked`. It reads the API token from `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` or
stdin, supports `--dry-run`, and needs `--replace-dns` to overwrite DNS.
