pages.description: ForkMesh Ads is a first-party, text-only ad network. Members write short ads, a person reviews every one, and approved ads run on a product surface: the web app, the website, the…
pages.markdown:
# ForkMesh Ads

ForkMesh Ads is a first-party, text-only ad network. Members write short ads,
a person reviews every one, and approved ads run on a product surface: the web
app, the website, the desktop app, the mobile apps, and World.

Three rules govern it:

1. **Placement is by surface, never by viewer.** The serve call takes only a
   surface name; no session, account, location, or history is read, and the
   network never learns who saw an ad.
2. **A person approves the exact words that run.** Automated screening only
   raises flags.
3. **The [prohibited list](#what-is-never-accepted) always applies**, and any
   signed-in member can report an ad.

Approval is not an endorsement and expires after 180 days. This network is
separate from [community-reviewed placements](../community-ad-governance.md)
and does not change the [business-model contract](../business-model.md):
personal data is never sold or used for advertising.

## Who can advertise

Any verified account can submit ads. There is no ad billing or bidding; an
active membership level (read from `role_grants`, see [Patreon](patreon.md))
funds live slots:

| Level | Ads running at once | Rotation weight per ad |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free | 0 | — |
| Supporter | 1 | 1 |
| Pro | 2 | 2 |
| Builder | 5 | 5 |
| Studio | 10 | 10 |

Ads beyond the allowance wait; without a membership they pause. An account may
hold 25 ads and 5 pending review. The numbers live in the `advertising` block
of [`business-model.json`](/business-model.json) and are pinned by
`app/tests/test_ad_network.py`.

## What an ad is

A headline (60 characters), optional body (160), call-to-action label (24),
sponsor name (48), one public `https://` destination, one category, surfaces,
and an optional schedule. No images, scripts, embeds, or HTML. Clients render
plain text, label the slot **Sponsored**, and open the destination with
`rel="sponsored noopener noreferrer"`. Link shorteners and cross-site click
identifiers (`gclid`, `fbclid`, ...) are refused; `utm_*` tags are allowed.

Allowed categories cover developer tools, open source, hosting and
infrastructure, defensive security and privacy, education, events, hiring,
accessibility, nonprofits, climate, open hardware, independent software, and
community projects.

## What is never accepted

Gambling; tobacco, alcohol, and drugs; weapons; adult content; promised returns
or speculative tokens; predatory credit; unproven health claims; tracking, data
brokers, and stalkerware; malware or offensive hacking services; political
persuasion; hate or harassment; misleading or dark-pattern claims; illegal
goods; exploitative labor; anything aimed at children; destinations that
fingerprint, force downloads, or redirect through trackers. Reviewers cite these
rules by code. `GET /api/ads/policy` serves the machine-readable policy.

## Review

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `draft` | Saved, not submitted |
| `pending` | In the review queue |
| `approved` | May run, subject to membership, schedule, and slots |
| `rejected` | Declined with a reason and cited rules |
| `suspended` | Held by a reviewer; only a reviewer reinstates (back to `pending`) |
| `withdrawn` | Pulled by the owner |

- Reviewers are platform administrators (`users.is_admin = 1`) working at
  `/dashboard/ads`; the server enforces the role on every review route.
- Approval is pinned to the content hash of the words reviewed. An edit during
  review is refused (`creative_changed`); editing an approved ad's words sends
  it back to `pending`. Schedule changes and pauses need no review.
- Decisions are appended to `ad_network_reviews` and the audit log
  (`ad_network.approve|reject|suspend|reinstate`) without ad text. Self-review
  is allowed but recorded as such.
- Five open member reports on a running ad suspend it automatically.

## Serving and measurement

`GET /api/ads/serve?placement=web|www|desktop|mobile|world` returns one ad or
`null`. The pick is weighted by level and rotates on a five-minute bucket with
no randomness and no viewer input, so responses are cacheable
(`public, max-age=300`) and a suspension takes effect within five minutes.

The only measurement is an aggregate click counter per ad, surface, and UTC day
(`ad_network_daily_stats`, via `POST /api/ads/{id}/click`), with no viewer
columns, deleted after 400 days. Impressions are not measured, and nothing is
billed on clicks.

Clients send no credentials to the serve call, render nothing on failure, never
delay the host surface, let users hide a slot for seven days, keep legal and
documentation pages ad-free, and in World request a network ad only when no
community placement exists.

## Operating it

Storage is `ad_network_ads`, `ad_network_reviews`, `ad_network_reports`, and
`ad_network_daily_stats`. Ad text is public; the submitting username is sealed
and shown only to reviewers. Renaming an account moves its ads; deleting it
deletes ads, reports, and counters. The down migration drops the four tables
and touches no membership data. No third-party ad code runs anywhere, ads never
affect ranking or moderation, and self-hosted instances run their own
instance-local network.

pages.title: ForkMesh deployment and scheduled automation
pages.description: Isolated deployment and automation tools. None of them writes wallet keys, API tokens or GitHub tokens to the repository.
pages.markdown:
# ForkMesh deployment and scheduled automation

Isolated deployment and automation tools. None of them writes wallet keys, API
tokens or GitHub tokens to the repository.

## Cloudflare Worker, D1, DNS, and relay bootstrap

`tools/cloudflare_bootstrap.py` creates or reuses D1 and KV storage, applies all
migrations, deploys one complete App Worker, creates proxied DNS, attaches
one broad `hostname/*` App route, and verifies health, release identity, public
snapshots and an authenticated database/encryption probe. Repository bytes stay
on independently operated mirrors; Cloudflare provides discovery and routing.
`--main-relay-url https://app.forkmesh.com` joins the instance to an existing
relay mesh once that relay approves it.

The scoped API token needs only: Account Settings read, Workers Scripts edit,
Workers KV Storage edit, D1 edit, Cloudflare Tunnel edit, Zone read, and DNS
edit plus Workers Routes edit for the selected zone. With exactly one account
and one active zone, `--auto-configure` derives every name; otherwise pass
`--hostname`, `--zone`, `--worker-name`, `--database-name` and `--node-name`.

```bash
export CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN="locally-supplied-token"  # forkmesh-secret-scan:ignore-line
python3 tools/cloudflare_bootstrap.py --auto-configure
```

### Secrets and identities

- **`DATA_KEY`.** On a new database the bootstrap generates `DATA_KEY` with the
  OS CSPRNG, writes a mode-`0600` recovery copy outside the repository
  (`--data-key-backup` selects the path), uploads it as a Worker secret and
  proves D1 plus encryption work. Losing both copies makes encrypted data
  unrecoverable. A rerun without a recovery copy fails closed until the value
  is restored with `--secret-env DATA_KEY`.
- **Router identity.** A new one-click installation needs no
  router secret in the environment: an Ed25519 router seed and public key are
  generated, cross-checked and saved to an owner-only recovery file
  (`--router-identity-backup`). For a restore, supply
  `MIRROR_ROUTER_SIGNING_SEED` and `MIRROR_ROUTER_PUBLIC_KEY`; the seed must
  derive the key exactly. The seed is never put in argv, a temporary config,
  a log or JSON output. Staging uploads the signing seed
  first and the public key last, so an interrupted install fails closed.
- **Token handling.** There is no `--api-token` flag; the token reaches
  Wrangler only through the child environment. `--secret-env NAME` pipes other
  secrets to `wrangler secret put`. The checked-in `wrangler.toml` is untouched.

### Rerun safety

Before any change the bootstrap confirms the App Worker exists, that the
hostname has only proxied address records, and that only the canonical App
route overlaps it. A legacy exact control route is a blocker that
`--replace-route` cannot remove. It then reads the public App identity route
`https://<hostname>/api/mirrors/https`; an unavailable, redirected or
unexpected response fails before D1, DNS, routes, secrets or the Worker change,
and a local key can never rotate a published one. Success requires
`/api/mainnode` and `/api/version` to report the same build and the matching
key. `--dry-run` performs all checks without mutation. `--with-world` also
deploys the optional World Worker on its own hostname.

### Direct-HTTPS mirror discovery contract

Trusted mirrors publish `https://<mirror-host>/forkmesh-mirror.json`
(schema: `www/docs/mirror-endpoint.schema.json`), signed with the node's
Ed25519 key over sorted compact JSON (`forkmesh-json-sort-v1`). It names the
node key, health URL, repository URL template, `transport: direct-https`,
`mainProxyMode: masked` and `repositoryBytesInD1: false`. The node key comes
from `FORKMESH_NODE_PUBLIC_KEY`; signatures come from the shell-free command in
`FORKMESH_MIRROR_MANIFEST_SIGNER`. `--skip-mirror-manifest` installs a
relay-only node.

## Daily one-way GitHub issue synchronization

`.github/workflows/github-issue-sync.yml` (daily, manual runs default to
dry-run) copies issues from `FORKMESH_ISSUE_SYNC_SOURCE` to
`FORKMESH_ISSUE_SYNC_DESTINATION`, one direction only. Cross-repository runs
need `FORKMESH_ISSUE_SYNC_SOURCE_TOKEN` and
`FORKMESH_ISSUE_SYNC_DESTINATION_TOKEN` (or one `FORKMESH_ISSUE_SYNC_TOKEN`). A
hidden `forkmesh-issue-sync:v1` marker maps each copy and its content digest, so
unchanged issues are not rewritten. `tools/github_issue_sync.py sync` runs the
same logic locally with token names passed via `--*-token-env`. Until
`FORKMESH_ISSUE_SYNC_DESTINATION` is set, the scheduled run writes a notice
and skips the sync instead of failing; a manual run without it still fails.

## Native daily public-safe security scan

`tools/native_security_scan_runner.py` runs hourly on the owner's node, decides
whether a scan is due, and leases a one-use capability bound to the repository
and commit. `tools/security_scan.py` inventories lockfile dependencies against
OSV (names and versions only), flags credential-shaped content without
recording values, and runs focused static checks. Artifacts
(`security-scan.json`, `security-clipboard.json`, `security-scan.md`) contain no
source excerpts or secret values; offline runs keep them locally and retry. The
relay encrypts ingested reports with `DATA_KEY`, keeps the 90 newest per
repository, and serves `security-scans/latest` and `/history`: public
repositories expose the redacted clipboard, everything else needs owner
authorization. Reports are not a guarantee of security.

## External Solana signer and reward scheduling

`tools/reward_scheduler.py` selects one eligible, attested mirror per round from
a frozen snapshot using public entropy, and never generates or accepts a private
key. An external signer receives the intent on stdin and returns a signed
transaction; responses containing key material are rejected. Pending rewards
are 24-hour reservations; funds move only after the signer approves a claim.

pages.title: ForkMesh desktop control node
pages.description: The desktop client's Control page is the operator surface for the current device. It never makes ForkMesh a custodian. Its tabs are Site deployment, Export, Import, Mirror…
pages.markdown:
# ForkMesh desktop control node

The desktop client's **Control** page is the operator surface for the current
device. It never makes ForkMesh a custodian. Its tabs are Site deployment,
Export, Import, Mirror client, Repository permissions, Keys and wallet, Reward
pool, Cloudflare relay, and API token (`desktop/src/MainWindowControlNode.cpp`).
Host management lives under **Network → Hosts**.

## Mirror client and permissions

The status card shows the relay connection, tracked local mirrors, managed-node
repositories, and sync jobs. The desktop itself never serves repositories or
registers endpoints. **Sync all mirrors** fetches every mirror; **Run health
check** verifies the local identity, Git, bootstrap tooling, mirror paths, and
relay connection.

Per-repository permissions: **Private** (discovery and authorized access),
**Serve** (whether managed hosts may publish it), **Run actions** (local
`.forkmesh` workflows), and **Secret scan** (push protection). Only a device
holding the owner's signing identity can change visibility or serving, and
every change is recorded in the local audit log.

## Identity and wallet

The Ed25519 identity key is generated locally with owner-only permissions and
can be backed up as a passphrase-encrypted keyfile. The wallet field accepts
only a 32-byte base58 Solana public address and rejects seed phrases and
private keys. Connecting an address authorizes nothing; private keys stay in
the user's own wallet.

## Export, import, and deployment

- **Export complete system…** writes one `forkmesh-complete-system-v1` JSON
  file with every setting, Actions variable and secret, the deployment
  environment file, and all application data (identity, SSH keys, stores),
  each with size, mode, and SHA-256. It is written owner-only and refuses
  symlinks. It contains private keys in clear text: store it encrypted.
- **New deployment…** validates a bundle's schema, paths, sizes, and digests
  before showing values, then applies it and hands off to the durable host
  provisioner.

Deployment runs the bundled `tools/cloudflare_bootstrap.py`. With a token
scoped to one account and zone it discovers the topology; with several it
requires explicit selection rather than guessing. **Validate** is a read-only
dry run; **Deploy** creates or reuses the database, deploys the server,
configures DNS and routes, provisions the tunnel, and runs health checks.

Credential rules: the token is never saved by the deploy card, never placed in
process arguments, passed only as `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` in the child
environment, never turned into a server secret, and redacted from output. A
missing `cloudflared` is installed by a bundled installer that verifies pinned
SHA-256 digests. Endpoint manifests are signed by launching the desktop binary
with `--sign-mirror-manifest`, which validates the manifest and returns only the
public key and signature.

## API token

**Check token permissions** verifies a Cloudflare token, reads its own policy
when allowed, and probes each capability read-only (a read probe cannot prove
edit rights).

| Cloudflare permission | Used for |
| --- | --- |
| Account Settings: Read | discovering the account |
| Workers Scripts: Edit | uploading the server, assets, triggers, and secrets |
| D1: Edit | creating and migrating the database |
| Zone: Read | finding the zone |
| DNS: Edit | relay and mirror records |
| Cloudflare Tunnel: Edit | the mirror gateway tunnel |

Optional: Workers Tail: Read, API Tokens: Read/Edit. **Generate and install a
new token** mints a replacement scoped to the resolved account, zone, and user,
replaces `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` in the device variables and deployment
environment file (owner-only, other entries preserved), and re-checks it. The
new token is shown only by its last four characters; the old one stays valid
until deleted, allowing rollback.

## Connected hosts

**Network → Hosts** adds remote machines, installs, updates, or removes
ForkMesh, signs in agent CLIs, and shows logs. Every host operation
authenticates with one shared fleet SSH key generated on first use and kept
owner-only on the desktop. Passwords are an optional fallback, stay on the
desktop, and are passed via environment or stdin, never arguments.

## Reward-pool signer

The Control page hosts the local signer for the community reward pool; see
[Community reward-pool local signer](community-reward-pool-signer.md).

pages.title: Git SSH public-key authentication
pages.description: ForkMesh serves standard ssh:// clone and push URLs from an independently operated OpenSSH origin; the HTTP control plane never terminates SSH. There are two planes
pages.markdown:
# Git SSH public-key authentication

ForkMesh serves standard `ssh://` clone and push URLs from an independently
operated OpenSSH origin; the HTTP control plane never terminates SSH. There are
two planes:

1. **Control plane.** Stores each user's normalized public key in an encrypted
   envelope indexed by a keyed blind index, and enforces repository owner and
   organization-team permissions through `POST /api/ssh/authorize`
   (`lookup` during key authentication, `authorize` per Git operation).
2. **SSH origin.** [`tools/ssh_gateway.py`](../../../tools/ssh_gateway.py) runs as
   `AuthorizedKeysCommand` and as a forced command that executes only
   `git-upload-pack` or `git-receive-pack` against an exact local allowlist.

Private keys never leave the user's SSH agent or filesystem.

## Keys and permissions

Users register one OpenSSH public-key line at `/dashboard/settings/ssh-keys`.
Accepted: Ed25519 (including FIDO), ECDSA P-256/384/521 (including FIDO P-256),
RSA 3072–16384 bits. DSA, short RSA, key options, multiple lines and duplicate
or revoked keys are rejected with a generic error. A key grants no write by
itself: `git-receive-pack` needs ownership or `write`/`maintain`/`admin` through
an organization. Revocation applies on the next authentication. Ordinary Git
semantics (force-with-lease, force pushes) work unchanged; repository hooks are
disabled. Branch protection comes from an `operatorPolicy` block in the gateway
config, enforced by a gateway-owned `pre-receive` hook; see
[Node operator policy](node-operator-policy.md#protected-branches).

## Control-plane configuration

```dotenv
SSH_GATEWAY_HOST=ssh.example.org
SSH_GATEWAY_PORT=22
SSH_GATEWAY_TOKEN=<32-512 base64url characters>
SSH_GATEWAY_REPOSITORIES=owner/widget=read-write,owner/docs=read-only
```

No SSH URL is published unless all four are valid, and only for listed
repositories (`*` lists every repository; see [Relay mode](#relay-mode-self-hosted-instances)). The token authenticates the gateway's control-plane calls only.
`SSH_GATEWAY_REPOSITORIES` must equal the gateway's
`ssh-gateway-entrypoint worker-allowlist` output; set it to `disabled` to stop
publication.

Two optional settings harden the token:

```dotenv
SSH_GATEWAY_TOKEN_NEXT=<the next token, during a rotation>
SSH_GATEWAY_ALLOWED_ADDRESSES=203.0.113.7,2001:db8:7::/64
```

`/api/ssh/authorize` compares the bearer token in constant time against
`SSH_GATEWAY_TOKEN` and, when set, `SSH_GATEWAY_TOKEN_NEXT`; either is
accepted, so a token rotates without downtime: set the new one as `_NEXT`,
move the gateway host to it, then make it `SSH_GATEWAY_TOKEN` and remove
`_NEXT` (`install_ssh_relay.sh --rotate-token`, then `--finish-rotation`).
`SSH_GATEWAY_ALLOWED_ADDRESSES` additionally pins the gateway host: authorize
calls from any other address (as the edge sees it, `cf-connecting-ip`) get
401 even with the right token. A malformed list admits nobody.

## Node-side boundary

Four non-root accounts separate duties:

| Account | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `forkmesh-ssh-auth` | Holds the bearer token, runs the [authorization broker](../../../tools/ssh_authorization_broker.py) on a Unix socket, checks `SO_PEERCRED` |
| `forkmesh-ssh-lookup` | `AuthorizedKeysCommand`; may only send `lookup` |
| `git` | Forced Git service; may only send `authorize`; cannot read the token or node keys |
| `forkmesh-mirror` | Owns the bare repositories' signing and encryption material; no SSH login |

Configuration: `/etc/forkmesh/ssh-gateway.json` from
[`ssh-gateway.json.example`](../../../server/packaging/ssh/ssh-gateway.json.example),
validated by [`ssh-gateway-config.schema.json`](../ssh-gateway-config.schema.json).
Its `limits` block bounds concurrent sessions and processes (with slots reserved
for authorized pushes), upload/receive deadlines, `receiveMaxInputBytes`,
per-repository `maxStorageBytes` and pack threads. The forced command parses
`SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND` without a shell, accepts only Git protocol v1/v2 and one
`<owner>/<repository>.git`, runs Git with a fixed argv and clean environment,
disables hooks, credential helpers and the `ext` transport, and kills the whole
process group on timeout. The `99-forkmesh-git.conf` sshd `Match` block denies
passwords, forwarding and TTYs for `git`. Storage limits are application limits;
use filesystem quotas for a hard boundary.

After a successful receive a fixed root-owned notifier writes a coalesced
marker; a systemd path unit runs the
[headless refresh](headless-mirror-refresh.md) as `forkmesh-mirror`, verifies
signed health, and registers the new generation, retrying with capped backoff
(see [`ssh-post-receive-refresh.schema.json`](../ssh-post-receive-refresh.schema.json)).
`forkmesh-mirror-reconcile.timer` reconciles every 30 minutes.

Validate before reloading: `ssh-gateway-entrypoint check`, `sshd -t`, then
`systemctl reload sshd` with an administrative session kept open.

## Relay mode (self-hosted instances)

An instance that hosts its repositories on its own core node can accept SSH
without giving the gateway any access to repository storage. With an
`httpGit` block in place of `repositoryRoot`/`repositories`, the gateway
authorizes each operation as usual, then relays the session byte for byte to
the instance's own HTTPS Git routes:

```json
"httpGit": {"origin": "https://git.example.org", "connectAddress": "127.0.0.1:443"}
```

- **Every repository, no list.** Set `SSH_GATEWAY_REPOSITORIES=*`: hosted
  repositories and new forks work over SSH the moment they exist. Each
  `authorize` still checks the key's account against the repository, and the
  relayed request is checked again by the HTTPS route.
- **One push path.** `authorize` returns a credential for that key, account,
  repository and operation, valid for 30 minutes and revoked with the key.
  The relayed push is an ordinary HTTPS push: the full ref advertisement (only
  new objects are sent), branch protection rule by rule, contributor pushes to
  `refs/heads/pr/<account>/` (at most 32 branches) on repositories listed in
  `HOSTED_GIT_CONTRIBUTOR_PUSH`, quotas, and the attestation and push
  bookkeeping recorded after an accepted push.
- **Protocol.** Fetch is relayed as protocol v2 (Git 2.26 or newer; older
  clients add `-c protocol.version=2`). A push's pack is parsed to find its
  end; packs over 1 MiB stream chunked. `connectAddress` keeps the traffic on
  the host, so a CDN's request-size limit does not apply. Without it the
  origin's name is resolved through DNS, as on a separate front host (see
  [Keep the origin private](#keep-the-origin-private)).
- **Short addresses.** With short repository addresses on, `git@host:Repo.git`
  names the short-address owner's repository, as `/Repo` does on the web.

`tools/install_ssh_relay.sh --host ssh.example.org` installs the accounts,
the broker (`apiConnectAddress` set to the same loopback front end), the
configuration under `/etc/forkmesh-ssh`, the `SSH_GATEWAY_*` settings in
`app.env` (instance updates keep them), and the
[`60-forkmesh-git-relay.conf`](../../../server/packaging/ssh/60-forkmesh-git-relay.conf)
`Match User git` block, validated with `sshd -t` before a reload.
`--check` reports the state; `--uninstall` removes the drop-in, the broker
and the settings.

The relay's HTTP requests carry `User-Agent: git/forkmesh-ssh-relay`; the
broker's authorize calls carry `ForkMesh-ssh-authorization-broker/1.0`.

For users, once a key is registered in Settings:

```sh
ssh -T git@ssh.example.org                   # a greeting; there is no shell
git clone git@ssh.example.org:owner/repository.git
git push origin HEAD:pr/<account>/my-fix     # contributor branch, where allowed
```

## Keep the origin private

An instance behind a CDN proxy hides its address: its HTTPS name resolves to
the CDN, and its firewall admits only the CDN's ranges. SSH cannot go
through an HTTP proxy, so the SSH name needs a DNS-only record, and that
record is the address of whatever host runs the gateway. With the gateway
on the instance itself, `dig ssh.example.org` publishes the origin.

Run the gateway on a separate, disposable **front host** instead. In relay
mode it needs no repository storage and no instance secrets: it reaches the
control plane and the HTTPS Git routes only through the public HTTPS name,
resolved through ordinary DNS (to the CDN) with ordinary TLS verification.
Its configuration has no `connectAddress` and no `apiConnectAddress`, so the
origin's address appears nowhere on it. It holds two secrets: the gateway
token and its own SSH host key.

1. **A small VPS** (1 vCPU, 512 MB-1 GB, any provider; Debian or Ubuntu
   with OpenSSH 8.5 or newer and Python 3), and a source checkout on it,
   e.g. `git clone --depth 1 <source> /opt/forkmesh-src`. Firewall: the SSH
   port in, HTTPS out.
2. **On the instance**, issue the token and publish the SSH addresses
   without installing a gateway there:

   ```sh
   sudo bash tools/install_ssh_relay.sh --control-plane-only --host ssh.example.org
   ```

3. **Copy the token to the front over SSH, straight into the installer**, so
   it is never written anywhere else (not to a shell history, a clipboard or
   a temporary file):

   ```sh
   sudo cat /etc/forkmesh-ssh/ssh-gateway.token |
     ssh root@front 'bash /opt/forkmesh-src/tools/install_ssh_relay.sh \
       --remote-front --api-origin https://git.example.org \
       --host ssh.example.org --token-file -'
   ```

   `--print-config` instead of installing shows the configuration it would
   write. `--check` on the front probes `/api/ssh/authorize` through the
   CDN and says whether the token was accepted.
4. **DNS:** a DNS-only (not proxied) `A`/`AAAA` record for `ssh.example.org`
   pointing at the front only. The HTTPS name stays proxied.
5. Optionally pin the front on the instance:
   `SSH_GATEWAY_ALLOWED_ADDRESSES=<front address>` in `app.env`, then restart
   the app.

**CDN limits.** Everything the front relays crosses the CDN like any HTTPS
client's traffic:

- *Request size.* Cloudflare's Free and Pro plans accept request bodies up to
  100 MB (Business 200 MB, Enterprise 500 MB by default). A push is one
  request, so the front sets `maxRequestBytes` (`--max-request-mb`, default
  100; 0 for none) and stops a larger push before uploading it, telling the
  user to push fewer commits at a time. A 413 from the proxy itself gets the
  same explanation; the repository quota's own 413 keeps its message. Fetches
  are unaffected (responses are not capped).
- *Time.* Cloudflare waits up to 100 seconds for the origin's response to
  start. A push whose server-side checks take longer gets a 524; the user is
  told the push may still have landed and to `git fetch` before retrying.
  Large pushes are streamed chunked; the front's own socket timeout is 10
  minutes.
- *Bot protection.* Git clients are not browsers and cannot solve a
  challenge. If the zone challenges the front (a response with
  `cf-mitigated`), the user gets a message naming bot protection. Add a WAF
  custom rule with action *Skip* (managed rules, rate limiting and, on paid
  plans, Super Bot Fight Mode) matching
  `ip.src eq <front address> and lower(http.user_agent) contains "forkmesh-ssh"`,
  or turn off Bot Fight Mode, which a Free plan cannot skip. Match the
  front's address, never the bearer token: a token in a rule is a secret
  copied into the CDN's configuration.

**Abuse controls on the front.** The front sees real client addresses (the
origin sees only the CDN's). `--remote-front` adds:

- `59-forkmesh-front-limits.conf`: `MaxStartups 10:30:60`,
  `PerSourceMaxStartups 4` and `LoginGraceTime 20` for unauthenticated
  connections (global settings, fine on a dedicated host);
- `maxSessionsPerClient: 4` in `httpGit`: at most four concurrent Git
  sessions from one address (IPv6 by /64), on top of the host-wide
  `limits`;
- a fail2ban jail, `forkmesh-git-ssh` (the `sshd` filter in aggressive mode,
  10 failures in 10 minutes bans for an hour). It is written either way and
  runs once `fail2ban` is installed.

**Trade-offs.** Every SSH operation takes an extra hop through the front and
the CDN, and inherits the CDN's size and time limits. The front is a single
point of failure for SSH (HTTPS is unaffected): run two fronts with the
same token behind two DNS records, or keep a spare that a DNS change can
promote. The front is disposable: rebuild it from a checkout and the token,
and nothing else is lost (give it the same host key, or users see a host key
warning).

## Controller-free operation

By default every lookup and authorization is an HTTPS call, so a control-plane
outage stops SSH. An independent mirror can authorize locally by adding
`localAuthorization` to the broker config:

```json
"localAuthorization": {
  "mode": "fallback",
  "grantsFile": "/etc/forkmesh/ssh-local-grants.json",
  "dynamicRepositoriesFile": "/var/lib/forkmesh-mirror/gateway/dynamic-repositories.json"
}
```

- `fallback` consults the grants file only when the control plane is
  unreachable, never after an authoritative denial.
- `local` never contacts the control plane; the grants file is the whole policy.

The grants file (`type: forkmesh.ssh-local-grants`) lists each key, its account
and per-repository `access`: `read-only`, `read-write` or `pull-request` (push
only to `refs/heads/pr/<account>/*`). Setting `pullSubmissionSpool` accepts
signed pull submissions via `forkmesh-pull-submit <owner>/<repo>` and replays
them later with `ssh_gateway.py spool-forward`. Setting
`dynamicRepositoriesPath` enables `forkmesh-fork <owner>/<repo>`.

## Transport and round-robin origins

Plain proxied DNS does not carry SSH: use a DNS-only record, a TCP proxy, or a
tunnel with a client `ProxyCommand`, on a hostname separate from HTTPS.
`tools/provision_ssh_gateway.sh <host-ip>` installs a read-only gateway
idempotently. Every member keeps its own host key and presents a certificate
from the host CA (`tools/sign_ssh_host_certs.sh`, CA key outside the repository
via `FORKMESH_SSH_HOST_CA`, one-year validity), so clients trust one CA line
in `known_hosts`:

```text
@cert-authority ssh.forkmesh.com,*.forkmesh.com ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAII5OvM7x8w4o1auHqYiSObIWHaVdAy4tT8dxLOai76Vs
```

## Failure and privacy behavior

Unknown, revoked and wrong-account keys fail identically; missing and
unauthorized repositories give the same denial. The gateway never runs a shell,
logs no paths, IPs, key material or tokens, and the broker returns no account
principal. The per-client session cap keys its lock files by a truncated hash
of the client address, in `/run` only. Account renames follow the key; account deletion removes its keys.

pages.markdown:
# Headless mirror identity

`tools/headless_mirror_identity.py` is the local cryptographic boundary for a
non-GUI mirror host. It runs as the same dedicated, unprivileged account as
`mirror_gateway.py` and:

- keeps one Ed25519 node identity and one age identity in an owner-only
  directory;
- signs only the bounded manifest, health, reclaim, registration, and public
  catalog-v2/state protocols, building each canonical message itself (there is
  no arbitrary-message signing);
- verifies routing capabilities only with the configured router public key.

It takes no private key, seed, token, or password on the command line. Requests
are bounded JSON on standard input; responses hold only public keys,
signatures, hashes, and public records.

Requirements: Python 3.12+, `cryptography`, `age`/`age-keygen`, and Git. The
identity directory must be an absolute path with mode `0700` (files `0600`),
outside any checkout, image, or shared repository.

## Initialize and configure

```bash
printf '%s\n' '{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "type": "forkmesh.headless-mirror-identity-init",
  "nodeName": "mirror-two",
  "routerPublicKey": "<MIRROR_ROUTER_PUBLIC_KEY>",
  "allowedOrigins": ["https://mirror.example.org"]
}' | python3 tools/headless_mirror_identity.py \
  --state-dir /var/lib/forkmesh/identity init
```

All values are public. `allowedOrigins` pins which hostnames the node key will
sign for. `init` is idempotent and reuses a valid existing key after an
interruption. `public-info` prints the public half. `configure`
(`forkmesh.headless-mirror-identity-configure`) changes only the router key and
origin pins, never the private identities.

## Gateway integration

Reference the helper from the gateway configuration as direct command arrays,
never through a shell:

```json
{
  "requestVerifierCommand": ["/usr/bin/python3", "/opt/forkmesh/tools/headless_mirror_identity.py",
    "--state-dir", "/var/lib/forkmesh/identity", "capability-verify"],
  "healthSignerCommand": ["/usr/bin/python3", "/opt/forkmesh/tools/headless_mirror_identity.py",
    "--state-dir", "/var/lib/forkmesh/identity", "health-sign"]
}
```

Public repositories are served straight from the bare repository with an
`integrity.expectedRefsSha256` pin; the age seal/materialize modes exist only
for upgrade compatibility. `manifest-sign` signs endpoint manifests for a
tunnel or public HTTPS origin, using `nodePublicKey` from `public-info`.

After each push, the refresh orchestrator computes the heads-and-tags pin and
atomically installs a gateway configuration pointing at the bare repository; it
skips archives and full fsck, which the periodic `check` command runs.

Run the service with a restrictive umask, no privilege escalation, a read-only
application tree, and write access only to identity, repository, and gateway
state. The gateway listens only on loopback behind a TLS proxy or tunnel.

## Operator-only signatures

These modes are for local operator use only, never exposed over HTTP:

- `sign-reclaim` (`forkmesh.account-reclaim-signing`: `nodeName`, six-digit
  `linkCode`) returns the `/api/accounts/reclaim-node` body.
- `sign-endpoint-registration` (`forkmesh.https-endpoint-registration-signing`:
  `node`, `baseUrl`) returns the `/api/mirrors/https` body.
- `sign-catalog-v2` (`forkmesh.catalog-v2-publication-signing`: a public
  `record` with `owner`, `name`, `visibility: "public"`, and `stateHash`)
  returns the record with `stateSig` and `catalogSig` for `/api/repositories`.

## Key handling and rotation

Back up the identity directory through an encrypted, owner-controlled process;
it cannot be recovered. File permissions do not protect against root or a
compromised service account; use an encrypted volume or hardware signer when
that matters. To rotate the router key, update the server first, then run
`configure` on each mirror. To rotate the node identity, provision a new state
directory, reclaim the node, republish manifests and catalog state, verify
health, and retire the old directory.

pages.title: Headless mirror refresh and publication
pages.description: tools/headless_mirror_refresh.py is the fail-closed bridge between an SSH-writable bare Git repository and mirror_gateway.py. It never loads a node private key, age identity, API…
pages.markdown:
# Headless mirror refresh and publication

`tools/headless_mirror_refresh.py` is the fail-closed bridge between an
SSH-writable bare Git repository and `mirror_gateway.py`. It never loads a node
private key, age identity, API token or wallet key: all signing and encryption
go through the bounded protocol of `headless_mirror_identity.py`.

## Modes

| Mode | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `refresh` | `git fsck --full --strict` on the bare source, new age-encrypted snapshot, staged gateway config validated with `mirror_gateway.py --check`, then atomically installed |
| `register` | Re-validates the active generation, then signs and POSTs the endpoint registration (`/api/mirrors/https`) and the catalog-v2 record (`/api/repositories`) |
| `renew` | Re-authenticates the active generation and republishes the signed endpoint/catalog lease, without fsck or a second materialization |
| `check` | Full active-state validation with no network and no reseal (too slow for `ExecStartPre`; use the gateway's own `--check` there) |
| `configure-actions` | Reads one boolean request on stdin and changes only `catalog.actionsEnabled`, then publishes like `renew` |

The intended sequence is `refresh` → restart the gateway → `register`, so the
catalog never advertises refs the running gateway does not serve. A failed
`register` leaves the valid generation active and can simply be retried.

## Configuration

The contract is `www/docs/headless-mirror-refresh.schema.json`
(`type: forkmesh.headless-mirror-refresh`). The runtime also rejects duplicate,
unknown and secret-shaped fields, oversized JSON, unsafe modes, wrong owners and
symlinks. Key fields:

- Paths: `sourceRepository` (a real bare repository), `archiveDirectory`,
  `gatewayConfigPath`, `identityStateDirectory`, `manifestPath`, optional
  `releaseStore`, and the program paths for Python, Git, the gateway and the
  identity helper.
- Identity: `nodeOwner` must match the identity helper's `public-info` and
  appear in `ownerAliases`; every alias is a gateway route onto the same refs,
  but only `nodeOwner` is published to the catalog.
- Origins: `workerOrigin`, `publicOrigin` and optional `mirrorUrl` are
  credential-free HTTPS origins pinned by the node identity.
- `operations`: the read operations to serve. `merge-pull` adds a fixed
  `mergeExecutorCommand` that verifies the pinned pull, stages objects in an
  owner-only quarantine and journal, and moves `main` and `forkmesh/pulls` in one
  compare-and-swap. `actions-status` and `actions-control` expose the
  [Actions summary and control](mirror-actions-control.md) files.
  `git-receive-pack` is never accepted here.
- Push hosting: `writableRepositoryRoot`, `writableOwners` (named owners or
  `["*"]`) and `receiveMaxInputBytes`; absent on a read-only node. See
  [direct-HTTPS mirror gateway](direct-https-mirror-gateway.md).
- `catalog`: description, branch, `actionsEnabled`, and opt-in
  `reportCpu`/`reportMemory`/`reportDisk` aggregates. Unavailable readings are
  omitted, never reported as zero.

Never put a seed phrase, private key, token or password in this file.

## Storage and permissions

Run the identity helper, refresh tool and gateway as one dedicated
unprivileged account. The config is a single-link `0600` file; identity,
archive and gateway-state directories are `0700` and owned by that account;
programs are not group- or world-writable; no sensitive path may traverse a
symlink. Set `TMPDIR` to an owner-only disk-backed directory sized for two
expanded copies when `/tmp` is a small tmpfs. Under systemd keep
`ProtectSystem=strict` and grant `ReadWritePaths` only to the identity, archive,
gateway-state, temp and bare-source directories.

## Running it

```bash
python3 -I headless_mirror_refresh.py --config <mirror-refresh.json> refresh
python3 -I headless_mirror_refresh.py --config <mirror-refresh.json> register
```

Output is a minimal JSON object such as
`{"aliasCount":2,"event":"refresh_complete","ok":true}`; paths, names, Git
output and remote bodies are never printed. HTTP calls disable redirects and
ambient proxies and bound response sizes.

`forkmesh-mirror-renew.timer` (in `server/packaging/systemd/`) runs `renew`
every four minutes, inside the ten-minute endpoint lease, so a dead mirror drops
out of routing. All modes share one owner-only lock.

After an SSH push (see [Git SSH gateway](git-ssh-gateway.md)) a systemd path
unit runs: `refresh` → restart gateway → verify signed health over loopback and
the public origin → `register`. Concurrent ref movement during sealing fails the
refresh so the next notification retries.

## Last-good and recovery

Archives are stored under content-addressed names and the generated gateway
JSON is the only active pointer, replaced atomically after fsck, sealing, ref
stability and `--check` all pass. Old ciphertext is never deleted
automatically. If `register` fails, confirm the gateway is live and rerun
`check` and `register`; if `check` reports source drift, run the full sequence.

pages.title: Legacy Solana custody migration
pages.description: The live server is non-custodial: it never creates, accepts, signs with, or broadcasts a Solana private key. Older deployments may still hold encrypted wallet seeds in…
pages.markdown:
# Legacy Solana custody migration

The live server is non-custodial: it never creates, accepts, signs with, or
broadcasts a Solana private key. Older deployments may still hold encrypted
wallet seeds in compatibility rows from retired signup-deposit, issue-bounty,
bounty-wallet, federated-signup, or central-fund flows. Until every such key is
migrated and scrubbed, the server refuses to start its database-backed API and
reports `legacy_custody_migration_required`.

`tools/legacy_solana_custody.py` performs the migration offline against an
exported SQLite snapshot. It never signs or submits a transaction, never moves
funds, never prints a seed, and never contacts the live database.

## Safety invariants

- Work on a trusted, tightly controlled machine with `umask 077`; quiesce
  server writes for the final snapshot; keep an encrypted database backup.
- Pass `DATA_KEY`, the artifact passphrase, and any RPC URL through hidden
  prompts or environment variables (`FORKMESH_LEGACY_DATA_KEY`,
  `FORKMESH_CUSTODY_ARTIFACT_PASSPHRASE`, `FORKMESH_SOLANA_RPC_URL`), never
  arguments. The passphrase must be new, at least 16 characters, and differ
  from `DATA_KEY`.
- Move funds manually with trusted wallet tooling.
- Never scrub while any inventoried address has a nonzero or unknown balance,
  and never send new funds to a historical address.

## Procedure

1. **Inventory.** Export the database to SQLite, then run `inventory --database
   <snapshot> --network mainnet-beta --output audit.json`. Every row is
   decrypted, each seed must derive its stored address, and finalized balances
   are fetched; any error aborts the whole run.
2. **Export.** `export ... --artifact legacy.fmcustody` writes an AES-256-GCM
   artifact keyed by scrypt from the new passphrase. Seeds exist only inside the
   ciphertext; the file is owner-only and never overwritten. Verify the owner
   can open it before continuing. The tool intentionally has no “sweep” command.
3. **Move funds externally** and rerun `inventory` on fresh snapshots until
   every address reports exactly zero.
4. **Confirm.** Create an owner-only confirmation file:

   ```json
   {
     "format": "forkmesh-legacy-solana-scrub-confirmation-v1",
     "artifactSha256": "64-lowercase-hex-characters",
     "auditSha256": "64-lowercase-hex-characters",
     "confirmedAt": 1784815200000,
     "confirmation": "I HAVE IMPORTED EVERY LEGACY KEY AND RECONCILED EVERY ADDRESS AT ZERO"
   }
   ```

5. **Prepare the scrub.** `prepare-scrub --database <final snapshot> --artifact
   ... --confirmation ... --output-sql scrub.sql` re-verifies the artifact,
   digests, phrase, exact record set, and zero balances, then writes (but does
   not apply) a SQL patch. The patch removes key fields and key-bearing rows
   using the original ciphertext in every predicate, aborts unless each change
   hits exactly one audited row, records key-free evidence in
   `legacy_custody_reconciliation` and a receipt in
   `legacy_custody_migration_audit`, sets the readiness marker last, and is
   idempotent. Do not add `BEGIN`/`COMMIT`; the database's file ingestion
   supplies the transaction.
6. **Apply and verify** through the normal database change process, then export
   again: `inventory` must find zero key-bearing records, the audit table must
   hold one `scrubbed` receipt, and the readiness marker must be `clean-v2:`.

If the guarded update fails, never remove the guard: take a fresh snapshot,
determine what changed, and repeat the audit.

## Retained data

After the scrub, account rows keep only historical public donation fields, and
the retired compatibility tables are empty. The only evidence kept is the public
address, finalized zero balance, RPC slot, timestamp, source-table label, and
digests.

pages.description: The website's repository Actions tab reads run state from, and sends control requests to, a mirror node running the Actions executor. This page is the wire contract between
pages.markdown:
# Mirror Actions control and summary v2

The website's repository **Actions** tab reads run state from, and sends
control requests to, a mirror node running the Actions executor. This page is
the wire contract between:

| Component | File |
| --- | --- |
| Website | `app/public/dashboard/js/06-repo-actions.js` |
| Relay server | `app/src/repository_actions.py` |
| Mirror gateway | `tools/mirror_gateway.py` |
| Executor (Go mirror daemon) | `server/actions.go`, `server/actions_control.go`, `server/actions_workflow.go` |

The Go daemon (`forkmesh-mirror-node`) is the executor: it runs workflows,
writes the summary, and consumes control requests. Desktops that publish their
own runs still write a read-only version 1 summary. Nothing here can enable an
executor its operator turned off.

## Enabling Actions on a mirror

Actions run repository-supplied shell, so they are opt-in and fail closed:

1. Deploy a matching gateway and daemon (the daemon names Actions keys only
   when its gateway understands them).
2. Install `server/packaging/systemd/forkmesh-mirror-node-actions.conf` as a
   drop-in for `forkmesh-mirror-node.service`; it allows the namespaces
   `bubblewrap` needs.
3. Set `"enableActions": true` in `mirror-node.json` and restart.

At start the daemon probes a sandbox. On failure it logs `mirror actions are
unavailable: …`, runs nothing, and advertises neither `actions-status` nor
`actions-control`; it never runs a step unsandboxed.

Each step runs under `bwrap --unshare-all --clearenv` with no outbound network,
read-only system directories, a `git archive` export of the commit at
`/workspace`, a scratch home and `/tmp`, and only `PATH`, `HOME`, `LANG`, `CI`,
`FORKMESH_*` run variables, and the workflow's own `env:`. Steps cannot see node
state, identity keys, or other repositories. **A mirror holds no Actions
variables**, so workflows needing secrets or network belong on the owner's own
node (`runs-on:`).

Triggers: `on: push` when a branch head moves (default branch only unless
`on.push.branches` is set; `paths` honoured; ledger branches ignored) and
`on: workflow_dispatch`. `runs-on:` matches the node name, `linux`, and
`mirror`; `needs:` waits for another workflow's success on the same commit.
`pull_request` and `release` runs do not start on mirrors. Limits: one run at a
time, one hour per run, 8 MiB of log, twenty queued, fifty kept; newer pushes
supersede queued runs of the same workflow and branch.

## Trust model

The internet-facing gateway is less trusted than the executor. The executor
writes `actions-summary.json`; the gateway only reads it. For control, the
gateway is a **courier, not an authority**: it stores the router capability
beside the exact request body, and the executor verifies the Ed25519 signature
itself. A compromised gateway can drop or delay a request but cannot author,
alter, or replay one. Authorization requires a session that is the repository
owner, an owner of the node, or an organization writer (checked and audited by
the server) **and** the router key.

## Operation `actions-control`

`POST /v1/repositories/{owner}/{repository}/actions-control`

- Listed in `PUBLIC_OPERATIONS` only; always requires the signed router
  capability; no query parameters.
- Requires `actions-status` and an `actionsControlPath` that is an absolute,
  owner-only (`0700`), non-symlink directory named `actions-control`.
- Body: at most 4 KiB of JSON with exact keys.

| Key | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `schemaVersion` | `1` |
| `type` | `"forkmesh.actions-control-v1"` |
| `requestId` | `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,64}$`, idempotency key |
| `action` | see below |
| `actor` | `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$` |
| `issuedAt` | integer ms, within ±60 s of the gateway clock |

| `action` | Extra keys |
| --- | --- |
| `dispatch` | `workflow`, `ref` |
| `rerun`, `cancel`, `approve`, `reject` | `runId` |
| `set-workflow-enabled` | `workflow`, `enabled` |
| `set-repository-enabled` | `enabled` |

`workflow` matches `^\.forkmesh/[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,96}\.ya?ml$`; `ref` matches
`^refs/heads/[A-Za-z0-9._/-]{1,200}$` without `..`, `//`, or a trailing `/` or
`.lock`; `runId` is an integer `1 … 2^53-1`.

### Gateway behaviour

1. Validate the body exactly.
2. Refuse when the summary cannot be loaded or is still version 1.
3. Atomically write `{actionsControlPath}/{requestId}.json` (`O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW`,
   `0640`, fsync, rename) as an envelope of type
   `forkmesh.mirror-actions-control` holding `node`, `owner`, `repository`,
   `receivedAt`, the `capability` (method, path, request id, issued-at, body
   SHA-256, signature), and the exact `body` string.
4. A repeated `requestId` with an identical body is accepted again; a different
   body fails.
5. Keep at most 32 pending files; files older than 10 minutes are removed.
6. Success is `202 {"ok":true,"status":"accepted","requestId":"…","node":"…"}`
   with `Cache-Control: no-store`; every refusal is the uniform
   `404 {"ok":false,"error":"not_found"}`.

### Executor behaviour

A 4-second loop reads each regular, single-link `*.json` file (≤ 16 KiB) and:

1. checks exact keys, its own `node`, and the owner/repository path;
2. recomputes `sha256(body)` against `capability.bodySha256`;
3. verifies the signature over
   `forkmesh-masked-proxy-v1\n<node>\nPOST\n<path>\n<bodySha256>\n<requestId>\n<issuedAt>`
   with the configured `routerPublicKey`;
4. rejects capabilities older than 10 minutes and any `requestId` in its saved
   ring of the last 256 (persisted before applying, so a request never runs
   twice);
5. parses the body, deletes the file, applies the action, and records the
   outcome.

| Action | Effect | Rejection reasons |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dispatch` | Run a workflow with `workflow_dispatch` at `ref` | `repository_not_found`, `actions_disabled`, `ref_not_found`, `workflow_not_found`, `workflow_invalid`, `not_manual`, `workflow_disabled`, `wrong_node` |
| `rerun` | New run of the same workflow and commit | `run_not_found`, `actions_disabled`, `wrong_node` |
| `cancel` | Stop or dequeue a run | `run_not_found`, `not_cancellable` |
| `approve` / `reject` | Nothing on a mirror awaits approval | `run_not_found`, `not_awaiting_approval` |
| `set-workflow-enabled` | Toggle the path in `disabledWorkflows` | `repository_not_found`, `workflow_not_found` |
| `set-repository-enabled` | Toggle `webDisabled` (can only narrow `enableActions`) | `repository_not_found` |

A `runId` from another repository is `run_not_found`.

## Summary v2 (`actions-summary.json`)

Readers accept `schemaVersion` 1 and 2; the Go runner writes 2. Version 2 adds:

- per run: `workflowPath`, `pullNumber` (0 if none), and up to 64 `steps` of
  `{"name","status"}` with status `pending | running | success | failed |
  skipped | cancelled`;
- `repositories` (≤ 64): `{"owner","repository","actionsEnabled","workflows"}`,
  each workflow (≤ 32) `{"path","name","events","manual","enabled","runsOn","valid"}`;
- `controls` (≤ 32, newest first): `{"owner","repository","requestId","action",
  "status","reason","runId","finishedAt"}` with status `applied | rejected`.

No workflow content, commands, variables, or local paths appear. The 256 KiB
bound applies, trimming log tails first. The gateway filters the response to
the requested repository; a repository without an entry reports
`actionsEnabled: false` and empty `workflows`.

## Server routes

| Route | Method | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/api/repo/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs` | GET | Revalidates and passes through v2 fields; adds `controlAvailable`. |
| `/api/repo/{owner}/{repo}/actions/control` | POST | Session required; audited as `repository.actions_control`. Browser sends `node`, `requestId`, `action`, action keys; the server adds `schemaVersion`, `type`, `actor`, `issuedAt`. |

The request goes only to the node named by `node` (run ids are per executor);
`node` is not forwarded in the gateway body. Responses: `202` accepted; `400`,
`401`, `403`, `404`, `405`, `413`; or `503 {"error":"actions_node_unavailable"}`
with the expected-degraded header. The browser learns the outcome from the next
`actions/runs` poll.

pages.title: Mirror node service
pages.description: forkmesh-mirror-node is the headless Go runtime for a public mirror host. It synchronizes repositories, supervises the loopback Git gateway (and optionally a Cloudflare Tunnel)…
pages.markdown:
# Mirror node service

`forkmesh-mirror-node` is the headless Go runtime for a public mirror host. It
synchronizes repositories, supervises the loopback Git gateway (and optionally a
Cloudflare Tunnel), publishes the node's signed catalog record and endpoint
lease, runs collaboration intake, and can execute owner-authorized merges and
website agent jobs. No desktop app or GUI process is involved.

## Architecture

- **Operator API, loopback only.** `GET /healthz` (event loop alive),
  `GET /readyz` (gateway running and a recent successful sync), `GET /v1/status`
  (bounded, secret-free process, sync and ref state) and `POST /v1/control/sync`
  (sync doorbell).
- **Gateway.** Listens on `127.0.0.1:8790` behind an operator-managed HTTPS
  reverse proxy. Set `disableCloudflared` when that origin is directly
  reachable; otherwise the daemon supervises Cloudflare Tunnel as a fallback.
  `mirrorUrl` advertises a separate direct Git origin while `publicOrigin`
  stays the Tunnel control endpoint.
- **Identity.** The owner-only Ed25519 node key (and the connector token, when
  enabled) is never accepted in argv, JSON, an HTTP request or a catalog record.
- **Event socket.** One WebSocket to the relay's per-owner node event channel
  (`wss://…/api/nodes/events`), authenticated with the node key. The relay
  pushes payload-free `{"type":"event","topic","repo"}` frames.

## Data flow

- **Collaboration intake.** An issue, pull or discussion frame makes the daemon
  lease only the changed inbox, write the repository-native record in a
  temporary worktree, commit it, and acknowledge the exact rows with a signed
  refs attestation. There is no poll; every reconnect fires one catch-up drain.
- **Repository sync.** A `commits` frame triggers a fetch. It carries the
  source's signed refs digest, so a fetch from a stale peer is retried on a
  2s→15s backoff until that generation lands. Direct pushes to a managed host
  ring the doorbell from a service-owned `post-receive` hook. Peers listed in
  `eventDrivenUpstreams` are push-notified; upstreams that cannot push use
  `syncInterval`. One reconciliation every 30 minutes covers a lost event.
- **Catalog and lease.** A four-minute heartbeat republishes the catalog record
  and renews the endpoint lease from local refs reads, over the event socket
  when the relay advertises that frame and over HTTPS otherwise.
- **First clone.** Until a repository has a readable clone the daemon retries it
  on 15s→5m backoff; the gateway refuses to serve refs it cannot pin
  (`integrity.expectedRefsSha256`). `journalctl -u forkmesh-mirror-node` shows
  the chain.

## Owner-authorized web merges

Every served repository advertises `merge-preview`, `merge-pull` and
`update-pull-branch`. The gateway's `mergeExecutorCommand` points at this binary
(`forkmesh-mirror-node --config … --execute-mirror-merge`). The relay
authenticates the account (an owner to merge; for `update-pull-branch`, anyone
who may push the pull's head branch), signs the exact-OID request and hands it
to one healthy mirror. The executor verifies the pinned pull record on the `forkmesh/pulls`
ledger, the base and head tips, the peer-review gate (an owner may waive it with
`overrideReview`) and any `.forkmesh/required-checks.json` policy, then moves the
base branch, the ledger and `forkmesh/pull/<n>` in one atomic `update-ref`.
Patch-backed pulls are replayed onto the exact base in a temporary worktree,
preserving authorship. The result carries a node-signed refs attestation that
the relay admits as the repository's current generation and announces with a
`commits` event. Nothing rewinds a ref: a stale pin fails closed. Job state lives
under `mirror-gateway/pull-jobs/` (owner-only). `"disableMergeExecutor": true`
keeps a node strictly read-only.

## Running website agent jobs

A node that finds `claude` or `codex` on its PATH (or Ollama beside Codex, for
`local-llama`) advertises those providers and runs sessions the website queues
for it. The relay rings the socket with an `org-agents` push; the daemon claims
the job over the signed `org-agent-jobs` lease. For each job it validates the
envelope (provider, model allowlist, prompt of at most 8,000 characters, kind
`start`/`continue`/`steer`, target node and repository), fetches up to five
verified image attachments, clones into `mirror-gateway/agent-jobs/work/`, runs
the provider on a new `agent/web-<job>-<title>` branch (never `main`), pushes
the branch, optionally opens a node-signed pull, and reports status, transcript,
token counts and cost. A run is capped at two hours; a failed run reports one
bounded `lastError`. The browser can sign a provider CLI in through a relayed
pseudo-terminal that runs only the provider's own login command.
`"disableAgentJobs": true` and `"disableAgentLogin": true` turn these off.

## Policy, hardening and logs

- Storage limits, takedowns and protected branches: see the
  [node operator policy guide](node-operator-policy.md).
- Key-only SSH (`server/packaging/ssh/10-forkmesh-hardening.conf`) and a
  fail2ban `sshd` jail (`server/packaging/fail2ban/forkmesh-sshd.local`).
- The gateway streams the host journal at `GET /v1/node/logs` to Ed25519 viewer
  keys in `/etc/forkmesh/log-viewer-keys` (signed, single-use requests).

## Setup

Start from `server/packaging/systemd/mirror-node.json.example`. Upstream lists
may hold several URLs, tried in order. For a tunnel-free bootstrap pass
`--disable-cloudflared` with the public HTTPS origin; the node then advertises
`https://<origin>/<owner>/<repository>.git` behind a signed direct-origin
manifest. Independent dashboard, SSH writes and forks are covered in
[direct-HTTPS mirror gateway](direct-https-mirror-gateway.md); backups,
`--preflight` and key moves in
[node backup, recovery, and key moves](node-backup-and-recovery.md).

## Build and test

```sh
cd server
go test -race -cover ./...
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -ldflags='-s -w' \
  -o forkmesh-mirror-node ./cmd/forkmesh-mirror-node
```

## Rolling migration

1. Install the binary, configuration and unit without stopping the old node.
2. Run `forkmesh-mirror-node --config ... --check` and `--preflight` as
   `forkmesh-node`.
3. Start `forkmesh-mirror-node` and confirm `/readyz`.
4. Remove any retired compatibility unit.
5. Confirm signed external health, one pushed collaboration submission and one
   clone before moving to the next host.

Keep the prior unit and binary as rollback artifacts until the whole fleet has
passed reachability checks.

pages.title: Mobile push notifications (APNs)
pages.description: Apple Push Notification service wakes the iOS app when iOS has suspended or killed it, the one case the account event socket cannot cover (see polling elimination). A write that…
pages.markdown:
# Mobile push notifications (APNs)

Apple Push Notification service wakes the iOS app when iOS has suspended or
killed it, the one case the account event socket cannot cover (see
[polling elimination](polling-elimination.md)). A write that changes an unread
count calls `notify_account_event`, which sends a payload-free socket frame
and, for the topics below, one alert to every phone registered to the account.

There is no third-party push provider: the server signs its own APNs provider
token and posts to Apple directly (`app/src/apns.py`). On the phone,
`native/ios/ForkMesh/Platform/ApplePushBridge.swift` registers the device and
the `native/ios/NotificationService` extension enriches each banner.

## Payloads

Every alert names its event; nothing generic is sent. Device tokens are stored
encrypted under a blind-index row key.

| Line | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| Title | Record and headline, e.g. `#42 Issue submitted` |
| Subtitle | `owner/repo · by actor` |
| Body | The notification body, up to 900 characters |
| Image, badge | Actor avatar and unread count, added on the phone |

Alerts set `mutable-content` and `thread-id` (per repository or conversation).
The extension reads `GET /api/push/alert` (unread rows, own account only) with
the session shared through the app's keychain group, stored
`AfterFirstUnlock`; Keychain Sharing must be enabled on both App IDs. If the
read fails, the banner keeps the server text.

Chat and direct-message text is end-to-end encrypted: the alert carries only
the relay `ref`, `keyVersion`, and `channelId`, and the extension fetches and
decrypts the ciphertext on the phone, falling back to "End-to-end encrypted".
Every payload includes `origin`, `alertId`, and `href` so a phone signed in to
several deployments routes taps correctly.

## Topics

`APNS_PUSH_TOPICS`: `pings`, `code-push`, `direct-messages`, and `chat`.
`catalog` and `issues` are freshness hints and never alert.

- Each ping and each direct message is its own banner (no collapse id).
- `code-push` (kind `code_push`) fires on observed pushes for readers of the
  repository, at most one banner per recipient per branch per 60 seconds, and
  can be turned off in ping settings.
- Chat alerts require the sender to set plaintext `notify: true` on a `chat` or
  `thread-reply` envelope. Audience: the other participant of a direct message,
  members of a private channel, or every registered phone for public channels
  and rooms, minus the sender where known; at most 32 phones per message and
  one push per room every two seconds.

## Configuration

`push_account_apns` is a no-op unless all three secrets are set; deploy refuses
to run without them.

| Secret | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `APNS_AUTH_KEY` | The `.p8` APNs key with its PEM armour (literal `\n` accepted). |
| `APNS_KEY_ID` | The ten-character Key ID. |
| `APNS_TEAM_ID` | The ten-character developer Team ID. |

The App ID needs the Push Notifications capability and the key must belong to
the same team. Debug builds and the Simulator register sandbox tokens; release
builds register production tokens. The app sends `environment` with its token
and the server routes each token to the matching gateway.

## Verification

Settings → Notifications on the phone shows each link of the chain and offers
**Send test notification**, which calls `POST /api/accounts/push-test` (one call
per ten seconds). It returns `configured`, `devices`, `delivered`, and Apple's
status per device:

| Answer | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `configProblem: missing_secrets` | Set the three secrets and redeploy. |
| `key_id_malformed` / `team_id_malformed` | Copy the ten-character IDs exactly. |
| `devices: 0` | Allow notifications or sign in again on the phone. |
| `400 BadDeviceToken` | Token from the other gateway; reopen the app to re-register. |
| `DeviceTokenNotForTopic` / `TopicDisallowed` | Key team or App ID mismatch. |
| `403 InvalidProviderToken` | Key ID or Team ID does not match the key. |
| `410 Unregistered` | App uninstalled; the token is pruned. |
| HTTP `502 apns_provider_key` | The key does not import; re-paste it. |

## Limits

Delivery is best effort and inline with the triggering request: at most eight
devices per event within three seconds, twenty tokens per account, and tokens
idle for 180 days are dropped. Android has no push transport; the native
Android app reports push as unsupported. Local `workerd` cannot speak HTTP/2 to
APNs, so delivery must be tested against a deployed server.

pages.title: Node backup, recovery, and key moves
pages.description: forkmesh-mirror-node backs up, restores, and checks the node it runs
pages.markdown:
# Node backup, recovery, and key moves

`forkmesh-mirror-node` backs up, restores, and checks the node it runs:

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--preflight` | Read-only checks of configuration, identity, Git version, disk space, and backup/drill freshness |
| `--backup PATH` | Writes one encrypted archive of everything the node needs |
| `--restore-drill PATH` | Restores into scratch space, verifies, times it against the RTO, then deletes it |
| `--restore PATH` | Restores onto a host, verifies, and removes what it created if a check fails |
| `--export-identity PATH` / `--import-identity PATH` | Moves only the Ed25519 identity key |

Every command takes `--config` and prints JSON. Run them as the service
account:

```sh
node() {
  runuser -u forkmesh-node -- /usr/local/bin/forkmesh-mirror-node \
    --config /var/lib/forkmesh/mirror-node.json "$@"
}
```

## Passphrases

Archives and identity exports contain the private key and connector token, so
they are encrypted with AES-256-GCM in 1 MiB authenticated chunks, keyed by
PBKDF2-SHA256. Any tampering or truncation fails to open. The passphrase is read
only from `--passphrase-file`, which must be owner-only and at least 12 bytes;
it is never accepted as an argument or environment variable. Keep a copy off
the node.

## Preflight

`node --preflight [--json]` reports `ok`, `warn`, or `error` per check and
exits `2` on any error: configuration does not load, a required binary or the
identity key is missing, `git` is older than 2.27, the key does not match the
advertised public key, the connector token is not owner-only, or a state volume
has under 512 MiB free. Warnings cover low free space or inodes, uncloned
repositories, a backup older than 24 hours (RPO), and a restore drill older
than 92 days, over its objective, or never run. Run preflight before and after
every install or update; if it fails after an update, reinstall the previous
release (see [rolling migration](mirror-node.md#rolling-migration)).

## Backups

```sh
node --passphrase-file /var/lib/forkmesh/backup.passphrase \
  --backup /var/backups/forkmesh/node-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).fmbackup
```

The service can keep running. An archive contains the service and gateway
configurations, identity key, connector token, the gateway state directory
(`mirror-gateway/`), and every path the gateway configuration names
(repositories, release stores, private replica store, fork registry, writable
root, operator policy state). Each bare repository is stored as a
`git bundle --all` snapshot plus its `HEAD`, `config`, hooks, and releases.

Excluded: `tmp/`, `.cache/`, agent and merge worktrees, partial files, and
agent CLI sign-ins (sign in again after a restore). Archives are written under
a temporary name and never replace an existing file; symlinks in state are
refused. Each run is recorded, without secrets, in
`mirror-gateway/node-ops/last-backup.json`.

Schedule backups daily (for example a systemd timer running the command above
as `forkmesh-node`, pruning old archives) and copy archives off the host.

## Restore drills

```sh
node --passphrase-file /var/lib/forkmesh/backup.passphrase \
  --restore-drill /var/backups/forkmesh/node-<timestamp>.fmbackup --rto 30m
```

A drill decrypts into `--work-dir`, checks every file's size, mode, and
SHA-256, each repository's refs digest and `git fsck --connectivity-only`, and
that the key and configurations load and agree. It then deletes the scratch
copy, records `last-restore-drill.json`, and exits `3` if it exceeded `--rto`.
Run one at least quarterly. `/v1/status` reports both objectives under
`recovery`.

## Restoring a node

1. Install ForkMesh on the new host without bootstrapping an identity or
   starting the service.
2. Copy the archive and passphrase file over, owned by `forkmesh-node`, mode
   `0600`.
3. Optionally rehearse: `node --passphrase-file ... --restore <archive> --dry-run`.
4. Restore: `node --passphrase-file ... --restore <archive>`.
5. Run `node --preflight`, enable the service, and confirm `/readyz`.

Files return to their original absolute paths (or under `--restore-root DIR`).
A restore never overwrites existing files, refuses existing repository
directories, refuses to run as root, and on failure removes only what it
created. `--config` must match the path stored in the backup. The restored node
keeps its name and key, so it takes over the old node's catalog entry and
lease; never run the old and restored hosts at once.

## Moving or replacing an identity key

```sh
node --passphrase-file ... --export-identity /var/lib/forkmesh/node.fmkey          # old host
node --passphrase-file ... --import-identity /var/lib/forkmesh/node.fmkey --dry-run  # new host
node --passphrase-file ... --import-identity /var/lib/forkmesh/node.fmkey --replace-identity
```

An export is bound to its node name. Import reports `install` (no key yet),
`unchanged` (same key), or `replace` (different key; requires
`--replace-identity` and keeps the old key as `ed25519.pem.replaced-<unix time>`).
A changed key also updates the gateway's advertised public key and, on a
tunnel-free node, re-signs the direct-origin manifest. Restart the service
afterwards.

pages.title: Node operator policy and legal response
pages.description: An operator decides, for their own node only, what it stores and serves, how much disk it may use, and how it answers abuse reports and legal requests. None of this is a…
pages.markdown:
# Node operator policy and legal response

An operator decides, for their own node only, what it stores and serves, how
much disk it may use, and how it answers abuse reports and legal requests. None
of this is a network-wide rule: a repository this node refuses or quarantines is
reported unavailable here and the router sends readers to another mirror. The
policy is opt-in; a gateway without `operatorPolicy` is unaffected.

## Enabling it

Create an owner-only (`0600`) policy file and a `0700` state directory for the
gateway's service user, then add to `mirror-gateway.json`:

```json
"operatorPolicy": {
  "policyPath": "/var/lib/forkmesh-mirror/operator-policy.json",
  "stateDirectory": "/var/lib/forkmesh-mirror/operator-policy"
}
```

`mirror_gateway.py --check` validates it; `node_operator_policy.py` must sit
beside the gateway or validation fails. Commands below are
`python3 -I tools/node_operator_policy.py <command>` and print JSON.

## Policy reference

`profile` (`home`, `community`, `commercial`) sets finite defaults for
`limits.maxRepositoryBytes`, `maxBlobBytes`, `maxPushBytes`, `maxRepositories`
and `storageBudgetBytes`, `seeding.privateReplicas` (off except commercial),
`violationAction` and `retention.evidenceDays`. Any field can be overridden.

- `repositories.allow` / `.block` take an owner or `owner/repository`; a
  non-empty allow list restricts the node to those repositories.
- `content.blockedExtensions`, `blockedPathPatterns` and `blockedObjectIds`
  refuse matching names, paths or exact objects in every new tree.
- `violationAction`: `quarantine` lets `enforce --apply` stop serving stored
  violators; `report` only lists them. Violating pushes are always refused.
- `jurisdiction` (`us`, `eu`, `uk`, `other`) selects the case runbook.
- `secrets` enables the [secret scanning](../security/secret-scanning.md) gate.
- Unknown fields, duplicate keys and group- or world-writable files are refused.

## Protected branches

```json
"branches": {
  "rules": [
    {"pattern": "main", "requireSignedCommits": true},
    {"pattern": "refs/tags/v*", "blockForcePush": false}
  ],
  "allowedSignersPath": "/var/lib/forkmesh-mirror/allowed_signers"
}
```

The same pre-receive hook enforces these on the HTTPS gateway and the
[SSH gateway](git-ssh-gateway.md). A bare `pattern` means `refs/heads/<name>`;
`repositories` scopes a rule. `blockDeletion` and `blockForcePush` default to
`true`. `requireSignedCommits` accepts only SSH signatures from the OpenSSH
allowed-signers file and checks every commit the update adds. A stale expected
old value is refused as `stale-ref`. A refused push changes no ref, stores no
object and prints recovery steps; admitted and refused protected pushes are
audited. Tightening a rule requires `apply --confirm`.

## Enforcement

- **Pushes.** The gateway sets `core.hooksPath` to `<stateDirectory>/hooks`,
  holding only its own `pre-receive`. Staged objects are checked for allow/block
  lists, quarantine, push and storage size, blob names and ids, and secrets. Any
  failure discards the staged objects. An unreadable policy refuses every push.
- **Stored data.** Upstream fetches bypass the hook, so run `enforce` (preview)
  and `enforce --apply` after tightening a policy or on a timer.
- **Quarantine** writes `<state>/quarantine/<owner>/<repo>.json`: the repository
  answers as not found and its signed health says `available: false`. Bytes stay
  on disk until `release` or `remove`.

## Changing a policy

Never edit the active file in place. `preview` reports capacity and which
repositories would become unavailable; `apply` archives the previous file under
`<state>/policy-history/` and requires `--confirm` for any change that reduces
availability; `history` and `rollback` restore through the same checks.

## Reports, appeals and removal

`report`, `action`, `appeal`, `resolve --decision reverse|uphold|dismiss` and
`remove` (quarantined repositories only, `--confirm`, irreversible on this node)
manage cases. Evidence holds metadata only, never refused content;
`prune-evidence` honours `retention.evidenceDays` and never prunes open,
appealed or legal-hold cases. `runbook` prints a jurisdiction checklist
(process reminders, not legal advice).

## Audit and status

Every policy, case, quarantine and push decision is appended to the hash-chained
`<state>/audit.jsonl`; `verify-audit` exits 4 at the first broken record.
`status` returns secret-free counters for dashboards. Bandwidth caps, a desktop
policy editor and per-pusher branch rules are not provided.

pages.title: Non-custodial organization succession
pages.description: Organization succession is a governance mechanism for one organization roster. It is not inheritance, account recovery, custody, or asset transfer.
pages.markdown:
# Non-custodial organization succession

Organization succession is a governance mechanism for one organization
roster. It is not inheritance, account recovery, custody, or asset transfer.

## Transfer boundary

A completed succession performs exactly two scoped changes: the configured
owner becomes an organization administrator, and the named successor becomes
the owner. Only those two `org_members.role` values change; repository records,
links, teams, memberships, private-repository shares, and encryption recipients
are untouched.

Never transferred:

- wallets, wallet addresses, funds, rewards, or signing ability;
- private keys, account credentials, agent credentials, or private agent data;
- user accounts, personal data, devices, or device ownership;
- repository ownership, content, or ACLs.

Every succession response states this boundary.

## Configuration and lifecycle

Only the sole current owner configures a policy with
`PUT /api/orgs/{org}/succession`. The successor must be an active existing
administrator or member. Unknown or transfer-shaped fields are rejected.

| Setting | Range | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Inactivity threshold | 30–730 days | 180 |
| Grace period | 7–90 days | 30 |
| Independent approvals | 2–20 | 2 |

Approvals cannot exceed the eligible roster; owner and successor cannot approve.

1. `POST .../check-in` (or enabled-device and owned-node activity) refreshes the
   owner's activity and cancels an open grace case.
2. An hourly job sends one warning before the deadline; it never opens a case.
3. After the threshold, a current member calls `POST .../activate` to open grace.
4. During grace the owner may `cancel` or `check-in`; other current members
   `approve` (idempotent; removed members' approvals stop counting). Only
   members who already held an approving role when grace opened may approve:
   opening the case records that roster in `org_succession_case_approvers`
   (a trigger on the case insert, migration 0295), and both the approval
   insert and the completion check require the approver to be in it. An
   account added or promoted during grace gets
   `approver_joined_after_grace_opened`, so an administrator cannot reach the
   threshold with accounts made for the purpose.
5. After grace, a member calls `POST .../finalize`. One transaction rechecks
   deadline, owner, successor, and current approvers before changing the roles;
   any change fails closed.

`DELETE /api/orgs/{org}/succession` disables the policy and cancels any case.

## Authorization and audit

The API uses organization session and roster checks only; it has no
platform-administrator authorization path, and the tables are hidden from the
generic admin editor. Cases and approvals are immutable snapshots, and every
action appends a metadata-only event; triggers keep history append-only.
`GET /api/orgs/{org}/succession` (`no-store`) returns status, counts, and
dates, never device data.

pages.title: Open pull-request audit method
pages.description: An audit of open pull requests evaluates each signed record whose status is open against the current main
pages.markdown:
# Open pull-request audit method

An audit of open pull requests evaluates each signed record whose status is
`open` against the current `main`:

- whether the exact head still exists on the authoritative remote;
- whether the stored patch applies to the current index, and whether the
  reverse patch applies (the change is already represented);
- for a live head, `git diff --check` and a `git merge-tree` conflict check;
- a conservative content/path scan (credential paths, dynamic code, HTML
  sinks, shell downloads) that marks the change for security review. A trigger
  is not itself a vulnerability finding.

Each record gets one disposition:

| Disposition | When |
|---|---|
| Merge | The head is live, merges cleanly, and focused tests pass. |
| Hold | The head is gone but the patch still applies: recreate a signed branch and review it before any merge. |
| Close | The patch conflicts, is empty, is already in `main`, or is superseded. |

The audit never edits signed pull metadata by hand: merged pulls close through
normal pull synchronization, and other closures go through the authenticated
pull-request workflow.
