pages.description: Organization owners can queue Claude Code and Codex work for the desktop linked to an organization repository while that desktop is offline. The queue is durable and has no…
pages.markdown:
# Organization agent offline queue

Organization owners can queue Claude Code and Codex work for the desktop linked
to an organization repository while that desktop is offline. The queue is
durable and has no admission-count limit; list responses are bounded.

## Admission

Offline admission requires that the requester holds the organization `owner`
role, the repository has an exact `org_repos` link, the requester owns the
linked source node, the signed catalog record places the repository on a
`desktop` runtime, and that record advertises the requested provider. Other
members use the online, provider-capable mirror route.

Admission does not authorize execution. The reconnecting desktop proves node
ownership when it claims a job, validates the lease envelope, and rechecks the
provider binary and login before dispatch. Job and session rows are encrypted
at rest.

## Drain and recovery

The server leases one job per repository at a time, oldest first, using a
conditional queued-to-leased update. The desktop requests the next job only
after its result is acknowledged. A lease abandoned for two minutes
(`ORG_AGENT_JOB_LEASE_MS`) returns to `queued`; queued and running rows are
never deleted by this flow. The desktop starts a drain after each sync,
persists the running job's lease with the local session, and retries the
terminal report after a restart.

## Diagnostics

Rejections carry a stable `error`, a user-facing `message`, `retryable`, and
where relevant `requiredAction`, `provider`, and `targetNode`. Actions include
`link_repository`, `publish_repository`, `link_owned_desktop`,
`link_desktop_target`, `publish_provider_capability`, `select_linked_desktop`,
`select_eligible_target`, `bring_agent_mirror_online`, and `relink_desktop`.
Clients show the server message verbatim.

## Verification

Run `python3 tools/quality_gate.py run --profile core` (and `--profile release`
before a release). Rolling back the server needs no data migration; do not
reintroduce a per-organization task-count trigger.

pages.title: Paid microjobs
pages.description: A useful issue report or a focused pull request can receive a small, discretionary SOL reward after a repository owner reviews it. There is no separate claim form, no fixed…
pages.markdown:
# Paid microjobs

A useful issue report or a focused pull request can receive a small,
discretionary SOL reward after a repository owner reviews it. There is no
separate claim form, no fixed amount, and no payout schedule.
ForkMesh never holds a key: the owner pays directly from the owner's ForkMesh
desktop wallet.
Page: [`/microjobs`](https://app.forkmesh.com/microjobs).

A reward is a thank-you for useful work, not employment, an investment, a
balance, or a promise of future payment.

## Contribute

Submit the work once, through the repository's normal form:

- **Issues:** the [New issue form](https://app.forkmesh.com/forkmesh/forkmesh/issues/new).
  Check for duplicates first, then include reproduction steps, what happened,
  what you expected, and the version you tested.
- **Pull requests:** the [New pull request form](https://app.forkmesh.com/forkmesh/forkmesh/pulls/new).
  Keep the change focused, explain what it fixes, and include verification
  evidence.

Nothing else needs to be filed. Duplicates and spam are closed without a
reward.

## Estimate, pending, paid

| Stage | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| No estimate | The owner has not attached a reward. Most work, including accepted work, may stay here. |
| Estimate | The owner recorded an amount on the issue or pull request. Issue estimates are typically 0.001–0.005 SOL. An estimate is not an approved or earned payment. |
| `pending_merge` | A pull request estimate. It stays conditional until the pull is merged; a pull that is closed unmerged is not paid. |
| `pending_wallet` | The work qualifies, but no payment has been sent yet. It stays blocked while the contributor has no payout address. |
| `paid` | The owner sent the transfer. The ledger row carries the finalized Solana transaction signature. |

Estimates and their status appear on the issue or pull request and in the
public [Ledger → Pending payments](https://app.forkmesh.com/ledger). Only a
`paid` row with a transaction signature is a completed payment.

## Getting paid

Save a public Solana address under
[Settings → Verification and payout](https://app.forkmesh.com/dashboard/settings).
Never give anyone a wallet key or recovery phrase. The owner's desktop unlocks
the owner's wallet locally and broadcasts the exact direct transfer; the server
never signs or broadcasts. Timing is up to the owner.

## Legacy claim API

The sections below describe an earlier fixed-amount claim system. The web app
no longer offers it: `/microjobs` and the issue and pull-request forms do not
submit claims. Its server code (`app/src/microjobs.py`, `/api/microjobs/claims`,
and the hourly `microjob-payouts` cron phase) is still present, so an
installation may still answer direct API calls, but nothing here applies to
work submitted through the normal forms above, and none of it is a promise of a
fixed amount or an hourly payout.

### Jobs

| Job | Amount | Paid when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `issue_report` | 0.005 SOL | An AI reviewer finds no existing issue or code already covering it |
| `merged_pull` | 0.05 SOL | The pull is merged **and** carries the MCP agent tool's signed marker |
| `referral_post` | 0.01 SOL | The public page still links the referral **and** its hostname has sent counted visitors |

Amounts are fixed in `microjobs.JOBS`. Claims reuse the
[community reward pool](community-reward-pool.md) custody boundary: an approved
claim becomes a public, unsigned `chain_intents` plan that the repository
owner's desktop re-validates, signs in its encrypted vault, and broadcasts.

### Claim lifecycle

```
submitted -> pending_review | approved | rejected
             pending_review -> approved
             approved -> queued -> paid
```

`pending_review` waits for referral counters; `queued` is batched into an
unsigned plan; `paid` records the matching finalized transaction signature;
`rejected` returns the reason. A UNIQUE blind index
(`microjob_claims.subject_bi`) over the exact work item makes each issue, pull,
or page claimable once.

- A merged pull's key is its signed MCP marker (number, base, head, author,
  ts), not the repository it was read from. Forks copy the pull ledger branch,
  so a key that named the repository let one merged pull be paid again from
  every fork.
- A referral page's key (`referral_subject` in `app/src/microjobs.py`) names
  the post, not the spelling of its URL, so one page cannot be claimed again
  under a variant link, and two different posts stay two claims:
  - When the fetched page has a `<link rel="canonical">` on the same site,
    that URL is the key. Every key, canonical or not, then goes through the
    steps below.
  - The host is lowercased and `www.`, `old.`, `m.` and `mobile.` are dropped.
    The path loses repeated and trailing slashes, and percent-encoding is
    normalised. The fragment is dropped.
  - On hosts that identify a post by query (`news.ycombinator.com`: `id`;
    `youtube.com/watch`: `v`; `/playlist`: `list`) only those keys are kept.
    On any other host the query is kept, sorted, without tracking keys
    (`utm_*`, `ref`, `fbclid`, `gclid`, `si`, `s`, `t` and similar). Dropping
    the whole query would merge every Hacker News item and every YouTube
    video into one claim.
  - `youtu.be/<id>`, `/shorts/<id>`, `/embed/<id>` and `/live/<id>` become
    `youtube.com/watch?v=<id>`.
  - Reddit (`*.reddit.com`, `redd.it`) is case-insensitive, so its path is
    lowercased. A post becomes `reddit.com/comments/<post>[/<comment>]`,
    without the subreddit or the slug Reddit ignores.
  - On other hosts without a same-site canonical link, extra query keys that
    aren't on the tracking list still make a separate key. A second key then
    stops one account reusing its own page:
    `microjob:referral_post:account:<account_bi>:<scheme://host/path>`, with
    no query. That allows one claim per account per page path. Another
    account can still claim the same path. Hosts on the allowlist, Reddit,
    and pages whose canonical link sets the key take no second key.
  - The second key is stored as a companion row in `microjob_claims`: same
    account, `status='rejected'`, `amount_lamports=0`, and `data` naming the
    claim it belongs to. One batch writes both rows. The claim insert refuses
    when any of its keys, the companion key included, already exists. The
    companion insert runs only if the claim row was written. The table's
    UNIQUE `subject_bi` index settles any race.
  - A companion row is never paid, counted against a cap, or batched into a
    payout. The claimant's list and the public ledger only show rows with
    `amount_lamports>0`.
- Keys written before these rules still count as claimed. That means the
  repository plus pull number, the full normalized URL, and the URL's own key
  when the page's canonical link gave the claim a different one.
- The claim insert is one conditional `INSERT ... SELECT` that re-checks the
  subject and the open, daily-count and daily-amount caps. Requests running at
  the same time on different cores cannot pass the caps together.

### Verification

- **Issue reports.** Existing issues are read over the public mirror gateway, a
  fixed-string `git grep` finds related code, and an AI model classifies the
  report as `new`, `duplicate`, `already_addressed`, or `unclear`. Only `new`
  files the issue and approves the claim. `unclear`, an unparseable answer, or a
  missing `AI` binding fails closed with a retryable response. The ordinary
  issue endpoint is unaffected.
- **Merged pulls.** `tools/forkmesh_mcp_server.py` writes `client:
  forkmesh-mcp-v1` and `clientSig`, an Ed25519 signature over
  `forkmesh-mcp-pull-v1\n<number>\n<base>\n<head>\n<author>\n<ts>`. The server
  checks the signature and that the signing node belongs to the claimant. Pull
  stores must carry both fields through rewrites.
- **Referral posts.** The URL is normalized to an ordinary public HTTPS page
  (no credentials, IP literals, non-443 ports, or internal names) and fetched
  once to find the claimant's `/r/<name>` link. `site_referrers` must show
  `MIN_REFERRAL_SITE_VISITS` visits from that hostname and `referral_stats`
  `MIN_REFERRAL_CLICKS` clicks. Until then the claim is `pending_review` and is
  rechecked hourly.

### Payout batching

The hourly `microjob-payouts` phase is `microjobs.queue_payouts`: it reads
approved claims oldest first, looks up each claimant's public payout address
(claims without one stay approved), merges claims per recipient, and writes one
`chain_intents` row of policy `microjob-payout-v1` with at most 8 transfers,
expiring in 4 hours. The owner's desktop picks it up from
`GET /api/rewards/signing-jobs`. A finalized matching transfer marks the claims
`paid`; a rejected or expired plan returns them to `approved`. The phase only
moves claims made through the API; it never touches issue or pull request
estimates.

### Limits

At most 12 open claims, 8 claims per day, and 0.12 SOL per day per account,
and one claim per work item globally. These bounds raise the cost of farming;
they are not proof of personhood.

Payouts need the reward pool configuration (`COMMUNITY_REWARD_POOL_ADDRESS` or
`TREASURY_SOLANA_ADDRESS`, `COMMUNITY_REWARD_NETWORK`,
`REWARD_SIGNER_ACCOUNT`); otherwise `queue_payouts` returns
`pool_not_configured`. `microjob_claims` cannot be edited from the admin
console.

pages.title: Patreon membership operations
pages.description: Patreon is the membership payment rail for the Supporter, Pro, Builder, and Studio tiers. The server never sees card data. Member OAuth tokens are discarded right after identity…
pages.markdown:
# Patreon membership operations

Patreon is the membership payment rail for the Supporter, Pro, Builder, and
Studio tiers. The server never sees card data. Member OAuth tokens are
discarded right after identity lookup and are never stored or logged.

## Application setup

1. Create a Patreon creator application for the campaign with OAuth scopes
   `identity`, `identity[email]`, and `identity.memberships`.
2. Register the callback `https://<your-origin>/api/integrations/patreon/callback`.
3. Point a webhook at `https://<your-origin>/api/integrations/patreon/webhook`
   for `members:pledge:create`, `members:pledge:update`, and
   `members:pledge:delete`.
4. Record the numeric campaign ID and a creator-scoped access token that can
   read `GET /api/oauth2/v2/members/{id}`.

## Configuration

Non-secret variable: `PATREON_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI`. Secrets, published together
by `./deploy.sh secrets` (checked by `./deploy.sh validate-secrets`):

```text
PATREON_CLIENT_ID
PATREON_CLIENT_SECRET
PATREON_WEBHOOK_SECRET
PATREON_CAMPAIGN_ID
PATREON_CREATOR_ACCESS_TOKEN
```

## Runtime behavior

- OAuth state is random, account-bound, single-use, and valid ten minutes.
- Callbacks redirect to `/dashboard/settings/account?patreon=<outcome>`.
- Webhooks verify `X-Patreon-Signature` (hex HMAC-MD5 of the raw body).
- Members are matched by linked Patreon user, then by email blind index.
  The email match counts only when the account has confirmed that email;
  signup accepts an unconfirmed address, so otherwise anyone who registered a
  patron's email first would receive their tier. An unconfirmed match stays
  unmatched until the patron links through OAuth.
- Entitled cents map to roles: 1–999 `supporting_member`; 1000–4999 adds
  `pro_member`; 5000–9999 adds `builder_member`; 10000+ adds `studio_member`.
  Higher tiers inherit every lower role.
- Deletion or zero entitlement revokes the membership roles after grace.
- Membership roles also fund [ForkMesh Ads](ad-network.md) slots, read from the
  same `role_grants` at serve time.

## Secret rotation

Generate the new secret in Patreon, update the deployment secrets, run
`./deploy.sh secrets`, confirm OAuth start and a test webhook succeed, then
revoke the old secret. Until a rotated creator token is published, webhook
reconciliation cannot fetch member snapshots.

## Failure recovery

| Symptom | Likely cause | Recovery |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OAuth start returns 503 | Missing client, campaign, or redirect config | Publish the secrets and variable |
| Callback `expired` / `replayed` | State TTL or retry | Start Connect again |
| Callback `wrong_campaign` | Membership on another campaign | Check `PATREON_CAMPAIGN_ID` |
| Callback `duplicate_identity` | Patreon user linked to another account | Unlink the prior account |
| Webhook 503 `patreon_webhook_not_configured` | Missing webhook secret | Publish `PATREON_WEBHOOK_SECRET` |
| Webhook 503 `patreon_reconciliation_not_configured` | Missing campaign or creator token | Publish `PATREON_CAMPAIGN_ID` and `PATREON_CREATOR_ACCESS_TOKEN` |
| Webhook 503 `patreon_reconciliation_failed` | Patreon member fetch failed or token revoked | Check the token; Patreon retries the delivery |
| Webhook accepted, roles unchanged | Creator token or campaign mismatch | Rotate the token; check the campaign |

The two `*_not_configured` answers, like OAuth start's, carry
`x-forkmesh-expected-degraded: 1`: a deployment without Patreon is a choice,
not an API failure, so they never reach the error log or the `/status` API
alert. A failed member fetch or membership write is still logged. The served
stack (ForkMesh Next) has no `PATREON_*` secrets in `secrets.env`; the retired
Cloudflare worker held them, while Patreon still posts to forkmesh.com
(2026-10-14 alert).

Git, collaboration, mobile, and self-hosted paths never depend on Patreon;
only Connect, webhook sync, and membership-gated hosted features do.
Authorization always comes from active `role_grants`; the account `membership`
projection is display metadata.

pages.markdown:
# Plan completion record

This page is the canonical record that the original product plan and live
notes were implemented and retired. Retired plan items must not be recreated
or reported as unfinished work.

Requirements that remain in force, and where they are documented:

| Area | Rule | Documentation |
|---|---|---|
| World | Public presence never exposes raw IP addresses or precise location; guests may use the public Town Square room without weakening authenticated room permissions. | [World community services](../world-community-services.md) |
| Moderation | No automated visitor quarantine; rate limits, integrity checks, audit logs, and manual moderation remain. | [Organization roles](../security/organization-roles.md) |
| Rewards | The reward program stays non-custodial; contributions are voluntary, user-signed transfers with no promise of ownership or returns; pool signing stays on the owner's local client. | [Community reward pool](community-reward-pool.md), [local signer](community-reward-pool-signer.md) |
| SSH Git | Only `git-upload-pack` and `git-receive-pack` are accepted through a restrictive `AuthorizedKeysCommand`; SSH URLs stay hidden unless the gateway is fully configured. | [Git SSH gateway](git-ssh-gateway.md) |
| History | Commit-message rewrites follow the guarded procedure and are never published by a blind `push --mirror`. | [Commit-history rewrite](commit-history-rewrite.md) |

The capability inventory is `www/docs/capability-matrix.md`.

pages.title: Plan trials and self-serve usage meters
pages.description: Users can start a trial, see usage, pay, change plan, and cancel without support intervention.
pages.markdown:
# Plan trials and self-serve usage meters

Users can start a trial, see usage, pay, change plan, and cancel without
support intervention.

## Endpoints

- `GET /api/plans/usage`: per-account usage meters (published repositories,
  owned organizations, SSH keys, stored notifications) against the operational
  caps their routes already enforce. Limits are plan-independent; a numeric plan
  allowance may be added only once it is published in `business-model.json`
  with metering tests.
- `GET /api/plans/trial`: `eligible`, `used`, `active`, `endsAt`. One trial per
  account, never while a paid membership is active.
- `POST /api/plans/trial`: starts the single 14-day Supporter trial. One batch
  writes the `plan_trials` register row (the primary key arbitrates races) and a
  `role_grants` upsert under `scope_type='promotion'`.

The dashboard's **Plan usage** card on `/dashboard/settings/account` renders
the meters and the trial button. Membership payment is described in
[Patreon](patreon.md).

## Grant scope

Membership sync revokes only platform-scope grants, so a trial in the
`promotion` scope expires by its own `expires_at`: a billing-provider outage
cannot revoke, extend, or resurrect it. The upsert only lengthens an unrevoked
expiry, so replays are safe. Trial expiry withholds member perks only; portable
identity, public read/clone, and protocol access are never affected.

## Register and metrics

`plan_trials` is the trial register that the `trialsCompleted` and
trial-to-paid metrics in `www/docs/outcome-metrics.json` reconcile to:

```sql
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM plan_trials WHERE ends_at > :start AND ends_at <= :end;
```

Account deletion purges the row; rename moves it with the account.

## Failure and rollback

- A failed trial batch writes nothing; the API returns `trial_already_used` or
  `already_subscribed`.
- The usage endpoint reads only local state; provider outages cannot affect it.
- The down migration drops only the register; live grants lapse on their own.

Managed services stay unavailable for purchase
(`launchGates.managedCheckoutEnabled: false`); managed plans must reuse this
register before checkout can open.

pages.title: Polling inventory and elimination plan
pages.description: Goal: no ForkMesh client polls the relay for data. Every "did anything change?" question becomes a payload-free push over a WebSocket, answered by the one signed HTTPS read the…
pages.markdown:
# Polling inventory and elimination plan

Goal: no ForkMesh client polls the relay for data. Every "did anything change?"
question becomes a payload-free push over a WebSocket, answered by the one
signed HTTPS read the client would have made anyway. The transport is the
per-owner `ForkMeshNodes` object behind `GET /api/nodes/events` (desktops,
headless nodes and, via tickets, browsers) plus the chat, world, office and note
room sockets.

## Rules

- **Read on a reason, never on a display timer.** A client reads when a page
  opens, when the reader presses Refresh, when the app or window comes back, or
  when a socket frame says something changed.
- **No fallback polls.** A safety-net poll silently becomes the load. The socket
  owns liveness: reconnect is unconditional with bounded backoff, and every
  (re)connect fires one catch-up read.
- **Heartbeats are not polls.** Liveness proofs (presence, endpoint lease) keep
  their cadence but ride an already-open socket; HTTPS is only the recovery path.
- **The socket is transport, never authority.** A frame carries the same signed
  proof as the HTTPS route and is handed to the same handler.
- **Count requests per event, not timers per minute.** One request per row or
  several callers reading the same resource is a poll in disguise; coalesce and
  revalidate with ETags.
- **Server phases read one indexed row to learn nothing changed**, never the
  table itself (for example the `catalog_rev` counter before a catalog scan).

## Account event channel

`notify_account_event(env, owner, topic)` fans a payload-free frame to the
account's `ForkMeshNodes` object from the writes that move a count: pings
(`pings`), direct messages (`direct-messages`), private channels, issues,
catalog changes and cloud agent runs (`cloud-agents`). Browsers join with a
60-second ticket from `GET /api/accounts/event-ticket` (a WebSocket upgrade
carries no `Authorization` header) through the shared `public/account-events.js`.
The chat header badge advances locally from the room socket
(`noteSeenChatActivity`) and is re-read once on `visibilitychange`/`pagehide`.

## Eliminated

| Former poller | Replacement |
| --- | --- |
| Mirror collaboration intake `GET /api/repo/*/pending` | Node event socket; push leases the changed inbox, catch-up on reconnect |
| Desktop inbox sync and `/pending` badge fetch | Socket-driven sync; badge fetched once and invalidated by push, drain or open |
| Unread counts: `refreshWebAlerts`, `startNotificationPolling`, `refreshDirectMessages`, `markChatActivitySeen` | One read on open, then account event pushes |
| Mirror git sync loop | `commits` push carrying the signed refs digest; 5-minute reconciliation backstop |
| Account heartbeat and endpoint lease over HTTP | Frames on the node socket, HTTPS fallback |
| Session validity, dashboard and World (`validateActiveWorldSession`) | Event-ticket handshake refusal; focus/visibility check behind a 5-minute floor (`WORLD_SESSION_REVALIDATE_MIN_MS`) |
| Signed-out session restore on every page | 401 remembered per tab (`forkmesh.sessionRestoreMiss`) |
| Portable grant re-signing on each session read | Reused while younger than `PORTABLE_SESSION_REISSUE_MS` |
| Desktop status/page probes on a minute tick | Launch, recheck and window activation (`refreshFooterStatusOnActivation`) |
| Desktop user directory (`m_chatDirectoryTimer`), notes, pull requests, agent sessions, host probes | Read on open, Refresh, or a socket frame |
| Mobile agents, actions and inbox timers | Tab open, pull to refresh, push and resume catch-up |
| World admin error badge (`ADMIN_ERROR_POLL_MS`) and Office agent bots (`WORLD_AGENT_BOT_POLL_MS`) | Slowed to 60s and 30s, visible tabs only |
| Catalog republish from several publishers | Single publisher (the Go mirror daemon), fingerprinted records |

## Still polling

- Desktop: admin pending-user verification (5m, admins only), mirror
  registration renewal (5m), agent limits (60s).
- Dashboard: pending badge while a repository shows pending items (10m).
- World: community events, mirror catalogs, action runs, QA/build/status boards,
  imports and deploy status; all visible-tab only.
- Chat pages: the visible-tab `USERS_DIRECTORY_REFRESH_MS` directory tick (a new
  account has no frame to announce itself) and the room presence proof.
- Server: the App minute cron, which runs every due phase on one coordinator
  object and continues in a fresh alarm when its subrequest budget runs out.

## Remaining plan

1. Fold per-topic tallies into event frames so the desktop `/pending` read
   disappears, and move admin, notes and agent-limit reads onto socket topics.
2. Add a read-only per-repository event channel for the website and move the
   dashboard badge and World repository pollers onto it.
3. For each minute-cron phase, trigger the work from the write that made it
   necessary; keep cron only for time-based work such as expiries.

Acceptance for each step: the eliminated endpoint's request group in the API
traffic chart drops to about zero, not merely lower.

pages.markdown:
# Pre-release commit-message rewrite

`tools/rewrite_commit_messages.py` rewrites local branch and tag history to one
short, deterministically generated, name-redacted sentence per commit while
preserving trees, graph topology, identity headers, and timestamps. It never
pushes.

## Safety boundary

- The default command, `plan`, is read-only. `rewrite` requires
  `--confirm REWRITE-COMMIT-HISTORY`, refuses to run while Git lock files
  exist, and touches only explicit `refs/heads/*` and `refs/tags/*`.
- Each run writes mode-0600 artifacts to
  `.git/forkmesh-history-rewrite/<UTC timestamp>/`: a verified
  `pre-rewrite.bundle`, `original-commit-messages.jsonl`, `old-to-new.json`, and
  scope manifests (schema `forkmesh.commit-history-rewrite.v1`). Backup refs
  live under `refs/forkmesh-history-backup/<UTC timestamp>/`.
- The summarizer strips trailers, email addresses, `@handles`, known names, and
  attribution phrases locally; no message data leaves the machine.
- Every rebuilt commit is validated (tree IDs, parent order, identity headers,
  sentence length, redaction) before all refs move in one `git update-ref`
  transaction.
- Commit signatures, signed tags, and links pinned to old IDs become invalid;
  embedded signatures are stripped and recorded.

## Procedure

1. Stop every writer: agents, editors, hooks, schedulers, CI.
2. `python3 tools/rewrite_commit_messages.py plan` and confirm the ref scope.
3. `python3 tools/rewrite_commit_messages.py rewrite --confirm REWRITE-COMMIT-HISTORY`
4. Run the full test gates plus `git fsck --full` and `git show-ref --heads --tags`.
5. On failure, restore:

   ```bash
   python3 tools/rewrite_commit_messages.py restore \
     --artifact-dir .git/forkmesh-history-rewrite/<UTC timestamp> \
     --confirm RESTORE-COMMIT-HISTORY
   ```

Publishing rewritten history to mirrors is a separate, explicitly authorized
operation: announce a window, publish the old-to-new mapping (never the message
archive), and have each mirror fetch and verify the exact new tips. Never use a
blind `push --mirror`; clones must re-clone or reset rather than merge old and
new histories.

pages.title: Pull request rules
pages.description: Repositories and organizations can set rules every pull request must meet: tests, documentation, size, commit message format, secrets, protected paths, and a required AI model.…
pages.markdown:
# Pull request rules

Repositories and organizations can set rules every pull request must meet:
tests, documentation, size, commit message format, secrets, protected paths,
and a required AI model. The pull request page lists each rule, whether it
passes, and how to fix it. Each rule either **blocks** the merge (no waiver
reaches it) or only **flags** the pull request (`warn`).

| Scope | Where the rules live | Who changes them |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Repository | `.forkmesh/pull-rules.json` on the base branch | Anyone who can push to that branch (or **Settings → Pull request rules**) |
| Organization | Stored by the hosted service, applied to every linked repository | Organization owners and admins |

Both sets apply. A pull request is judged by the rules on its **base** commit,
never its head, so it cannot loosen its own rules.

## The rules file

```json
{
  "schema": "forkmesh-pull-rules-v1",
  "rules": [
    { "id": "tests", "kind": "tests", "branches": ["main"] },
    { "id": "docs", "kind": "docs", "paths": ["api/**"], "enforcement": "warn" },
    { "id": "small", "kind": "size", "maxFiles": 40, "maxLines": 800 },
    { "id": "commits", "kind": "commits", "subjectPattern": "^(feat|fix|docs|chore)(\\(.+\\))?: ", "maxSubjectLength": 72 },
    { "id": "secrets", "kind": "secrets" },
    { "id": "workflows", "kind": "paths", "paths": [".github/workflows/**", "deploy/**"] },
    { "id": "model", "kind": "model", "models": ["claude-opus-5-5"] }
  ]
}
```

Every rule takes `id` (lowercase, digits, dashes, up to 48 characters, unique),
`kind`, and optional `title`, `branches` (up to 16 base-branch patterns; `*`
matches within a segment, `**` across segments; empty means all),
`enforcement` (`block` default, or `warn`), and `suggestion` (fix text).

| Kind | Checks | Fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tests` | A change to `paths` includes a change to `testPaths`. | `paths`, `testPaths` (sensible defaults) |
| `docs` | A change to `paths` includes a change to `docsPaths`. | `paths`, `docsPaths` |
| `size` | At most `maxFiles` files and `maxLines` changed lines. | `maxFiles`, `maxLines` |
| `commits` | Every non-merge subject matches `subjectPattern` and fits `maxSubjectLength`. | RE2 pattern, length |
| `secrets` | No added line looks like a private key or common cloud/API credential, or matches `patterns`. | `patterns`, `paths` |
| `paths` | No changed file matches `paths`. | `paths` |
| `model` | Every commit carries a verified model attestation for one of `models`. | `models` (1–16) |

Patterns without `/` match a file name at any depth; patterns with `/` match
from the root. Regular expressions use RE2. A rules file that does not parse
locks every merge it covers.

## Model attestation

Commit trailers such as `Co-Authored-By` are ignored. The `model` rule accepts
a commit only with a verified `ForkMesh-Attestation` trailer:

1. When a hosted pool runner claims an agent job, the router signs a **model
   grant** naming the runner key, repository, branch, provider, model, and
   lease. Personal runners, mirrors, and desktops never receive one.
2. The runner daemon rewrites each new commit with `ForkMesh-Agent:
   <provider>/<model>` and `ForkMesh-Attestation: <grant>.<signature>`, signed
   with its node key over tree, parents, message, and grant. The sandboxed agent
   process never holds that key.
3. At merge, the host verifies the grant under the trusted router key, the
   commit signature under the granted key, and the model against the rule.

Editing, amending, or rebasing an attested commit breaks the signature. A merge
commit that only brings in the base passes if its tree equals the automatic
merge of its parents. The proof covers which model the runner ran, not the
provider's internals.

## Enforcement points

| Step | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Pull request page | The host evaluates both rule sets on current base and head; a failing blocking rule locks the merge button. |
| Hosted merge request | Organization rules are evaluated on the pinned commits; refusal is `rules_required`. |
| Repository host merge | The Go merge executor evaluates the base's rules file and refuses with `rules_required`. A headless Python mirror cannot verify signatures and refuses every merge into a base with a rules file. |

Rules gate merges made through ForkMesh; a direct push to the base branch is
not stopped, the same limit as [signed required checks](required-checks.md).
Organization rule management needs `organization.pull_rules.manage`
([Organization roles](../security/organization-roles.md)).

pages.markdown:
# Self-hostable service roles

ForkMesh's network services are split into eight roles. This page lists which
roles an independent operator can run, how to start them, what replaces each
optional dependency, and how to check a running deployment. It matches the
machine-readable manifest
[`conformance/service-roles/v1/manifest.json`](../../../conformance/service-roles/v1/manifest.json);
`tools/forkmesh_service_roles.py validate` fails if either names a path, flag,
source route, or heading that no longer exists.

## Role status

| Role | Status | Independent profile | Contract checks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `web-ui` | partial | Mirror gateway dashboard | `/health`, `/api/version`, `/dashboard`, `/api/accounts/sessions` |
| `relay` | partial | Mirror gateway Smart HTTP + `forkmesh-mirror-node` | clone advertisement, signed endpoint manifest |
| `public-index` | partial | Mirror gateway local catalog | `/api/repositories` |
| `search` | hosted-only | — | `/api/repositories/search` (hosted) |
| `identity-resolver` | partial | Node key, SSH broker `local` mode, portable sessions | evidence tests only |
| `collaboration-relay` | partial | Daemon intake, gateway submissions, SSH pull spool | evidence tests only |
| `automation-broker` | partial | Desktop ActionRunner + signed checks | evidence tests only |
| `organization-service` | hosted-only | — | none yet |

- **independent**: runs from this repository with open-source dependencies
  only, needs no default endpoint, and lists no gaps.
- **partial**: an independent profile covers part of the role; the manifest's
  `gaps` list says what still needs the hosted deployment
  (`python3 tools/forkmesh_service_roles.py gaps`).
- **hosted-only**: runs only on the hosted service.

A role moves to `independent` only when its gaps list is empty, it has no
proprietary required dependency, and it has a contract; the validator enforces
all three.

## Starting the independent profiles

Every partial role runs on two open-source processes:

1. `tools/mirror_gateway.py --config gateway.json` serves Git, the dashboard,
   the local catalog, and the signed endpoint manifest on a loopback port. Run
   `--check` first. Schema:
   [`mirror-gateway-config.schema.json`](../mirror-gateway-config.schema.json).
2. `forkmesh-mirror-node --config mirror-node.json` synchronizes repositories,
   supervises the gateway, commits collaboration submissions, and reports
   `/healthz`, `/readyz`, and `/v1/status`. Run `--preflight --json` first. See
   [Mirror node service](mirror-node.md).

For SSH pushes, pull submissions, and forks without a controller, add the SSH
gateway and the authorization broker in `localAuthorization` mode `local`
([Controller-free operation](git-ssh-gateway.md#controller-free-operation)).
Put a TLS-terminating reverse proxy in front of the loopback listeners.

## Optional dependencies and substitutes

| Dependency | Used by | Substitute |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cloudflare Tunnel (`cloudflared`) | `web-ui`, `relay` | `--disable-cloudflared` (or `disableCloudflared`) with your own HTTPS reverse proxy |
| Hosted login origin | `web-ui` | Omit `dashboard.canonicalOrigin`; the dashboard stays signed out except for existing portable sessions |
| Hosted node event socket | `relay` | The `post-receive` doorbell (`POST /v1/control/sync`), direct peer upstreams, and `syncInterval` |
| Hosted catalog publication | `public-index` | `disableCatalog`, or `--catalog-url` pointing at another operator's catalog |
| Hosted account registry | `identity-resolver` | SSH broker `localAuthorization` mode `local` with a grants file |
| Hosted collaboration inboxes | `collaboration-relay` | `forkmesh-pull-submit` over SSH, or signed submissions to the gateway |
| Hosted agent CLIs | `automation-broker` | Leave website agent jobs off; workflows and signed required checks run without them |

## Default endpoints

`forkmesh-mirror-node` has three flags whose defaults point at forkmesh.com.
An independent deployment overrides all three.

| Flag | Default | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--upstream` | `https://forkmesh.com/forkmesh/forkmesh` | `relay` |
| `--catalog-url` | `https://app.forkmesh.com/api/repositories` | `public-index` |
| `--accounts-url` | `https://app.forkmesh.com/api/accounts` | `identity-resolver` |

## Checking a running role

```sh
python3 tools/forkmesh_service_roles.py probe --role web-ui \
  --base-url https://mirror.example.org
python3 tools/forkmesh_service_roles.py probe --role relay \
  --base-url https://mirror.example.org --param owner=alice --param repository=demo
```

`probe` sends only read-only `GET`/`HEAD` requests and prints a
`forkmesh-service-role-report-v1` JSON report: one result per check, the role
status, `defaultPublicService`, and request/latency telemetry. Credentials and
query strings are stripped from the printed base URL.

| Verdict | Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pass` | 0 | Every check answered as specified. |
| `degraded` | 3 | Every failing check returned the role's declared degradation (for example `503` with a JSON `error`). |
| `fail` | 1 | A check answered outside the contract and the declared degradation. |
| `unreachable` | 4 | Nothing answered. Treat as service loss, never as an empty result. |

A usage or manifest error exits 2.

## Failure behavior and canonical data

Git objects, refs, and signed collaboration records under `.forkmesh/` live in
repositories on configured nodes; catalog rows, search results, and dashboard
pages are rebuilt from them. Losing a role never deletes canonical data:

- Without the hosted service, the gateway keeps serving clones and the last
  validated dashboard projection.
- Submissions made during an outage stay in the pull submission spool and are
  acknowledged only once committed.
- In `fallback` mode the SSH broker uses local grants only when the hosted
  authority is unreachable, never after a denial.
- Search answers `503 catalog_unavailable` when no catalog can be read.
- A required status check with no signed result keeps the merge gate closed.

Backups are covered by [Node backup and recovery](node-backup-and-recovery.md).
`app/tests/test_service_roles_contract.py` runs the `web-ui`, `relay`, and
`public-index` contracts against a real gateway with no forkmesh.com
configuration.

pages.markdown:
# Signed required checks

A repository can require status checks before a pull request merges on a
mirror node. Each result is an Ed25519-signed attestation from a runner the
repository trusts, so the gate does not depend on any runner service or
storage location. Forged, stale, replayed, and unauthorized results cannot
satisfy it. The Go mirror node (`forkmesh-mirror-node`) enforces it for web
merges (`merge-pull`).

## Policy

Commit `.forkmesh/required-checks.json` to the base branch:

```json
{
  "schema": "forkmesh-required-checks-v1",
  "branches": ["main"],
  "maxAgeSeconds": 604800,
  "checks": [
    { "name": "CI tests", "signers": ["<runner public key, 43-character base64url>"] }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `schema` | Exactly `forkmesh-required-checks-v1`. |
| `branches` | Base branches covered; empty covers every base. |
| `maxAgeSeconds` | 60 to 31,622,400. Older results do not count. |
| `checks` | 1–32 checks with distinct names (1–128 bytes, no control characters). |
| `signers` | 1–16 canonical, prime-order Ed25519 runner keys per check. |

Unknown keys or any validation failure lock merges into covered branches; a
broken file never disables the gate. The policy is read from the **base
commit**, never the pull request's head. A runner prints its key with
`forkmesh-mirror-node --config <path> --public-key`.

## Reporting a result

```sh
printf '%s' '{"schema":"forkmesh-check-v1","owner":"example","repository":"demo","commit":"<head sha>","check":"CI tests","conclusion":"success","runId":"run-1234"}' \
  | forkmesh-mirror-node --config /etc/forkmesh/mirror-node.json --sign-check-attestation
```

The signer adds `issuedAt`, `signer`, and `signature`; callers cannot supply
them. `conclusion` is `success`, `failure`, `cancelled`, or `skipped`; only
`success` satisfies a check. Publish the JSON on the `forkmesh/pulls` ledger
branch as `.forkmesh/pulls/<N>/checks/<name>.json` (name matching
`[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*\.json`; at most 256 files of 8 KiB each).

The signature covers these fields joined by LF, no trailing LF:

```
forkmesh-check-v1
<owner, lowercase>
<repository>
<commit, lowercase hex>
<hex SHA-256 of the check name>
<conclusion>
<runId>
<issuedAt, decimal milliseconds>
```

## Evaluation

For each required check the mirror discards attestations that fail to parse or
verify, name another owner, repository, or head commit, are signed by a key not
listed for that check, are older than `maxAgeSeconds`, or are dated more than
five minutes ahead. The newest remaining `issuedAt` wins; on a tie a
non-success beats a success. The merge proceeds only when every check's winner
is `success`; otherwise the executor records `checks_required` and moves no
refs. The review waiver (`overrideReview`) never waives required checks.

## Limits

- Patch-backed pulls have no published head to attest and cannot merge on the
  web under a covering policy.
- `tools/headless_mirror_refresh.py` has no Ed25519 verifier and refuses every
  merge whose base carries a policy.
- An attestation is bound to the owner name in the merge request.

Tests: `server/checks_test.go`, `server/merge_test.go`, and
`app/tests/test_pull_merge_executor.py`.

pages.title: Stock Git conformance operations
pages.description: The public compatibility matrix is generated from the claims in conformance/git/v1/matrix.json and the retained run reports in conformance/git/v1/evidence/ (indexed by…
pages.markdown:
# Stock Git conformance operations

The public [compatibility matrix](../git-compatibility.md) is generated from
the claims in `conformance/git/v1/matrix.json` and the retained run reports in
`conformance/git/v1/evidence/` (indexed by `conformance/git/v1/results.json`).
Never hand-edit the generated Markdown, HTML, JSON, results index, or evidence;
change the source or a probe, then run:

```sh
python3 tools/git_conformance.py validate
python3 tools/git_conformance.py render
python3 tools/git_conformance.py render --check
```

## Published status

A cell marked `supported`, `local`, or `conditional` keeps that status only
when a retained run covering it passed within `suite.freshnessDays` (30 days).
Otherwise it is published as `failing` (a covering run failed), `stale` (the
newest pass is too old), or `unverified` (no covering run). Only smart-HTTP
runs count for the relay and mirror-failover columns. The hosted page re-checks
run dates against the reader's clock, and
`/docs/git-compatibility/evidence/<run>.json` holds each raw report.

## Attesting evidence

```sh
python3 tools/git_conformance.py attest \
  artifacts/git-conformance-v0.json artifacts/git-conformance-v2.json
```

`attest` validates reports (suite version, operation inventory, summary
consistency, privacy flags, and a scan for unredacted paths, file URLs, or
loopback addresses), stores them by content address, and regenerates outputs.
The newest report per client configuration replaces older ones. Bumping
`suite.version` invalidates existing evidence. `attest --drop <run-id>` retires
a configuration.

## Release gate

```sh
python3 tools/git_conformance.py gate
python3 tools/git_conformance.py gate --operations-only \
  --report artifacts/git-conformance-v2.json
```

`gate` exits non-zero and names every failing, stale, or unverified claim.
`--report` also counts a fresh unattested run; `--operations-only` skips
hand-recorded client rows. The `release` quality-gate profile runs the full
gate.

## Evidence chain

The conformance workflow runs Git protocol v0 and v2 on Linux, macOS, and
Windows. Protocol v2 proves partial clone and lazy fetch; protocol v0 proves the
safe rejection without relaxing hidden-object policy. Each matrix cell maps to a
stable probe ID, and each report records the repository commit, exact
Git/Python/OS versions, per-operation status and time, generalized
origin/proxy counts, the signed fixture commit, and a digest of the final refs.

The offline smart-HTTP fixture exercises direct read/write, a masked relay
proxy, and failover from a failed origin to a matching mirror. Gateway tests
separately prove that HTTPS receive-pack returns an actionable 501, SSH
receive-pack enforces authorization and quotas, upload-pack serves shallow and
partial clones while rejecting hidden-object wants, object bytes survive every
read path, and damaged refs or packs fail strict fsck.

With `--transport auto` the suite selects HTTP only after a completed loopback
round trip (IPv4, then IPv6) and otherwise falls back to a clearly labelled
file-transport run that does not count as relay evidence. The public workflow
requires `--transport http`. CI runs each suite in a private network namespace
(`unshare -rn`) when possible so host firewalls cannot drop loopback traffic.

## Promoting a client row

Run the suite with the exact Git executable a client ships, for both protocol
versions, then attest the reports:

```sh
python3 tools/git_conformance.py run \
  --git /path/to/client/bundled/git \
  --client-label "Client name and version" \
  --transport http --protocol-version 2 \
  --output artifacts/git-conformance-client-v2.json
```

A passing bundled-Git probe proves protocol compatibility only; a desktop UI
stays pending until its own authentication, clone, push, and recovery flows are
exercised.

## Failure and recovery

Probes run entirely in temporary directories and never touch production
repositories. Keep a failed report and log, reproduce with the same Git and
protocol version, and attest the failure before a release so the gate blocks
it; a later passing run supersedes it. For a failed production fetch, retry
rather than delete the clone, run `git fsck --full --strict` after corruption,
and create and verify a bundle before force-updating a ref.

## Telemetry and privacy

Reports are retained for 30 days and contain no repository contents, paths,
URLs, credentials, SSH keys, client addresses, or raw Git stderr: only
generalized request and timing counts.

## Rollout and rollback

Partial-clone filtering and protocol-v2 forwarding are gateway transport
policies requiring no repository migration. Deploy them through the normal
packages, validate the scoped `AcceptEnv GIT_PROTOCOL` SSH drop-in with
`sshd -t`, then run the conformance workflow. Rollback removes
`uploadpack.allowFilter=true`, protocol-v2 forwarding, and the SSH hint;
existing clones are unaffected, and the matrix must change with the contract.

pages.description: The ForkMesh iPhone app works with Apple Health. It uses Apple's HealthKit framework to connect seven optional tools to the Health app: Pedometer, Water Intake, Calorie Counter…
pages.markdown:
# Apple Health on iPhone

The ForkMesh iPhone app works with Apple Health. It uses Apple's HealthKit
framework to connect seven optional tools to the Health app: Pedometer, Water
Intake, Calorie Counter, Sleep, Sugar Break, Stretch Break and Food Guide. This
page lists
what each tool reads and writes, what reaches your ForkMesh account, and how
to turn it off.

Nothing is read or written until you turn on a tool's Apple Health switch and
allow it in the iOS permission sheet. The rest of ForkMesh does not use
HealthKit.

## Where to find it in the app

- **In each tool.** The Apple Health switch sits in a card marked **Works with
  Apple Health**, with the data that tool reads and writes listed under it and
  a **How ForkMesh uses Apple Health** button.
- **In Settings.** **Settings > Legal > Apple Health** opens the same guide for
  all seven tools, whether or not you have installed them.

The tools are installed from Market in the app. A tool you have not installed
never asks for Apple Health access.

## What each tool reads and writes

| Tool | Reads from Apple Health | Writes to Apple Health | Saved to your ForkMesh account |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pedometer | Steps, walking and running distance, flights climbed, active energy | Heart rate, only when you tap out your pulse and choose **Save to Apple Health** | One total per day, so your steps show on web and desktop. Heart rate is never sent. |
| Water Intake | Water that other apps logged | Each drink you log, as Water | Water from other apps is added to your drinks log |
| Calorie Counter | The meals ForkMesh wrote, so edits and deletions stay in step | Dietary energy, protein, carbohydrates and fat for the meals you log | Nothing from Apple Health |
| Sleep | Sleep that an Apple Watch or another app recorded | Nights your phone detected, only with **Save detected sleep to Apple Health** on | Each night's sleep |
| Sugar Break | Dietary sugar that other apps logged | Nothing | Nothing. Apple Health sugar never leaves the phone. |
| Stretch Break | Minutes of Flexibility and Mind and Body workouts | Each guided session you finish, as a workout | Nothing from Apple Health |
| Food Guide | The last 14 days of dietary energy, protein, fiber, sugar, saturated fat, sodium, iron, calcium, potassium, magnesium, folate and vitamins C, D and B12 that other apps logged | Nothing | Nothing. The nutrition history and the meal ideas worked out from it stay on the phone. |

Pedometer and Sleep also use the iPhone's motion sensor, which iOS asks about
separately under Motion & Fitness.

## What ForkMesh does with it

- The readings saved to your account are there so a tool shows the same
  numbers on web, desktop and mobile. They are encrypted with a key created
  for your account alone.
- ForkMesh does not use Apple Health data for advertising or marketing, does
  not sell it, and does not share it with data brokers or any other third
  party.
- ForkMesh does not store Apple Health data in iCloud.
- ForkMesh never deletes or changes health data that another app wrote.

The [privacy policy](https://forkmesh.com/privacy#apple-health) says the same.

## Turning it off

- Turn off the Apple Health switch in the tool. Reading and writing stop at
  once. What was already written to Apple Health stays there.
- Or open the iPhone **Settings** app, then **Health > Data Access & Devices >
  ForkMesh**, and turn off any type of data.
- Uninstalling a tool deletes its data from your ForkMesh account on every
  device. Deleting your account does the same for every tool. Apple Health
  keeps its own copy, which you manage in the Health app.

pages.markdown:
# Editing files and opening pull requests from the phone

From the repository browser in the iOS or Android app, a person can edit one
text file and propose it as a pull request with no clone, no fork and no push
access. Related: [mobile node contract](mobile-node-contract.md).

## Why no fork is needed

A ForkMesh pull request is a signed patch, not a pointer to a branch. The
relay verifies only the author's Ed25519 signature over title, base, head,
patch and commits, plus size, inbox depth and per-author quota. The receiving
node merges from the carried patch (`git apply --index --3way`, or `git am
--3way` when commits are included) and never resolves the head branch. So a
contributor needs nowhere to push. A fork on ForkMesh is a durable copy you
keep, not a gate in front of an edit button.

## Every edit opens a pull request

Even with write access, the phone opens a pull request, so nothing merges
unreviewed from a phone. Round one is one file per pull request; multi-file
work goes through a clone.

## Building a patch without a clone

A Git blob id is `sha1("blob " + <byte length> + "\0" + <bytes>)`, so the phone
can compute both sides of an `index` line:

1. Fetch the file's raw bytes for the ref being browsed.
2. `oldId` from those bytes, `newId` from the edited text as UTF-8.
3. Emit one `diff --git` section with `index <oldId>..<newId>` and Myers hunks.
4. Sign and submit.

Rules that keep the patch valid:

- Diff the raw bytes, never a decoded string, so `oldId` is the real blob id
  for the three-way fallback.
- If the server supplies a blob id and it disagrees with the computed one,
  refuse and offer the clone path.
- Omit the mode on the `index` line; the tree API does not expose modes, and
  guessing `100644` would strip an executable bit.
- Refuse bytes that are not valid UTF-8 rather than decoding them lossily,
  because the decoded text becomes the new file content.

## Submission

```json
{"pull": {"title": "…", "base": "main", "head": "<account>:mobile-edit/<label>",
  "patch": "diff --git …", "commits": "", "description": "…",
  "author": "<node pubkey>", "authorName": "<account>", "ts": 0, "sig": "…"}}
```

`base` is the branch being browsed. `head` is informational. `commits` is
empty because there are no local commits. The signature covers
`"\x00".join([title, base, head, patch, commits])` under
`forkmesh-pull-event-v1`. The relay assigns the number outside the signed
bytes.

## Limits

| Condition | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Binary or non-UTF-8 content | Refused, clone path offered |
| File over 512 KB | Refused, clone path offered |
| Served blob id disagrees | Refused, clone path offered |
| Inbox full (`429 inbox_full`) or author quota (`429 author_quota`) | Shown as "not accepting pull requests right now" |
| Upstream moved while editing | Submitted; `--3way` absorbs drift, real conflicts surface at merge |

Because a single-file edit carries no commit mbox, the owner merges it under
their own name and the relay records the contributor.

## Forks from the phone

A phone cannot host, but it can publish. A fork is a clone published as
`<me>/<name>` with `forkedFrom` set in the signed catalog record. The field is
omitted, not empty, when a repository is not a fork, so older catalog
signatures stay valid.

Not built yet: a push-access probe (the signed `info/refs?service=git-receive-pack`
request answers it: `200` yes, `401` no, `503 push_unavailable` unknown),
multi-file edits, file creation and deletion, and a fork button.

pages.title: ForkMesh-Owned Git Engine Specification

pages.markdown:
# ForkMesh-Owned Git Engine Specification

The mobile apps carry their own Git engine: Swift in
`native/ios/ForkMeshCore/Sources/FMGit` and Kotlin in
`native/android/core/src/main/kotlin/com/forkmesh/nativeapp/git`. It treats all
repository and network data as attacker-controlled and is a security boundary.

## Dependency boundary

Runtime code is owned ForkMesh code plus platform standard libraries
(Foundation, system zlib and a pinned SHA1DC detector on iOS; the JDK on
Android). No libgit2, JGit, go-git, other Git library, Git executable, shell or
process fallback. System Git is used only in tests, as fixture generator,
disposable smart-HTTP server and interoperability oracle. A source and runtime
guard fails the build if production code can spawn a process.

## Supported subset

- Non-bare SHA-1 repositories, `core.repositoryformatversion = 0`, app-private
  worktree with `<worktree>/.git`. Bare repositories, linked worktrees,
  `core.worktree`, alternates, grafts, replace refs and extensions other than
  `objectFormat = sha1` are rejected; SHA-256 returns
  `unsupportedRepositoryFormat` without touching disk.
- Objects: blobs, trees, commits; annotated tags parsed. Modes `100644`,
  `100755`, `120000`; gitlinks rejected. Commits are written UTF-8 with no
  `encoding` header.
- Refs: loose refs under `refs/heads/`, `refs/remotes/`, `refs/tags/`, symbolic
  or detached `HEAD`, packed refs read-only. Writes use lock files and atomic
  rename; reflogs only for `HEAD` and `refs/heads/*`.
- Config: only `.git/config`, and only `core.repositoryformatversion`,
  `core.filemode`, `core.bare`, `extensions.objectformat`, `remote.<n>.url`
  (HTTPS, no credentials), `remote.<n>.fetch`, `branch.<n>.remote`,
  `branch.<n>.merge`. Includes, aliases, hooks paths, helpers and external
  commands are rejected.
- Index version 2 only, no extensions written. Pack v2 and index v2 read
  (including `OFS_DELTA` and `REF_DELTA`); non-delta packs written. Thin packs
  rejected.
- Local operations: status, add, remove, branch, checkout, commit, log, read
  tree and blob.

## Transport

HTTPS smart HTTP only; no `git://`, `ssh://`, `http://`, `file://` or URL
user-info. Fetch is protocol v2 only (`Git-Protocol: version=2`) with stateless
negotiation (32 `have` lines per round, at most 8 rounds), no thin packs. Push
uses the receive-pack advertisement with expected-old-OID commands,
`report-status-v2` when offered, and a typed result per ref. Non-fast-forward
and force updates are refused locally before any body is sent; ref deletion is
not expressible. Redirects are never followed. Authentication headers come
from a caller-supplied provider that sees the final method, URL and body; the
engine stores no credentials and sends no cookies. Downloaded packs land in a
quarantine directory and are installed atomically only after every hash and
limit check passes.

## Not supported

SHA-256 repositories, shallow and partial clone, LFS, SSH, submodules, linked
worktrees, merge and rebase, hooks, credential helpers, signature verification,
and server-side hosting. Each fails with a typed error instead of a lossy
approximation.

## Resource limits

Limits are part of the protocol boundary. Callers may lower defaults but never
raise hard caps.

| Resource | Default | Hard cap |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| pkt-line length | 65,520 B | 65,520 B |
| pkt-lines per response | 50,000 | 200,000 |
| refs per advertisement | 25,000 | 100,000 |
| object size | 64 MiB | 256 MiB |
| compressed pack per operation | 512 MiB | 1 GiB |
| inflated pack per operation | 768 MiB | 1 GiB |
| delta chain depth | 32 | 50 |
| delta expansion ratio | 32:1 | 64:1 |
| tree depth / entries per tree | 64 / 25,000 | 128 / 100,000 |
| checkout files / bytes | 100,000 / 512 MiB | 250,000 / 1 GiB |
| path component / path length | 255 B / 1,024 B | 255 B / 4,096 B |
| connect or first byte / idle read | 15 s / 30 s | 30 s / 60 s |
| operation deadline | 5 min | 15 min (30 min if approved) |

Cancellation is checked before every network read and write, every 64 KiB of
body, every inflate append, delta instruction, file write and rename. A
cancelled operation leaves the repository in its prior state.

## SHA-1 policy

Plain SHA-1 is not collision-safe. Complete object frames are screened through
the pinned SHA1DC detector; for untrusted transport the engine fails closed
(`hashScreeningUnavailable`) whenever a clear detector result is unavailable.
Network SHA-1 operations stay gated on collision-corpus evidence and
independent cryptography review.

## Worktree and filesystem policy

Checkout happens only inside an app-private root, one validated path component
at a time. Absolute paths, empty, `.` or `..` components, NUL, backslash,
control characters, trailing dot or space, reserved device names and
platform-ambiguous colons are rejected, as are case or normalization
collisions. A checkout is built in a sibling staging directory, verified to
stay below its root, then promoted atomically. Repository-controlled symlinks
are never followed; a symlink is written only if its target cannot escape.

## API and errors

`GitRepository` exposes open/init, `status`, `add`, `remove`, `commit`,
`createBranch`, `checkout`, `clone`, `fetch`, `push`, `readTree`, `readBlob`
and `log`. Network operations report bounded, redacted progress to a
`GitProgressListener` and honour a `GitCancellationToken`. Errors are typed:
`invalidRepository`, `unsupportedRepositoryFormat`, `invalidObject`,
`objectHashMismatch`, `invalidTree`, `invalidRef`, `refLocked`, `indexCorrupt`,
`packCorrupt`, `packChecksumMismatch`, `deltaDepthExceeded`,
`resourceLimitExceeded`, `pathEscapesWorktree`, `symlinkEscape`,
`networkUnavailable`, `tlsRejected`, `authenticationFailed`,
`protocolUnsupported`, `remoteRejected`, `nonFastForward`, `cancelled`,
`operationInterrupted`. Callers never parse message text.

## Atomicity and recovery

Every mutation writes a bounded journal in `.git/forkmesh-journal/` (operation,
staging paths, expected old and new refs) with no credentials or content.
Objects and packs are written to private temporary paths, verified, then
renamed; index, config, reflog and ref changes go through lock files in a fixed
order. On open, recovery removes uncommitted staging or completes an idempotent
rename; if preconditions cannot be proven, the repository opens read-only with
`operationInterrupted`. A partial clone never produces a valid-looking `HEAD`.

## Threat model

| Threat | Mitigation |
| --- | --- |
| Path traversal, symlink escape, case-folding overwrite | Component validation, staging-root containment, no symlink traversal |
| Malformed objects, zlib or delta bombs | Checked cursors, declared-size checks, streamed inflate, depth and ratio caps, hash verification |
| Pack or index corruption | Signature, count, CRC, checksum and ordering checks before use |
| Ref injection, lock races, stale push | Ref grammar, lock files, expected-old-OID commands, no force |
| Credential disclosure | No URL user-info, redaction, request-scoped memory only |
| TLS downgrade or redirect to another host | HTTPS only, strict validation, zero redirects, no trust-all API |
| Protocol desync | Exact pkt-line framing, MIME checks, capability allowlist, count caps |
| Crash or cancellation mid-operation | Quarantine, journal, idempotent recovery, read-only fail-closed |
| SHA-1 collision | Full-frame screening, fail closed without a detector result |
| Executable fallback | No third-party runtime dependencies, process guard |

Interrupted operations surface `operationInterrupted` rather than inferred
success, and recovery preserves a diagnostic copy instead of deleting a
repository.

## Testing

Published vectors for SHA-1, SHA-256, zlib, framing, tree order and refs;
bidirectional fixtures against system Git for local authoring; packs from
several Git versions plus malformed corpora, delta bombs and cancellation;
disposable smart-HTTP remotes for credentials, TLS, rejection and stale push;
fuzz and property tests for every parser.

pages.markdown:
# Mobile access to owner-encrypted agent sessions

Agent sessions are end-to-end encrypted to the owner's devices. The phone is an
owner device with its own key, so it can read sessions, queue prompts for a
mirror, and control a desktop live on the LAN or through the relay.

## The owner-device model

Each owner device holds a hybrid recipient key and registers only the public
halves at `POST /api/security/owner-keys`. The desktop seals every session
snapshot and transcript tail into one `forkmesh.owner-sealed` envelope with one
wrap entry per enrolled device. The relay stores ciphertext and holds no
private key.

```json
{
  "kind": "forkmesh.owner-sealed", "v": 1,
  "alg": "x25519+mlkem768/aes256gcm",
  "nonce": "…", "tag": "…", "body": "…",
  "recipients": [{ "kid": "…", "x25519": "…", "mlkem768": "…", "nonce": "…", "tag": "…", "key": "…" }]
}
```

- One random AES-256-GCM content key encrypts the payload; it is wrapped per
  device under X25519 + ML-KEM-768.
- 1 to 6 recipients (`MAX_OWNER_ENVELOPE_RECIPIENTS`), no duplicates; the
  sealing device's entry comes first.
- A recipient id is `base64url(SHA-256(x25519Pub || mlkemPub))`.
- Wrap key: `HKDF-SHA256(ssX25519 || ssMlKem, salt "forkmesh-mirror-kem-v1",
  info ephemeralX25519Pub || mlkemCiphertext)`.
- Each device opens its own entry by key id.

**Authorization is membership.** The repository privacy policy names the
desktop vault key (`ownerKeyId`). The relay requires that key to be among the
recipients, so the desktop can seal to itself plus every companion device; an
envelope without it is rejected with `wrong_owner_key`.

The desktop refreshes companion bundles every ten minutes and re-seals when the
set changes. Revocation is not retroactive: stored envelopes stay readable by
the devices they were sealed to.

| Runtime | Role | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Relay | Validates framing and bounds, never decrypts | `app/src/security_controls.py` |
| Desktop | Generates the vault key, seals to vault plus companions | `desktop/src/MirrorCrypto.cpp` |
| iOS, Android | Enroll the device key, open their own entries | `FMCrypto/OwnerCrypto.swift`, `security/OwnerCrypto.kt` |

When sessions exist but are sealed to other devices, the app says how many
and how to enroll this one, instead of showing an empty list. Cross-runtime
tests seal with the desktop binary and open in Swift and Kotlin.

## Sending a prompt to a mirror

A prompt typed on the phone uses the relay-readable agent queue, as the web
does. `GET /api/repo/{o}/{r}/agent-sessions` (or the organization
`agent-bots` route) lists nodes that can take the job; an online mirror is
suggested first. Failed or stopped runs can be retried: a claimed session
continues on its branch, an unstarted one is re-queued. Prompts can carry
photos, downscaled to 2048 px with metadata stripped, within a 10 MB total.
The Cloud section lists runs that mirrors are working; the relay's
`cloud-agents` event topic refreshes it. A queued session shows its chain:
prompt, mirror, branch, pull request, merge.
Merging a mirror agent's branch straight onto its base is owner-only: the
node's owner, or an owner of the organization. Anyone else gets `forbidden`
and opens a pull request instead.

## Controlling a desktop on the LAN or through the relay

Live control opens the desktop's local-control protocol directly over the mesh
TCP port on the same network, or inside `{"type":"control"}` chunks forwarded
by the account event relay when away. The Ed25519-authenticated handshake
derives per-direction AES-256-GCM keys, so the relay sees only routing
metadata.

Discovery: `GET /api/accounts/desktops` returns the caller's enabled desktop
keys and labels. The phone caches the list for ten minutes, tries at most four
candidates, and checks the answering desktop's public key. No LAN pairing is
needed: this is automatic same-account desktop discovery.

Admission: the desktop checks the phone key against its account's enabled
`owner_sign` devices. A same-account phone is accepted without a code and
stored as an account-held, desktop-local pairing (`"approval": "account"` in
`data/local_control/paired-devices.json`). The desktop re-checks the account on
connect and every ten minutes, and closes the channel (`revoked`) when the
phone is gone. Through the relay, a phone is admitted only if the account
confirmed it within 24 hours (`account_check_failed` otherwise). A phone from
another account must pair on the LAN with a six-digit code.

Channel recovery: idle relayed channels are pinged every 30 seconds; a desktop
that lost a channel answers `channel_gone` so the phone redials; the desktop
closes channels silent for 15 minutes, holds at most eight, and limits
half-open relayed hellos to 16 with a 30-second expiry.

| Action | Methods | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List, start, read, prompt, stop, continue | `agents.*` | Authenticated channel |
| Attach photos | `agents.image.begin`, `agents.image.chunk` | Desktop checks size, type and SHA-256 |
| Answer tool requests | `agentops.approvals`, `agentops.prepare`, `agentops.answer` | One-use desktop confirmation plus phone device authentication |
| Review changes and images | `agentops.diff`, `agentops.file` | Read-only; credentials redacted; images up to 2 MiB |
| Merge and clean up | `agentops.prepare`, `agentops.merge` | Agent must be idle; unstaged edits in the desktop checkout that clash with the merge can be set aside first (**Set aside and merge**, backed up on a `wip/` branch) |
| Delete agent, worktree and branch | `agentops.prepare`, `agentops.delete` | Explicit confirmation; agent must be idle |

An older desktop answers `unsupported` and the phone asks for an update.

## Limitations

- Away-from-home control needs the desktop online, signed in and connected to
  the relay.
- A relay reconnect closes the live channel; the next action opens a new one.
- File transfer is LAN-only.

pages.description: The wire and policy contract that makes the iOS and Android apps mobile nodes of a ForkMesh account: peers of the desktop node, coupled to it through the account on the relay.…
pages.markdown:
# Mobile node contract

The wire and policy contract that makes the iOS and Android apps **mobile
nodes** of a ForkMesh account: peers of the desktop node, coupled to it through
the account on the relay. The owned Git engine is specified in
[`owned-git-engine-spec.md`](owned-git-engine-spec.md).

Principle 1.2's "never device-to-device" boundary is
superseded for optional desktop control: a phone may open the desktop's authenticated, end-to-end
encrypted control protocol on the LAN or through the relay. See
[Mobile access to owner-encrypted agent sessions](mobile-agent-access.md#controlling-a-desktop-on-the-lan-or-through-the-relay).
The phone stays independently useful and never hosts repositories.

## 1. Principles

1. **Nodes author and publish; mirrors serve.** A mobile node creates, commits
   and publishes repositories. It never hosts clones and never runs in the
   background.
2. **Coupled through the account.** Desktop and phone are each fully useful
   alone (optional desktop control aside).
3. **Login is the bind.** Password (plus TOTP when enrolled) authenticates the
   person; the phone's Ed25519 key is registered as a `mobile_node` device on
   that login. No QR code or second ceremony.
4. **The web app is the node registry.** Listing and revoking nodes happens on
   the web.
5. **User presence only for destructive actions** (section 6).
6. **Capabilities limit blast radius.** A `mobile_node` key can publish and
   sign as the owner but never host, mirror, or touch payout settings, secrets
   or mirror process control.

## 2. Device kinds and capabilities

| Kind | Capabilities |
| --- | --- |
| `desktop_node` | `browse,comment,submit_issue,submit_pr,host_repo,mirror_repo,publish_repo,owner_sign` |
| `mobile_node` | `browse,comment,submit_issue,submit_pr,publish_repo,owner_sign` |
| client (web) | `browse,comment,submit_issue,submit_pr` |

`contribution_key_proof` is appended once the device proof verifies. A
`mobile_node` row never satisfies a hosting check (`host_repo`, `mirror_repo`,
mirror process control, node reservation). `_owner_signing_pubkeys(owner)`
unions every enabled, unrevoked `owner_sign` device, so a phone key signs
sync, catalog publications and other owner-signed requests.

## 3. Bind (login)

`POST /api/accounts/login` with `identifier`, `password`, optional `totp`,
`pubkey`, `deviceTs`, `deviceSig`, `deviceKind: "mobile_node"` and
`deviceLabel`.

- `deviceSig` signs `forkmesh-device-bind-v1\n{account}\n{pubkey}\n{deviceTs}`.
- A mobile bind registers the device with `MOBILE_NODE_CAPABILITIES`, never
  becomes the account's primary key and never counts as `desktopCapable`.
  Unknown kinds return `400 invalid_device_kind`.
- The session records the device (`account_sessions.device_bi`). The response
  reports `sessionKind`, `capabilities`, `canHost: false`, `canPublish`,
  `canOwnerSign`, `deviceId` and the account's devices.
- The first bind of a new device raises a "new node added" notification.

## 4. Node registry

| Route | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/accounts/devices` | Devices with kind, label, capabilities, enabled, last seen, and `current` |
| `DELETE /api/accounts/devices/{id}` | Re-authenticated (password, TOTP). Revokes the device and every session it opened |
| `POST /api/accounts/devices/check` | Whether a key belongs to the caller's account; used by the desktop to admit same-account phones |
| `POST /api/accounts/devices/revoke-all` | Re-authenticated. Revokes every other device and session, optionally by kind |

Revocation removes the key from owner signing at once, sessions fail with
`401` and `device_revoked`, and a revoked row is permanent: the app rotates its
seed, keeps local repositories and returns to login.

## 5. Audit

`account.device_bind`, `account.device_revoke` and
`account.device_revoke_all` are audited. Catalog records store the signing key
as `maintainer`, so the web can show which node published.

## 6. Destructive actions

Deleting a local repository; deleting, transferring or archiving a published
one; revoking devices; changing password or security settings. These require
Face ID, Touch ID or the device passcode, or an explicit confirmation when none
is enrolled.

## 7. Publish and push

The engine speaks smart HTTP to the app origin only; the relay is a masked
proxy in front of the mirror gateway.

- `GET /{owner}/{repo}/info/refs?service=git-receive-pack`
- `POST /{owner}/{repo}/git-receive-pack`

Writes carry `X-ForkMesh-Pubkey`, `X-ForkMesh-Ts` and `X-ForkMesh-Sig` over
`forkmesh-git-push-v1\n{owner}\n{repo}\n{method}\n{ts}\n{sha256hex(body)}`. The
relay accepts the owner's primary key, an enabled `owner_sign` device with
`publish_repo`, or a key with organization write permission, then forwards
under a per-request masked-proxy capability for
`/v1/repositories/{owner}/{repo}/git-receive-pack`.

- Bodies up to 8 MB are verified in full. Larger packs send
  `X-ForkMesh-Body-Sha256`; the relay streams the body and binds the capability
  to that digest. Otherwise `413 push_too_large`.
- The gateway runs `git receive-pack --stateless-rpc` with deletes and
  non-fast-forwards denied, `fsckObjects` on, hooks disabled and a bounded
  input size. It creates a bare repository on first push only for owners on
  its `writableOwners` allowlist, and removing an owner revokes push and read.
- With no healthy push endpoint, the first push goes to
  `HOSTED_GIT_WRITE_NODE`, else `503 push_unavailable`.
- After a first push the phone publishes the signed catalog record itself. A
  publish from a non-authoritative device is accepted only as a subordinate
  mirror (`202`, `mirror: true`); replays get `409 stale_update`.
- Stock Git can push with a Basic credential the website issues from a
  signed-in session (see [hosted repositories](../hosted-repositories.md)).

Client guardrails: no force, no delete, no hooks, foreground only, resource
caps and cancellation.

## 8. Platform notes

No background modes, no runtime code download, no hook execution. Store
listings say "publish", never "host" or "server".

pages.markdown:
# Using Siri with ForkMesh on iPhone

The ForkMesh iPhone app adds its commands to Siri and the Shortcuts app. You
can start an agent, ask what your agents are doing, answer their requests, and
stop, continue, message, merge or delete them without opening the app.

## Before you start

- Install the app and sign in. For commands that control an agent, sign in to
  the ForkMesh desktop app with the same account; the phone reaches it through
  the relay.
- Open the app once after installing or updating it so Siri learns your
  agents' names.
- In **Settings → Siri**, turn Siri on and allow ForkMesh to work with it.

Apple requires the app's name in every built-in phrase: say "in ForkMesh" (or
"for", "on", "with ForkMesh"). For shorter phrases, see
[Your own phrases](#your-own-phrases).

## Naming an agent

Siri knows each desktop agent by its session number ("Agent 754"), spoken as a
number or digit by digit, or by part of its title or repository. Leave the
agent out and Siri lists your agents and asks which one.

## What you can say

| Goal | Example phrases |
| --- | --- |
| Start an agent | "Start a new agent in ForkMesh", "Start a ForkMesh agent on *repository*" |
| Check status | "What are my ForkMesh agents doing?", "What did agent 754 change in ForkMesh?" |
| Answer a request | "Approve ForkMesh request", "Deny the ForkMesh request" |
| Message | "Tell agent 754 in ForkMesh" |
| Stop or continue | "Stop agent 754 in ForkMesh", "Continue agent 754 in ForkMesh" |
| Merge | "Merge and clean up agent 754 in ForkMesh" |
| Delete | "Delete agent 754 in ForkMesh", "Delete all agents in ForkMesh" |
| Open a screen | "Open inbox in ForkMesh", "Open *owner/repository* in ForkMesh" |
| Listening | "Start listening in ForkMesh", "Turn the ForkMesh Genie on", "Stop listening in ForkMesh" |

- Starting an agent opens the prompt composer, even if the app was closed.
- Approving, merging and deleting read a summary from the desktop, ask for
  confirmation, and need the iPhone unlocked. Merge and continue work only on
  desktop agents. "All agents" means the agents ForkMesh started on your
  desktop; deleting removes each agent with its worktree and branch.
- Listening turns on the in-app voice assistant while ForkMesh is on screen.
  Speech is recognised on the device and nothing is kept.

## Apple Watch

Say "Start a new agent in ForkMesh" on the watch, dictate the prompt and
confirm. The iPhone starts the agent with the last model you used, on the last
repository you used unless you name one. The **Start an agent** action takes an
optional **Repository** (`owner/name` or just the name), so a shortcut can fix
it. The iPhone must be nearby and signed in.

## Commands without a built-in phrase

Apple allows ten built-in commands per app, so **Stop all agents**, **Start a
timer**, **Open agent run**, **Open inbox**, **Open agent approvals**, **Open
issue**, **Open note** and **Start a new iOS build** are available in the Shortcuts
app only.

## Start a new iOS build

"Hey Siri, start a new iOS build" builds `main` ad hoc on the Office MacBook
and emails the install link to the iOS testers, like the iOS button on the
office MacBook row of the Desktops page. Set it up once:

1. In the Shortcuts app, tap **+**, then **Add Action**, and pick ForkMesh's
   **Start a new iOS build**.
2. Keep the shortcut's name, **Start a new iOS build**, and tap **Done**.

Siri asks you to confirm before the build starts, and needs the iPhone
unlocked and paired with the desktop. If a build is already running, Siri says
so and leaves it running.

## Your own phrases

In the Shortcuts app, add a ForkMesh action (for example **Start an agent**),
fill in fixed values, and name the shortcut with the phrase you want. "Hey
Siri, *shortcut name*" then runs it without saying "ForkMesh".

## Troubleshooting

| Siri says | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| Agent number not recognised | Open the app to refresh the agent list, or pick from the list |
| "Sign in to ForkMesh first." | Sign in on the phone |
| "Pair this phone with your desktop first." | Run the desktop app, signed in to the same account |
| "Siri can only do that for agents on your desktop." | Manage cloud agents in the app |
| "Update ForkMesh on the desktop to delete agents from here." | Update the desktop app |
| "Allow the microphone and speech recognition…" | Enable both in **Settings → ForkMesh** |
| A web search opens instead | Include "ForkMesh" in the phrase |
