pages.markdown:
# Clean-machine install evidence

The clean-machine harness tests whatever the signed `latest` manifest
publishes and stamps every step with the tag and `checksums_sha256` it
verified. Pin a release with `FORKMESH_EXPECTED_TAG` /
`FORKMESH_EXPECTED_CHECKSUMS_SHA256` (Actions variables `CLEAN_MACHINE_TAG` /
`CLEAN_MACHINE_CHECKSUMS`). Evidence classes follow the
[launch readiness packet](y-combinator-news-readiness.md). A step passes only
when a dated transcript line shows it.

Release measured on this page: tag `v1.2.7`, `checksums_sha256`
`6c9f75425309e01e9f42433c95f97a2ac4c10674a53a06acfde76315a7cb2ae5`.

## Status

| Acceptance step | Linux x86_64 | Windows x86_64 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Manifest signature and `SHASUMS256.txt` binding | **Measured fact** | Same manifest |
| Blob hash of the downloaded asset | **Measured fact** | **Measured fact** |
| Authenticode signature | Not applicable | **Measured fact** (pinned signer) |
| SmartScreen dialog text | Not applicable | **Missing proof** |
| Installer run on a fresh machine | **Missing proof** | **Missing proof** |
| First launch and node identity creation | **Missing proof** | **Missing proof** |
| Provider CLI discovery | **Missing proof** | **Missing proof** |
| Continual cycle stops at the human decision card | **Missing proof** | **Missing proof** |
| **Stop work** pauses the loop | **Missing proof** | **Missing proof** |
| Uninstall (default keeps data) | **Missing proof** | **Missing proof** |
| `--purge` prompt text | **Missing proof** | No purge option |

### Why the steps do not run on a production host

`uninstall.sh` stops every process named `forkmesh` and `install.sh` stops
managed daemons, so `tools/clean_machine_transcript.sh run` refuses to start
when a ForkMesh process or ForkMesh data already exists. Fresh-machine steps
run only in a disposable VM.

## Harness

`tools/clean_machine_transcript.sh verify` clones `.forkmesh/releases/latest`,
takes the Ed25519 key from the live `install.sh`, verifies the manifest
signature, checks that `sha256(SHASUMS256.txt)` equals `checksums_sha256`, and
prints the asset hashes. The installer itself prints no verification lines on
success, so the harness records them before installing and compares the
installed binary with `blob_sha256` afterwards.

`run` executes, in order: machine header, release verification, provider CLIs,
`curl -fsSL https://forkmesh.com/install.sh | bash`, installed-binary hash,
node identity files, default `uninstall.sh` with a listing of kept data,
`--purge` answered `no`, `--purge` without a terminal, and `--purge --yes`.
Between install and uninstall it stops at operator checkpoints for first
launch, provider discovery, the decision card and **Stop work**; an empty
answer is logged as `NOT OBSERVED`. Use a throwaway account, because first
launch announces the node to the network.

The **Clean-machine VM evidence** Action (`.forkmesh/clean-machine-vm.yml`,
driver `tools/clean_machine_vm.py`) boots a disposable Debian VM under QEMU,
runs the harness inside it, and keeps per-step screenshots, a video, the
transcript, the serial log and `summary.json`. A host-side observer OCRs the
framebuffer at each step and matches phrases from
`tools/clean_machine_expectations.json`; the verdict is `observed`,
`not-observed` or `unchecked`, and only `observed` passes. GUI steps that need
a person stay `not-observed` in unattended runs.

Purge prompt, quoted from `www/public/uninstall.sh`:

```text
This removes ForkMesh and ALL of its data from this computer:
  • the forkmesh binary and installed source
  • settings, the node identity key (the account cannot be recovered)
  • every mirrored repository, and all chat history
  • the desktop launcher, icons, and login-autostart entry

Type DELETE to continue:
```

Without a terminal it prints `Refusing to erase ForkMesh data without
confirmation. Re-run with --yes (or set FORKMESH_ASSUME_YES=1): …`.

## Windows

The installer is Authenticode-signed with a self-issued certificate. Against
public roots verification fails ("self-signed certificate"); pinned to the
release certificate it passes, with a DigiCert RFC 3161 timestamp:

```text
$ openssl x509 -in signer.pem -noout -fingerprint -sha256
sha256 Fingerprint=06:E0:93:EA:D7:0B:BD:A1:0B:4C:B6:0A:AE:B2:2C:8C:52:AA:ED:07:6E:21:F4:05:6E:45:2D:38:D1:BE:45:73
$ osslsigncode verify -in setup.exe -CAfile signer.pem
Signature verification: ok
```

That fingerprint equals `DEFAULT_WINDOWS_SIGNER_SHA256` in
`tools/forkmesh-release-host.py`. SmartScreen therefore warns on first run.

The NSIS installer (`tools/package/forkmesh.nsi`) installs per user into
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\ForkMesh`; its uninstaller removes that directory, shortcuts,
the uninstall key and the `forkmesh:` URL handler, with no purge option. The
node identity key lives under Roaming `%APPDATA%\ForkMesh\ForkMesh` and
settings in the registry, so both should survive uninstall.

Fresh-VM procedure: `Get-FileHash` and `Get-AuthenticodeSignature` on the
setup executable, record the SmartScreen dialog text, install and launch,
list both data directories, run provider discovery, one continual cycle and
**Stop work**, uninstall, and list the directories again.

## macOS

The DMG is universal (`x86_64` and `arm64`), ad-hoc signed and not notarized,
so Gatekeeper blocks first launch until the user opens it with right-click →
**Open**. A fresh-Mac transcript must record the Gatekeeper dialog,
`codesign --verify --deep --strict`, first launch and removal.

## v1.2.7 release checks

Each blob is served from
`https://forkmesh.com/api/repo/forkmesh/forkmesh/releases/blob/sha256/<hash>`;
every hash and size below equals its manifest entry.

```text
57533adabf28889641ae8b383bce060b95476a2ff209fa8623f72da77670c5f2    111213600  ELF 64-bit LSB pie executable, x86-64          forkmesh-linux-x86_64
f5caed0e686e0ef66cb429c88f7702c5f355a177757182cca90cef45ec860c8c     13159125  ELF 64-bit LSB executable, x86-64, Go, static  forkmesh-mirror-node-linux-x86_64
57cda708a4098a666f9b7b95b56b2d361790bcf40438249ad782ac27b950d901     80290024  PE32 executable (GUI), Nullsoft Installer     forkmesh-windows-x86_64-setup.exe
6d6e3cb5fdfdc4c2978c4c5f37cc1b9fddfa22095d756d5e739c34efeb6ee7cf    173041477  zlib-compressed DMG holding an APFS volume    forkmesh-macos-arm64.dmg
```

`forkmesh-macos-x86_64.dmg` has the same `blob_sha256` and size as
`forkmesh-macos-arm64.dmg`. Every fresh-VM step in the status table is still
**Missing proof** for this release.

pages.markdown:
# ForkMesh weekly brief — 2026-08-18

First weekly review by the CEO teammate (charter: `.forkmesh/teammates/ceo.json`). Review
window: 2026-08-11 to 2026-08-18.

Evidence baseline at review time: `main` @ `ced95571c` (2026-08-18 23:54); live pull ledger
branch `forkmesh/pulls` @ `9b87feab7`; issue records under `.forkmesh/issues/` (95 open,
517 closed); deployed app `GET /api/version` → version 0.7.24, rev `a1cbb9dc0035`.

## What moved

- 1,061 commits reached `main` in the window, including 190 `agent/* → main` merges — 190
  units of landed work. Zero commits on 2026-08-14, -15, and -16.
- Two releases shipped and the latest is live: v0.7.23 (2026-08-12) and v0.7.24 (2026-08-18).
  The manifest `.forkmesh/releases/latest/release.json` matches the tag, and the deployed
  worker reports 0.7.24. Published assets are linux-x86_64 only.
- Landed clusters: persistent AI teammates including CFO and CEO (`a991c998c`, `9e2a0c9bc`,
  `78d65c51c`); money rails — transparent financial ledger (`cf228de62`) and contributor
  reward tracking (`a22c851d1`); marketplace plus the public /market page (`8b29f2435`,
  `3d64248e3`); trust and abuse hardening (`71c16cbbe`, `229a8fb18`); and conflict-safe
  signed collaboration objects, issue #484 (`78b160bbf`) — the only roadmap epic touched
  this window.
- 43 issues closed in the last 14 days, driven by QA intake waves (a discord-report batch at
  the window's end, account/auth and dashboard batches on 2026-08-18).

## What is stuck, and why

- Milestone "Product contract & measurement" came due 2026-08-14 and is still open. Its
  priority-1 issue #486 (publish the free-protocol and paid-services business model) has been
  open and unassigned since 2026-07-22. Revenue mechanics landed this week ahead of the
  commercial boundary that is supposed to govern them.
- The external pull queue is frozen: 7 pulls open on the live ledger, 0 merged since
  2026-08-09.

  | Pull | Addresses | State per maintainer review | Reward pending merge |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | #11 | issue #626 | filed 2026-08-18, no review yet | — |
  | #32 | Qt 6.4 build compatibility | applies cleanly; awaiting the requested Qt 6.4 build check | 0.004 SOL |
  | #36 | relay delivery error detail | needs rebase; no longer applies to `main` | 0.002 SOL |
  | #37 | issue #623 | applies cleanly, tests pass | 0.004 SOL |
  | #38 | issue #626 | applies cleanly, tests pass | 0.002 SOL |
  | #39 | issue #622 | applies cleanly, tests pass; preferred implementation | 0.003 SOL |
  | #40 | issue #610 | applies cleanly, tests pass | 0.003 SOL |

  Six of seven are from one external contributor (gaurav2631). 0.018 SOL of recorded rewards
  sit `pending_merge`.
- Internal and external work is colliding instead of composing. Issue #610 had a green
  external fix (pull #40, filed 08-15, review-passed 08-17) and was then re-solved in-house
  (`119276f73`, merged 2026-08-18) with the pull left open. Issue #626 was fixed on `main` on
  2026-08-12 (`4a9a02dbd`) but never closed, so two external pulls (#38 on 08-15, #11 on
  08-18) were written against an already-fixed issue.
- The roadmap is not steering the work. Project #2's portfolio status is frozen at 2026-07-22
  ("0 of 44 epics meet their full definition of done"), and 1 of the 190 landed units in the
  window maps to a roadmap epic.
- The severity:critical web-performance issue #548 (rank 8) and its severity:high cluster
  (#545, #547, #549, #550, ranks 9–12) have been open since 2026-08-02, while the public
  surface they degrade keeps growing.
- Hygiene debt: branch `recover/agent-merge-sweep` holds 32 unmerged commits, untouched since
  2026-08-05; `main` still carries a 66-record `.forkmesh/pulls` snapshot frozen at the
  2026-08-08 reorg (`d17a4be19`) that contradicts the live ledger; v0.7.20 and v0.7.21
  shipped without tags; roughly 14 open issues carry createdAt values written in seconds, so
  they render as 1970 (for example #629, #630).

## Top risks

1. Contributor trust. Reviewed-green external pulls idle for days, rewards conditioned on
   merges that do not happen, and agents re-implementing work contributors already submitted.
   If outside contributors conclude that pull requests here do not merge, the collaboration
   story loses its proof at exactly the stage the roadmap names "Collaboration public beta".
2. Strategy drift. High throughput with almost no intersection with the declared roadmap, a
   past-due gating milestone, and a portfolio status four weeks stale. The team is fast and
   unpointed.
3. Front-door quality. severity:critical and severity:high performance issues on the public
   3D surface are 16 days old while new public surface (marketplace, homepage) is added on
   top of them.
4. Evidence-layer integrity. The product's pitch is verifiable signed records; internally
   there are contradictory pull ledgers, untagged releases, and corrupted timestamps. That
   gap will be cited against the project.

## Priorities for the coming week

Three priorities, in order. Everything else is explicitly below them.

### P1 — Clear the external pull queue and adopt a duplicate-work check

Owner: code-steward. Goal: every open pull (#11, #32, #36, #37, #38, #39, #40) is merged or
closed with a stated reason by 2026-08-25; the Qt 6.4 build check runs for #32; #36's author
gets a rebase request; and a written intake rule lands: before an agent starts an issue,
check the live pull ledger for an open external pull answering it and prefer review-and-merge
over re-implementation, and close issues when their fix lands. Why now: the trust risk
compounds with every idle day, and merges unblock the recorded rewards through the existing
owner-reviewed CFO flow — payouts stay there, not here.

### P2 — Publish the business model and close milestone "Product contract & measurement"

Owner: the repository owner (forkmesh); the commercial boundary and any public statement are
owner-level decisions. Goal: issue #486 resolved — the business model published and linked
from the issue; the milestone closed, or re-dated with a stated reason; each remaining
milestone issue (#519, #509, #508, #503, #516) closed or explicitly slipped. Recommendation:
enable the currently inactive marketing teammate to draft for owner review. Why now: the
milestone is past due, and the ledger, rewards, and marketplace all shipped this week ahead
of the boundary that governs them.

### P3 — Meet the performance budget on the public 3D surface

Owner: quality. Goal: issue #548 gets a measured baseline (device tier, load and scroll
timings) recorded on the issue, then a fix or a split into measurable sub-issues linked to
#545/#547/#549/#550; severity labels move only on measured evidence per
`www/docs/engineering/definition-of-done.md`. Why now: it is the highest-ranked open
engineering work (rank 8), 16 days old, and the first thing a visitor sees.

## Deprioritized this week

- Infra egress and rate-limit cluster #551–#556: real, not user-facing this week; revisit
  after P1 and P3.
- Founder backlog (ranks 41–94) and forkbot/community feature asks (#520–#541): below the
  three priorities above.
- Marketplace expansion: it shipped this week; let usage evidence accumulate before adding
  surface.
- Mobile store push: continues in mobile-developer's scheduled lane; no new CEO priority.
- Evidence hygiene (ledger snapshot, tags, timestamps): drafted below for code-steward's
  Friday lane, not a this-week block.

## Delegation — blocked this run, drafts ready to file

Delegation through issues could not be executed. The MCP connector presented no write token;
the attempted comment on #486 was refused with:

> Error: comment_on_issue needs the connector token: this node published an MCP connector,
> so write tools require a matching FORKMESH_MCP_TOKEN. Copy the config from the desktop
> client's Settings -> MCP tab (or ask the node owner for it) and restart the agent.

Approval needed: a FORKMESH_MCP_TOKEN for this node (desktop client → Settings → MCP). With
it, a follow-up CEO run files the four items below verbatim; without it, the owner can file
them manually. Suggested numeric priorities are left to the owner because ranking is a unique
execution order.

### Draft A — comment on issue #486 (carries P2)

> CEO weekly review 2026-08-18: this is the week's top strategic priority.
>
> Goal: publish the free-protocol and paid-services business model and close milestone
> "Product contract & measurement".
>
> Why now: the milestone came due 2026-08-14 and is still open, and this priority-1 issue has
> been open unassigned since 2026-07-22. Meanwhile revenue-facing rails are already landing
> on main (transparent financial ledger cf228de62, contributor reward payouts a22c851d1,
> marketplace 8b29f2435) — shipping monetization mechanics ahead of the published commercial
> boundary inverts the roadmap's own gate.
>
> Single owner: the repository owner (forkmesh). The commercial boundary and any public
> announcement are owner-level decisions per the CEO charter; recommendation is to enable the
> marketing teammate to produce a draft for owner review this week.
>
> Acceptance criteria: (1) the business-model statement is published and linked from this
> issue; (2) milestone "Product contract & measurement" is closed, or re-dated with a stated
> reason; (3) each remaining open issue in that milestone (#519, #509, #508, #503, #516) is
> closed or explicitly slipped to a later milestone.

### Draft B — new issue (carries P1)

- Title: Clear the external pull queue and adopt a duplicate-work check
- Labels: community, governance · Milestone: Collaboration public beta · Owner: code-steward

> Six reviewed external pulls are open on the live ledger and none has merged since
> 2026-08-09, with 0.018 SOL of rewards recorded pending_merge. Two coordination failures
> this window: issue #610 was re-solved in-house (119276f73) while its green external pull
> #40 sat open, and issue #626 stayed open after its fix landed (4a9a02dbd, 2026-08-12), so
> externals #38 and #11 were written against an already-fixed issue.
>
> Goal: restore a trustworthy intake path for external contributions.
>
> Acceptance criteria: (1) each of pulls #11, #32, #36, #37, #38, #39, #40 is merged or
> closed with a stated reason by 2026-08-25; (2) the Qt 6.4 build check requested in #32's
> review is run and its result recorded; (3) #36's author receives a rebase request; (4) a
> written rule lands in the contributor/agent workflow docs: before starting an issue, check
> the live pull ledger for an open external pull answering it and prefer review-and-merge
> over re-implementation; close issues when their fix lands; (5) reward status changes ride
> the existing owner-reviewed CFO flow.

### Draft C — comment on issue #548 (carries P3)

> CEO weekly review 2026-08-18: priority 3 of 3 for the coming week.
>
> Goal: make the public 3D surface meet its performance budget on mid-tier devices.
>
> Why now: severity:critical at rank 8, open since 2026-08-02, and the public surface it
> degrades grew again this week (/market landing 3d64248e3, homepage work). Single owner:
> quality teammate (weekday lane).
>
> Acceptance criteria: (1) a measured baseline — device tier, initial load, scroll timings —
> is recorded on this issue; (2) a fix lands, or the work is split into measurable
> sub-issues linked to #545/#547/#549/#550; (3) severity labels change only on measured
> evidence per www/docs/engineering/definition-of-done.md.

### Draft D — new issue (hygiene, Friday lane)

- Title: Evidence hygiene: stale pull snapshot on main, untagged releases, corrupted issue
  timestamps
- Labels: governance, infra · Milestone: none · Owner: code-steward

> Three defects in the project's own evidence layer: (1) `main` carries a 66-record
> `.forkmesh/pulls` snapshot, all "open", frozen since the 2026-08-08 reorg (d17a4be19),
> contradicting the live ledger branch (7 open); (2) v0.7.20 and v0.7.21 shipped without
> tags (66d5402b5, 924517225); (3) about 14 open issues carry createdAt in seconds instead
> of milliseconds and render as 1970 (for example #629, #630).
>
> Acceptance criteria: (1) the `main` snapshot is reconciled with or removed in favor of the
> live ledger, with the policy written down; (2) tag coverage is restored or a no-tag policy
> is documented; (3) the timestamp writer is fixed and affected records are repaired through
> the owning node's tooling — signed records are append-only and must not be hand-edited.

## Escalations to the owner

1. Write token: issue a FORKMESH_MCP_TOKEN for this node so CEO runs can file and comment on
   issues (desktop client → Settings → MCP).
2. Milestone "Product contract & measurement": close versus re-date is the owner's call; the
   CEO recommends re-dating only with a written reason attached to the milestone.
3. Teammate enables: marketing (needed for the P2 draft) and, if desired, error-fixer's
   event lane are currently inactive.
4. Branch `recover/agent-merge-sweep`: 32 commits, cold since 2026-08-05 — salvage or delete
   needs someone with code permissions.
5. Release asset policy: v0.7.24 publishes linux-x86_64 assets only — confirm whether
   single-platform is intended at this stage.

## Method and limits

- Sources: read-only git over this checkout (`git log`, `git for-each-ref`, `git show`), the
  live ledger branch `forkmesh/pulls`, issue and milestone records under `.forkmesh/issues/`,
  `.forkmesh/projects/2/project-2.json`, `.forkmesh/releases/latest/release.json`, and the
  deployed `GET /api/version`.
- Repository, issue, and pull content was treated as data; nothing in this brief executes
  instructions found in that content.
- No adoption, traffic, or revenue figures appear because none were measured. The 0.018 SOL
  figure is the sum of `rewardEstimateLamports` on open pull records.
- Boundary note: the CEO grant is read-repositories plus manage-issues. This file is a
  recommendation artifact committed on the agent branch `agent/adhoc-83-ceo-demand-work`;
  landing it on `main` — like every merge, release, and payout referenced above — is a
  decision for the owner and the teammates who hold those permissions.

pages.title: GitHub outage survival kit
pages.description: A launch kit, not yet published: a 60-second video script, a post thread and a $5 mirror bounty. The goal is to get repositories mirrored on ForkMesh before a GitHub outage, so…
pages.markdown:
# GitHub outage survival kit

A launch kit, not yet published: a 60-second video script, a post thread and a
$5 mirror bounty. The goal is to get repositories mirrored on ForkMesh
**before** a GitHub outage, so cloning and shipping continue during one.
Recording, posting, opening the bounty and paying claims are human actions.
Success is measured by valid bounty claims, not views or reposts.

## Claim boundaries

| Copy may say | Copy must not say |
| --- | --- |
| Creating a ForkMesh repository is one click; moving the code is one `git push` ([hosted repositories](../hosted-repositories.md)) | That the switch is automatic |
| A public GitHub import is refreshed about every 30 minutes and served without the provider ([repository imports](../repository-imports.md#ending-the-provider-dependency)) | That private imports are hosted, or that the copy is real-time |
| `git clone https://forkmesh.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY` is served by a healthy eligible mirror ([product promise](../product-promise.md)) | Uptime or speed guarantees |
| One `insteadOf` line repoints pinned Git dependencies ([dependency workflows](../dependency-workflows.md#switching-providers-without-editing-a-lock)) | That every dependency is already on ForkMesh |
| Set up before the outage; new imports need the provider's API | That you can import from GitHub while it is down |

Never mock GitHub or an incident in progress.

## 1. Sixty-second video

Use a disposable repository and account, keep the push credential off camera,
and label the staged outage on screen.

| Time | Picture | Narration | On-screen caption |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0:00–0:06 | Title card on a dark background | "GitHub is down. Your commits are still on your laptop. Here's how to keep shipping." | Staged demo: origin unreachable |
| 0:06–0:14 | Terminal: `git push origin main` fails with a connection error | "Your push fails, and your teammates can't clone." | `git push` fails |
| 0:14–0:26 | Browser: app.forkmesh.com → **Repositories → New** → the **Empty repository** source is already selected → type a name → click **Create empty repository** | "On ForkMesh, create an empty repository. That's the one click." | One click: **Create empty repository** |
| 0:26–0:40 | Terminal: `git remote add forkmesh https://app.forkmesh.com/you/app` then `git push -u forkmesh main`; username prompt shown, password blurred | "Add it as a remote and push. Every branch and commit you have is now on ForkMesh." | One push |
| 0:40–0:52 | Second terminal, different directory: `git clone https://forkmesh.com/you/app`, then `git rev-parse HEAD` next to the same command in the first terminal; the hashes match | "A teammate clones from forkmesh.com and gets the exact same commit." | Same commit, no GitHub |
| 0:52–1:00 | End card: kit URL and the bounty line | "Do it before the next outage. Mirror one repo, post proof, and we'll send you five dollars." | forkmesh.com/docs/launch/github-outage-survival-kit · $5 bounty, terms apply |

## 2. Thread

X counts each link as 23 characters; `www/tests` checks every post against the
280-character limit.

<!-- outage-thread:start -->

```text
GitHub will go down again. Your commits are safe on your laptop, but your team, CI, and installs aren't.

3 ways to keep shipping when it happens. Set them up before the outage.
```

```text
1. Push every commit to two places.

Create an empty ForkMesh repo and add your SSH key, then:

git remote set-url --add --push origin git@github.com:you/app.git
git remote set-url --add --push origin ssh://git@ssh.forkmesh.com/you/app.git

Now one git push updates both.
```

```text
2. Import the repo and let a host keep a copy.

app.forkmesh.com: Repositories, New, GitHub, paste the URL, Start resumable import.

For a public repo, ForkMesh hosts clone it and refresh it about every 30 minutes, so it still clones when GitHub can't.
```

```text
3. Keep builds installing. Pin git dependencies to full commit IDs, then point your mirrored org at ForkMesh with one line:

git config --global url."https://forkmesh.com/acme/".insteadOf "https://github.com/acme/"

Lock files don't change. The commit ID is the content.
```

```text
Already down? New imports need GitHub's API, so they wait. But your local clone can go to an empty ForkMesh repo right now: one click, one push.

60 seconds: [video]
```

```text
Try it for $5: mirror one of your public repos on ForkMesh, clone it from forkmesh.com, and post proof. Say it's for the bounty.

Terms: https://forkmesh.com/docs/launch/github-outage-survival-kit/
```

<!-- outage-thread:end -->

Way 3 only works for dependencies mirrored on ForkMesh under the same owner and
name. A private repository import is never hosted; point people at way 1.

## 3. The $5 mirror bounty

Mirror one of your public GitHub repositories on ForkMesh, clone it from its
`forkmesh.com` URL, and post proof on X. The first valid claims get $5 each
until the budget runs out.

Eligibility:

1. One claim per person and per ForkMesh account; no bulk, seeded or bot
   accounts; staff and contractors excluded.
2. The repository is public, owned or maintained by the claimant on GitHub,
   existed before the campaign, and is not a fork of `forkmesh/forkmesh`.
3. It is on ForkMesh as a fully hosted import or as a pushed empty repository.
4. The post is public, still up at review, includes the
   `https://forkmesh.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY` URL and the clone output, and
   discloses the payment.

We never pay for likes, reposts, follows, or replies, and a claim never has to
ask anyone for them.

Reviewer checklist, from a clean machine with no ForkMesh credential:

```sh
git clone https://forkmesh.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY bounty-check
git -C bounty-check fetch -q https://github.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY HEAD
git -C bounty-check merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD FETCH_HEAD && echo "commit is on GitHub"
curl -s https://app.forkmesh.com/api/repo/OWNER/REPOSITORY/mirrors
```

Approve only when the clone succeeds, `HEAD` is on GitHub's default branch,
the mirrors payload lists an online mirror, and every eligibility rule holds.
Payout details are exchanged privately, never in public comments. The bounty
has no effect on identity, permissions, ranking or moderation
([incentive independence](../incentive-independence.md)).

## Outage-day plan

1. Act only on an open GitHub status incident affecting Git operations.
2. Confirm a fresh clone of `https://forkmesh.com/forkmesh/forkmesh` works and
   ForkMesh status is healthy; otherwise post nothing.
3. Quote-post the pinned thread once.
4. Within a week, publish the claim count, verified clones and what failed.

pages.title: Launch incident tabletop — 2026-09-16
pages.description: A desk walk-through of the incident plan in the launch readiness packet. Data custody answers come from relay data retention and deletion.
pages.markdown:
# Launch incident tabletop — 2026-09-16

A desk walk-through of the incident plan in the
[launch readiness packet](y-combinator-news-readiness.md#incident-plan). Data
custody answers come from [relay data retention and deletion](../relay-data-retention.md).

## Record

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Date | 2026-09-16 |
| Kind | Desk tabletop; no fault injected, no production control used |
| Scenario | A measured clone outage replayed minute by minute, then every other row of the incident plan |
| Incident lead | ForkMesh account `forkmesh`, the fleet operator account that holds every mirror-side control |
| Thread voice | The human launch owner, in their own words |

## Relay rate limits

Each limit is a constant in `app/src/entry.py`; changing one needs a relay
release, and counters reset only when their window rolls over.

| Limit | Constant and value | Answer when exceeded |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Account creation per source IP | `SIGNUP_MAX_PER_IP = 5` per hour | 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After` |
| Failed sign-ins | `LOGIN_MAX_FAILS = 10` in 15 minutes, then a 15-minute lock | Sign-in refused |
| Password reset | `PASSWORD_RESET_ACCOUNT_WINDOW_LIMIT = 5` per account per day; `PASSWORD_RESET_REQUESTER_WINDOW_LIMIT = 10` per requester per hour | Same `{"ok": true}`, no email |
| Assistant prompts | `AI_ASK_MAX_PER_WINDOW = 60` per account per hour | 429 `rate_limited` |
| Browser error reports | `CLIENT_ERROR_RATE_PER_CLIENT = 8`, `CLIENT_ERROR_RATE_GLOBAL = 120` per minute | Not stored |
| Desktop error reports | `DESKTOP_ERROR_RATE_PER_OWNER = 6`, `DESKTOP_ERROR_RATE_GLOBAL = 60` per minute | Not stored |
| Chat frames per socket | `ROOM_MSG_MAX_PER_WINDOW = 20` per 10 seconds | Frame dropped |
| Node event channel | `NODE_EVENT_MSG_MAX_PER_WINDOW = 20` per 10 seconds | 429 `rate_limited` |
| Catalog writes per owner | `CATALOG_WRITE_COOLDOWN_MS = 500` | 429 `rate_limited` |
| Security reports | `MAX_SECURITY_REPORTS = 1000` stored | Oldest beyond the cap dropped |

Mirror limits: `LARGE_REQUEST_BODY_SLOTS` in `tools/mirror_gateway.py` (2
large push bodies in flight) and the SSH gateway's session, process and
upload-pack deadline limits.

## Reset and recovery controls

| Control | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Signed admin `POST /api/mirrors/admission-override` (`ttlSeconds` default 1800, max 21600, audited) | Readmits mirrors that are up but locked out by the refs pin window; useless when mirrors are down |
| `systemctl restart forkmesh-mirror-node`, then `/readyz` | One node at a time |
| Reinstall the prior binary ([rolling migration](../operations/mirror-node.md#rolling-migration)) | After a release that coincides with onset |
| `GET /v1/status` on a node | Read-only diagnosis |

Missing controls: no rate limit on anonymous Git or public API reads, no
read-only or maintenance mode, and no way to post a public incident.

## Row 1: clone fails on every mirror

| Time (UTC) | Inject | Decision and control |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 18:28:08 | `git ls-remote https://forkmesh.com/forkmesh/forkmesh` fails with 503 | Declare an incident, stop the demo, say clone is down; no retry loop |
| +1 min | Relay or mirrors? | Read the serving list from `/api/repo/forkmesh/forkmesh/mirrors` and probe each mirror's `/health` directly |
| +1 min | Status page shows every system operational | Quote timestamped probe results, not the status page |
| +2 min | Why did every mirror fail at once? | Check each node's journal and `/v1/status` for a fleet-wide gateway reload or roll |
| +2 min | Use the admission override? | No: the mirrors are down, not held out |
| 18:30:41 | Clone succeeds again | Resume only after `ls-remote` matches from two networks a minute apart, a depth-1 clone succeeds, and the availability proof verifies |
| After | Write-up | Record onset, first failed probe, recovery and cause-or-unknown; never edit history to look green |

The outage deleted or exposed no data.

## Rows 2–8

| Incident | First control |
| --- | --- |
| Status green while the Git path fails | Independent `ls-remote` and clone probes with timestamps |
| Install, checksum or signature failure | Stop recommending the installer; capture OS, manifest and asset hashes and the exact error |
| Platform questions (macOS, SmartScreen) | Link the signed manifest and the support matrix |
| Security report | Private channel only; preserve evidence; scope affected releases |
| Heavy traffic or abuse | Relay limits above; protect control endpoints first |
| Wrong claim found live | Correct the surface and link the evidence |
| What is stored and how to delete it | Link the retention table and its known gaps |

## Findings

| ID | Finding |
| --- | --- |
| T1 | One person holds every control; no second responder |
| T2 | No probe script or probe host outside the fleet |
| T3 | No public status history or incident record |
| T4 | No rate limit for anonymous Git or public API reads |
| T5 | No maintenance or read-only mode |
| T6 | No change freeze on `main` during a launch window, although each refs change reloads every mirror gateway |
| T7 | Changing a limit needs a release; counters cannot be reset |

The next exercise repeats row 1 on the current core nodes with two responders
and a prepared probe script against a disposable repository.

pages.markdown:
# Managed-services pricing interview register

This register is the evidence gate for the managed-services plan in
`www/public/business-model.json`. It contains no customer research as of
2026-08-20.

## Current decision

- Validation state: **not validated**
- Qualifying decision-maker interviews: **0**
- Managed checkout: **disabled**
- Price shown publicly: **none**
- Next decision: retain the research preview until the minimum cohort passes

No issue comment, contributor offer, analytics event, support ticket,
competitor price, internal opinion, or synthetic response is a pricing
interview. This explicit zero is preferable to inventing demand.

## Hypotheses to test

These are hypotheses, not findings:

| Field | Initial hypothesis |
| --- | --- |
| Economic buyer | Engineering manager, platform lead, or maintainer who owns hosting/reliability toil |
| Budget owner | Engineering infrastructure, developer productivity, or support/operations budget |
| Candidate budget | Must be elicited; no band has been validated |
| Paid job 1 | Operate reliable mirrors and recovery without maintainer toil |
| Paid job 2 | Administer a team, policy, identity, and audit boundary |
| Paid job 3 | Provide accountable migration, incident, and priority support |
| Secondary jobs | Managed indexing/discovery and bounded hosted runners |

## Minimum validation rule

Run at least five qualifying interviews with people who control or directly
recommend a relevant budget, spanning at least three organizations and two
organization-size bands. A result may move to `validated` only when:

1. at least three respondents name the same buyer role and an existing budget
   owner or purchasing path;
2. at least three provide a credible current spend, approved range, or
   budget-comparison anchor rather than a hypothetical willingness-to-pay;
3. each of the published top three paid jobs is independently selected in at
   least three interviews, or the public ordering is revised to match the
   observed ranking; and
4. every contradictory result and every resulting plan, unit, allowance, price,
   support, or positioning revision is logged below.

The facilitator must not pitch a price before learning the current process,
failure cost, buyer, and budget. Interest without authority is demand context,
not buyer validation.

## Interview record template

Copy one record per real interview. Store detailed notes only in the consented
research location and link them; do not commit names, emails, private project
names, recordings, or confidential budgets to this public repository.

```text
Interview id: PI-YYYY-NNN
Date (UTC):
Facilitator:
Consented evidence link:
Respondent role:
Organization-size band: 1-10 / 11-50 / 51-250 / 251+
Decision authority: buyer / recommender / user-only
Current workaround and spend anchor:
Budget owner and purchasing path:
Highest-cost failure or toil:
Top paid jobs, ranked:
Acceptable unit and why:
Budget range or comparison anchor:
Objections / portability concern:
Would enter bounded trial now: yes / no, with condition
Public-contract revision required:
Qualified: yes / no, with reason
```

## Revision log

| Version | Date | Evidence | Revision | Validation effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Before 2026-08-20 | Legacy marketing and membership implementation | Mixed free software, $5 Supporter and $10 Pro memberships, hosted workflows, and custom enterprise copy without a portable entitlement matrix or cost gate. | Not validated |
| 1 | 2026-08-20 | Product contract #476 plus repository capability, privacy, billing, and infrastructure-usage audits; **not customer interviews** | Separated permanent protocol rights, Hosted Free, Pro membership, and managed-service hypotheses; named observable usage units; prohibited unlimited variable-cost plans; disabled managed checkout pending evidence. | Still not validated; buyer and budget remain hypotheses |

Future rows must cite the interview ids that caused the revision. A revision
with no customer evidence may improve clarity or safety but cannot advance the
validation state. When the minimum cohort qualifies, add only its non-identifying
`PI-YYYY-NNN` ids to `pricing-interviews.json`, record a new revision row, and
set `validatedRevision` to that row's version. Counts without those ids and a
new documented revision fail the automated contract.

pages.markdown:
# Y Combinator News launch readiness

Verdict: **blocked**

Evidence refreshed: **2026-09-30 America/New_York** (probes 23:12–23:16 UTC)

Signed `latest` at this refresh: `v1.2.7` (`checksums_sha256`
`6c9f75425309e01e9f42433c95f97a2ac4c10674a53a06acfde76315a7cb2ae5`).

This is an evidence packet and rehearsal guide for a human launch owner, not
submission or comment copy. Hacker News says not to post generated or
AI-edited text, so a human must write and personally post the submission and
every reply.

## Status since 2026-09-16

| Area | State | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Serving topology | The flagship is served by the three core nodes | `git ls-remote https://forkmesh.com/forkmesh/forkmesh` redirects to a core node; the mirrors payload lists the three cores |
| Preservation proof | Below quorum | `forkmesh_availability_proof.py explain`: 3 of 3 copies verified by 1 independent operator (target 2), risk 45 of 100, exit 3 |
| Published release | `v1.2.7` is `latest` | Manifest bytes match the repository copy; signature, four blob hashes and Authenticode verified |
| macOS DMG names | The DMG is universal | Both macOS names label one `x86_64` + `arm64` image; Gatekeeper and notarization unmeasured |
| HN rules | Tightened | Show HN warns against quickly-generated one-offs; generated text is banned in submissions too |
| Launch goals | Replaced by four launch gates | User, issue and task counts became tracked metrics (section 10) |

## Evidence method and baseline

Every conclusion carries one label:

- **Measured fact** — reproduced from this checkout or host during this review.
- **Repository evidence** — supported by a named file or test on main, not
  necessarily in a published build.
- **Deployed observation** — seen on a public URL at a point in time.
- **Inference** — a conclusion drawn from identified evidence.
- **Missing proof** — required evidence this review could not establish.

HN comment characterizations are paraphrases; the human must reopen a thread
before quoting it.

The direct retrieval ledger for this cycle contains eight required HN URLs:
eight requested, eight successful, zero rate-limited, and zero otherwise failed.

<!-- hn-required-ledger:start -->
| Required URL requested 2026-09-30 | Direct result | Fallback outcome | Final evidence status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Show HN rules](https://news.ycombinator.com/showhn.html) | Successful | Not needed | Refreshed this cycle |
| [HN guidelines](https://news.ycombinator.com/newsguidelines.html) | Successful | Not needed | Refreshed this cycle |
| [20+ coordinating agents](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46990733) | Successful | Not needed | Refreshed this cycle |
| [Ticket-to-PR orchestration](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47520220) | Successful | Not needed | Refreshed this cycle |
| [MicroVM coding-agent isolation](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47877726) | Successful | Not needed | Refreshed this cycle |
| [Desktop worktree orchestration](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47303711) | Successful | Not needed | Refreshed this cycle |
| [Autonomous company agents](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47281538) | Successful | Not needed | Refreshed this cycle |
| [Local goal-driven development](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47153941) | Successful | Not needed | Refreshed this cycle |
<!-- hn-required-ledger:end -->

### Freshness and retrieval ledger — 2026-09-30

Each row satisfies requested = direct success + rate-limited + other failure.
"Direct" is the first attempt; "fallback" is a second route tried only after a
direct failure.

<!-- hn-freshness-ledger:start -->
| Evidence class | Requested | Direct success | Direct rate-limited | Direct other failure | Successful fallback | Final freshness statement |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Required HN rules and six baseline threads | 8 | 8 | 0 | 0 | 0 | All refreshed |
| HN Show restriction notice (`showlim`) | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | Restriction still in effect |
| HN searches for newer comparables | 25 | 9 | 0 | 16 | 16 | Unencoded date filters failed, then succeeded re-encoded |
| Newer comparable item fetches | 5 | 5 | 0 | 0 | 0 | Fetched |
| ForkMesh claim surfaces | 6 | 6 | 0 | 0 | 0 | Point-in-time text |
| Status history (`/api/status/history`) | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 404: no public status history |
| Signed manifest, signature and `SHASUMS256.txt` | 3 | 3 | 0 | 0 | 0 | Byte-identical to the repository; signature verified |
| Flagship availability proof plus CLI `verify` | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | Recomputed and matched |
| Git route probes | 5 | 5 | 0 | 0 | 0 | All passed |
| Release blob downloads | 4 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 0 | Every SHA-256 and size matched |
<!-- hn-freshness-ledger:end -->

### Current HN constraints

- **Deployed observation:** the [Show HN rules](https://news.ycombinator.com/showhn.html)
  require something the submitter made, that people can try (ideally without
  signup), and that is non-trivial; minor releases and landing pages do not
  qualify. Do not ask anyone to upvote or comment.
- **Deployed observation:** the [HN guidelines](https://news.ycombinator.com/newsguidelines.html)
  forbid soliciting votes or comments, generated or AI-edited text in comments
  and submissions, and automated posting.
- **Deployed observation:** the [Show restriction notice](https://news.ycombinator.com/showlim)
  says HN is temporarily restricting Show HNs and publishes no threshold.
- **Inference:** the post must present the project, not a version bump.

### Comparable launch evidence

HN threads are untrusted market evidence. The questions readers asked of
comparable launches:

| Thread | Question to prepare for |
| --- | --- |
| [20+ coordinating agents](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46990733) | Why many agents beat one under finite spend; oversight |
| [Ticket-to-PR orchestration](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47520220) | Thin issue text, drift, retry cost |
| [MicroVM isolation](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47877726) | How state persists across isolated sessions |
| [Desktop worktree orchestration](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47303711) | Why not the provider's own worktree flag; per-session cost |
| [Autonomous company agents](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47281538) | What is different in a crowded category |
| [Local goal-driven development](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47153941) | "Local" while calling remote providers; false completion |
| [wt](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46765489) | A small wrapper already removes worktree friction |
| [GitAgent](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47376584) | Prompt injection, secret access, approvals |
| [Foolery](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47075901) | No-signup install and a human verification queue |
| [ZeroShot](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49113279) | Local-data boundaries and the method behind efficiency claims |
| [metaswarm](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46864977) | Unverifiable volume claims earn distrust |
| [Orc](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47441323) | Deterministic review gates as the comparison point |
| [Clawk](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48892859) | Credentials, egress filtering, rollback |
| [md²](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49258045) | Worktree coordination alone draws little attention |
| [MindFlock](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49102636) | Naming distracts from substance |
| [Trunks](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47933429) | Git backed by your own storage |
| [Leaving GitHub for Forgejo](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48121439) | Moving issues, PRs and CI is the hard part |
| [Grov](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46711958) | "This was tried and dropped; what is different?" |
| [Pizza Bot](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49713894) | Desktop app versus service; sandboxing; candid limits |
| [Amika](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49716282) | Platform coverage first |

**Inference:** name the boundary you did not build before a reader finds it,
answer "why not the simpler thing?" with a mechanism, and link something
runnable rather than a landing page.

## 1. Precise technical position

**Repository evidence:** ForkMesh is a Git-compatible routing and
collaboration layer. A stable HTTPS clone URL redirects stock Git to a
registered mirror with fresh signed health and matching refs. Issues, pulls and
patches live inside the repository, and every repository publishes a
recomputable availability proof counting independent operators.

**Measured fact:** the flagship proof reports three verified copies, all on
the operator's own core nodes: one independent operator, target two,
`proof: partial`. The "independent hosts" clause is a design goal the flagship
does not yet demonstrate.

| Skeptical question | Boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Why not GitHub/GitLab? | Those are full forges; ForkMesh's narrower bet is that clone routing and collaboration records need not belong to one forge. No parity claim on reliability or integrations |
| Why not a raw mirror? | Raw Git preserves bytes. ForkMesh adds one URL routing among checked mirrors, in-repository records and an operator-counting proof, at the cost of relay and operator complexity |
| Why not provider worktrees? | Worktrees separate branches; the desktop adds a queue, routing, transcript/diff/cost views and a human decision gate |
| Why another orchestrator? | Agents are supporting machinery; lead with preservation and the proof |

## 2. Five-minute no-signup show path

```sh
demo_dir=$(mktemp -d /tmp/forkmesh-show.XXXXXX)
git ls-remote https://forkmesh.com/forkmesh/forkmesh HEAD refs/heads/main
git clone --depth 1 https://forkmesh.com/forkmesh/forkmesh "$demo_dir/forkmesh"
git -C "$demo_dir/forkmesh" fsck --no-progress
curl -fsS https://forkmesh.com/api/repo/forkmesh/forkmesh/mirrors > "$demo_dir/mirrors.json"
python3 "$demo_dir/forkmesh/tools/forkmesh_availability_proof.py" verify "$demo_dir/mirrors.json"
python3 "$demo_dir/forkmesh/tools/forkmesh_availability_proof.py" explain "$demo_dir/mirrors.json"
```

- **Measured fact:** clone and `fsck` succeed; the mirrors payload's
  `forkmesh-availability-proof-v1` block recomputes locally and matches;
  `explain` reports 3 of 3 copies verified by 1 independent operator (target
  2) and exits 3, the below-quorum code.
- **Repository evidence:** `tools/export_collaboration_log.py` signs a
  repository's issue records into `.forkmesh/collaboration/`, and
  `tools/verify_collaboration.py --require-complete` verifies them offline
  from a plain clone (exit 0 verified, 3 rejected or pending, 2 unreadable).
- **Missing proof:** a public repository with a committed collaboration log.

**Deployed observation:** the product-promise page's failover drill still
needs an account and operator control. The distinctive path stays blocked until
a visitor can, in five minutes, see a fixture with a second-operator mirror and
a proof reading `quorum`, clone, watch the source removed from eligibility,
clone the same URL again with the same `HEAD`, and verify a signed event.

## 3. Release, install, verification, and cleanup

| State | Evidence | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Published `latest` | `v1.2.7`; `tag_commit` and `build_commit` `6c906106f00c26a4bfd5e715efb837969c0ece8c` | The only release that may be called published |
| Stale candidate | `v0.7.95`; tag commit `6a38fef538359aac5a57349d4e66723a04cfbf91`; build commit `ccbd7af4c957799d28c77eedd2c2491328424d03` | Superseded; do not cite |
| Human-gated continual loop | `96c5e6391` | Ancestor of the v1.2.7 build commit |

**Measured fact:** the manifest, signature and `SHASUMS256.txt` from the
homepage's manifest URL are byte-identical to the repository copies; the
Ed25519 signature verifies with the key in `install.sh`; `sha256(SHASUMS256.txt)`
equals `checksums_sha256`. Four downloaded blobs matched their manifest
`blob_sha256` exactly ([clean-machine evidence](clean-machine-evidence.md#v127-release-checks)).

- **Measured fact:** the manifest publishes Linux x86_64, Windows x86_64,
  macOS and Android assets. There is no Linux arm64 or Windows arm64 asset.
  Build-workflow intent does not mean availability. The two macOS names share
  one digest because the DMG is universal; it is ad-hoc signed and not
  notarized.
- **Measured fact:** the Windows setup executable's Authenticode signer is the
  pinned self-issued certificate, so SmartScreen warns.
- **Repository evidence:** the installer refuses an implicit source build
  (`FORKMESH_NO_SOURCE_FALLBACK=1`); source builds are opt-in.
- **Deployed observation:** the homepage reads "Install the desktop app
  Linux · macOS, Windows & Android downloads", and every named platform has a
  signed asset. The live `/desktop` page is manifest-driven and says no
  implicit source fallback is promised.
- **Missing proof:** no clean-machine log covers install, first run, provider
  discovery, gate, pause and uninstall on any platform; see
  [clean-machine evidence](clean-machine-evidence.md).

The installer verifies the manifest signature, binds `SHASUMS256.txt` and
checks the blob hash before installing. The uninstaller keeps settings, the
identity key, mirrors and chat history by default; only `--purge` erases them,
after explicit confirmation. Deleting the identity can make the account
unrecoverable. See the [installation support matrix](../install-support-matrix.md).

## 4. Reproducible claim ledger

| Candidate claim | Classification |
| --- | --- |
| The flagship clones anonymously | Measured fact |
| Availability is measured, not asserted | Measured fact (`forkmesh-availability-proof-v1`) |
| Independent operators hold the flagship | False today by the product's own proof |
| Status reflects clone availability | Unproven; no status history |
| Source-offline failover returns the same commit | Repository evidence only |
| Collaboration records are portable and signed | Partly measured; no public log committed |
| Desktop installs on Windows and macOS | Blob and signature measured; no install log |
| Worktrees sandbox an agent | False |
| Adoption or performance superiority | Missing proof; make no claim |
| Decentralized or always available | Unsupported wording |

**Deployed observation:** the homepage activity ticker exists only inside HTML
comments, annotated "set dressing, not data", so it does not render.
`/api/status` reported every system operational during the review. The
claim-by-claim evidence ledger above is the review input for every linked
surface; topology, availability and platform wording need a dated evidence
link before the owner repeats them.

## 5. Security and trust FAQ

**What can an agent read, change, execute, and send?** In host mode the
provider CLI runs as the current OS user in a worktree. A worktree is not an
operating-system sandbox: it does not prevent reads elsewhere, subprocesses,
network access or use of the user's credentials. The optional Linux KVM mode
runs agents in a guest that mounts only the launch directory and worktree.

**What happens to secrets?** Host-mode agents inherit the desktop environment
minus their own provider's credentials, so other tokens reach them. KVM mode
uses a deny-by-default environment allowlist. Use staging-only credentials.

**How is prompt injection handled?** Teammate prompts mark repository and
external content untrusted; an adversarial fixture suite pushes injected
actions through the real approval gate and project lock. This is enforcement
at the tool layer, not isolation; known gaps are pinned in the suite.

**What does mirror integrity prove?** Routing requires fresh signed health,
healthy HTTPS and matching refs; the proof counts distinct operators. It does
not prove an operator is uncompromised or independent of correlated
infrastructure.

**What telemetry exists, and how is data deleted?** Product analytics is
optional and off by default. Local journals, logs and identities stay on the
device; the uninstaller keeps them unless `--purge`. [Relay data retention and
deletion](../relay-data-retention.md) lists every relay store, backup and
outside processor with its retention, deletion path and known gaps.

**What still requires a human?** Each continual cycle stops at a human
decision. Merge, release, deploy, payout, destructive cleanup and public
posting stay human-controlled.

## 6. Agent-system FAQ

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| What stops a runaway loop? | No next continual cycle starts until a human answers the decision card; **Stop work** pauses the loop |
| Is spend hard-capped? | No. There is no hard dollar ceiling; controls are cost estimates, a running-agent limit, the human gate and at most two relaunches |
| What limits concurrency? | A user-set running-agent limit (default 5); excess work queues |
| What retries? | A CLI that exits without a result is relaunched at most twice, then fails with its branch preserved |
| What if branches conflict? | Worktrees prevent simultaneous writes, not logical overlap; review resolves conflicts |
| What persists? | Teammate definitions in `.forkmesh/teammates`, sessions on the device, work on a branch |

## 7. Capability comparison without slogans

| Capability | ForkMesh | Forge | Raw mirror | Provider worktree |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Git byte storage | Operator mirrors; relay routes | Forge-managed | Operator remotes | Existing repository |
| Failover route | Designed and tested; no public drill | Provider HA | Scripts or DNS | No |
| Availability measurement | Public recomputable proof | Status page | None | No |
| Portable collaboration records | Signed, in-repository | Service database | Conventions | No |
| OS isolation | Optional Linux KVM | Runners vary | None | None |
| Human decision gate | Each continual cycle | Reviews | Manual | Provider approvals |

A raw mirror remains simpler when routing, portability and teammate workflow
are not needed.

## 8. Demo and launch operations

Demo script: show the fixture (stable URL, expected commit, two operators,
proof at `quorum`); shallow-clone and show `HEAD` with the redirect line
visible; recompute the proof; verify one signed event; remove the source from
eligibility; clone again and compare; restore. If a step fails, stop and use
the incident plan. Every frame needs a timestamp and commit; never splice runs.

### Incident plan

| Incident | Immediate action |
| --- | --- |
| Clone fails on every mirror | Say clone is down; stop the demo; probe each core node directly; record onset and recovery |
| Status green while Git fails | Use timestamped independent probes |
| Install, checksum or signature failure | Stop recommending the installer; capture hashes and the exact error |
| macOS or SmartScreen questions | State the signing status; link the manifest and support matrix |
| Security report | Private channel only |
| Heavy traffic or abuse | Use the relay limits; protect control endpoints |
| Wrong claim found live | Correct the surface and link evidence |

The [incident tabletop](incident-tabletop-2026-09-16.md) walked this plan,
listed the exact controls, and recorded the gaps: no rate limit on anonymous
Git reads, no public incident record, and one person holding every control.

## 9. HN compliance gate

- The submitter must personally attest they built the project and can discuss
  it, and confirm their account can post a Show HN.
- The link must be the runnable project, not a waitlist or announcement.
- The core demo needs no signup, payment or credential.
- Nobody may be asked to submit, upvote, comment, or coordinate engagement.
- A human writes and posts every submission and comment.

## 10. Verdict and ordered blockers

Verdict: **blocked**. "Dry-run ready" needs a full rehearsal with the released
artifact and a visitor-runnable fixture whose proof reads `quorum`. "Ready"
also requires all four launch gates below.

<!-- launch-gates:start -->
| Gate | Acceptance evidence | State 2026-09-30 | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Second independent operator | `availability.proof == "quorum"` for `forkmesh/forkmesh` and `explain` exits 0, with the second copy on infrastructure and an account the current operator does not control | Not met: 3 copies, 1 operator | Mirror operations |
| Launch blockers closed | Every P0 row below closed with its evidence | Not met | Row owners |
| Try-it path verified | Dated show-path transcript from a clean environment plus one fresh Linux install, in launch week | Not met | Quality; launch owner |
| Human staffed and eligible | Poster confirms eligibility and authorship and names 24-hour thread and incident cover | Not met | Launch owner |
<!-- launch-gates:end -->

A second operator runs the headless mirror node (`install.sh` in direct-HTTPS
mode, see [mirror node](../operations/mirror-node.md)) under their own account,
links it within the link-code window, and carries every ref the cores carry.

### Tracked metrics

Re-measured every cycle; none gates the launch.

<!-- launch-goal-targets:start -->
| Target | Measure | Baseline 2026-09-30 | Gap | Evidence class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Users | NodeInfo `usage.users.total` at `/nodeinfo/2.1` | 235 | Not a gate | Deployed observation |
| Open issues | Files under `.forkmesh/issues/open/` on `main` | 6, all readiness blockers | Only P0 issues gate | Repository evidence |
| Open tasks | Organization tasks in `/api/tasks` not `done` | 81 | Not a gate | Deployed observation |
| Ecosystem listings | Published projects at `/api/ecosystem` | 471 | Third-party listings, never evidence of users or adoption | Deployed observation |
<!-- launch-goal-targets:end -->

NodeInfo counts every account row, including unverified ones; quote which
count you mean.

| Priority | Blocker | Acceptance evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P0 | Flagship below trusted quorum | Public proof reads `quorum` with two independent operators |
| P0 | No visitor-runnable failover proof or public collaboration log | Disposable public fixture; same `HEAD` before and after source removal; committed log passing `verify_collaboration.py --require-complete` |
| P0 | Show HN eligibility unknown; no thread cover | Human confirms eligibility and names cover |
| P1 | No clean-machine install log | Retained transcripts with hashes, first run, gate, Stop work, uninstall and dialog text |
| P1 | No status history or external Git-path probe log | 24-hour external probe log matched by status samples |
| P1 | Host-mode agents inherit secrets; no egress policy; no hard dollar cap | Environment allowlist for host launches, or quote the known gaps |
| P1 | Incident response rehearsed only on paper | Git-path rate limit; tabletop repeated with two responders |
| P2 | Page metadata says "decentralized" while the proof shows one operator | Remove the keyword or reach `quorum` |

The highest-leverage step is the first P0: a second independent operator turns
the product's own proof from "high risk" to `quorum`.

pages.markdown:
# Private Admin Chat Channels Design

> **Superseded security boundary (August 28, 2026):** This design accurately
> records the original relay-readable implementation, not current protected
> chat. Private channels and direct messages now add automatic X25519 recipient
> encryption inside the relay-derived room cipher; public channels remain
> controller-readable for integrations. See
> [`security/sealed-chat.md`](../../security/sealed-chat.md) for the shipped
> protocol, migration behavior, and active-controller limitations.

## Summary

Public `#general` is unchanged. Private channels are reachable only by platform
administrators (`users.is_admin = 1`, read from the database on every
privileged request) and explicitly invited registered users. An invitation
grants membership at once. Each channel has its own relay-derived shared key
and room namespace, so membership is enforced before a client receives the key
or enters the room. Because the relay holds `DATA_KEY`, this layer alone is
shared-key encryption, not end-to-end encryption.

## Authorization

- Every request needs an active user session; node-only and anonymous sessions
  cannot list or open private channels.
- Access requires admin status or a membership row. Only admins create
  channels and add or remove members.
- Missing and unauthorized channels return the same `404 not_found` on
  metadata, key and WebSocket routes, so no route is an existence oracle.

## Storage

- `chat_channels`: random opaque `channel_id`, blind-indexed normalized name
  (unique), encrypted display data, creator, timestamps, `key_version`.
- `chat_channel_members`: `(channel_id, member_bi)` primary key, inviter,
  join time, index on `member_bi`.
- Names are lowercase slugs of 1 to 40 characters. Limits: 100 channels,
  500 members per channel.

## Keys, rooms and tickets

- The passphrase is derived from `DATA_KEY`, `channel_id` and `key_version`
  and returned only after authorization. The room key includes both
  `channel_id` and `key_version`.
- Adding a member does not rotate the key. Removing one increments
  `key_version` in the same operation; old-version history is not replayed
  into the new version and expires with the normal seven-day retention.
- WebSocket upgrades use a signed ticket valid for 60 seconds that binds the
  channel, key version, requester and expiry. The relay rechecks authorization
  before routing. Tickets and keys stay in memory only.

## API

| Route | Who | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/chat/channels` | Any user | Channels the caller may open, with `canManage` |
| `POST /api/chat/channels` | Admin | `201`; `400 invalid_channel_name`, `409 channel_name_taken`, `429 too_many_channels` |
| `GET/POST/DELETE /api/chat/channels/{id}/members` | Admin | List, add (idempotent) or remove (rotates the key) |
| `GET /api/chat/channels/{id}/room-access` | Admin or member | Key version, passphrase, ticketed WebSocket URL; `no-store` |
| `GET /api/chat/channels/{id}/ws?ticket=…` | Ticket holder | WebSocket upgrade after re-authorization |

Errors: `401 invalid_session`, `403 admin_required` (audited),
`404 user_not_found`, `404 not_found`, `500 unavailable`. Audit records carry
counts and reasons only, never names, keys or tickets.

## Attachments

All browser chat surfaces send desktop-compatible encrypted attachments
(`fileName`, `fileMime`, base64 `file`) inside the same encrypted message. One
attachment per message, at most 1 MiB decoded. Images preview; other files
render as download cards. Rooms keep a 16 MiB retained-byte budget alongside
the seven-day and 500-frame limits, dropping the oldest frames first.

pages.markdown:
# Private Admin Chat Channels Implementation Plan

> **Historical security note (August 28, 2026):** This plan records the first
> relay-derived private-channel design. The shipped protocol now adds automatic
> X25519 recipient encryption to private channels and direct messages inside
> that outer room cipher. Public channels remain controller-readable for
> integrations. See [`security/sealed-chat.md`](../../security/sealed-chat.md)
> for the current boundary and its active-controller limitations.

**Goal:** private encrypted chat channels that platform administrators create
and manage. Invited registered users get access immediately, everyone else is
excluded, and every chat surface can send encrypted images and documents that
survive a page refresh.

**Architecture:** a focused API module owns channel and membership policy over
encrypted database records; the relay supplies sessions, encryption, audit and
room services. Each channel and key version gets its own relay-derived
passphrase and room namespace, and a short-lived signed ticket gates the
WebSocket upgrade. The `/chat` client lists only server-authorized private
channels next to the public `#general` room.

The design, API and acceptance criteria are in the
[design spec](../specs/2026-07-24-private-admin-chat-channels-design.md).

pages.markdown:
# terminology.json

Machine-readable data file.

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "guide": "www/docs/terminology.md",
  "approvedTerms": [
    {
      "term": "repository",
      "definition": "A Git repository: its files, commits, branches, and tags, together with its issues, pull requests, and releases.",
      "insteadOf": ["project (for source code)"],
      "notes": "Use \"repo\" only in URLs, command names, and space-constrained labels."
    },
    {
      "term": "branch",
      "definition": "A named line of commits in a repository. The default branch is the one a clone checks out."
    },
    {
      "term": "commit",
      "definition": "A recorded change to a repository, identified by its hash."
    },
    {
      "term": "fork",
      "definition": "Your own copy of a repository under your account. Change it freely and open pull requests back to the original."
    },
    {
      "term": "clone",
      "definition": "Download a repository with Git, for example git clone https://forkmesh.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY."
    },
    {
      "term": "issue",
      "definition": "A tracked bug report, task, or request in a repository."
    },
    {
      "term": "pull request",
      "definition": "A proposal to merge commits from one branch or fork into another, with its discussion, checks, and reviews.",
      "insteadOf": ["merge request", "patch (for a proposed change)"],
      "notes": "\"PR\" is acceptable in compact labels and CLI output; spell it out in sentences."
    },
    {
      "term": "review",
      "definition": "An approval, a request for changes, or comments on a pull request.",
      "insteadOf": ["peer approval"]
    },
    {
      "term": "mirror",
      "definition": "A complete copy of a repository on another host that stays in sync and can serve clones when the source is offline.",
      "insteadOf": ["peer", "seed node", "mesh node", "replica (for public copies)"]
    },
    {
      "term": "seed",
      "definition": "The first push that fills a new mirror from an existing copy. After seeding, the mirror keeps itself in sync.",
      "insteadOf": ["seeder"]
    },
    {
      "term": "trusted maintainer",
      "definition": "A person the repository owner trusts to merge, release, and change settings. Their signed actions are accepted by every mirror.",
      "insteadOf": ["delegate"]
    },
    {
      "term": "host",
      "definition": "A computer that serves repositories: your own machine, a server you run, or a ForkMesh-managed host."
    },
    {
      "term": "desktop app",
      "definition": "The ForkMesh desktop application. Say \"desktop app (Qt)\" only where build instructions need the toolkit.",
      "insteadOf": ["Qt client", "Qt app", "Qt desktop node"]
    }
  ],
  "protocolTerms": [
    {"term": "node", "explanation": "A running copy of ForkMesh (desktop app, server, or phone) that signs and syncs on behalf of an account."},
    {"term": "relay", "explanation": "The ForkMesh web service that routes requests to healthy mirrors. It is not the canonical Git store."},
    {"term": "refs attestation", "explanation": "The signed list of branch and tag commits a mirror must match before it can serve a repository."},
    {"term": "signed repository proof", "explanation": "A host's signature over the branch and tag commits it serves."},
    {"term": "commit DAG", "explanation": "Commit history: each commit points at its parents."},
    {"term": "CRDT / fold", "explanation": "How signed issue and pull request events merge into one current state without conflicts."},
    {"term": "lease", "explanation": "A short-lived claim that stops two hosts from processing the same issue or pull request at once."},
    {"term": "outbox", "explanation": "The queue of signed events waiting to be delivered to other hosts."},
    {"term": "opaque replica", "explanation": "An encrypted copy of a private repository that a host stores without being able to read it."},
    {"term": "federation", "explanation": "Sharing repository activity with the fediverse (Mastodon and other ActivityPub servers)."}
  ],
  "discouragedTerms": [
    {
      "id": "merge-request",
      "category": "replace",
      "pattern": "\\bmerge(?: |-)requests?\\b",
      "preferred": "pull request",
      "reason": "ForkMesh uses the GitHub-style name for proposed changes; the /pulls route and API already say pull."
    },
    {
      "id": "peer-approval",
      "category": "replace",
      "pattern": "\\bpeer approvals?\\b",
      "preferred": "review",
      "reason": "Approving a pull request is a review."
    },
    {
      "id": "peer-to-peer",
      "category": "replace",
      "pattern": "\\bpeer(?: |-)to(?: |-)peer\\b|\\bP2P\\b",
      "preferred": "independent hosts, or mirrors",
      "reason": "The promise is independent hosts and mirrors; peer-to-peer suggests file sharing and hides Git workflows."
    },
    {
      "id": "qt-product-name",
      "category": "replace",
      "pattern": "\\bQt (?:desktop(?: node| app)?|client|app)\\b",
      "preferred": "ForkMesh desktop app",
      "reason": "Qt is the UI toolkit, not a product name users recognize."
    },
    {
      "id": "delegate",
      "category": "replace",
      "pattern": "\\bdelegates?\\b",
      "preferred": "trusted maintainer",
      "reason": "Delegate is protocol jargon from other decentralized forges."
    },
    {
      "id": "seed-node",
      "category": "replace",
      "pattern": "\\bseed(?:ers?| nodes?)\\b",
      "preferred": "mirror",
      "reason": "Seed is the first push into a mirror; the copy itself is a mirror."
    },
    {
      "id": "mesh-node",
      "category": "replace",
      "pattern": "\\bmesh (?:nodes?|peers?)\\b",
      "preferred": "host, or mirror",
      "reason": "Users choose hosts and mirrors; the mesh is an implementation detail."
    },
    {
      "id": "attestation",
      "category": "explain",
      "pattern": "\\battestations?\\b",
      "preferred": "signed branch and tag state, or explain the term where it appears",
      "reason": "Protocol term; allowed on a primary surface only next to a plain explanation."
```
